ref.title: Holderrieth & Erives, An Introduction to Flow Matching and Diffusion Models (MIT course notes, 2026)
ref.role: Background for ODE sampling and conditional FM constructions; cited for eq (11) independent-endpoint conditional FM, and App C (non-Gaussian priors valid).
ref.focus: Conditional vs marginal velocity, conditional FM loss equivalence, requirements on source distribution, guidance (classifier-free / classifier), any discussion of ODE well-posedness and of fine-tuning/steering FM models. Check the proposal's use of these results in Sec 7, Sec 11 and App C.

reading.summary:
The notes are the 2026 MIT 6.S184 lecture notes, a self-contained tutorial that derives flow matching (FM) and diffusion models from ODE/SDE basics. Generation is framed as sampling from p_data, or from p_data(.|y) for guided generation. A flow model samples X_0 ~ p_init and integrates dX_t = u^theta_t(X_t) dt, usually with the Euler method (Algorithm 1). Theorem 3 gives existence and uniqueness: a C^1 field with bounded derivative yields a unique flow that is a diffeomorphism. The notes assert that this assumption is "almost always fulfilled in machine learning". Training works as follows. Choose a conditional probability path p_t(.|z) with p_0(.|z) = p_init and p_1(.|z) = delta_z for all z. Choose a conditional field u_t(x|z) that generates it. The marginal field u_t(x) = integral u_t(x|z) p_t(x|z) p_data(z)/p_t(x) dz then generates the marginal path (Theorem 9, the marginalization trick, proved via the continuity equation, Theorem 11). The conditional FM loss equals the intractable marginal FM loss up to a constant, so their gradients coincide (Theorem 12). Its minimizer equals the marginal field "assuming an infinitely expressive parameterization". For the Gaussian CondOT path this reduces to regressing u^theta_t(t z + (1-t) eps) on z - eps with eps ~ N(0, I) (Algorithm 3, Example 13). Training is "simulation-free".

Sec 4 relates velocity, score and denoiser for Gaussian paths (Proposition 1: u = a_t grad log p_t + b_t x; Remark 16: all are linear reparameterizations of the posterior mean E[z|x]). It gives the SDE extension that keeps the marginals for any sigma_t (Theorem 17), plus denoising score matching. Sec 5 covers guidance. Vanilla guidance feeds y to the network and trains with the guided CFM loss (eq 58). Classifier guidance writes u_t(x|y) = u_t(x) + a_t grad_x log p_t(y|x) and amplifies the second term with w > 1 (eq 62). The notes flag this explicitly as a heuristic that no longer targets p(.|y). Classifier-free guidance uses u~ = (1-w) u(x|null) + w u(x|y), trained with label dropout (eqs 63-67, Algorithm 5). The notes call it "a heuristic that is predominantly justified by its excellent empirical results". Sec 6 covers architectures (DiT with AdaLN, U-Net), latent-space generation with VAEs, and the SD3 and Movie Gen case studies (SD3: CFM objective, 50 Euler steps, CFG 2.0-5.0). Sec 7 extends the recipe to discrete state spaces with CTMCs, including masked diffusion with a point-mass initial distribution p_init = delta_[mask]^d. App E states that FM and stochastic interpolants "allow you to go from an arbitrary distribution pinit to an arbitrary distribution pdata", unlike classical diffusion, which needs Gaussian sources.

For the proposal, the notes are background. They justify eq (11), the Euler sampler (9), the conditional-mean identification claim in Sec 7, the endpoint distillation construction in Sec 11 (eqs 21-22), the averaging interpretation of path regression in Sec 12, and the source-distribution statements in App C. They do not discuss fine-tuning, reward steering, test-time adaptation, memory, continual learning or distillation. On steering, they cover only guidance and a one-paragraph pointer to GLASS Flows for alignment. So [1] cannot support any proposal claim about adaptation or steering beyond guidance. The guidance section matters structurally: the proposal's centered residual velocity (eqs 4-5) is a learned additive correction to a frozen velocity field. That is exactly the form of classifier guidance, and its W_0-centering mirrors the CFG difference u(x|y) - u(x|null).
reading.core_mechanism:
Flow model: X_0 ~ p_init (usually N(0, I_d); "whatever distribution you choose, it must be one that we can easily sample from at inference-time"), dX_t/dt = u^theta_t(X_t), with Euler update X_{t+h} = X_t + h u^theta_t(X_t), h = 1/n.
Conditional path: p_0(.|z) = p_init and p_1(.|z) = delta_z for all z (eq 11). Marginal path: p_t(x) = integral p_t(x|z) p_data(z) dz, so p_0 = p_init and p_1 = p_data.
Gaussian path: p_t(.|z) = N(alpha_t z, beta_t^2 I), with alpha_0 = beta_1 = 0 and alpha_1 = beta_0 = 1. Conditional field: u_t(x|z) = (alpha_dot_t - (beta_dot_t/beta_t) alpha_t) z + (beta_dot_t/beta_t) x (eq 20).
Marginalization trick (Theorem 9): u_t(x) = integral u_t(x|z) p_t(x|z) p_data(z)/p_t(x) dz, i.e. the posterior average E[u_t(x|Z) | X_t = x], generates p_t. Proved with the continuity equation d_t p_t = -div(p_t u_t) (Theorem 11).
Losses: L_FM(theta) = E_{t,x~p_t} ||u^theta_t(x) - u_t(x)||^2 and L_CFM(theta) = E_{t~U[0,1], z~p_data, x~p_t(.|z)} ||u^theta_t(x) - u_t(x|z)||^2, with L_FM = L_CFM + C (Theorem 12). CondOT instance (alpha_t = t, beta_t = 1-t): L = E ||u^theta_t(t z + (1-t) eps) - (z - eps)||^2 (Algorithm 3).
Gaussian-path conversions: u_t(x) = a_t grad log p_t(x) + b_t x, with a_t = beta_t^2 alpha_dot_t/alpha_t - beta_dot_t beta_t and b_t = alpha_dot_t/alpha_t (Proposition 1). For CondOT, a_t = (1-t)/t. Denoiser: D_t(x) = E[z|x] (Remark 16, eq 43).
SDE extension (Theorem 17): dX_t = [u_t(X_t) + (sigma_t^2/2) grad log p_t(X_t)] dt + sigma_t dW_t has the same marginals for any sigma_t >= 0.
Guidance: guided CFM loss E_{(z,y), t, x~p_t(.|z)} ||u^theta_t(x|y) - u_t(x|z)||^2 (eq 58). Classifier guidance: u_t(x|y) = u_t(x) + a_t grad_x log p_t(y|x), amplified as u~ = u_t(x) + w a_t grad_x log p_t(y|x) (eq 62). CFG: u~ = (1-w) u_t(x|null) + w u_t(x|y) (eq 65), trained by replacing y with null with probability eta (eqs 63-64).
Discrete analog: CTMC rate matrices, marginalization trick (Theorem 36), and a cross-entropy discrete FM loss.
key_results: Theorem 3 (p.8): "If u : R^d x [0,1] -> R^d is continuously differentiable with a bounded derivative, then the ODE in (2) has a unique solution given by a flow psi_t ... psi_t is a diffeomorphism". The notes add: "the assumptions ... are almost always fulfilled in machine learning, as we use neural networks to parameterize u_t(x) and they always have bounded derivatives."

Sec 2.1 (p.9) on the source: "In most cases, we set pinit = N(0, Id) ... Most importantly, whatever distribution you choose, it must be one that we can easily sample from at inference-time." Also: "an ODE itself is not random but fully deterministic. To inject some randomness, we simple make the initial condition X0 random."

Eq (11) (p.14): a conditional path must satisfy p_0(.|z) = p_init and p_1(.|z) = delta_z "for all z", so the source cannot depend on the data point. The discrete section repeats this: "interpolates between a distribution that is independent of z to a distribution that has all mass on z" (p.59).

Theorem 9, marginalization trick (p.16): the posterior-weighted average of conditional fields generates the marginal path, so X_1 ~ p_data. The intuition given is that the marginal field weighs each conditional velocity "by how much we believe that x comes from z".

Theorem 12 (p.20): L_FM(theta) = L_CFM(theta) + C, so the gradients coincide. "for the minimizer theta* of LCFM, it will hold that u^theta* = u^target ... (assuming an infinitely expressive parameterization)." Training is "simulation-free" (p.21).
Algorithm 3 and Example 13 (p.22): CondOT path x = t z + (1-t) eps, eps ~ N(0, I), target z - eps. The notes say SD3 and Movie Gen use this objective.

Proposition 1 and Remark 16 (p.26): for Gaussian paths, velocity, score and denoiser are linear reparameterizations of E[z|x]. The denoiser parameterization "might even be preferable from a numerical/training stability standpoint."

Theorem 17 (pp.27-28): adding (sigma_t^2/2) grad log p_t plus sigma_t dW_t keeps the marginals for any sigma_t. Footnote 2: a "best sigma_t" is "an artifact of imperfectly trained models and finite compute budgets". Remark 21: GLASS Flows gives stochastic transitions with ODEs, to "exploit the stochastic nature of SDEs (e.g. via search algorithms)".

Sec 5.1 (pp.34-35): guided CFM. "the label y does not affect the conditional probability path ... (although in principle, we could make it dependent)". Vanilla guidance "in theory ... should lead to a faithful generation procedure" but empirically adheres weakly to y, for example because "the model might underfit".

Sec 5.2 (pp.36-39): classifier guidance u(x|y) = u(x) + a_t grad log p_t(y|x). "this is a heuristic: for w != 1, it holds that u~(x|y) != u^target(x|y)". CFG is (1-w) u(x|null) + w u(x|y), trained by label dropout. "Classifier-free guidance is therefore a heuristic that is predominantly justified by its excellent empirical results ... w >= 4." Remark 26: the CFG construction is valid for any probability path.
Sec 6.3 (p.52): SD3 samples with 50 Euler steps and CFG weight 2.0-5.0. Movie Gen uses alpha_t = t, sigma_t = 1-t.
Sec 7 (p.64): masked diffusion LMs use the point mass p_init = delta_[mask]^d. The initial distribution is deterministic and the randomness comes from the stochastic CTMC dynamics.
App B (pp.73-74): the continuity/Fokker-Planck derivation requires integral p_t ||u_t|| < infinity ("almost always holds in machine learning"). Sufficiency rests on PDE uniqueness.

App E (p.84): "sampling from a flow matching model will be deterministic (only the initial X0 ~ pinit will be random)". FM and stochastic interpolants "allow you to go from an arbitrary distribution pinit to an arbitrary distribution pdata - while denoising diffusion models only work for Gaussian initial distributions".

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Reference list: "[1] ... MIT course notes, 2026. Background for ODE sampling and conditional FM constructions."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: The notes cover ODE sampling (Sec 2.1, Algorithm 1: Euler "X_{t+h} = X_t + h u^theta_t(X_t)", with Heun's method also shown) and conditional FM constructions (Sec 3, Theorems 9 and 12, Algorithm 3). Authors, title, course and year match the PDF title page.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Pin the version (18 Mar 2026 PDF or arXiv:2506.02070 latest version), because the course URL can change.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7, eq (11): "construct the usual independent-endpoint conditional FM training sample [1, 2]: x_t = (1-t) eps + t a*_k, u_t = a*_k - eps", with t uniform and eps ~ N(0,I).
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Algorithm 3 (p.22): "Sample a random time t ~ Unif[0,1]. Sample noise eps ~ N(0, Id). Set x = tz + (1 - t)eps. Compute loss ||u^theta_t(x) - (z - eps)||^2". Example 13 calls this the "(Gaussian) CondOT probability path". The guided version (eq 58) draws (z, y) jointly and eps independently, matching conditioning on (c_k, H_k).
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Only the wording of the independence condition is loose: "eps ~ N(0,I) is independent of the target conditional on the episode". The notes' construction needs p_0(.|z) = p_init for every z (eq 11), and in the guided case eps is drawn independently of both z and y. The clean statement is: eps ~ N(0,I) drawn independently of (a*_k, c_k, H_k). If eps may depend on the episode, its conditional law need not be N(0,I), and deployment with fresh N(0,I) noise would be mismatched.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7 (not explicitly cited, but grounded in [1]): "For a fixed causal history, standard conditional-mean regression identifies the marginal velocity of the interpolating distribution when the function class can represent it. With compressed history, the best predictor can only use information retained in W_k."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Theorem 12 (p.20): minimizer equals marginal field "assuming an infinitely expressive parameterization"; App A.2 eqs (103)-(104): conditional expectation is the least-squares minimizer; guided CFM eq (58) extends this to conditioning variables.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Two refinements. (i) theta is frozen and only r is learned, so the representability condition applies to the residual class: r must represent E[a*-eps | x_t, t, c_k, W_k] - v_theta(x_t, t, c_k), not the marginal field itself. (ii) Identification holds only p_t-almost everywhere, i.e. on the support of the interpolation marginals. Off-support behavior, which matters once solver or model error pushes z_t off-path, is not identified.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7: "Unlike the whole-path optimization alternative, this direct-reader objective does not require unrolling a sampling solver during each meta-training query."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: p.21: "we never actually simulate any ODE during training. People call this feature of the algorithm simulation-free." The CFM target a* - eps is analytic.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The claim holds, but each query still needs a transformer forward pass to compute h_theta, plus the second-order differentiation through the writes that the proposal already notes.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7: "No claim is made that this interpolation is a globally optimal transport path."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: The notes call p_t(x|z) = N(tz, (1-t)^2) the "CondOT" path, a conditional (per-z) construction. Nothing in the notes claims that the marginal flow is OT.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: App C: "FM does not require a standard Gaussian in every formulation. One needs a source that can be sampled at inference, a valid training construction relating source and target, and suitable conditions for the desired transport/sampler. A full-rank Gaussian mixture is a reasonable candidate if its structure is useful and available at deployment [1, 2]."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Supporting: p.9, "whatever distribution you choose, it must be one that we can easily sample from at inference-time"; eq (11) defines conditional paths for a general p_init; App E (p.84), FM and SIs "allow you to go from an arbitrary distribution pinit to an arbitrary distribution pdata"; Sec 7 uses arbitrary factorized p_init and a point mass. Not supporting: every continuous construction the notes actually give needs p_init = N(0, I) (Example 8: "this choice of p_t(x|z) fulfills Equation (11) for pinit = N(0, Id)"; Algorithm 3; Proposition 1; the guidance derivations). App E promises non-Gaussian sources "later in this class" but the notes never deliver one. Gaussian-mixture sources are not discussed anywhere.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Keep [1] for the principle (App E, Sec 2.1, eq 11). For an explicit non-Gaussian source construction (x_t = (1-t) x_0 + t z with x_0 ~ p_init independent of z), cite the stochastic interpolants paper (already [13]), Lipman et al. 2024 "Flow Matching Guide and Code" (arXiv:2412.06264, notes ref [26]), Liu et al. 2022 rectified flow (arXiv:2209.03003), and Tong et al. 2024 (minibatch-OT CFM). I did not read [2] in this task. From memory, not verified here: Lipman et al. 2023's own constructions use a standard Gaussian source, so [2] is also weak support for a Gaussian-mixture prior.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: App C (implicitly grounded in [1]): "a deterministic ODE with a unique solution maps a fixed initial point to a fixed endpoint ... It cannot produce a nondegenerate conditional action distribution without another source of randomness."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: p.9: "an ODE itself is not random but fully deterministic. To inject some randomness, we simple make the initial condition X0 random." p.84: "sampling from a flow matching model will be deterministic (only the initial X0 ~ pinit will be random)." Sec 7 (p.64): masked diffusion uses p_init = delta_[mask]^d with stochastic CTMC dynamics, an example of "another source of randomness".
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Optional refinement (my derivation, not in the notes). With a point-mass source and the linear interpolation x_t = t z, the exact FM marginal field is u_t(x) = x/t. It is singular at t=0, violates Theorem 3's bounded-derivative hypothesis, and the ODE from 0 has infinitely many solutions X_t = t z. So the exact FM target for a deterministic start is the non-unique case, and a smooth learned approximation collapses to one output.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 6 "Stability and validity": "A sufficient condition for a well-defined continuous sampler is local Lipschitz continuity in z, together with suitable growth bounds preventing finite-time blow-up. Smooth, bounded feature maps help but do not automatically certify the full transformer."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Theorem 3 (p.8) gives a stronger sufficient condition (C^1 with bounded derivative). The notes then say neural networks "always have bounded derivatives", which overstates the case for attention over unbounded inputs.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The proposal is appropriately more careful than [1] and should not cite [1]'s "always bounded derivatives" remark as a certificate for the transformer backbone.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 11 (endpoint FM distillation, eqs 21-22): "This teaches the student the teacher's conditional endpoint distribution under the chosen teacher/context sampling protocol ... With sufficiently regular target distributions, suitable capacity, and successful optimization, this is a standard FM construction."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: This is the guided CFM loss (eq 58) with (z, y) = (A^T, c) and fresh eps' independent of z, as eq (11) of the notes requires. Theorem 9 and Theorem 12 give endpoint law = teacher's context-conditional law, "assuming an infinitely expressive parameterization". Fig. 7 caption: samples match "up to training error".
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The notes need no regularity of p_data for the construction itself, since p_data may be arbitrary. Regularity matters only for flow well-posedness (the Lipschitz constant grows as t -> 1 for sharp targets), which the notes do not discuss. The proposal's phrasing is acceptable.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 12: "Different teacher trajectories can pass through the same state with different velocities; conditional regression averages those velocities" (b* = E[V_t | Gamma_t = z, C = c]).
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: This matches Theorem 9, which treats the marginal field as a posterior average of conditional velocities. The proof (continuity equation per conditional plus linearity, p.19) carries over to conditioning on a whole teacher path in weak form, which the proposal cites to [13].
proposal_claim_checks.correction: [1] could additionally be cited for the averaging interpretation. [1] states the continuity equation only in strong (density) form, so [13] remains the right citation for the weak form.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 19 eqs (29)-(30): exact Gaussian FM field v_mu(z,t) = b_t z + kappa_t mu, with s_t^2 = (1-t)^2 + t^2 sigma^2, b_t = (-(1-t) + t sigma^2)/s_t^2, kappa_t = 1 - t b_t.
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: This is not cited to [1], but I checked it against [1]'s framework: for the CondOT path and target N(mu, sigma^2 I), E[z - eps | x] = mu + Cov(z-eps, x)/Var(x) (x - t mu) = b_t x + (1 - t b_t) mu, the posterior-mean linear form of Remark 16 and eq (43).

reading.relevance_to_proposal:
Sec 3 and eq (2), base policy: this is exactly [1]'s guided flow model with y = c_k (Sec 5.1). The proposal's point that "initial noise remains random even if W_k is deterministic" matches [1] p.9.

Sec 4, eqs (3)-(5), centered residual reader: [1] Sec 5.2 gives the closest textbook analog. Classifier guidance adds a separately learned correction a_t grad_x log p_t(y|x) to a base velocity. CFG uses the difference u(x|y) - u(x|null), which vanishes when y = null, just as r vanishes at W_0. Using [1] eqs (59)-(62) with y = W_k: if v_theta equals the exact history-marginal field u_t(x|c), the population-optimal residual from eq (12) is r* = u_t(x|c,W_k) - u_t(x|c) = a_t grad_x log p_t(W_k | x, c), with a_t = (1-t)/t for CondOT. Equivalently, r* = (E[a|x,c,W] - E[a|x,c])/(1-t) via Remark 16. So the direct reader is a learned memory-likelihood guidance term. This sharpens the Sec 8 table entry "No explicit optimality principle": the reader has a Bayes/MSE-optimal target, though not a control-optimal one.

Sec 6, eq (9) Euler and stability: matches Algorithm 1. The well-posedness discussion is consistent with, and more careful than, Theorem 3.

Sec 7, eqs (11)-(12): directly Algorithm 3, eq (58) and Theorem 12. The CFM-to-FM equivalence extends to the writer parameters (my derivation using [1]'s Theorem 12 proof technique). Let u_bar_H = E[a*-eps | x_t, t, c_k, H_k] be the full-history field. The model output depends only on (x_t, t, c_k, H_k), and eps is independent of H, so the cross term vanishes and L_meta(phi, W_0) = E||v_theta + r - u_bar_H||^2 + const, with a constant independent of theta, phi and W_0. The outer loop therefore regresses onto a fixed, full-information target. The loss further splits into approximation error plus an information-loss term E||E[u_bar_H | x,c,W_k] - u_bar_H||^2.

Sec 8, reader table: classifier guidance is the textbook precedent for the value/control reader's gradient correction u* = -grad V. [1] warns that amplified guidance (w != 1) no longer targets p(.|y), which parallels the proposal's warnings in Secs 9-10 about diversity loss.

Secs 11-12, consolidation: endpoint distillation (21)-(22) is guided CFM with teacher samples. Its correctness rests on Theorems 9 and 12, and the fresh-noise requirement follows from [1] eq (11) (p_0(.|z) = p_init for all z). This supports the Sec 12 warning that success-filtered teacher noise corrupts the initial law. The path-distillation target (24) is the marginalization-trick average of Theorem 9 applied to path-valued conditioning.

Sec 13, retention: [1] offers no stability bounds. Its Gaussian-path formulas can be used to evaluate the Lipschitz constants that the bound (27)-(28) needs; see technical issues.

Sec 17, baselines: [1] exposes CFG and guidance-scale sweeps as the standard way to strengthen a conditioning signal. The baseline table lacks them.

Sec 18, extra-compute and search baselines: Theorem 17 (SDE sampling with the same marginals) and Remark 21 (GLASS Flows) are candidate stochastic search/reranking baselines.

App C: [1] supports the easy-sampling requirement, the general conditional-path definition and the generality claim for FM (App E). It gives no explicit non-Gaussian continuous construction and nothing on Gaussian mixtures. It supports the deterministic-start discussion (p.9, p.84, masked-diffusion point-mass source). The remark "although in principle, we could make it dependent" (p.35) is consistent with App C's conditional source z_0 = mu(H) + Sigma(H)^{1/2} eps, provided training and inference match.
novelty_threats: No direct threat. [1] is a tutorial with no memory, fast weights, test-time training, continual learning or consolidation content, so the proposal's core contributions (causal fast-weight writer, reader factorial, consolidation/reset lifecycle) are not pre-empted.

Weak threat to presenting the direct reader's design features as distinctive: adding a separately learned velocity correction at every denoising step (classifier guidance, eq 62) and taking the difference between a conditioned and a null-conditioned evaluation so that the correction vanishes when the condition is removed (CFG, eq 65) are both textbook. The proposal's "explicit reset centering" (eq 4) is structurally CFG with W_0 as the null condition. Novelty should be claimed for the condition itself (gradient-written fast weights) and the lifecycle, not for the per-step additive, centered velocity interface. Sec 6 already says the difference from internal TTT is "intervention location and lifecycle", which is consistent with this.

[1]'s vanilla guided FM (eq 58), i.e. a policy conditioned directly on history tokens, is the default way to make generation depend on extra information. It is the history-tokens baseline in Sec 17. [1] notes that vanilla conditioning often under-uses y and that CFG with w > 1 fixes adherence in practice. A history-conditioned FM with CFG may therefore be a stronger and simpler competitor than the proposal currently anticipates.
ideas_to_borrow: State the population-optimal residual explicitly, following [1] eqs (59)-(62) and Remark 16. r* = E[a*-eps | x,t,c,W_k] - v_theta(x,t,c). When v_theta equals the history-marginal field, this equals a_t grad_x log p_t(W_k | x, c) = (E[a|x,c,W_k] - E[a|x,c])/(1-t), with a_t = (1-t)/t for CondOT. This gives the direct reader a precise Bayes-optimality characterization (as distinct from control-optimality). It also yields a diagnostic: ideal corrections are scaled gradient fields in x.

Add a memory-guidance scale: sample with v_theta + w * r for w in {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}. Treat w != 1 as a heuristic that departs from the Bayes-conditioned distribution ([1]: "for w != 1 ... not the true guided vector field"). Report mode coverage and success versus w.

Add a CFG baseline: train a history-conditioned FM policy (history tokens or retrieval) with condition dropout of rate eta, as in Algorithm 5, and sample with CFG weight w. This is the standard FM mechanism for amplifying a conditioning signal and belongs in the Sec 17 History tokens/retrieval row.

Use the extended CFM identity to motivate and monitor the outer loop. L_meta(phi, W_0) = E||v_theta + r - u_bar_H||^2 + const, where u_bar_H is the full-history field. Train an oracle full-history conditioned FM (or history-token model) to estimate u_bar_H, and report the information-loss term E||E[u_bar_H | x,c,W_k] - u_bar_H||^2 as a function of memory capacity (the 16-32-16 MLP versus larger sizes).

Try a denoiser (posterior-mean shift) parameterization of the reader: predict delta_t = E[a|x,c,W] - E[a|x,c] and set r = delta_t/(1-t), or equivalently use kappa_t-type time weighting as in Sec 19. [1] Remark 16 notes denoiser parameterizations "might even be preferable from a numerical/training stability standpoint", and the analytic check already has correction kappa_t * delta_mu with kappa_t -> 0 as t -> 1.

Use [1] Theorem 17 (SDE sampling with identical marginals; for Gaussian paths the score comes free from the velocity via Proposition 1) and Remark 21 (GLASS Flows) as stochastic extra-compute and search baselines in Sec 18. Also use SDE sampling as a within-episode randomness source for the App C discussion.

Run the same-noise-coupling ODE/SDE comparison of Sec 18 at several solver resolutions. SD3 practice (50 Euler steps) and [1]'s footnote that the best sigma_t is "an artifact of imperfectly trained models and finite compute budgets" both support separating solver error from model error, as the proposal already intends.
Cite [1] Theorem 9's proof pattern (continuity equation per conditional plus linearity) as the elementary version of the Sec 12/App A argument. Keep [13] for the weak-form, density-free version.
technical_issues_in_proposal: Eq (11) independence wording (minor). "eps ~ N(0,I) is independent of the target conditional on the episode" should be "eps ~ N(0,I) drawn independently of (a*_k, c_k, H_k)". [1] eq (11) needs p_0(.|z) = p_init for every z, and eq (58) draws eps independently of (z, y). If eps's law varied with the episode, the deployment protocol (fresh N(0,I) noise, Sec 15 step 2) would not match training.

Sec 7 identification claim (minor). With theta frozen, "when the function class can represent it" must refer to the residual target E[u|x,t,c,W_k] - v_theta, not the marginal field. Identification is only p_t-a.e., so the reader's behavior off the interpolation support, where deployment trajectories may go under model error, is unconstrained. [1] Theorem 12 assumes an "infinitely expressive parameterization" of the whole field.

Sec 8 understatement. The table says the direct reader has "No explicit optimality principle", and Sec 10 forbids calling it optimal. By [1]'s classifier-guidance decomposition, (12) has a well-defined Bayes/MSE-optimal residual target, r* = a_t grad_x log p_t(W_k|x,c) when v_theta is the exact history-marginal field. Stating this is both more accurate and more useful than "no optimality principle".

Confound between memory and backbone correction. By the same decomposition, the regression target of r also absorbs backbone misfit: r* = [u(x|c,W) - u(x|c)] + [u(x|c) - v_theta]. Centering makes r = 0 at W_0 only, so after any write the reader could learn a history-content-independent correction to v_theta on the meta-training distribution. The proposal's shuffled and wrong-history controls (Stage B) would catch this, but only if they use the same number of writes. That requirement should be stated.

Missing standard baseline. Sec 17 has no classifier-free-guidance variant of the history-conditioned policy and no guidance-scale sweep for the proposed reader. Per [1] Sec 5.2, CFG is the default FM mechanism for strengthening a conditioning signal, and vanilla conditioning is known to under-use y.

App C citation strength. [1] states the generality of p_init (App E, p.9) but gives only Gaussian-source continuous constructions and never discusses Gaussian-mixture priors. [1, 2] alone is thin support for the full-rank Gaussian-mixture claim. Add [13], Lipman et al. 2024 (FM Guide), rectified flow, or Tong et al. 2024.

Sec 13, eqs (27)-(28): retention bound is vacuous for the planned multimodal targets. This is my analysis using [1]'s Gaussian-path/posterior-mean formulas, not a claim of [1]. [1] Theorem 3 needs a global derivative bound, and the proposal's bound uses a global Lipschitz L with C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L). For a 1-D target 0.5 N(+1, 0.1^2) + 0.5 N(-1, 0.1^2), the exact FM field has spatial derivative about 361 at the decision boundary near t = 0.94; analytically, about 0.325 m^2/sigma^3. Even a one-sided (log-norm) Gronwall factor integrates to about exp(2*48), i.e. exp(m^2/sigma^2). A single sharp Gaussian (sigma = 0.1) already gives |b_t| up to about 5. The bound is therefore not merely "loose" for the Sec 16 multimodal benchmark; it is uninformative. This is a real phenomenon (small velocity errors near mode boundaries flip modes), not a proof artifact. Report the bound for unimodal cases only, or switch to a one-sided Lipschitz version and measure Jacobian norms along trajectories using the eq (10) machinery.

Sec 6 and Sec 13 well-posedness. Do not lean on [1]'s remark that neural networks "always have bounded derivatives". Self-attention over unbounded action tokens is not globally Lipschitz, so the global-L assumption in Sec 13 may fail for the proposed 4-block transformer backbone. The proposal's own Sec 6 wording is appropriately cautious; Sec 13 should cross-reference it.

App C deterministic start (refinement, not an error). The exact FM field for a point-mass source with linear interpolation is x/t, which is non-Lipschitz at t=0 with non-unique solutions. The "unique solution" premise in App C therefore never holds for the exact FM target of a deterministic start; it holds only for smooth learned approximations, which collapse to a single output.
stated_limitations: Theorem 12 and Theorem 22: the minimizer equals the marginal field or score only "assuming an infinitely expressive parameterization". Fig. 7 notes a match only "up to training error".

Classifier guidance and CFG with w != 1 are explicitly heuristic: "for w != 1, it holds that u~(x|y) != u^target(x|y)". CFG is "a heuristic that is predominantly justified by its excellent empirical results".
Vanilla guidance, though theoretically faithful, often adheres poorly to y in practice, for example because "the model might underfit" or the data is noisy.

SDE sampling: Theorem 17 holds for any sigma_t in theory, but "in practice, we suffer from both training error ... and simulation error". A best sigma_t is an artifact of imperfect training and finite compute.

Regularity assumptions (bounded derivatives in Theorem 3, integrability of p_t u_t in App B) are asserted to "almost always" hold in ML rather than verified. The Fokker-Planck sufficiency argument defers to PDE uniqueness results.

The notes focus on unconditional generation in Secs 1-4. The guidance derivations assume Gaussian paths, with Remark 26 extending CFG to general paths. Non-Gaussian continuous sources are asserted possible (App E) but not constructed.
The notes do not cover fine-tuning, reward alignment, distillation, test-time adaptation or continual learning. GLASS Flows is mentioned only in passing.
cited_works_worth_adding: Ho & Salimans, Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance, 2022 (arXiv:2207.12598; notes ref [18]). The canonical difference-of-conditioned-fields construction that the centered reader mirrors, and the source of a missing CFG baseline and guidance-scale sweep.

Dhariwal & Nichol, Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis, 2021 (arXiv:2105.05233; notes ref [11]). Classifier guidance: an additive, separately trained gradient correction to a frozen generative field. Precedent for the value/control reader and for interpreting r* as memory-likelihood guidance.

Lipman et al., Flow Matching Guide and Code, 2024 (arXiv:2412.06264; notes ref [26]). General treatment of arbitrary sources, couplings and conditional FM. Stronger support than [1, 2] for the non-Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture source claims in App C.

Liu, Gong & Liu, Flow Straight and Fast: rectified flow, 2022 (arXiv:2209.03003; notes ref [27]). Arbitrary source-target couplings and reflow, i.e. re-pairing endpoints with noise and re-training. Directly relevant to the endpoint versus same-seed/path distillation comparison in Secs 11-12.

Holderrieth et al., GLASS Flows: Transition Sampling for Alignment of Flow and Diffusion Models, 2025 (arXiv:2509.25170; notes ref [20]). Inference-time alignment and search with FM models. A candidate extra-compute steering baseline for Sec 18.

Karras et al., Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models, 2022 (notes ref [23]). Solver and stochasticity choices and error decomposition, relevant to "separately measure solver error and distribution quality" (Sec 6).

Holderrieth et al., Generator Matching, 2024 (arXiv:2410.20587; notes ref [19]). General Markov-process generative modeling, including jump/stochastic samplers. Relevant to App C's "another source of randomness".
Chen & Lipman, Flow Matching on General Geometries, 2023 (arXiv:2302.03660; notes ref [8]). Relevant if robot action chunks include rotations or other manifold-valued components (Stage E).

errors_found.reader_claim: Sec 7 claim-check refinement (ii) and technical issue #2: "Identification holds only p_t-almost everywhere, i.e. on the support of the interpolation marginals. Off-support behavior, which matters once solver or model error pushes z_t off-path, is not identified."
errors_found.problem: In x this is wrong for the proposal's setting. Eq (11) uses a full-rank Gaussian source, so for every t < 1 the interpolation marginal p_t(x|c,W) = integral N(x; t a, (1-t)^2 I) p(a|c,W) da is strictly positive on all of R^d. No x lies off-support. The actual gaps are (a) conditioning values (c_k, W_k) outside the meta-training distribution, e.g. memory states produced by unseen histories, and (b) low-density regions where finite data constrain r poorly. That is a statistical problem, not a failure of identification. The off-support concern is legitimate only for the path-distillation setting of Sec 12 / App A, where the teacher paths have thin support.
errors_found.evidence: [1] Example 8 / eq (16): "z ~ pdata, eps ~ pinit = N(0, Id) => x = alpha_t z + beta_t eps ~ pt" with beta_t > 0 for t < 1. Eq (13): pt(x) = integral pt(x|z) pdata(z) dz, a Gaussian convolution. Proposal Sec 7: "eps ~ N(0,I)".

(ii) we reparameterized x -> (x - alpha_t z)/beta_t", with no Gaussian step in the field derivation. With compressed history, the best predictor can only use information retained in W_k". But it presumes a density for W_k, a 1,072-dim deterministic function of H_k whose law may be singular. The robust form needs only densities in x, which exist for t < 1: r* = a_t [grad_x log p_t(x|c,W_k) - grad_x log p_t(x|c)].

The ratio max*sigma^3/m^2 is 0.361 at sigma = 0.1 and tends to about 0.326 as sigma -> 0. The integral tends to m^2/(2 sigma^2). Max |b_t| is 5.05 for sigma = 0.1. But the proposal never specifies mode separation or width, so 'vacuous for the planned targets' is contingent. For m/sigma of about 2 the factor is about e^4 (loose, not vacuous). The relevant L is the Lipschitz constant of the new learned field, not the exact FM field. This is also the reader's own analysis, not content of [1]. The proposal already says "a large Lipschitz constant makes the bound loose."

claim_check_overrides.claim: App C: "FM does not require a standard Gaussian in every formulation. One needs a source that can be sampled at inference, a valid training construction relating source and target, and suitable conditions for the desired transport/sampler. A full-rank Gaussian mixture is a reasonable candidate if its structure is useful and available at deployment [1, 2]."
claim_check_overrides.reason: As a background citation, [1] supports every factual component. (a) Non-Gaussian sources are allowed: App E p.84, "allow you to go from an arbitrary distribution pinit to an arbitrary distribution pdata". (b) The source must be sampleable at inference: p.9, "whatever distribution you choose, it must be one that we can easily sample from at inference-time". (c) A valid construction is needed: eq (11), Theorem 9 and Summary 14 are stated for general p_init, and the Example 10 flow-map derivation does not use Gaussianity. A full-rank GMM is an easily sampled p_init, so it falls under [1]'s criterion. Calling it 'reasonable if useful' is the proposal's own judgment, not a factual claim attributed to [1]. The support weakness lies with [2]: Lipman et al. 2023 say p0 is "a simple distribution, e.g., the standard normal", and all their conditional paths start from N(0,I) (ref02.txt lines 125-126, 237). Adding [13] or Lipman et al. 2024 would still strengthen the citation.

missed_points: [1] Example 8 / eq (16) implies that for the Gaussian source in proposal eq (11), the interpolation marginals have full support in R^d for all t < 1. So the Sec 7/11 regression identifies the field everywhere in x. The real identification gap is coverage of the conditioning variables (c_k, W_k), i.e. memory states from unseen histories, plus data sparsity. The reader framed this as an off-support-in-x issue.

[1] Theorem 3 (flows are diffeomorphisms with unique trajectories) sharpens proposal Sec 12. For one exact, smooth teacher ODE with fixed context c and fixed memory state W, trajectories never meet at the same t. Then b* = E[V_t | Gamma_t = z, C = c] equals the teacher field on its support, and path distillation would reproduce same-seed trajectories. The velocity averaging the proposal warns about ('Different teacher trajectories can pass through the same state with different velocities') therefore arises only from (a) mixing teacher memory states or histories under a shared student context, which is exactly the App B.4 hidden-fact problem, or (b) Euler/piecewise-linear discretization, where the Euler map can be non-injective when h*L is large. The proposal half-acknowledges this ('Exact continuous paths of a smooth direct-reader ODE are a better behaved special case'), but it should name the source of the averaging.

[1] p.21 presents 'simulation-free' training as FM's key advantage. The proposal's retention penalty R_old (eq 25) is evaluated on old-policy ODE trajectories, so it needs ODE rollouts or cached trajectories. It gives up simulation-free training for the Gronwall bound. The proposal offers the simulation-free alternative (old teacher endpoints with fresh FM noise), but the cost trade-off is not stated.

By [1] Remark 16 / eq (43), an x1-prediction (denoiser) residual applied inside every step is linearly equivalent to a velocity residual: for CondOT, delta_velocity = delta_E[a|x]/(1-t). A 'final action residual' baseline is therefore a distinct method only if the correction is applied once after sampling, not re-parameterized per step. Sec 6/17 of the proposal implicitly assumes the former; it should say so.

[1] p.35 attributes the weak prompt adherence of vanilla guidance to underfitting ('the model might underfit (i.e. we do not actually learn the true marginal vector field)'). The analogous risk for the proposal is that a regression-trained reader under-uses memory. This supports adding the memory-guidance-scale sweep the reader proposed, and it is a concrete failure mode for the 'Without a dependence on history, a successful policy can simply ignore memory' concern in Sec 7.
verification.novelty_threat_assessment: None to low. I checked all 84 pages of the 18 Mar 2026 PDF, the version matching arXiv:2506.02070v3. [1] is a pedagogical tutorial covering ODE/SDE generative models, conditional FM (Thms 9, 11, 12), score/denoiser conversions, SDE sampling, guidance, architectures, VAEs and discrete CTMC FM. It contains nothing on fast weights, test-time training, memory writing, continual learning, consolidation, retention or reset lifecycles, so none of the proposal's core contributions is pre-empted. The only overlap is at the interface level. Classifier guidance (eq 62) adds a separately learned per-step correction to a base velocity, and CFG (eq 65) uses a conditioned-minus-null difference that vanishes at the null condition, which is structurally like the W_0-centered residual in eq (4). Both are textbook, so the proposal should not claim novelty for 'additive per-step centered velocity correction' as such. It currently does not (Sec 6 locates the difference in 'intervention location and lifecycle'). [1] also makes a history-conditioned FM policy with CFG a natural, simple competitor, and the Sec 17 baseline table omits it. That is a gap in the baselines, not a novelty threat.

reading.summary:
Problem. Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs: an ODE dx/dt = v_t(x; theta) that pushes a simple prior p_0 to p_1) had been trained by maximum likelihood. That needs expensive ODE simulation. The existing simulation-free alternatives either involved intractable integrals (Moser Flow) or gave biased minibatch gradients (Ben-Hamu et al. 2022). Diffusion models scale, but only along a narrow family of diffusion probability paths. The paper wants a scalable, simulation-free CNF training method that works for general probability paths.

Method. Flow Matching (FM) regresses a network v_t onto a target vector field u_t that generates a chosen probability path p_t from noise (t=0) to data (t=1). The marginal u_t is intractable, so the path is built as a mixture of per-sample conditional paths p_t(x|x1), and the marginal field is defined as the posterior-weighted average of conditional fields (eq 8). Theorem 1: this marginal field generates the marginal path (continuity equation). Theorem 2: assuming p_t(x) > 0 for all x and t, the per-sample Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) loss equals the FM loss up to a theta-independent constant, so the two have the same gradients. Section 4 specializes to Gaussian conditional paths N(mu_t(x1), sigma_t(x1)^2 I) with mu_0 = 0, sigma_0 = 1, mu_1 = x1 and sigma_1 = sigma_min "sufficiently small". Theorem 3 gives the unique conditional field of the affine flow psi_t(x) = sigma_t x + mu_t. This family recovers the VE and VP diffusion probability-flow fields (Appendix D). It also introduces the "OT" path mu_t = t x1, sigma_t = 1 - (1 - sigma_min) t, whose conditional flow is the McCann displacement map between N(0,I) and N(x1, sigma_min^2 I). The paper states that this conditional optimality does not make the marginal field an OT solution.

Results. The same U-Net (Dhariwal & Nichol) was trained with each loss on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 32/64. FM with the OT path gives the best NLL, FID and adaptive-solver NFE in every column. On ImageNet-128 it reaches NLL 2.90 and FID 20.9 (state of the art among the listed unconditional models, excluding IC-GAN). It trains with less image throughput, needs about 60% of the NFEs of diffusion models to reach the same ODE error, and holds up better at low NFE. It also works for conditional 64->256 super-resolution (FID 3.4 vs SR3's 5.2). FM with diffusion paths is reported as more stable than score matching. The paper has no limitations section. Its caveats are the regularity assumptions in the proofs, the sigma_min approximation p_1 ≈ q, the non-OT marginal field, and an unoptimized CIFAR-10 architecture.

For the proposal, this is the foundational justification for eqs (11)-(12) and (21)-(22). The proposal's usage is essentially consistent with it, including its disclaimer about optimal transport. The discrepancies are small. The proposal's interpolant is the sigma_min = 0 limit, which lies outside Lipman's stated setting. The paper also exposes a structural issue in the proposal's retention bound (27)-(28): exact FM marginal fields can have very large spatial Lipschitz constants.
reading.core_mechanism:
Setup (Sec 2-3). CNF: d/dt phi_t(x) = v_t(phi_t(x)), phi_0(x) = x, p_t = [phi_t]_* p_0. Time convention: t=0 is noise and t=1 is data. p_0 = p is "a simple distribution, e.g., the standard normal". A field "generates" p_t if the continuity equation d/dt p_t + div(p_t v_t) = 0 holds (App B, eq 26).

FM loss (eq 5): L_FM(theta) = E_{t~U[0,1], x~p_t} ||v_t(x) - u_t(x)||^2.

Conditional construction (Sec 3.1): choose p_t(x|x1) with p_0(x|x1) = p(x) and p_1(x|x1) concentrated at x1, e.g., N(x1, sigma^2 I) with "a sufficiently small standard deviation sigma > 0". Marginal path p_t(x) = ∫ p_t(x|x1) q(x1) dx1 (eq 6), with p_1 ≈ q (eq 7). Marginal field (eq 8, stated under "we assume p_t(x) > 0 for all t and x"):
  u_t(x) = ∫ u_t(x|x1) p_t(x|x1) q(x1) / p_t(x) dx1, i.e., u_t(x) = E[u_t(X|x1) | X_t = x].

Theorem 1: if u_t(·|x1) generates p_t(·|x1), then u_t from eq 8 generates p_t from eq 6. The proof differentiates under the integral and assumes "the integrands satisfy the regularity conditions of the Leibniz Rule".

CFM loss (eq 9): L_CFM(theta) = E_{t, q(x1), p_t(x|x1)} ||v_t(x) - u_t(x|x1)||^2.
Theorem 2: "Assuming that p_t(x) > 0 for all x ∈ R^d and t ∈ [0,1], then, up to a constant independent of theta, L_CFM and L_FM are equal. Hence ∇θ L_FM = ∇θ L_CFM." The proof (App A) additionally assumes "q(x) and p_t(x|x1) are decreasing to zero at a sufficient speed as ||x|| → ∞, and that u_t, v_t, ∇θ v_t are bounded", and uses Fubini together with bilinearity of the squared norm. The only property it needs is that the regression target does not depend on theta.

Gaussian paths (Sec 4): p_t(x|x1) = N(x | mu_t(x1), sigma_t(x1)^2 I) with mu_0 = 0, sigma_0 = 1, mu_1 = x1, sigma_1 = sigma_min. The flow is psi_t(x) = sigma_t(x1) x + mu_t(x1), and the reparameterized loss is L_CFM = E_{t,q(x1),p(x0)} ||v_t(psi_t(x0)) - d/dt psi_t(x0)||^2 (eq 14). Theorem 3: u_t(x|x1) = (sigma_t'/sigma_t)(x - mu_t) + mu_t' (eq 15).

OT path (Example II, eqs 20-23): mu_t = t x1 and sigma_t = 1 - (1 - sigma_min) t, so
  u_t(x|x1) = (x1 - (1 - sigma_min) x) / (1 - (1 - sigma_min) t),
  psi_t(x0) = (1 - (1 - sigma_min) t) x0 + t x1,
  L_CFM = E ||v_t(psi_t(x0)) - (x1 - (1 - sigma_min) x0)||^2.
With sigma_min = 0 this is exactly the proposal's eq (11): x_t = (1-t) eps + t a*, target a* - eps. The paper claims optimality only for the conditional flow: psi_t is the McCann (1997) displacement map between N(0,I) and N(x1, sigma_min^2 I). It adds: "although the conditional flow is optimal, this by no means imply that the marginal VF is an optimal transport solution. Nevertheless, we expect the marginal vector field to remain relatively simple."

Diffusion special cases: reversed VE, u_t(x|x1) = -(sigma'_{1-t}/sigma_{1-t})(x - x1) (eq 17); reversed VP, eq 19. These coincide with the probability-flow ODE of Song et al. (App D).

Likelihood (App C): log p_1(x1) = log p_0(x0) - f(0), obtained by integrating div v backward with a Hutchinson trace estimator (eqs 27-35).

Sampling: draw x0 ~ N(0,I) and solve the ODE to t=1 with dopri5 (atol = rtol = 1e-5) or with fixed-step Euler, midpoint or RK4.
key_results: Table 1, CIFAR-10 (NLL bpd / FID / NFE): FM w/ OT 2.99 / 6.35 / 142; FM w/ Diffusion 3.10 / 8.06 / 183; DDPM 3.12 / 7.48 / 274; Score Matching 3.16 / 19.94 / 242; ScoreFlow 3.09 / 20.78 / 428.

Table 1, ImageNet 64x64: FM-OT 3.31 / 14.45 / 138; FM-Dif 3.33 / 16.88 / 187; DDPM 3.32 / 17.36 / 264; SM 3.40 / 19.74 / 441; ScoreFlow 3.36 / 24.95 / 601. The paper notes: 'FM-OT consistently obtains best results across all our quantitative measures'.
Unconditional ImageNet 128x128: FM-OT NLL 2.90, FID 20.9, versus PGMGAN 21.7 and unconditional BigGAN 25.3. IC-GAN is excluded because it uses conditioning.

Training efficiency on ImageNet-128: FM used 500k iterations at batch size 1.5k, versus 4.36M iterations at batch size 256 for Dhariwal & Nichol, i.e. '33% less image throughput'. The adaptive-solver NFE stays roughly constant during FM training but varies during score-matching training (Fig 10).

Low-NFE sampling on ImageNet-32 with the midpoint scheme: measured as per-pixel MSE against 1000-NFE solutions over 256 noise seeds, FM-OT reaches the same error threshold with 'roughly only 60% of the NFEs' of diffusion models, and it keeps a better FID at low NFE for Euler, midpoint and RK4 (Fig 7).

2D checkerboard (5-layer, 512-unit MLP): the OT path 'introduces the checkerboard pattern much earlier' along the path and gives more stable training (Fig 4). On ImageNet-64 with shared seeds, OT paths remove noise roughly linearly, while diffusion paths remove it mostly at the end (Fig 6).
Conditional super-resolution 64->256 on ImageNet validation (FID / IS / PSNR / SSIM): FM-OT 3.4 / 200.8 / 24.7 / 0.747; SR3 5.2 / 180.1 / 26.4 / 0.762; regression 15.2 / 121.1 / 27.9 / 0.801.

Theory: Theorem 1 (marginal field generates the marginal path), Theorem 2 (CFM and FM gradients are equal when p_t > 0 everywhere), Theorem 3 (closed-form conditional field for Gaussian paths). The OT conditional flow is the McCann displacement map between N(0,I) and N(x1, sigma_min^2 I); the marginal field is explicitly not claimed to be OT.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7: 'At each later decision k, construct the usual independent-endpoint conditional FM training sample [1, 2]: x_t = (1-t) eps + t a*_k, u_t = a*_k - eps (11). Here t is sampled uniformly, eps ~ N(0,I) is independent of the target conditional on the episode...'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Lipman eqs 20-23: mu_t(x) = t x1, sigma_t(x) = 1 - (1 - sigma_min) t; psi_t(x) = (1 - (1 - sigma_min) t) x + t x1; L_CFM = E_{t,q(x1),p(x0)} ||v_t(psi_t(x0)) - (x1 - (1 - sigma_min) x0)||^2, with t ~ U[0,1] and x0 ~ N(0,I) drawn independently of x1 (the expectation is over the product q(x1) p(x0)). Sec 3.1 requires p_1(x|x1) to have 'a sufficiently small standard deviation sigma > 0'. Sec 4: 'sigma_1(x1) = sigma_min, which is set sufficiently small'. Theorem 2 assumes p_t(x) > 0 for all t in [0,1], and its proof in App A assumes bounded u_t.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Eq (11) is Lipman's OT-CFM sample in the limit sigma_min = 0. Lipman always uses sigma_min > 0 and never analyses sigma_min = 0. At sigma_min = 0 the conditional field (x1 - x)/(1-t) is singular at t = 1. For singular or discrete action targets, Theorem 2's positivity-at-t=1 and boundedness assumptions then fail. This is harmless in practice (the endpoint t = 1 has measure zero, and the 16-step Euler grid never evaluates it), but the citation should either (a) write x_t = (1 - (1 - sigma_min) t) eps + t a*, u_t = a* - (1 - sigma_min) eps with a stated sigma_min, or (b) keep sigma_min = 0 and cite rectified flow (Liu et al. 2022) or stochastic interpolants ([13]; Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden 2022), whose assumptions cover this form. 'Independent-endpoint' is not Lipman's term. His per-x1 construction with a common N(0,I) source is equivalent to the independent coupling, so the description is otherwise accurate.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7: 'For a fixed causal history, standard conditional-mean regression identifies the marginal velocity of the interpolating distribution when the function class can represent it. With compressed history, the best predictor can only use information retained in W_k.'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Eq 8: u_t(x) = ∫ u_t(x|x1) p_t(x|x1) q(x1)/p_t(x) dx1, which is the posterior mean of the conditional field. Theorem 2: 'up to a constant independent of theta, L_CFM and L_FM are equal. Hence ∇θ L_FM(θ) = ∇θ L_CFM(θ).' Theorem 1: the marginal field 'generates the marginal probability path'. Sec 6.3 shows FM used for conditional generation (super-resolution).
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The claim is correct under Lipman's regularity assumptions: p_t > 0, Leibniz/Fubini regularity, bounded fields. Lipman states the theorems only for unconditional q(x1). The conditional (c_k, H_k) version follows by applying them per condition, which Lipman demonstrates empirically but does not state. One nuance should be made explicit. For the meta-gradient with respect to writer and interface parameters (phi, W_0) to equal an FM gradient, the FM target must be the full-history marginal field u*(x,t,c_k,H_k) = E[a*-eps | x_t = x, t, c_k, H_k]. It must not be the W_k-conditional field, because what W_k retains depends on phi, so Theorem 2's 'constant' would then depend on the learned parameters. Since W_k is a function of H_k only, the cross-term vanishes and equivalence holds for the H_k-target. This also means the causality rule ('the query target must not appear in its own preceding memory writes') is mathematically required: if W_k depended on (eps, a*_k), the regression target would no longer be a marginal field.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7: 'No claim is made that this interpolation is a globally optimal transport path.' Also the reading map: 'What is not assumed? ... guaranteed optimal transport', and Sec 12: 'Neither option turns the learned field into optimal transport by definition.'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Lipman Sec 4.1: 'The conditional flow psi_t(x) is in fact the Optimal Transport (OT) displacement map between the two Gaussians p0(x|x1) and p1(x|x1)'. Also: 'we note that although the conditional flow is optimal, this by no means imply that the marginal VF is an optimal transport solution. Nevertheless, we expect the marginal vector field to remain relatively simple.' The abstract limits OT to the conditional paths: 'using Optimal Transport (OT) displacement interpolation to define the conditional probability paths.'
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The disclaimer is fully consistent with Lipman, who makes the same disclaimer. For precision, the proposal could state what Lipman does claim. Each per-sample path is the McCann displacement interpolant, a W2 geodesic between N(0,I) and N(a*, sigma_min^2 I) (at sigma_min = 0, between N(0,I) and delta_{a*}). The marginal flow induced by the independent coupling is in general not the W2-optimal map between N(0,I) and the action distribution, and its trajectories need not be straight. Lipman's 'guaranteed to stay straight' (Fig 3) refers to the conditional paths only.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 11 (eqs 21-22): 'Independently draw a new source sample eps' and train a memory-free student with ordinary FM ... This teaches the student the teacher's conditional endpoint distribution ... With sufficiently regular target distributions, suitable capacity, and successful optimization, this is a standard FM construction. Singular endpoints may require smoothing or a terminal noise floor for a regular continuous flow.'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Eq 23 is the same loss with x1 := A^T and sigma_min = 0. Eq 7: 'p1(x) = ∫ p1(x|x1) q(x1) dx1 ≈ q(x)'. Lipman's sigma_min > 0 is exactly a terminal noise floor. Theorem 2 needs p_t(x) > 0, and the proofs need boundedness and decay assumptions.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: This is a standard CFM construction with a fresh independent source. One small caveat: with Lipman's sigma_min > 0, the population student learns the teacher endpoint law convolved with N(0, sigma_min^2 I), not the law itself. The proposal's 'terminal noise floor' remark covers this but could name sigma_min and its value.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Appendix C: 'FM does not require a standard Gaussian in every formulation. One needs a source that can be sampled at inference, a valid training construction relating source and target, and suitable conditions for the desired transport/sampler. A full-rank Gaussian mixture is a reasonable candidate if its structure is useful and available at deployment [1, 2].'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Lipman Sec 3: 'we let p_t be a probability path such that p_0 = p is a simple distribution, e.g., the standard normal distribution'. Sec 3.1: conditional paths satisfy 'p0(x|x1) = p(x)'. Theorems 1-2 are stated for general conditional paths. However, Sec 4 (the only concrete construction) sets 'mu_0(x1) = 0 and sigma_0(x1) = 1, so that all conditional probability paths converge to the same standard Gaussian noise distribution', and every experiment uses N(0,I). The Conclusion's future work mentions only 'non-isotropic Gaussians or more general kernels' for the paths.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Lipman's general Sec 3 framework allows a non-Gaussian source p with positive density, so a Gaussian mixture is admissible there. The paper never constructs, analyses or tests a non-Gaussian source, and its Theorem 3 construction assumes the standard Gaussian. More direct support is [13] (stochastic interpolants), Tong et al. 2023 (arXiv:2302.00482, CFM with arbitrary source/coupling) or Pooladian et al. 2023 (arXiv:2304.14772). I did not check [1].

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 7: 'Unlike the whole-path optimization alternative, this direct-reader objective does not require unrolling a sampling solver during each meta-training query.' (This relies on FM being simulation-free; it is not cited to [2] explicitly.)
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Abstract: 'Flow Matching (FM), a simulation-free approach for training CNFs based on regressing vector fields of fixed conditional probability paths.' Sec 5: 'the Flow Matching framework allows simulation-free training with unbiased gradients'.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: None needed with respect to the ODE. As the proposal already notes, the meta-gradient still differentiates through the inner fast-weight writes, which is outside Lipman's scope.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Reference-list entry [2]: 'Lipman, Y., Chen, R. T. Q., Ben-Hamu, H., Nickel, M., and Le, M. Flow Matching for Generative Modeling. ICLR 2023; arXiv:2210.02747.'
