reading.summary:
WAM-TTT tackles a deployment problem: how to steer a pretrained robot world-action model (WAM) toward new task variants or user-preferred behaviours using only raw, unlabelled human videos. It avoids robot demonstrations, retargeting, hand-pose annotation, full fine-tuning and long-context conditioning. The backbone is LDA (LDA-1B), a Qwen3-VL-4B VLM plus a 16-block DiT-L MMDiT head. Each MMDiT block has a video expert (visual latent tokens; in LDA these are DINO-feature latents) and an action expert (action-chunk tokens), and the two interact through joint attention. LDA trains both streams with flow-matching velocity objectives. WAM-TTT adds a TTT residual branch to the video expert of every block: z^(l+1) = zhat^(l+1) + theta_O f_W(theta_Q(z^(l))), while the action stream is left untouched (x^(l+1) = xhat^(l+1)). Actions are affected only indirectly, through joint attention. Because the branch sits inside the denoiser, the fast weights are read at every denoiser evaluation.

Training has two stages.
- **Meta-training** uses 2,286 paired human-robot episodes, phase-synchronised by nearest normalised phase t/T_r. The inner loop starts from a learned W_init and takes N=1 SGD step on a human-side objective: the LDA video-prediction loss on the human clip, computed on final-block latents (so the gradient passes through the whole WAM), plus lambda times a per-layer key-value reconstruction loss ||f_W(K_h) - V_h||^2 / (B L_h d).
- **The outer loss** is LDA's robot multitask loss (video plus action flow matching) evaluated with the adapted weights W_N. It is backpropagated through the inner update into Theta_WAM (the backbone is also trained), theta_{K,V,Q,O} and W_init. Fast weights are discarded and reset to W_init after each training example.
- **At deployment**, Theta_WAM, the slow projections and W_init are all frozen. A small batch of in-scene human videos drives the same combined objective for N=1 step with inner learning rate 0.01; meta-training used 0.1. After that step, "the adapted fast weights W_N are fixed during robot rollout" (Eq. 9).

Appendix A argues that in the linear case the KV-reconstruction optimum is the Hebbian outer product sum_i v_i k_i^T, so reading it with robot queries gives a softmax-free linear-attention readout of the human keys and values. The authors present the branch as a parametric substitute for robot-to-human cross-attention.

The evaluation covers 9 real-robot tasks on three embodiments (Unitree G1, Galbot gripper, Galbot sharpa), scored by a partial-credit "progress" metric over 25 trials per cell. There are two settings: Orig. (the training cubicle) and New (unseen household scenes with lighting, height and object changes). In New, WAM-TTT averages 46.2%, against 32.5 for LDA, 25.3 for WAM-CoTrain, 15.0 for an EgoScale re-implementation, 14.8 for pi0.5 and 7.1 for WAM-ICL. In Orig. it averages 61.1, against 50.2 (LDA) and 48.4 (ICL).

The ablations use 10 trials on two tasks. They show the gain depends on meta-training (without it: 9.0 and 0.0), that the KV reconstruction term helps (without it: 66.7 and 72.0, versus 100 and 88.9), and that TTT beats LoRA (30.0 and 0.0). Appendix experiments cover:
- a meta-training data-ratio sweep;
- a VLM ablation, where freezing the VLM during meta-training gives 54 versus 100;
- a pseudo-action forward-dynamics loss on human data, which hurts badly (72.3 to 28.9);
- qualitative robustness rollouts.

There is also a no-human-video deployment in which only W_init drives the branch. The stated limitations are the phase-pairing assumption, adaptation bounded by the fast network and the fixed slow projections (the boundary is not characterised), and RGB-only human input.

The paper has several internal problems.
- The text of Sec. 4.2 disagrees with its own Table 1 on which tasks WAM-TTT wins.
- For the same cell (Swap Place, New), Table 2 reports 88.9 and Table 1 reports 66.7.
- Evaluation tasks are described as "unseen-task", yet the meta-training data covers the same 9 tasks, and human meta-training videos were recorded in the New household scenes.
- No seeds, error bars or latency figures are reported.
- The conclusion says the method "matches or exceeds online-adaptation baselines", but no online-adaptation baseline is evaluated.
reading.core_mechanism:
**Backbone (LDA-1B, from the LDA paper).** An MMDiT with separate video and action experts that share self-attention. Actions and future DINO latents are trained with flow matching: l_action = E || v^a_theta - (eps_a - a_{t+1:t+k}) ||^2, and likewise for observations. WAM-TTT says it adopts "LDA's exact loss formulation, weighting, and noise schedule without modification" and calls it a "flow-matching / diffusion denoising loss".

**Architecture (Eqs. 1-2).** For every block l (all L=16 are "TTT-augmented"):
- z^(l+1) = zhat^(l+1) + Dz_TTT^(l), and x^(l+1) = xhat^(l+1).
- Dz_TTT^(l) = theta_O^(l) f_{W^(l)}( theta_Q^(l)(z^(l)) ).
- Slow parameters are theta_{K,V,Q,O} and W_init. The fast network f_W is a small MLP; Table B.1 gives TTT head dim d=48 and fast hidden width f_h=128, with D=1536 and H=32.
- The residual is not centered: at W = W_init the branch still outputs theta_O f_{W_init}(.), which is generally nonzero. App. E.2 deploys exactly this branch with no human data.

**Write losses.**
- KV reconstruction (Eq. 3): L_KVM^(l)(W_i) = 1/(B L_h d) || f_{W_i^(l)}(K_h^(l)) - V_h^(l) ||_2^2, with K_h = theta_K(h_phi), V_h = theta_V(h_phi), where h_phi is the phase-synchronised human token.
- Robot queries: Q_r = theta_Q(z_r).
- Inner objective (Eq. 4): L_adapt(W_i) = L_vg^human(u_h; Theta_WAM, theta_TTT, W_i) + lambda sum_l L_KVM^(l)(W_i), with lambda = 4e-2. L_vg is the LDA video-prediction loss on final-block latents z^(L). Its gradient with respect to W therefore passes through the whole WAM, and the residual also acts on the human-video tokens during the write.
- Update (Eq. 5): W_{i+1} = W_i - eta grad_W L_adapt, starting from W_0 = W_init, with N=1 and eta = 0.1 at meta-training.

**Outer loop (Eq. 6).** L_meta = L_WAM^robot, the video plus action FM loss on the paired robot data, computed with W_N. Gradients go "through the TTT residual and the inner fast-weight update" (the analytical Spatial-TTT update) into Theta_WAM, theta_{K,V,Q,O} and W_init. Fast weights are reset to W_init per example.

**Test time (Eqs. 7-9).**
- Theta_WAM, theta_TTT and W_init are frozen.
- L_TTT(W_i) = 1/|B_h| sum_{u in B_h} [ L_vg(u; ...) + lambda sum_l L_KVM^(l)(u; W_i) ], with W_{i+1} = W_i - eta grad L_TTT, eta = 0.01 and N = 1.
- Rollout: a_{t:t+k} ~ p_{Theta_WAM, theta_TTT, W_N}(a_{t:t+k} | o_t, g), with W_N fixed throughout.

**Interpretation (App. A).**
- Linear case: min_W ||K_h W^T - V_h||_F^2 gives W* = V_h^T K_h (K_h^T K_h)^{-1}.
- Under the isotropy assumption K_h^T K_h ≈ (L_h/d) I, this becomes W* ∝ sum_i v_i k_i^T.
- Then f_{W*}(Q_r) ∝ sum_i (k_i^T Q_r) v_i, which is linear cross-attention from robot queries to human keys and values.
key_results: Main result, New household setting (Table 1; 9 tasks, 25 trials per cell, average progress %): WAM-TTT 46.2, LDA 32.5, WAM-CoTrain 25.3, EgoScale (re-implementation) 15.0, pi0.5 14.8, WAM-ICL 7.1.

Orig. cubicle setting (Table C.1): WAM-TTT 61.1, LDA 50.2, WAM-ICL 48.4, pi0.5 31.8, EgoScale 30.1, WAM-CoTrain 29.8. New/Orig retention ratios: WAM-TTT 0.76, CoTrain 0.85 (the paper calls this 'largely artifactual'), LDA 0.65, EgoScale 0.50, pi0.5 0.47, ICL 0.15.

Ablation (Table 2; 10 trials; Table Bussing / Swap Place, New): WAM-TTT 100.0/88.9; WAM-LoRA 30.0/0.0; without meta-training 9.0/0.0; without memory reconstruction 66.7/72.0; without TTT 40.0/74.1. Without meta-training, test-time adaptation drives Swap Place from 74.1 (no TTT) to 0.0, so un-meta-trained writes can be destructive.
Failure case: Stamp Paper, where WAM-TTT scores 8.3 against LDA's 33.3 (New) and 35.0 against 50.0 (Orig.). Adaptation hurt this task, and the method has no gate that would detect it.
Generalization after adaptation (Table 3; Deliver Drink only; trial count not stated): lighting 66 vs LDA 54, ICL 12, pi0.5 28; spatial 56 vs 28, 20, 0.

Data-ratio sweep (Table E.1; 3-task average, New): (robot 100, human 0) 59.5; (10,190) 51.4; (100,100) 74.1; (200,0) 73.7; (100,200) 73.3. Paired human data substitutes roughly 1-for-1 for robot data at a fixed total budget but cannot replace robot grounding.

Backbone ablation (Table E.2; Table Bussing; 10 trials): DiT only 72; VLM without pretraining 80; VLM frozen during meta-training 54; VLM trained ('open') 100. Freezing the conditioning backbone during meta-training cost 46 points.

Pseudo-action ablation (Table E.3; 4 tasks, 25 trials): action-free video-generation-only writes 72.3; adding a MANO-retargeted pseudo-action forward-dynamics loss 28.9 (-43.4). Noisy action targets in the write/meta objective were strongly harmful.

Hyperparameters (Table B.1): N=1 inner step at both meta-training and test time; inner learning rate 0.1 at meta-training vs 0.01 at test time; lambda = 4e-2; 100k meta-training steps; global batch 128; 8x H800.

Internal inconsistency: Sec. 4.2 says WAM-TTT 'wins 7 outright and ties on Flip Steak (10.0); the single exception is Stamp Paper'. Table 1 instead shows LDA 56.0 > WAM-TTT 55.6 on Transfer Bottle, CoTrain 12.0 > 10.4 on Pyramid Stacking, and WAM-TTT at 34.3 (not 10.0) on Flip Steak. Swap Place (New) is 88.9 in Table 2 but 66.7 in Table 1.

Not reported: seeds, confidence intervals, adaptation latency or rollout latency, total fast-parameter count, and any held-out-task evaluation. All 9 evaluation tasks appear in the meta-training data.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: WAM-TTT [5] — Relevant mechanism: 'Residual TTT in a video expert'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Sec. 3.1: 'We keep the pretrained WAM architecture unchanged except for adding TTT residual branches to the video expert.' Eq. 1: z^(l+1) = zhat^(l+1) + Dz_TTT^(l), x^(l+1) = xhat^(l+1). Eq. 2: Dz_TTT = theta_O f_W(theta_Q(z^(l))). App. A: 'The TTT residual modifies only the video stream, leaving the action expert's output untouched'.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Accurate but underspecified. The branch is in every one of the L=16 MMDiT blocks ('Propagating u_h through the L TTT-augmented blocks'). It acts on hidden video-stream features, not on the action velocity, and influences actions only through joint attention. The residual is NOT centered: W_init produces a nonzero branch output that is used even without any human video (App. E.2). It is also 'internal TTT' in the proposal's Sec. 8 taxonomy.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: 'adaptation from human-video prediction and KV objectives'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Eq. 7: L_TTT(W_i) = 1/|B_h| sum_u [ L_vg(u; Theta_WAM, theta_TTT, W_i) + lambda sum_l L_KVM^(l)(u; W_i) ]; 'Both L_vg and L_KVM^(l) are computed from the human side alone (Eq. 3), so no robot-side supervision is needed.' Eq. 3: L_KVM = 1/(B L_h d) ||f_W(K_h) - V_h||^2.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Details worth adding. Test-time adaptation is a single inner SGD step (N=1) with eta = 0.01 on a small batch of in-scene human videos. The video loss backpropagates through the whole WAM. The same combined objective is the inner loop in meta-training, where the outer loss is the robot FM multitask loss and the backbone Theta_WAM is also trained. App. E.6 inconsistently says 'only the video-generation loss L_vg^human drives the inner SGD' at test time, contradicting Eq. 7.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: 'adapted weights fixed during robot rollout'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Sec. 3.3: 'After N test-time updates (the same step budget as in Eq. 5; see Table B.1), the adapted fast weights W_N are fixed during robot rollout: a_{t:t+k} ~ p_{Theta_WAM, theta_TTT, W_N}(a_{t:t+k} | o_t, g)' (Eq. 9). Also: 'No WAM parameter, TTT slow projection, initialization parameter, or action-expert parameter is updated.'
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Correct. Note that Sec. 4 and Sec. 5 say the fast weights 'adapt online via inner SGD on a small set of unseen-task human demonstrations'. That 'online' refers to deployment-time adaptation before rollout, not to writes during rollout.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Research distinction: 'Continual causal writes from the chosen robot experience protocol.'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: WAM-TTT writes once (N=1) from a pre-collected human-video batch B_h before rollout and then holds W_N fixed (Eq. 9). No robot observation, action, correction or outcome is ever written into the fast weights, neither at meta-training (both inner-loop terms 'depend only on the action-free human side') nor at deployment. Fast weights are reset to W_init per training example.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: True as a difference from WAM-TTT. It is a weak stand-alone novelty claim, however. Persistent fast weights across decisions are attributed to RoboTTT [6] in the proposal's own table, and continual self-supervised robot adaptation during deployment exists in works WAM-TTT cites (Hansen et al., ICLR 2021; Evolve-VLA; test-time RL for VLAs). The distinctions that actually separate the proposal from WAM-TTT are: (i) a centered residual with exact reset recovery, which WAM-TTT lacks; (ii) a velocity-level external reader; (iii) a consolidation/retention/reset lifecycle. None of these appears in WAM-TTT, and the table should state them.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec. 8 reader table: Internal TTT layer — 'Fast memory changes transformer features; strong established comparison [3, 5, 6].'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: WAM-TTT's branch changes hidden video features inside each DiT block (Eqs. 1-2), so it is an internal TTT reader. It is a July 2026 preprint with no released code found, no seeds or error bars, 10-trial ablations on two tasks, and text/table inconsistencies in Sec. 4.2.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The 'internal TTT' characterisation is right. 'Established' overstates the evidence. The proposal should treat WAM-TTT as a recent, single-group demonstration, not as a validated baseline.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec. 6: 'An internal TTT layer changes hidden features that determine the velocity. It therefore also changes the denoising path. ... The difference is the intervention location and lifecycle, not whether denoising is affected at all.'
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: WAM-TTT's residual is inside every MMDiT block of LDA, whose action head is trained with a flow-matching velocity objective (LDA-1B Sec. III: 'the model predicts a denoising vector field v^a_theta ... trained using a flow-matching objective'). The fast weights therefore enter every denoiser evaluation, and the query theta_Q(z^(l)) depends on the current noisy tokens through joint attention.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: WAM-TTT does not state whether future video tokens are jointly denoised during robot rollout or replaced by LDA's visual register token in policy mode, so exactly how the memory couples to the evolving action candidate is unspecified.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Role assigned in the brief: WAM-TTT as the 'closest robot TTT prior'.
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: WAM-TTT is a real-robot fast-weight TTT memory inside a flow-matching WAM. It has a meta-learned W_init and slow Q/K/V/O interfaces trained through the inner update, a KV-reconstruction writer, and a frozen backbone at deployment. This closely matches the proposal's strict fast-only TTT protocol.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Closest in writer and meta-training structure. For persistent, continually written fast weights across robot decisions, RoboTTT [6] is closer. WAM-TTT has no continual writes, no consolidation and no reset gate.

reading.relevance_to_proposal:
- **Sec. 1, Eq. (1)** pi(a_k | c_k, W_k), W_k = Write(H_k). WAM-TTT instantiates this form with p(a | o_t, g; W_N), W_N = Write(B_h), where history is a pre-rollout human-video batch, not a causal robot prefix. Its WAM-ICL vs WAM-TTT comparison is the "weights vs context tokens" test the proposal plans as the History tokens / retrieval baseline (Sec. 17): 7.1 vs 46.2 in New, 48.4 vs 61.1 in Orig.
- **Sec. 3 ("What changes when").**
  - WAM-TTT holds W fixed within a solve and across the whole rollout, and writes only once.
  - In meta-training it updates W_init, the slow interfaces AND the backbone Theta_WAM. The proposal freezes theta initially.
- **Sec. 4, Eqs. (3)-(5).**
  - Proposal: an external velocity residual r = R(.., f_{W_k}(q)) - R(.., f_{W_0}(q)), exactly zero at W_0.
  - WAM-TTT: an uncentered hidden-feature residual theta_O f_W(theta_Q z) in the video stream of all 16 blocks.
  - WAM-TTT therefore offers no exact reset-to-base guarantee. Its W_init branch changes behaviour even with no data (App. E.2), and its "reusable/frozen WAM" claims hold only relative to the meta-trained backbone plus the W_init branch, not relative to the original LDA.
  - This is a clean point of contrast the proposal can claim.
- **Sec. 5, Eqs. (6)-(8).**
  - WAM-TTT's L_KVM = ||f_W(K_h) - V_h||^2 plays the same role as the proposal's l_assoc = 1/2 ||f_W(q_e) - sg(y_e)||^2, with one gradient step as in Eq. (8).
  - Differences: WAM-TTT adds a global self-supervised loss propagated through the whole backbone, and learns theta_K and theta_V jointly (outer loop only, no stop-gradient). The proposal uses a fixed pretrained target encoder.
  - WAM-TTT's fast MLP is multi-head and per layer (head dim 48, hidden 128). My inference from Table B.1: about 1.2e4 parameters per head per layer, far larger than the proposal's 1,072-parameter memory.
- **Sec. 6, Eqs. (9)-(10).** WAM-TTT shows that an internal TTT reader in an FM robot policy already affects every denoising step, which supports the proposal's admission that the difference is intervention location and lifecycle.
- **Sec. 7, Eqs. (11)-(12).**
  - WAM-TTT's outer loop has the same structure as Eq. (12): an FM loss on target actions (and video) evaluated with the adapted weights W_N, second-order backprop through the inner update, reset to W_init per example.
  - This pre-empts the meta-training recipe but not the causal multi-write episode design: WAM-TTT has a single write, and its human write source is phase-synchronised with the robot target episode.
- **Sec. 8.** WAM-TTT is an instance of the "Internal TTT layer" reader row.
- **Secs 11-14 (consolidation, retention, refresh).**
  - WAM-TTT has none of these. Its only slow learning is offline meta-training, and each deployment task restarts from W_init.
  - Its WAM-CoTrain baseline (a direct slow update with new human data) degrades in-distribution performance (Orig. 29.8 vs LDA 50.2). This is empirical support for the proposal's concern that naive slow updates damage old behaviour and need replay and gates.
  - The Stamp Paper regression (33.3 to 8.3) shows adaptation can harm specific tasks; the proposal's accept/reject gate is designed to catch this.
- **Sec. 14 (two protocols).** WAM-TTT's deployment is exactly the proposal's "strict fast-only TTT" protocol, so it is the natural strict-protocol comparator for Stage E.
- **Sec. 17 (baselines).** WAM-TTT's LoRA, CoTrain, ICL, no-meta-training and no-KV-reconstruction baselines map onto missing or needed controls in the proposal.
- **Sec. 21 (table).** The three clauses are verified as accurate. The "Relevant mechanism" column omits the most overlapping parts: meta-learned W_init and interfaces through the inner update on a robot FM loss; joint backbone training in meta-training; a frozen backbone at deployment.
novelty_threats: WAM-TTT already demonstrates, on real robots with three embodiments, a small gradient-written fast-weight MLP inserted as a residual into a flow-matching robot policy and read at every denoiser evaluation. It has a meta-learned initialization W_init and slow Q/K/V/O interfaces trained by backpropagating a downstream FM policy loss through the inner write, a key-value reconstruction write loss, and a frozen backbone at deployment. For the proposal's 'strict fast-only TTT' protocol, this leaves as architectural distinctions only: velocity-level external readout vs hidden-feature readout, centering, the write source, and write timing.

The writer of proposal Eq. (7)-(8) (association loss ||f_W(q) - y||^2 with one gradient write, meta-trained through the write) is essentially WAM-TTT's L_KVM plus Eq. (5). It also follows TTT layers [3] and Spatial-TTT. 'Association-based writing' is not a novelty axis.

'Residual' fast-memory injection into a robot denoising transformer is pre-empted: WAM-TTT's Eq. 1 is a residual branch. Only the centered form (Eq. 4, exactly zero at W_0) and its placement on the action velocity are unclaimed by WAM-TTT.

Proposal requirement 2 ('memory is queried while the action candidate evolves') is partly realised by WAM-TTT. Its queries theta_Q(z^(l)) are computed from hidden tokens at every denoiser call and depend on the noisy action tokens through joint attention. The proposal's distinguishing element is direct query access to z_t and t with an explicit velocity correction, not denoising-time interaction as such.

WAM-TTT claims forgetting-free 'reusable steering' by construction: 'domain shift in the human videos cannot reach into and overwrite the WAM's pretrained capability'. This occupies part of the 'adapt without damaging the slow model' story. The proposal's added value is continual consolidation into the slow model with measured retention, which WAM-TTT does not attempt.

App. A gives a linear-case argument that the KV-reconstruction write equals linear cross-attention. This reinforces [4] and means any 'nonlinear fast memory beyond attention' framing would be contested. The proposal already avoids that claim.

The 'continual causal writes from robot experience' distinction is not threatened by WAM-TTT itself. It is weakened by RoboTTT [6], which has persistent fast weights across decisions, and by continual deployment-time self-supervised adaptation works WAM-TTT cites (Hansen et al. 2021 PAD; Evolve-VLA 2025; on-the-fly VLA test-time RL 2026). Novelty therefore rests on the full lifecycle: continual writes, consolidation with replay, a reset gate, and an episodic store, combined with centered velocity reading.
ideas_to_borrow: Add baselines WAM-TTT uses that the proposal's Sec. 17 table lacks: (a) parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) of the slow policy on the same few experiences with matched compute ('WAM-LoRA'); (b) direct co-training or fine-tuning of the slow policy on the new data without fast memory ('WAM-CoTrain'), as a naive-consolidation comparator; (c) 'without meta-training', i.e. a writer and reader not trained through the write; (d) writer-loss ablations: without the association/KV term, and without any global self-supervised term.

Consider a combined write objective: the local association loss plus a global self-supervised predictive loss propagated through the frozen backbone (WAM-TTT's L_vg). Ablate each term, since WAM-TTT found the KV term adds roughly 17-33 points. Report write latency, because the global term needs a full backward pass through the backbone.

Precedent for learning key and value (target) projections jointly: WAM-TTT trains theta_K and theta_V only through the outer robot FM loss, while the inner loss is minimized only with respect to W. There is therefore no inner-loop collapse pressure on the target projection. This could let the proposal test a learned target encoder earlier than planned.

Include a 'memory at initialization, no writes' control in the evaluation: WAM-TTT's App. E.2 W_init-only deployment. For the proposal this should reproduce the base sampler exactly, which empirically confirms the centering advantage over an uncentered branch.

Test how the writer step size is calibrated between meta-training and deployment. WAM-TTT silently uses inner LR 0.1 in meta-training and 0.01 at test time. For continual writes, meta-train on write-sequence lengths that match deployment and sweep eta_f at deployment.

Adopt WAM-TTT's generalization-preservation test: after adaptation, evaluate under perturbations (lighting, spatial layout) and compare with the unadapted and in-context-conditioned models. Also borrow its Orig/New retention ratio, used alongside the proposal's per-task retention matrix.

Consider action-free or cross-embodiment demonstrations (e.g. human video) as one of the 'chosen robot experience protocols' in Stage E. WAM-TTT's E.6 result (noisy pseudo-action targets reduced performance from 72.3 to 28.9) motivates a noisy-label write control alongside the proposal's wrong- and shuffled-memory controls.
Borrow the iso-budget data-ratio design (fixed total episodes, varied source mix) for the proposal's meta-training data and replay-budget sweeps.

Use the linear-case analysis (App. A, Eqs. A.2-A.4) as an interpretability check on what the association writer stores, e.g. compare f_W(q) with a linear-attention readout over the written (q_e, y_e) pairs.
technical_issues_in_proposal: Sec. 21's WAM-TTT row understates the overlap. Besides the three clauses listed (all verified accurate), WAM-TTT also: meta-learns W_init and the slow Q/K/V/O interfaces by backpropagating a robot FM loss through the inner write (the same structure as proposal Eq. 12 and Sec. 7); uses a KV-reconstruction writer equivalent to Eq. 7; jointly trains the backbone Theta_WAM during meta-training; and freezes everything except the fast weights at deployment (the proposal's strict fast-only protocol). The 'Research distinction' should add what WAM-TTT verifiably lacks: a centered residual with exact reset recovery (WAM-TTT's W_init branch is active with no data, App. E.2), action-velocity-level readout, and consolidation, retention and reset gates. Relying only on 'continual causal writes' is weak, because RoboTTT [6] already has persistent fast weights across decisions.

Assumption that theta can be frozen during meta-training (Secs 3, 7, 15: 'Initially hold the backbone fixed'). WAM-TTT trains Theta_WAM jointly in meta-training, and its App. E.5 ablation found that freezing the VLM conditioning backbone during meta-training cut Table Bussing progress from 100 to 54 (10 trials, one task; weak evidence). The proposal should anticipate that a frozen backbone may cap what a small external reader can do. It should add a jointly-meta-trained variant, and report memory-off performance of both the original and any meta-trained backbone, since centering only guarantees recovery of the current theta.

Missing baseline in Sec. 17: a direct parameter-efficient fine-tune (LoRA) or plain fine-tune of the slow FM policy on the same few experiences, with matched compute and data. This is the natural competitor for immediate adaptation and for naive consolidation. WAM-TTT includes it (WAM-LoRA) along with co-training.

Fast-memory capacity. The proposal's 1,072-parameter memory (Eq. 6) is orders of magnitude smaller than WAM-TTT's per-layer, per-head fast MLPs. Table B.1 gives head dim 48, hidden 128, 16 layers and 32 heads; my inference is about 1.2e4 parameters per head per layer. WAM-TTT states its adaptation is 'bounded by the expressiveness of the fast-weight network'. Stage E will likely need a capacity sweep well beyond 1,072, and the proposal should not carry the Stage B size forward by default.

Continual writes are untested in the closest robot prior. WAM-TTT uses exactly one inner step and a fixed step budget, and even then needed a different test-time inner learning rate (0.01) from meta-training (0.1). The proposal's persistent multi-write deployment (Sec. 15, online loop step 5) goes beyond the meta-trained regime unless meta-training episodes match deployment write counts. Write-count drift and step-size calibration should be explicit experimental variables.

Evidence hygiene. WAM-TTT's results should not be cited as evidence for adaptation to genuinely held-out tasks. Its evaluation tasks are the same 9 tasks covered by meta-training ('2,286 paired robot-human episodes spanning these 9 manipulation tasks'; '(100, 100) paired robot/human episodes per task'), and human meta-training videos were 'recorded ... directly in the actual household environments that we later evaluate as the New setting', despite 'unseen-task' wording. The proposal's task-disjoint splits (Sec. 15-16) are the right safeguard. The same care applies when invoking WAM-TTT's claims about preserving generalization.

The proposal's statement that 'the residual is a policy component: it changes the generated action distribution' (Sec. 4) is correct. It usefully contrasts with WAM-TTT's claim that its residual 'cannot rewrite the policy itself'. WAM-TTT's Stamp Paper drop (33.3 to 8.3) shows a fast-weight residual can degrade a task, which supports the proposal's gating. The proposal could cite this as motivation for a validation gate even in the strict fast-only protocol, which currently has no accept/reject step for fast writes.
stated_limitations: (1) 'Meta-training phase pairing assumes the paired human episode covers the same skill phase distribution as the robot episode; mis-aligned manifests degrade the inner adaptation signal in a way the loss does not flag.'

(2) 'The deployment-time fast-weight adaptation is bounded by the expressiveness of the fast-weight network and by the slow projections fixed at meta-training; the further the deployment task drifts from the meta-training pairing distribution, the weaker the adaptation. We have not characterised the boundary empirically.'
(3) 'Our deployment-time interface accepts only egocentric human RGB frames; it does not exploit hand-pose, contact, or 3-D scene cues that related work has shown useful.'

Not stated by the authors (my observations): no seeds, error bars or confidence intervals; ablations use 10 trials on two tasks; evaluation tasks overlap the meta-training tasks; no latency or compute figures for adaptation; test-time KV synchronization h_phi is undefined without a paired robot trajectory; only a single write (N=1) with fast weights frozen during rollout (no continual adaptation); the video-expert placement is not ablated against action-expert placement; the pi0.5 and EgoScale baselines differ in backbone, confounding the claim that they 'quantify the contribution of test-time adaptation itself'; the text of Sec. 4.2 contradicts Table 1.
cited_works_worth_adding: Hansen et al., 'Self-Supervised Policy Adaptation during Deployment' (PAD), ICLR 2021. Continual self-supervised test-time updates of a robot policy during deployment. A direct precedent for 'continual writes from robot experience' that the proposal's novelty statement should acknowledge.

Liu, F. et al., 'Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training', 2026, arXiv:2603.12255. The TTT-layer formulation and 'analytical, differentiable inner update' WAM-TTT adopts. A concrete template for the proposal's internal-TTT baseline in streaming visual settings.

Behrouz, Zhong, Mirrokni, 'Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time', 2025, arXiv:2501.00663. Persistent test-time memory with forgetting and momentum mechanisms. Relevant to the proposal's continual writes and its decay/proximal-penalty discussion (Sec. 5).

Bai, Gao, Shou, 'Evolve-VLA: Test-Time Training from Environment Feedback for Vision-Language-Action Models', 2025, arXiv:2512.14666. Deployment-time adaptation of a VLA from robot interaction; a competitor for the continual-adaptation claim.

Liu, C. et al., 'On-the-fly VLA Adaptation via Test-Time Reinforcement Learning', 2026, arXiv:2601.06748. Online test-time adaptation from robot rollouts; relevant to the proposal's separate reward-only experiment (Sec. 7).

Lyu et al., 'LDA-1B: Scaling Latent Dynamics Action Model via Universal Embodied Data Ingestion', 2026, arXiv:2602.12215. The flow-matching MMDiT world-action backbone under WAM-TTT; a candidate Stage E backbone and the setting in which an internal-TTT vs external-velocity-reader comparison would be most directly comparable to WAM-TTT.

Shah et al., 'MimicDroid: In-Context Learning for Humanoid Robot Manipulation from Human Play Videos', 2025, arXiv:2509.09769. The in-context alternative to weight-based memory; relevant to the proposal's history-token baseline.
Yang, Ze, Xu, 'MoVie: Visual Model-Based Policy Adaptation for View Generalization', NeurIPS 2023. Test-time policy adaptation in robotics via a model-based objective.

Katharopoulos et al., 'Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention', ICML 2020. The linear-attention equivalence WAM-TTT App. A invokes; pairs with the proposal's [4] and [12] discussion.

Zhu et al., 'Unified World Models: Coupling Video and Action Diffusion for Pretraining on Large Robotic Datasets', 2025, arXiv:2504.02792. The joint video/action diffusion formulation behind LDA; relevant if the proposal considers a video-predictive write signal.

errors_found.reader_claim: Key result: 'Without meta-training, test-time adaptation drives Swap Place from 74.1 (no TTT) to 0.0, so un-meta-trained writes can be destructive.'
errors_found.problem: The 'w/o Meta Training' and 'w/o TTT' rows are different models, so 74.1 is not the pre-write state of the model that scores 0.0. 'w/o TTT' is the meta-trained pipeline without human-video adaptation; 'w/o Meta Training' skips meta-training altogether. The 0.0 also cannot be pinned on the writes: inserting an un-meta-trained, uncentered residual branch could by itself produce the collapse. Separately, 74.1 exactly equals WAM-CoTrain's Orig. Swap Place cell in Table C.1 and cannot arise as a 10-trial average under the Swap Place rubric (see missed points).
errors_found.evidence: Sec. 4.3: 'w/o Meta Training removes the human-robot meta-training stage, so the TTT branch is not explicitly trained to align human Keys/Values with robot Queries' and 'w/o TTT removes human-video adaptation entirely and evaluates the frozen WAM.' Table C.1: 'WAM-Cotrain Orig. 11.6 40.0 59.4 74.1 ...'.
errors_found.corrected: Supported claim: the full pipeline without meta-training (untrained branch plus adaptation) scored 9.0 on Table Bussing and 0.0 on Swap Place, far below LDA's New scores of 70.0 and 44.4. The paper does not separate whether the untrained branch or the writes cause the collapse.

errors_found.reader_claim: Stamp Paper failure: 'Adaptation hurt this task, and the method has no gate that would detect it.' The same point is repeated in relevance_to_proposal and technical issue 7 ('shows a fast-weight residual can degrade a task').
errors_found.problem: WAM-TTT differs from LDA both in test-time adaptation and in meta-training, which retrains Theta_WAM on the paired data. No w/o-TTT result exists for Stamp Paper, so the drop cannot be attributed to adaptation. The drop also appears in the in-distribution Orig. setting (35.0 vs 50.0), which points at least as much to meta-training changes. It also contradicts the paper's own explanation, which blames the household perturbation.
errors_found.evidence: Sec. 3.2: 'The optimized parameters are the WAM parameters, the TTT slow projections θ{K,V,Q,O}, and the initialization Winit.' Table C.1: LDA Orig. Stamp Paper 50.0; WAM-TTT Orig. Stamp Paper 35.0. Sec. 4.2: 'the household-scene perturbation breaks an alignment that the human videos do not visibly correct.'
errors_found.corrected: The WAM-TTT pipeline (meta-training plus adaptation) regresses on Stamp Paper in both settings (New 8.3 vs 33.3; Orig. 35.0 vs 50.0). The cause is not isolated. It still motivates an accept/reject gate, but only as a pipeline-level regression.

errors_found.reader_claim: 'The conclusion says the method "matches or exceeds online-adaptation baselines", but no online-adaptation baseline is evaluated.'
errors_found.problem: Overstated. The Table 2 ablation includes WAM-LoRA, an adaptation baseline that replaces the fast-weight mechanism with parameter-efficient adaptation. The paper does not specify its training data, loss, when it is applied, or its compute. What is true is that none of the deployment-time adaptation methods the paper cites (PAD, MoVie, Evolve-VLA, on-the-fly TTRL) is compared, and the only adaptation baseline appears on 2 tasks.
errors_found.evidence: Sec. 4.3: 'WAM-LoRA replaces the TTT fast-weight mechanism with a generic parameter-efficient adaptation baseline.' Sec. 5: 'matches or exceeds online-adaptation baselines on a real-robot manipulation suite (Section 4).'
errors_found.corrected: The only adaptation baseline is an under-specified WAM-LoRA ablation (2 tasks, 10 trials). No published online-adaptation method is compared.

errors_found.reader_claim: Relevance: 'Its WAM-CoTrain baseline (a direct slow update with new human data) degrades in-distribution performance (Orig. 29.8 vs LDA 50.2). This is empirical support for the proposal's concern that naive slow updates damage old behaviour and need replay and gates.'
errors_found.problem: WAM-CoTrain is trained on the same 9 tasks' paired data it is evaluated on. The Orig. drop is lower performance on the target tasks, not loss of previously learned skills, so it is not a retention or forgetting measurement. WAM-TTT also slow-updates the backbone on the same paired data. The comparison is between two ways of using human data during training, not slow update vs no slow update.
errors_found.evidence: Sec. 4.2: 'WAM-Cotrain: the same WAM further trained with paired human play data via the WAM multitask objectives.' Sec. 5: meta-training 'jointly updates the WAM and the branches' slow projections via the WAM multitask outer loss'.
errors_found.corrected: CoTrain shows that naively mixing human video into the multitask loss can hurt the target tasks. It says nothing about retention of old tasks. WAM-TTT measures no retention of LDA's pretraining capabilities at all.

errors_found.reader_claim: Technical issue 2: WAM-TTT's App. E.5 ablation ('VLM frozen' 54 vs 100) warns that the proposal's plan to hold theta fixed during meta-training may cap a small external reader.
errors_found.problem: E.5 freezes only the VLM conditioning backend. The DiT, which corresponds to the proposal's FM transformer theta, and the TTT slow parameters are still trained in every row. No WAM-TTT experiment freezes the DiT backbone during meta-training. LDA itself keeps the VLM frozen in pretraining, and 'DiT only (no VLM)' at 72 beats 'VLM frozen' at 54. The single-task, 10-trial result has no bearing on freezing theta.
errors_found.evidence: App. E.5: 'every row carries our full meta-training and test-time TTT pipeline, and only the VLM side is varied.' LDA-1B Sec. III-E: 'we keep the parameters of the VLM [55] and the DINO [50] encoder frozen throughout the pre-training process'.
errors_found.corrected: The recommendation to add a jointly meta-trained variant is reasonable. It is motivated by WAM-TTT jointly training Theta_WAM, not by the E.5 VLM-freeze ablation.

errors_found.reader_claim: Proposal claim check 7: 'Role assigned in the brief: WAM-TTT as the "closest robot TTT prior"' (verdict partially_accurate).
errors_found.problem: The phrase 'closest robot TTT prior' appears in neither the proposal nor the brief. The proposal's only statements about [5] are the Sec. 21 row and the citation in the Sec. 8 table. This check evaluates a claim the proposal does not make.
errors_found.evidence: A grep of proposal_fulltext.txt for 'closest' returns only 'Which option is closest to this analogy?' (line 230). The brief's [5] entry reads: 'WAM-TTT: residual TTT in a video expert; adaptation from human-video prediction and KV objectives; adapted weights fixed during robot rollout.'
errors_found.corrected: Drop the check or mark it unverifiable (not a proposal claim). The substantive point, that RoboTTT is closer on persistence across decisions, can stay as commentary.

errors_found.reader_claim: The distinction the proposal can claim is 'a centered residual with exact reset recovery, which WAM-TTT lacks'; 'WAM-TTT therefore offers no exact reset-to-base guarantee.'
errors_found.problem: Resetting fast weights to W_init in WAM-TTT exactly restores the deployed pre-adaptation model, since fast weights are simply reinitialised. What WAM-TTT lacks is centering: its memory-off policy includes the nonzero W_init branch and depends on the slow interface parameters. The proposal's centered residual makes the memory-off policy equal to the backbone alone and unchanged by reader or interface updates. The reader states this correctly elsewhere ('hold only relative to the meta-trained backbone plus the W_init branch').
errors_found.evidence: Sec. 3.2: 'The adapted fast weights are discarded after each training example and reinitialized from Winit.' App. E.2: 'the TTT branch is driven entirely by the meta-trained slow projections and Winit' with no human data.
errors_found.corrected: Phrase the distinction as: a centered residual is exactly zero at W_0, so the memory-off policy equals v_theta and is invariant to reader, interface and W_0 training. Reset-to-initial-state recovery is not the distinction; WAM-TTT has that trivially.

errors_found.reader_claim: Relevance Sec. 1: 'Its WAM-ICL vs WAM-TTT comparison is the "weights vs context tokens" test the proposal plans as the History tokens / retrieval baseline (Sec. 17): 7.1 vs 46.2 in New, 48.4 vs 61.1 in Orig.'
errors_found.problem: WAM-ICL is the frozen model conditioned on human videos at inference, with no indication it was trained to use in-context demonstrations. WAM-TTT's slow interface, by contrast, was meta-trained on paired data. ICL in New (7.1) falls far below LDA with no human data at all (32.5), which suggests an untrained, mismatched comparator. It is not the matched control that proposal Sec. 17 requires ('Same experience access').
errors_found.evidence: Sec. 4.4: 'WAM-ICL conditions the frozen model on the demonstration at inference time'. Sec. 1: conditioning on raw human videos 'requires learning such capabilities during large-scale pretraining'. Table 1: WAM-ICL 7.1 vs LDA 32.5.
errors_found.corrected: Cite it only as weak, unmatched evidence. A fair weights-vs-tokens test must meta-train the context-conditioning baseline on the same paired data.

errors_found.reader_claim: Technical issue 4: WAM-TTT's fast memory is 'orders of magnitude' larger, and 'the proposal should not carry the Stage B size forward by default.'
errors_found.problem: The per-head, per-layer layout and the ~1.2e4 parameter figure are inferences; the paper gives no TTT head count or fast-parameter total. The proposal already says its 1,072-parameter memory is not a capacity claim.
errors_found.evidence: Table B.1 gives only 'TTT head dim d / fast-weight hidden width fh 48 / 128'. Proposal Sec. 5: 'It is a starting configuration, not a demonstrated optimal capacity.'
errors_found.corrected: Recommending a capacity sweep is fine, but the proposal does not assume the Stage B size carries over, and WAM-TTT's total fast-parameter count is unknown.

errors_found.reader_claim: Relevance Sec. 7: WAM-TTT's outer loop uses 'second-order backprop through the inner update'.
errors_found.problem: The paper says only that it backpropagates 'through the analytical, differentiable inner update of Spatial-TTT'. Neither second-order terms nor a first-order truncation are stated.
errors_found.evidence: App. A: 'by backpropagating through the analytical, differentiable inner update of Spatial-TTT [52]'.
errors_found.corrected: Gradients flow through the inner update. Whether second-order terms are kept is unspecified.

claim_check_overrides.claim: Role assigned in the brief: WAM-TTT as the 'closest robot TTT prior'.
claim_check_overrides.reason: The proposal and the brief never make this claim. The proposal describes [5] only in the Sec. 21 row and cites it in the Sec. 8 'Internal TTT layer' row. It is not a checkable proposal claim.

missed_points: Table 2 (captioned 'under the New setting; 10 trials per cell') reproduces Orig.-setting cells from Table C.1 exactly. The WAM-TTT column (Table Bussing 100.0, Swap Place 88.9) equals 'WAM-TTT Orig.' (100.0, 88.9). The 'w/o TTT' column (40.0, 74.1) equals 'WAM-Cotrain Orig.' (40.0, 74.1). So the 88.9-vs-66.7 discrepancy is a likely copy or mislabel, not random run noise. The only direct test of test-time writes (WAM-TTT vs w/o TTT) may in fact be a comparison with a mislabeled CoTrain number, and the ablation table should not be relied on.

Rubric arithmetic: App. D defines discrete additive milestones, for example Swap Place weights 0.2/0.3/0.3/0.2, so per-trial scores are multiples of 0.1 and 25-trial averages must be multiples of 0.4 pts. I checked every Table C.1 cell against its rubric: 28 of 108 cannot be 25-trial averages. These include WAM-TTT's Swap Place 66.7 (New) and 88.9 (Orig.), Deliver Drink 66.7, Stamp Paper 8.3 and Pour Water 63.3. Table 2 values 88.9, 74.1, 9.0 and 66.7, and Table E.2 values 72 and 54, cannot be 10-trial averages under the stated rubric (Table Bussing assuming the default N=1 item). Many values look like fractions over 3, 9 or 27. Either the stated trial counts or the scoring procedure are not as described; this is a serious evidence-hygiene concern for citing any WAM-TTT number.

The headline gain is not isolated as a test-time-adaptation effect. WAM-TTT vs LDA confounds retraining Theta_WAM on 2,286 paired episodes with the TTT writes; the paper itself says the LDA gap 'quantifies the contribution of human play data'. In Table E.1, robot-only (200, 0), which involves no human-video writes, reaches 73.7, versus 74.1 for the full method (100, 100). The whole WAM-TTT gain on those 3 tasks is matched by 100 more robot demos per task. The (100, 0) row (44.1/90.0/44.4) also disagrees with LDA's Table 1 cells (56.0/70.0/55.0), a further cross-table inconsistency.

App. C claims WAM-TTT 'strictly improves over the WAM backbone in the same standardized setting', but Table C.1 shows Stamp Paper Orig. at 35.0 vs LDA's 50.0. The Orig. regression also undermines Sec. 4.2's attribution of the Stamp Paper failure to household perturbation.

Weakness in App. A's analysis, relevant to proposal [4] and Eq. (8). The argument rests on the closed-form least-squares optimum W* and an isotropy assumption, but the deployed write is a single SGD step (N=1, η=0.01) from a nonzero W_init with an added whole-network L_vg term. In the linear case one gradient step on the KV loss already gives a delta-rule/Hebbian update, W_0 + c(V^T K − W_0 K^T K), with no isotropy needed. The proposal's one-step association write is likewise a linear-attention-like delta rule in the linear case. The proposal should say so explicitly and not rely on WAM-TTT's optimum-based argument.

WAM-TTT's KV write is self-associative: K_h and V_h are two slow projections of the same phase-synchronised human token h_phi, following the TTT-layer convention. The proposal's writer is heteroassociative, mapping a masked cue view q_e to separate content y_e from a fixed pretrained target encoder. This is a small but real distinction the Sec. 21 row could state.

At deployment the KV term needs 'synchronized human tokens' h_phi, but phase sync (φ = t/T_r) is defined only against a paired robot episode. Also, App. E.6 and Table E.3 say the test-time loss is L_vg only, contradicting Eq. 7. The actual deployed write objective is therefore ambiguous.

The Outlook explicitly generalises the design: 'any auxiliary modality with a phase-pairable training signal could in principle drive a parallel fast-weight branch under the same loss-only-then-residual regime', framed as 'adaptation seats'. This anticipates using the same meta-trained fast-weight interface with other experience sources, including robot experience, which slightly narrows the proposal's 'chosen robot experience protocol' distinction.

The robustness and generalization evidence is thin. Table 3 covers one task (Deliver Drink) with no trial count. App. E.2 (no-human-data, W_init-only deployment) and App. E.3 (six perturbation axes) are single qualitative rollouts with no numbers. The 'W_init-only' control the reader suggests borrowing has no quantitative WAM-TTT counterpart.
