reading.bibliographic_check:
The bibliographic details are correct.
- Title "Progress & Compress: A scalable framework for continual learning", ICML 2018, PMLR volume 80, pages 4528-4537: all confirmed on the PMLR landing page ("Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80:4528-4537, 2018").
- "Schwarz, J., et al." is fine.
- Minor author-order discrepancy (irrelevant to the "et al." citation): the PDF lists Jonathan Schwarz, Jelena Luketina, Wojciech M. Czarnecki, Agnieszka Grabska-Barwinska, Yee Whye Teh, Razvan Pascanu*, Raia Hadsell* (* equal contribution). The PMLR BibTeX lists Schwarz, Czarnecki, Luketina, ....
- arXiv ID: 1805.06370 (v2, 2 Jul 2018). The proposal gives no arXiv ID and gives no URL in its extracted text. The summary line "Prior art for current-task learning, protected distillation, and renewed capacity" matches the paper.
reading.core_mechanism:
ARCHITECTURE (Sec 2.1)
- Two columns of identical architecture: the knowledge base KB (parameters theta^KB) and the active column AC.
- Layer i of the AC (Eq. 1): h_i = sigma( W_i h_{i-1} + alpha_i (elementwise*) U_i sigma( V_i h^KB_{i-1} + c_i ) + b_i ).
- alpha_i is a trainable per-unit gate initialised from U(0, 0.1). Convolutional nets use 1x1-conv adaptors.
- The adaptors are "multi-layer perceptrons" and are "an idea borrowed from Progressive Nets".

PROGRESS PHASE
- The KB is fixed. The AC and adaptors are optimised on task k with the ordinary task loss (supervised cross-entropy, or actor-critic policy gradient with a value baseline and entropy cost).
- "parameters in the active column (green) are optimised without constraints or regularisation".
- Reset rule: "one could make this phase similar to naive finetuning ... by not resetting the active column or adaptors upon the introduction of a new task. Empirically, we found that this can improve positive transfer when tasks are very similar. For more diverse tasks however, we recommend re-initialising these parameters".

COMPRESS PHASE (Sec 2.2, Eq. 2)
- The AC is kept unchanged. Minimise over theta^KB: E_x[ KL( pi_k(.|x) || pi^KB(.|x) ) ] + 1/2 || theta^KB - theta^KB_{k-1} ||^2_{gamma F*_{k-1}}.
- "E denotes expectation over either the dataset or the states of the environment under the active column".
- Policies are computed at inverse temperature tau (tau = 2.0 on Omniglot).
- "Note that pi_k is fixed throughout the consolidation process to that learnt on task k."
- Distillation is chosen partly because "the scale of the distillation loss does not depend on the (scale of the) reward scheme".

ONLINE EWC (Sec 4)
- Bayesian starting point: p(theta|T_{1:k}) ∝ p(theta|T_{1:k-1}) p(T_k|theta) (Eq. 3-4).
- Standard EWC uses a Laplace approximation per task, p(T_i|theta) ≈ N(theta; theta*_i, F_i^{-1}) (Eq. 5), which gives one penalty per task: 1/2 sum_j ||theta - theta*_j||^2_{F_j} (Eq. 6).
- Following Huszar 2017, Laplace is applied to the whole posterior instead: 1/2 ||theta - theta*_{i-1}||^2_{sum_j F_j} (Eq. 7). This is "re-centred" at the latest MAP, and the paper warns: "Shifting the mean to the latest MAP value will mean that older tasks will be remembered less well".
- Stochastic-EP variant: the loss is -log p(T_i|theta) + 1/2 ||theta - theta*_{i-1}||^2_{gamma F*_{i-1}} (Eq. 8), with the running update F*_i = gamma F*_{i-1} + F_i (Eq. 9) and gamma < 1.
- Each F_i is a diagonal Fisher, normalised per task. The reason: the Fisher "favours policies that are more deterministic ... This results in Fisher matrices of variable norm ... We counteract this issue by normalising the Fisher information matrices F_i for each task".
- In RL, 100 minibatches estimate the diagonal Fisher.
- Memory cost is constant: one anchor plus one Fisher.
- It needs task boundaries but not task IDs: "Identifying task boundaries is significantly easier than identifying task ids"; in RL, "changes in reward statistics can be used".

EVALUATION PROTOCOL
- The AC is used to measure forward transfer (Table 1, Fig. 3).
- The KB, after distillation, is used for overall performance (Table 2, Fig. 4).
- On Atari: "we only show rewards collected during the compress phase as the parameters remain unchanged when the active column is learning a new task."

MAPPING ONTO THE PROPOSAL (Secs 11-15; proposal equation numbers)
- P&C KB (theta^KB) ↔ slow FM transformer theta. The proposal also treats phi and W_0 as slow parameters, and P&C has no analogue of these.
- P&C AC trained on the task loss ↔ fast weights W_k written by W_{k+1} = W_k - eta_f grad l_assoc (Eq. 7-8) from 1-16 causal experiences.
- P&C lateral adaptors (Eq. 1) ↔ query q_t = Q_phi(z_t, t, c_k, h_theta(...)) (Eq. 3), which reuses slow features.
- P&C AC output = the policy itself ↔ proposal output v_theta + r_{phi,W} with centred r (Eq. 4-5).
- P&C compress KL + online EWC (Eq. 2) ↔ L_slow = L_fit + beta E_{c~D_old} R_old(c) (Eq. 21-22 or 23, 25-26).
- P&C theta*_{k-1} anchor ↔ v_old = the latest accepted slow snapshot. Both are "re-centred" anchors.
- P&C AC re-initialisation ↔ gated reset of W to W_0, followed by an episodic rebuild (Sec 14).
key_results:
Omniglot (Table 2, test accuracy averaged over all 50 alphabets, mean ± SD over 5 task permutations, after 1 / 5 passes):
- P&C (lambda=15, gamma=0.99): 70.32 / 82.84, 659K parameters
- online EWC (lambda=17.5, gamma=0.95): 69.99 / 79.15, 446K
- EWC (lambda=12.5): 67.32 / 75.96, 11,100K
- LwF: 62.06 / 66.48, 217K
- Finetuning: 26.20 / 60.74, 217K
- Non-scalable references: single model per task 88.34 (5,680K); Progressive Nets 86.50 (108,000K).

Omniglot retention (Fig. 2a, accuracy on the first alphabet while 49 more are learned, averaged over 5 initial tasks): "we do not observe a significant difference between online EWC and EWC". P&C is "comparable to the application of (online) EWC within a single neural network". LwF is excellent up to about 5 tasks and then degrades. Finetuning collapses. Read from the plot: by 50 tasks, EWC, online EWC and P&C sit at roughly 0.5-0.7 of normalised performance, LwF near 0.3 and finetuning near 0. Forgetting is reduced, not eliminated.

Omniglot forward transfer (Fig. 2b): "we observed no generalisation improvement achieved by Progressive Nets or any other method across all alphabets when compared to training dedicated models per task." Online EWC falls to about 0.85 and LwF to about 0.5 (plot readings). Supplement Fig. 3: P&C learns faster (higher area under the learning curve) after pretraining on 1-4 alphabets, with the benefit "plateauing for more than 4 tasks".

Atari forward transfer (Table 1, % of single-task performance after 1/2/3/4/5 previous tasks):
- P&C (active column, re-init): 127 / 129 / 125 / 129 / 128
- P&C (active column, no re-init): 131 / 127 / 114 / 106 / 101
- Finetuning: 117 / 125 / 117 / 105 / 98
- EWC: 55 / 53 / 53 / 50 / 54
- online EWC: 53 / 53 / 49 / 50 / 57
The paper: "both EWC versions show significant negative transfer, resulting in a decrease of final performance by over 40% on average". Without re-initialisation the benefit vanishes, "suggesting only a small utilisation of connections to the knowledge base".

Mazes (Fig. 3, final held-out maze after 7 previous mazes, 4 final mazes, 4 seeds): "P&C performs on par with Finetuning, which in turn suffers from catastrophic forgetting. While online EWC does show positive transfer, the method underperforms". Plot readings: about 1.4-1.45 vs about 1.2-1.25 normalised reward at 2.5e8 frames.

Atari overall (Fig. 4, knowledge-base curves; 6 games × 5 visits × 50M frames): "a significant improvement for P&C on several games while performing comparable (or slightly worse) on the remaining tasks". Visually, the P&C KB is clearly better on Beamrider, Stargunner and Ms. Pac-man, and comparable or worse on Space Invaders and Hero. It shows marked dips between re-visits, so forgetting is visible.

Multi-visit gamma effect: "allowing more forgetting to happen (i.e. choosing a lower gamma) can lead to an overall higher performance ... particularly well observed in the case of P&C where an initial high amount of forgetting allows the knowledge base to perform overall better."

Appendix A (permuted MNIST, 5 tasks, 30-30-10 MLP): EWC retains Task A better than online EWC. With little training per task (500-1000 steps) EWC beats online EWC on all tasks. With a high learning rate, online EWC "doesn't seem to find a good balance between the loss and penalties" but still beats no penalty.

Where the gain comes from: P&C's Omniglot advantage is explained mainly by plasticity, not retention: "The main observation explaining those results is a higher amount of negative transfer for online EWC, allowing some room for P&C to take advantage of the two phases of learning."

Setup:
- Omniglot: 4-block conv net (64 filters), SGD with learning rate 0.1 (0.05 for distillation), batch 32, 2,500 updates per task; lambda/gamma chosen by grid search on a validation split.
- RL: Mnih-2013 network with actor-critic heads, RMSProp, 4 seeds, 68% bootstrap confidence intervals.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 21 table, 'Relevant mechanism' for Progress & Compress [16]: "Current-task learning, distillation into a protected knowledge base, and reinitialization."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Abstract: "A knowledge base ... which is connected to an active column that is employed to efficiently learn the current task. After learning a new task, the active column is distilled into the knowledge base, taking care to protect any previously acquired skills." Sec 2.1: "For more diverse tasks however, we recommend re-initialising these parameters". Table 1 reports both "P&C (Active col, re-init)" and "P&C (Active col)".
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Correct as a summary, with two nuances. (1) Re-initialisation of the AC and adaptors is a recommended option, not a fixed step. The paper advises against it for very similar tasks, and reports results both with and without it. (2) The table omits the lateral adaptors from KB to AC (Eq. 1), which are P&C's slow-to-fast channel and the closest analogue of the proposal's h_theta-based query (Eq. 3). Adding them would make the comparison more honest.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 21 table, 'Research distinction to test' for [16]: "FM-specific transfer objectives and controlled reader comparisons."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: P&C distills categorical policies or class probabilities with KL at inverse temperature tau (Eq. 2). It has no generative flow policy, no denoising readout, and no reader ablations. Its experiments are Omniglot, Atari and 3D mazes only.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Both listed distinctions are true, but the list is too narrow and one-sided. Substantive differences it omits: few-shot, meta-learned, episode-local fast weights vs a full column trained to convergence on each task; exact reset through the centred residual; function-space replay retention vs weight-space online EWC; the accept/reject gate; the episodic store; and interface drift across backbone checkpoints. It also omits a direction in which the proposal is weaker than P&C: P&C claims "no access to or storing of previous data or tasks", while the proposal's R_old needs stored old contexts D_old. A reviewer could otherwise read the proposal as "P&C plus FM distillation".

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 21 text: "Progress & Compress uses online EWC; our initial replay-based retention choice is not a claim that replay is required by that method."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Sec 1: "We propose a modified version of Elastic Weight Consolidation (Kirkpatrick et al., 2017) to mitigate forgetting in the knowledge base." Sec 4: "We refer to our modified method as online EWC." Sec 5: "when writing P&C, we assume the application of online EWC on the knowledge base." Abstract: the cycle "requires no architecture growth, no access to or storing of previous data or tasks". Sec 6: "future methods to mitigate catastrophic forgetting should be easily integrable within our framework."
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Accurate. Two additions would sharpen it. (a) P&C's online EWC is modified: it uses stochastic-EP re-centring, a gamma-decayed running Fisher, and per-task Fisher normalisation, so it is not vanilla EWC. (b) P&C does not merely not require replay; it presents storing no past data as a design goal. So the proposal's replay store is a relaxation relative to P&C, and any P&C or online-EWC comparison must be labelled with this storage asymmetry. Online EWC stores roughly 2|theta| floats (anchor plus diagonal Fisher); replay stores contexts. P&C's framework explicitly admits other protection methods, which is consistent with the proposal's framing.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 13: "Parameter protection such as EWC is a useful alternative comparison [16], but no finite replay or penalty should be advertised as preventing all catastrophic forgetting."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: P&C protects parameters with online EWC (Eq. 2, 8, 9). Fig. 2a shows only partial retention of the first Omniglot alphabet after 49 more tasks, for EWC, online EWC and P&C alike. Fig. 4 shows P&C knowledge-base dips between Atari re-visits. Sec 4: "Without forgetting, EWC misbehaves when the model runs out of capacity".
proposal_claim_checks.correction: The warning that no penalty prevents all forgetting is supported by P&C's own data. The citation, however, is indirect: EWC itself is Kirkpatrick et al. 2017 (PNAS; arXiv:1612.00796) and online EWC builds on Huszar 2017 (arXiv:1712.03847), and neither is in the proposal's references. More importantly, the proposal calls EWC "a useful alternative comparison" but never lists it in the Sec 17 baseline table. That table has only "No replay, no consolidation, no refresh", so the comparison is never actually required.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: References: "[16] Schwarz, J., et al. Progress & Compress: A scalable framework for continual learning. ICML 2018, PMLR 80:4528-4537. Prior art for current-task learning, protected distillation, and renewed capacity."
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: PMLR landing page: "Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80:4528-4537, 2018." Renewed capacity: AC re-initialisation (Sec 2.1), and "forgetting older tasks is necessary to make space for learning newer ones, since our model capacity is fixed" (Sec 4).
proposal_claim_checks.correction: No correction to the bibliography. "Renewed capacity" has two meanings in P&C: a re-initialised AC gives renewed plasticity, and gamma-decay frees knowledge-base capacity through graceful forgetting. The proposal takes up only the first.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Orchestrator/brief role statement: the active column learns the task, is distilled into the knowledge base protected by online EWC, and is re-initialised, with lateral connections from the KB to the active column.
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: Fig. 1 caption: "In the compress phases (C), the policy learnt most recently by the active column (green) is distilled to the knowledge base (blue) while protecting previous contents with EWC ... In the progress phases (P), new tasks are learnt by the active column while reusing features from the knowledge base via lateral, layerwise connections." The lateral connections are given in Eq. 1.
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Re-initialisation is conditional: it is recommended for diverse tasks and skipped for very similar ones. The lateral connections are non-linear MLP adaptors with a learned gate alpha_i.

proposal_claim_checks.claim: Sec 21 (implicit claim about prior art such as [16]): "The memory lifecycle is not new merely because it uses the words short and long memory. The defensible contribution would be a complete algorithm for continual FM adaptation, a qualified account of behavior/path transfer, and experiments establishing which denoising interface is useful".
proposal_claim_checks.evidence: P&C already implements a plastic-learner, distill, protect, reset cycle with an explicit sleep analogy: "The approach is purposefully reminiscent of daytime and nighttime, and of the role that sleep plays in memory consolidation in humans".
proposal_claim_checks.correction: Consistent with P&C. The lifecycle concept is pre-empted by P&C (2018), so novelty must rest on the FM-specific and few-shot/meta-learned components.

reading.relevance_to_proposal:
STEP-BY-STEP MAPPING OF P&C ONTO THE PROPOSAL'S LIFECYCLE (Secs 11-15)

(1) Progress ↔ online decision loop (Sec 15; Eq. 3-8).
- Shared: in both, the slow model is frozen while a separate plastic component absorbs the new task. P&C: \"the knowledge base (light blue) is fixed, while parameters in the active column (green) are optimised without constraints\". Proposal: theta is fixed during immediate adaptation, and W_k is updated by Eq. 8. P&C's lateral adaptors (Eq. 1) correspond to the proposal's slow-to-fast flow, where the query is Q_phi(z_t, t, c_k, h_theta).
- Scale: P&C's AC is a full, randomly initialised column trained on the task loss to convergence (2,500 SGD updates per alphabet; 50M frames per Atari visit). The proposal writes a 1,072-parameter MLP from 1-16 experiences with a meta-learned writer.
- Output composition: P&C's AC is itself the acting policy. The proposal adds a centred residual to v_theta.
- Readout: the proposal reads memory at every denoising step; P&C has no iterative generation.

(2) End of progress ↔ Sec 11 / Sec 15 step 1, \"freeze and independently evaluate an adapted teacher snapshot\". P&C freezes the teacher (\"pi_k is fixed throughout the consolidation process\") but has no independent teacher-quality check.

(3) Compress ↔ Sec 11-13 (Eq. 21-26). P&C minimises E_x KL(pi_k || pi^KB) plus a weight-space Fisher penalty, with x drawn from the dataset or from AC-visited states. The proposal minimises L_end or L_path plus a function-space velocity penalty beta E_{c~D_old} R_old. Both transfer behaviour rather than weights; P&C already embodies Sec 11's principle that averaging weights is not a transfer rule.

(4) Online EWC anchor update ↔ Sec 13. Both re-centre on the latest accepted parameters: P&C anchors theta*_{k-1}, the proposal anchors v_old, the latest frozen snapshot. P&C/Huszar's warning about re-centring therefore applies to Eq. 25 across cycles.

(5) AC re-initialisation ↔ Sec 14 gated reset. P&C resets unconditionally, when the reset option is used. The proposal resets only after four gates pass, keeps the teacher when transfer fails, and rebuilds non-identifiable facts from an episodic store.

(6) Evaluation ↔ Secs 16-17. P&C evaluates forward transfer with the AC and overall performance with the KB. This parallels the proposal's memory-on teacher vs memory-off student, and its two protocols (Sec 14).

WHAT THE PROPOSAL ADDS BEYOND P&C
- Meta-learned few-shot, causal, episode-local fast writes (Sec 7; Eq. 11-12).
- Exact reset through centring (Eq. 4; App. B.2).
- Denoising-time readout and the sensitivity analysis (Eq. 9-10).
- FM endpoint/path distillation, including selection-bias handling (Sec 11-12; Eq. 21-24; App. A).
- A velocity-replay retention penalty with a W2 bound (Eq. 25-28; App. B.1).
- The accept/reject gate and rollback (Sec 14).
- The episodic store and the impossibility result for hidden facts (App. B.4).
- Meta-training of the writer/reader across accepted backbone checkpoints (Sec 14). P&C sidesteps interface drift entirely because it re-initialises the adaptors and retrains them with abundant task data.
- Explicit resource accounting (Sec 17).

WHAT P&C HAS THAT THE PROPOSAL LACKS
- Zero storage of past data.
- A per-task scale normalisation of the retention penalty (Fisher normalisation).
- An explicit graceful-forgetting parameter gamma.
- A stated task-boundary assumption.
- A defined distillation state distribution (AC-visited states).
- Evidence from long sequences (50 tasks) and multi-visit protocols.

SECTION-BY-SECTION BEARING
- Sec 13 (Eq. 25-28): the natural alternative/baseline.
- Sec 17: the Stage D baseline table should include P&C/online-EWC arms.
- Sec 21: the positioning needs the fuller distinction list.
- Sec 2: the sleep analogy is pre-empted.
- Sec 16 Stage D: P&C's 50-task and 5-pass protocols set a stronger bar than \"at least 10 task arrivals\".
novelty_threats: The lifecycle concept is pre-empted. A plastic learner acquires the task while the slow model is frozen, the behaviour is distilled into the protected slow model, and the plastic learner is reset for renewed plasticity, all under a day/night sleep-consolidation framing. P&C published exactly this in 2018. The proposal's lifecycle (Secs 11-15) and its biological motivation (Sec 2) are therefore not novel at the conceptual level. The proposal partly concedes this in Sec 21; the Sec 21 table's distinction column should say so explicitly.

Behavioural transfer rather than weight transfer (Sec 11: "Consolidation transfers behavior, not the numerical fast-weight tensors") is P&C's mechanism: distillation between architecturally separate networks. It cannot be claimed as a contribution.

The slow-to-fast channel is pre-empted in spirit. P&C's lateral adaptors let the fast learner reuse slow features, and the proposal's query Q_phi(..., h_theta) does the same. Only the denoising-time, candidate-dependent query is new.

P&C's framework is explicitly generic about protection methods ("future methods to mitigate catastrophic forgetting should be easily integrable within our framework"). A reviewer could frame the proposal's consolidation as "P&C with FM distillation, replay instead of online EWC, and a tiny meta-learned active column". The distinctive contributions must therefore be demonstrated against a P&C-style baseline instantiated for FM policies: a full AC or adapter trained on the task, FM distillation into theta, and online EWC. Otherwise the benefit of the few-shot fast memory and the gate is not isolated.

Constant parameter count and no task-specific parameters were already achieved by P&C. The proposal's fixed-size fast memory is not a scalability novelty; its scalability claim must instead cover replay and episodic-store growth, which P&C avoids.

P&C already shows that resetting the plastic learner is needed for sustained forward transfer on diverse tasks (Table 1: 127-129% with re-init vs a decline to 101% without). Any proposal claim that reset renews plasticity is confirmatory, not new.

Outside P&C (titles and IDs verified on arXiv abstract pages; content not read in this session), several works sit close to parts of the lifecycle and should be checked as novelty threats:
- CLS-ER, "Learning Fast, Learning Slow" (arXiv:2201.12604): complementary fast/slow semantic memories plus episodic replay.
- Kaplanis et al., "Policy Consolidation for Continual Reinforcement Learning" (arXiv:1902.00255): multi-timescale policy consolidation.
- TAIL (arXiv:2310.05905): task-specific adapters for continual imitation learning with large pretrained policies.
- LIBERO (arXiv:2306.03310): a lifelong robot-learning benchmark.
ideas_to_borrow: Add a zero-storage functional retention arm in the style of LwF (Li & Hoiem 2017, cited by P&C). Evaluate R_old (Eq. 25) at current-task contexts c ~ D_new instead of stored old contexts. It isolates how much of the retention benefit comes from storing old contexts.

Normalise the retention penalty per task, analogous to P&C's per-task Fisher normalisation. P&C found that raw Fishers "favour policies that are more deterministic" and normalised them to "protect each task equally". The same effect appears in R_old: for Gaussian FM targets (proposal Eq. 29-30), the velocity sensitivity to a mean shift is kappa_t, and the integral of kappa_t^2 over [0,1] equals pi/(4 sigma). Checked numerically: 7.85 at sigma = 0.1 and 78.5 at sigma = 0.01. So R_old for the same W2 change is inflated by 1/sigma for near-deterministic tasks. Normalise per old task (for example by R_old at a reference perturbation, or by E||v_old||^2) and report per-task results.

Add an explicit graceful-forgetting control like gamma in online EWC: per-task decay of replay weight or anchor weight, swept on validation. P&C found gamma < 1 helpful and that allowing initial forgetting improved overall KB performance under revisits. The proposal currently has no such knob; Sec 14 only says "prioritize, compress, expand ... or accept loss".

Run a reset vs carry-over ablation of the fast state across tasks, split by task similarity. This mirrors P&C Table 1 (re-init vs no re-init): carry-over helped similar tasks, and re-init was needed for diverse ones.

State the distillation state distribution explicitly. P&C uses "the states of the environment under the active column" (teacher-visited states). For closed-loop robot consolidation, compare teacher-visited and student-visited contexts; see Czarnecki et al., "Distilling Policy Distillation" (arXiv:1902.02186), which is not cited by P&C and was only verified to exist.

Make the task-boundary assumption and trigger explicit, as P&C does ("we made the assumption that the learner is aware of when changes in the task distribution occur"). If boundaries are not given, borrow P&C's suggestion to detect them from shifts in reward or outcome statistics.
Measure backward transfer (P&C desideratum iv) from the proposal's per-task retention matrix, alongside forgetting.

Measure slow-policy plasticity (intransigence) across cycles. Report teacher-gain recovery (the proposal's 90% target) as a function of cycle index, since P&C shows that accumulated EWC constraints cause more than 40% negative transfer on Atari.
technical_issues_in_proposal: Missing baseline / internal inconsistency. Sec 13 calls parameter protection such as EWC [16] "a useful alternative comparison", but the Sec 17 comparisons table lists only "No replay, no consolidation, no refresh". There is no EWC, online-EWC, P&C or LwF arm. Stage D (at least 10 task arrivals) is exactly P&C's setting, so without these arms the proposal cannot show that its replay-based consolidation beats the standard no-storage alternative at a stated storage budget.

Storage asymmetry is not flagged in the retention comparison. P&C's defining claim is "no access to or storing of previous data or tasks". The proposal's R_old (Eq. 25-26) needs c ~ D_old, i.e. stored old contexts, or old teacher endpoints. Sec 14 counts replay bytes in general, but the Sec 17 fairness rules should state that retention arms differ in stored data (replay contexts vs about 2|theta| floats for online EWC vs nothing for LwF-style), and label the asymmetry as Sec 14 already requires for slow updates.

Re-centred anchor. R_old compares the new field only against v_old, the latest accepted snapshot. This is the function-space analogue of online EWC's re-centring. P&C (Sec 4) warns: "Shifting the mean to the latest MAP value will mean that older tasks will be remembered less well". Its Appendix A shows full EWC retaining the first task better than online EWC when training per task is short. The proposal acknowledges that W2 errors accumulate by the triangle inequality (App. B.1) but offers no mitigation. Consider per-task anchors (old teacher endpoints per task) or periodic re-anchoring, and compare the two as an EWC vs online-EWC trade-off.

Retention-scale heterogeneity (P&C's Fisher-normalisation issue, carried over to R_old). Using the proposal's own Gaussian family (Eq. 29-30), dv/dmu = kappa_t and the integral of kappa_t^2 over [0,1] = pi/(4 sigma). So a mean shift delta gives R_old = |delta|^2 pi/(4 sigma), while W2^2 = |delta|^2. Averaging R_old over c ~ D_old therefore over-weights near-deterministic tasks and under-protects broad, multimodal ones. A single beta and a single tolerance do not "protect each task equally", which is P&C's stated goal and the reason it normalised Fishers.

Looseness of Eq. 27-28 (my own analysis, prompted by the previous point, not a claim made in P&C). For narrow Gaussian targets the global spatial Lipschitz constant of the FM field is about 1/(2 sigma): sup|b_t| = 5.05 at sigma = 0.1 and 50 at sigma = 0.01 (computed numerically). This gives C_L ≈ 2.4e3 and ≈ 2.7e41, so the bound is vacuous for near-deterministic action chunks. Because b_t < 0 there (the flow contracts), a one-sided Lipschitz (contractivity) Gronwall bound would be far tighter: max b_t = 1 gives an e^{2l+1}-type constant of about 20. The proposal says a large L makes the bound loose, but it should use the one-sided form.

The task-boundary assumption is implicit. The proposal resets "at a valid boundary" (reading map; Sec 15 consolidation step 5) and runs "periodic" consolidation, but never defines what a boundary is or who provides it. P&C states its equivalent assumption explicitly as a limitation. The proposal should either assume given boundaries in Stages C-D and say so, or specify a detection rule.

The unit of the teacher is unspecified. In P&C one active column is trained on all of one task's data, giving one teacher per task. In the proposal the fast state is episode-local (Sec 15 offline step 3: "Initialize W from W_0 for each independent episode"), so a task can produce many different adapted fast states. The proposal does not say whether consolidation distils a single accepted episode's teacher, a mixture of per-episode teachers (multi-teacher distillation in the style of Distral or PLAiD, both cited by P&C), or a pooled task-level fast state. Distilling a mixture of histories is exactly what Sec 11 warns against for hidden facts.

The distillation context distribution is unspecified. Sec 11/15 say "Generate teacher actions at suitable contexts" / "at supported contexts". P&C specifies "the dataset or the states of the environment under the active column". For closed-loop robots, covariate shift between teacher-visited and student-visited states matters, and producing those contexts requires environment rollouts. P&C counts environment frames during compress. The proposal's cost list (Sec 17) omits the environment interaction used to generate consolidation contexts.

Teacher-strength mismatch. P&C's teacher is an AC trained to convergence with the full task signal (RL reward or labels). The proposal's teacher is limited to few-shot adaptation from 1-16 experiences through a fixed meta-learned writer, so the proposal can only consolidate what that adaptation achieves. The proposal should not treat P&C's forward-transfer and consolidation numbers as indicative of what its own lifecycle will achieve. A P&C-style arm (a full adapter trained on the task and then distilled) is needed to separate "fast memory is a good teacher" from "consolidation works".

Citation gap. The only EWC citation is [16]. The canonical sources are Kirkpatrick et al. 2017 (PNAS; arXiv:1612.00796) for EWC and Huszar 2017 (arXiv:1712.03847) for the online/re-centred form, and both should be added.
stated_limitations: Known task boundaries are assumed: "Throughout this work, we made the assumption that the learner is aware of when changes in the task distribution occur, allowing for the computation of a new posterior approximation." The paper presents this as a relaxation of needing task identities, and suggests boundaries could be detected from changes in reward statistics.

Re-centring in online EWC weakens memory of older tasks: "Shifting the mean to the latest MAP value will mean that older tasks will be remembered less well". The running sum of Fishers "is another approximation, as Fisher information is a local measure and all F_i's should more correctly be recomputed for the new theta*". Appendix A shows EWC beating online EWC on retention in short-training regimes.

Capacity is fixed: "forgetting older tasks is necessary to make space for learning newer ones, since our model capacity is fixed. Without forgetting, EWC misbehaves when the model runs out of capacity".
The raw Fisher "favours policies that are more deterministic", so the per-task Fishers must be normalised.
Without re-initialising the active column, positive transfer vanishes on diverse tasks, "suggesting only a small utilisation of connections to the knowledge base".
P&C is "best used in domains that allow for some positive transfer". On Omniglot no method gained generalisation over single-task models, and "online EWC on its own is a competitive method."
On Atari the P&C knowledge base is only "comparable (or slightly worse)" on some games, and its curves show dips between re-visits.
The regularisation strength lambda is not comparable between P&C and the EWC variants "as the scale of the loss (policy gradients or policy distillation) is different."
The Omniglot results are not comparable to few-shot learning setups; the paper notes it does "not learn Omniglot in a few-shot learning setup".
cited_works_worth_adding: Kirkpatrick et al., "Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks", PNAS 2017 (arXiv:1612.00796). The original EWC. The proposal names EWC in Sec 13 but cites only [16].

Huszar, "On quadratic penalties in elastic weight consolidation", arXiv:1712.03847, 2017. The basis for the re-centred (online) EWC. It is relevant to the proposal's R_old, which likewise anchors only to the latest snapshot.
Rusu et al., "Progressive neural networks", arXiv:1606.04671, 2016. The origin of P&C's lateral adaptors, and prior art for slow-to-fast feature reuse without forgetting.
Rusu et al., "Sim-to-real robot learning from pixels with progressive nets", arXiv:1610.04286, 2016. A robotics instance of column-based transfer, directly relevant to Stage E.

Rusu et al., "Policy distillation", arXiv:1511.06295, 2015, and Hinton et al., "Distilling the knowledge in a neural network", 2015. The teacher-to-student policy distillation (with temperature) that P&C uses; the precedent for the proposal's Sec 11 behavioural transfer.
Li & Hoiem, "Learning without forgetting", TPAMI 2017. Zero-storage functional distillation on current data; the natural no-replay variant of R_old.
Rebuffi et al., "iCaRL", arXiv:1611.07725, 2016. An exemplar replay store plus distillation, the closest precedent to the proposal's "distillation + declared replay store" retention.

Robins, "Catastrophic forgetting, rehearsal and pseudorehearsal", Connection Science 1995. Pseudo-rehearsal uses the old network's own outputs as targets, conceptually the same as R_old's use of old-policy trajectories from fresh noise.

Shin et al., "Continual learning with deep generative replay", arXiv:1705.08690, 2017. Relevant to the proposal's future "learned decoder" / generative replay (Sec 14). P&C notes it "shifts the catastrophic forgetting problem to the training of the generative model."
Lopez-Paz & Ranzato, "Gradient episodic memory for continual learning", NeurIPS 2017. An episodic-memory constraint baseline for the retention arm.

Berseth et al., "PLAiD: Progressive reinforcement learning with distillation for multi-skilled motion control", ICLR 2018. A two-stage learn-then-distill scheme for motion skills; a model for multi-teacher consolidation.
Teh et al., "Distral: Robust multitask reinforcement learning", NeurIPS 2017. A distilled shared policy; relevant if several per-episode or per-task teachers must be consolidated.

Chaudhry et al., "Riemannian walk for incremental learning: Understanding forgetting and intransigence", arXiv:1801.10112, 2018. Forgetting and intransigence metrics that match the proposal's retention and renewed-learning outcomes.
Zenke et al., "Continual learning through synaptic intelligence", ICML 2017. An online importance-weighted parameter-protection baseline.
Nguyen et al., "Variational continual learning", arXiv:1710.10628, 2017. Bayesian continual learning with coresets; a principled combination of replay and regularisation.

errors_found.reader_claim: Summary: "P&C matches online EWC on retention". Key result: P&C is "comparable to the application of (online) EWC within a single neural network", and all three methods "sit at roughly 0.5-0.7".
errors_found.problem: Overstated. The paper's word is "comparable", but its own Fig. 2a shows the P&C curve below both EWC variants for almost the whole 50-task sequence. The reading repeats the paper's framing without noting the gap.
errors_found.evidence: I rendered page 6 at 250 dpi and traced the curve colours. Approximate normalised retention of the first alphabet, averaged over tasks 2-50: P&C ~0.58, online EWC ~0.67, EWC ~0.72 (LwF ~0.56, Finetuning ~0.11). Averaged over tasks 48-50: P&C ~0.56, online EWC ~0.64, EWC ~0.71. The gap is similar in every 10-task bin (e.g. tasks 10-20: 0.59 vs 0.70 vs 0.72). Paper text: "The results for online EWC as applied within the P&C framework are encouraging, yielding results comparable to the application of (online) EWC within a single neural network."
errors_found.corrected: On retention of the first task, P&C is about 0.1 (normalised) worse than online EWC and about 0.13 worse than EWC applied in a single network. Its better overall Omniglot score comes from online EWC's negative transfer, not from better retention ("The main observation explaining those results is a higher amount of negative transfer for online EWC").

errors_found.reader_claim: Relevance/ideas: "P&C's 50-task and 5-pass protocols set a stronger bar than 'at least 10 task arrivals'"; "What P&C has that the proposal lacks ... Evidence from long sequences (50 tasks)".
errors_found.problem: Only the supervised Omniglot experiment has 50 tasks. The RL experiments, which are the analogue closest to robot policies, used 6 distinct Atari games (revisited 5 times) and 8 mazes. Both are fewer distinct tasks than the proposal's minimum of 10 arrivals.
errors_found.evidence: "we also consider the sequential learning of 6 games in the Atari suite"; "We also evaluate our method on 8 navigation tasks in 3D environments"; Fig. 4 caption: "Each game is visited 5 times".
errors_found.corrected: P&C sets a longer-sequence bar only for supervised classification (50 tasks). For policy learning its sequences (6-8 distinct tasks) are shorter than the proposal's Stage D. What it adds there is the revisit (multi-pass) protocol, not length.

errors_found.reader_claim: Bibliographic check: "The proposal gives no arXiv ID and gives no URL in its extracted text."
errors_found.problem: Misleading. The proposal PDF embeds a hyperlink on the word "Paper." in reference [16], and it points to the correct PMLR page.
errors_found.evidence: Running `strings` on continual_memory_flow_proposal.pdf yields the URI https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/schwarz18a.html. The reference text ends with "... renewed capacity. Paper."
errors_found.corrected: The proposal links the correct PMLR landing page through an embedded hyperlink. Only the arXiv ID is absent.

errors_found.reader_claim: Technical issue (re-centred anchor): "The proposal acknowledges that W2 errors accumulate by the triangle inequality (App. B.1) but offers no mitigation. Consider per-task anchors (old teacher endpoints per task)".
errors_found.problem: Partly wrong. The proposal already names the per-task-anchor option. What it does not do is present that option as a fix for drift across cycles or require it to be compared with the re-centred penalty.
errors_found.evidence: Proposal Sec 13: "Replay can instead use old teacher endpoints with fresh FM noise; the trajectory penalty above is useful because it admits a qualified stability bound." App. B.1: "Across cycles, Wasserstein distances obey the triangle inequality; small one-cycle deviations can accumulate."
errors_found.corrected: The proposal mentions old-teacher-endpoint replay (the EWC-like, non-re-centred anchor) but treats it only as an alternative. It should be made a required comparison against the re-centred R_old across cycles, which is the analogue of P&C's EWC vs online-EWC trade-off (Supp. A).

errors_found.reader_claim: Distinction listed repeatedly: "function-space (velocity) replay retention with a W2 bound, instead of weight-space Fisher protection".
errors_found.problem: This overstates a categorical difference. P&C itself describes the EWC penalty as protecting the policy's behaviour in expectation over states, because the Fisher is the curvature of the expected KL. By my own derivation (not in P&C), R_old expanded to second order around theta_old is a Gauss-Newton quadratic form, so online EWC is roughly a diagonal, data-free quadratic approximation to a function-space penalty of the same kind.
errors_found.evidence: P&C Sec 4: "each EWC penalty protects the policy in expectation over the state space, regardless of the reward scheme of the task ... the Fisher matrix measures the curvature of the KL term." Derivation: with R_old(theta) = E∫||v_theta(X_t) - v_old(X_t)||^2 dt on fixed old trajectories, R_old(theta_old + Δ) ≈ Δ^T (E∫ J_t^T J_t dt) Δ, where J_t = ∂v_theta/∂theta.
errors_found.corrected: The real differences are: (i) an exact, full penalty vs a diagonal quadratic one; (ii) stored old contexts (D_old) vs no stored data; (iii) curvature evaluated at the current anchor vs a stale running Fisher sum ("Fisher information is a local measure and all F_i's should more correctly be recomputed"). Both methods re-centre on the latest solution.

errors_found.reader_claim: Technical issue: "The unit of the teacher is unspecified ... The proposal does not say whether consolidation distils a single accepted episode's teacher, a mixture of per-episode teachers ..., or a pooled task-level fast state."
errors_found.problem: Overstated. The proposal specifies a single frozen snapshot that contains one adapted fast state, keeps that state across decisions until a boundary, and explicitly warns against mixtures. What remains unclear is which history produced the snapshot's state, and whether deployment-time writes stay inside the 1-16-experience regime the writer was meta-trained for.
errors_found.evidence: Sec 11: "First freeze an adapted teacher snapshot: the backbone, encoders, writer/reader, initial fast weights, and adapted fast state." Sec 15 online loop: "Continue from the updated fast weights. Do not reset between action chunks when the task depends on earlier context." Sec 11: "Otherwise the student learns a mixture of incompatible histories."
errors_found.corrected: The teacher is one snapshot with one fast state. The real gap is that the proposal never says how many deployment writes that state has absorbed relative to the meta-trained 1-16 experiences, or what selects it.

errors_found.reader_claim: Technical issue: "P&C counts environment frames during compress."
errors_found.problem: The paper does not state this. It never says how the 50M frames per visit are split between progress and compress. It says only that rewards collected during compress are shown, and that distillation uses states "under the active column". This implies environment interaction during compress but does not document how those frames are counted.
errors_found.evidence: "In the case of P&C, we only show rewards collected during the compress phase as the parameters remain unchanged when the active column is learning a new task." Eq. 2 text: "E denotes expectation over either the dataset or the states of the environment under the active column".
errors_found.corrected: P&C's compress phase implies environment rollouts under the active column, but the paper does not document how those frames are accounted for. The point that the proposal's cost list should count consolidation-context generation still stands.

errors_found.reader_claim: Claim check 3 correction: "P&C's online EWC is modified: it uses stochastic-EP re-centring, a gamma-decayed running Fisher, and per-task Fisher normalisation".
errors_found.problem: Minor mislabel. The re-centring comes from Huszár's Laplace approximation of the whole posterior (Eq. 7). Stochastic EP is what motivates the gamma down-weighting on revisits (Eq. 8-9).
errors_found.evidence: "as pointed out by (Huszár, 2017), we can apply Laplace's approximation to the whole posterior ... re-centred at the latest MAP"; "We will instead take a stochastic EP (Li et al., 2015) approach"; Sec 6: "very similar to the proposal of Huszár (2017). We add an explicit forgetting mechanism".
errors_found.corrected: The components are: Huszár-style re-centring, stochastic-EP gamma decay of the running Fisher, and per-task Fisher normalisation. P&C's own additions are gamma and the normalisation.

errors_found.reader_claim: "Policies are computed at inverse temperature tau (tau = 2.0 on Omniglot)."
errors_found.problem: The paper is inconsistent on this point and the reading silently merges the two versions. The main text says "inverse temperature τ" and the supplement says "softmax temperature τ = 2.0".
errors_found.evidence: Main text: "The policies are computed at inverse temperature τ (a hyperparameter)." Supp. C.1: "we found a softmax temperature τ = 2.0 to work best."
errors_found.corrected: τ = 2.0 on Omniglot. Whether it acts as a temperature or an inverse temperature is ambiguous in the paper.

claim_check_overrides.claim: Sec 13: "Parameter protection such as EWC is a useful alternative comparison [16], but no finite replay or penalty should be advertised as preventing all catastrophic forgetting."
claim_check_overrides.reason: Taken as a statement about what [16] supports, it is accurate. P&C uses EWC and online EWC as its main comparisons and concludes "online EWC on its own is a competitive method". Its Fig. 2a shows that every penalty-based method (EWC, online EWC, P&C) still loses a large fraction of first-task performance (about 0.56-0.72 normalised after 49 further tasks). The reading's objections are separate issues: the missing primary EWC citation (Kirkpatrick 2017) is citation hygiene, and the absent EWC arm in Sec 17 is an internal inconsistency in the proposal. Neither makes the sentence inaccurate about [16].

missed_points: Retention is P&C's weak link, not a strength. Fig. 2a (pixel-traced) shows P&C's knowledge base retaining the first alphabet about 0.09 below online EWC and about 0.13 below EWC applied directly in one network. The extra teacher-to-student distillation step costs retention. For the proposal, the key comparator P&C used is exactly what is missing: a single-network arm that updates theta directly on the new task with the same R_old/replay budget, with no fast memory and no distillation. The reading's suggested arms, (a) online EWC plus distillation and (d) naive fine-tuning, do not isolate this. Without such an arm the proposal cannot show that routing learning through fast memory and then distillation beats simply updating the slow policy under replay.

In a single pass P&C does not beat online EWC: Omniglot after 1 pass is 70.32 ± 3.3 vs 69.99 ± 3.2, a statistical tie. Its advantage appears only with revisits (82.84 vs 79.15 after 5 passes), and "All hyperparameters are optimised for maximum performance after five visits." The proposal's Stage D consists of single task arrivals, so P&C gives almost no evidence that a two-phase lifecycle beats single-network protection in the proposal's own regime.

P&C describes the EWC penalty as behavioural ("protects the policy in expectation over the state space"; the Fisher "measures the curvature of the KL term"). This implies a directly matched, zero-storage baseline for the proposal, sketched here in my own terms: an 'FM-Fisher', diag E∫(∂v_theta/∂theta)^2 dt, computed at consolidation time on current-task contexts, after which the data are discarded. This is the diagonal second-order version of R_old. P&C estimates its Fisher from current data only ("We use 100 minibatches of equal size to estimate the diagonal Fisher"). Such an arm would separate what exact function-space replay buys from what storing D_old buys.

P&C explicitly criticises the proposal's chosen retention route. On episodic replay: "An inherent problem is the constraint on the amount of experience that can be stored in memory, which could quickly become a limiting factor in large scale problems." On generative replay (the proposal's future 'learned decoder', Sec 14): it "shifts the catastrophic forgetting problem to the training of the generative model." The proposal should answer this with a storage-scaling analysis, not only byte accounting.

Supplement A cuts both ways, and the reading reports only one side. It says online EWC "is often a better choice" "For an optimal setting, where the optimisation converges", and EWC is better only for short training (500-1000 steps). With 10,000 steps, EWC's old anchors make it "more difficult to retain the most recent tasks". The proposal prescribes "small, repeated slow updates" behind gates, which is the short, unconverged regime in which per-task anchors helped. That strengthens the case for comparing an old-teacher-endpoint anchor (already mentioned in Sec 13) against the re-centred v_old anchor.

Evaluation-protocol detail worth borrowing: P&C fixes lambda across EWC methods for the isolated forgetting and transfer plots, but tunes all hyperparameters for the overall-performance tables (Supp. C.1: "in which case we fix λ for all EWC methods to provide a fair comparison"). The proposal's fairness rules do not say how retention and transfer diagnostics are tuned relative to headline results.

Calibration of the proposal's '≤2 pp old-task loss over ≥10 arrivals' target. No-storage protection in P&C is far from that level: first-task retention falls to about 0.56-0.72 normalised, and after 5 passes overall accuracy (82.84) is still 5.5 pp below single-task models (88.34), 18 pp below after 1 pass. The target therefore depends entirely on replay coverage and capacity, and P&C offers no support for it at ≥10 tasks. The proposal should say this.

P&C found that without re-initialising the active column, transfer vanished, "suggesting only a small utilisation of connections to the knowledge base". Carried to the proposal, this warns that a plastic learner can learn to ignore slow features. The proposal should ablate the h_theta input to the query Q_phi (with vs without slow features) and measure how much the slow-to-fast channel is actually used. The reading lists the quote as a limitation but does not turn it into an ablation.

The dual-memory, sleep-consolidation framing has uncited precedents beyond P&C (arXiv abstracts verified in this session, full papers not read). FearNet (Kemker & Kanan, arXiv:1711.10563): "new memories are consolidated from a network for recent memories inspired by the mammalian hippocampal complex to a network for long-term storage inspired by medial prefrontal cortex. Memory consolidation is inspired by mechanisms that occur during sleep." It is also generative and stores no examples. DualNet (arXiv:2110.00175): explicit CLS fast/slow systems. Kaplanis et al., 'Continual Reinforcement Learning with Complex Synapses' (arXiv:1802.07239): multi-timescale synapses in RL. From background knowledge only, not verified here: Hinton & Plaut (1987), 'Using fast weights to deblur old memories', the canonical fast/slow-weights paper. Together with P&C and CLS-ER, these leave the hippocampus-to-cortex framing of Sec 2 fully pre-empted.
verification.novelty_threat_assessment:
Medium overall: high for the lifecycle concept and the biological framing, low for the flow-matching-specific technical contributions.

What P&C already published (2018):
- A plastic learner trained with the slow model frozen, reusing slow features through lateral adaptors.
- Behavioural distillation of that learner into the slow model under a retention penalty.
- Re-initialisation of the plastic learner to renew plasticity (Table 1: 127-129% with re-init vs a decline to 101% without).
- Fixed size with no task-specific parameters.
- An explicit day/night sleep analogy.

The proposal's own Sec 21 concedes the lifecycle is not new, so this is not fatal. But Secs 2 and 11-15 cannot claim novelty for the lifecycle, for behavioural (non-weight) transfer, or for fast-to-slow consolidation. FearNet (2018), CLS-ER and DualNet further pre-empt the hippocampus-to-cortex framing.

The retention component is closer to P&C than the proposal or the reading admits. R_old is the exact, stored-data counterpart of P&C's online EWC, which is a diagonal quadratic approximation to an expected-KL penalty. Both anchor to the latest accepted solution. "Replay instead of online EWC" is therefore an engineering choice with a storage cost P&C deliberately avoided, not a contribution.

What P&C does not pre-empt:
- Denoising-time readout inside a flow-matching sampler.
- The centred residual with exact reset.
- Meta-learned, few-shot, causal fast weights (1,072 parameters, 1-16 experiences) instead of a column trained to convergence.
- FM endpoint/path distillation with selection-bias correction.
- The velocity-replay W2 bound.
- The reader factorial, the accept/reject gate, and the episodic store for non-identifiable facts.

The practical threat is reviewer framing: "P&C instantiated for FM policies, with replay and a tiny meta-learned active column". To defend against it, the proposal needs three things:
1. A P&C-style arm: a full adapter trained on the task with lateral access to theta, FM-distilled under online EWC or an FM-Fisher penalty, then reset.
2. A single-network direct-update arm with the same replay.
3. Evidence that the few-shot fast memory and gate add value beyond both.

P&C's own evidence also shows that the two-phase design helped only where the single-network method suffered negative transfer. It tied online EWC in a single pass on Omniglot and retained worse. So the proposal's lifecycle has no guaranteed advantage over direct slow updates with replay.

ref.title: Bechtle et al., Meta-Learning via Learned Loss (2019)
ref.role: Alternative writer: learned scalar write loss whose gradient drives fast-weight updates, trained by future behavior.
ref.focus: ML^3 framework, how the learned loss is meta-trained (task loss after inner updates), use of extra info at meta-train time, RL/robot experiments, generalization. Relevance to eq 7-8 alternative writer and to the proposal's warning that minimizing the scalar in isolation is meaningless.

reading.accessed: I read the full arXiv PDF, latest version v4 (19 Jan 2021, 9 pages), from https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.05374. Copies are saved at .../scratchpad/refs/ref17.pdf, ref17.txt (pdftotext -layout) and ref17_flow.txt (non-layout, easier to read). Page renders are ref17_p-1..9.png; I looked at pages 3, 5, 6 and 7 to check equations, algorithms and figure values. I read everything: abstract, intro, related work, Sec. III (equations 1-9, Algorithms 1-2), Sec. IV (all experiments), conclusions, references and the appendix (Algorithms 3-5 and environment details). I also fetched the arXiv abstract page (ref17_abs.html) for metadata and version history.
