reading.relevance_to_proposal:
Sec 9, eq. (15) (whole-path optimisation):
- [18]'s framework gives the exact conditions under which the first term of J_W would be a relative entropy. It would need a stochastic Euler-Maruyama reference z_{i+1} = z_i + dt v_theta + sigma sqrt(dt) xi. Then (dt/2) sum ||(z_{i+1}-z_i)/dt - v_theta||^2 = sigma^2 (-log p_ref(Z|z_0)) + const.
- In that case J_W / sigma^2 is the negative log density of the tilted path law Q* proportional to P_ref exp(-lambda E~/sigma^2). This Q* minimises KL(Q|P_ref) + E_Q[lambda E~/sigma^2] (Gibbs variational principle; my derivation, consistent with Lemma 19 and my Monte Carlo check).
- K gradient steps on a single Z approximate the MODE of Q*, not a sample from it. That explains the proposal's own warning that the procedure "may reduce diversity": the entropy term that would prevent collapse is absent.
- With sigma = 0 the path law is a Dirac, and Prop 24 shows that any other path from the same z_0 has infinite KL. The proposal's sentence is therefore correct.
- Seen through the control identity, Sec 9 is open-loop direct transcription of the same kind of deterministic control problem as Sec 10: take u_i = (z_{i+1}-z_i)/dt - v_theta(z_i) and running cost from E~.

Sec 10, eqs. (17)-(20) (value/control reader):
- The HJB (20) has no diffusion term. It is the zero-noise limit of the entropy-regularised control problem whose sigma > 0 version is linked to SB through Doob h-transforms and Schrödinger potentials ([18] App D.2, H.2: "Pi^{n+1} is a Doob h-transform of Pi^n").
- With sigma > 0 the Hopf-Cole transform V = -sigma^2 log h linearises the HJB, and u* = sigma^2 grad log h, where h can be estimated by Feynman-Kac expectations over base-policy rollouts (path-integral control; my derivation, not in [18]).
- This addresses the proposal's worry that "Optimizing each noise seed can send many seeds to the same outcome": KL-regularised control on stochastic dynamics yields a reweighted distribution rather than a collapsed one. An SB goes further and fixes the terminal distribution outright.

Sec 13, eqs. (25)-(28) (retention):
- Lemma 19 gives a Lipschitz-free alternative to the Gronwall W2 bound. For a stochastic sampler with noise sigma and the same initial law, KL(P_old || P_new) = (1/(2 sigma^2)) E_old integral ||drift_old - drift_new||^2 dt, and data processing bounds the action-level KL.
- R_old is already evaluated on old-policy trajectories, which is exactly the direction KL(P_old || P_new) needs.
- Caveat: the SDE-sampler drift also contains the score. For Gaussian-path FM the score is affine in v, s = (t v - z)/(1-t), so the noise schedule must vanish near t = 1.

Sec 11, eqs. (23)-(24) (path distillation, b* = E[V_t | Gamma_t = z]):
- Structurally the same as DSB's mean-matching regression on simulated trajectories (Prop 3, App E). DSB's cached-trajectory training (Algorithm 3), EMA 0.999, and fine-tuning from the previous iterate (App I Techniques 3, 5, 6) are directly reusable engineering for path-distillation consolidation.

Sec 4, eq. (4) (centering at W_0):
- SB analogy: if the base terminal marginal already equals the target, the Schrödinger potential is constant and the correction sigma^2 grad log h is zero. The IPF starts at pi^0 = reference.

App C (priors and deterministic starts):
- [18] supports the point that prior choice matters in practice (Technique 4, Fig 11).
- It shows that an SB can start from a Dirac, because the diffusion noise supplies the randomness (Prop 43 remark: with a Dirac target, "IPF converges in two iterations"). This is consistent with the proposal's claim that a deterministic ODE from a point mass needs "another source of randomness".

Sec 21 related-work table: [18] is not listed there.
novelty_threats: No direct threat to the core contributions (fast-weight memory, velocity reader, consolidation lifecycle). [18] has no memory, test-time training, few-shot adaptation or robotics content.

Indirect threat to Sec 9/10 framing ('memory changes the transition objective', minimal departure from the base field). The SB/KL-control literature that [18] builds on already gives a principled formulation of 'minimal departure from a reference generative process subject to new endpoint information'. Any claim that the Sec 9/10 objectives are new formulations must be positioned against it; the novelty can only lie in the learned memory-dependent cost and the lifecycle.

[18] App J.3 already uses a pretrained generative diffusion as the reference process for a new bridge problem ("the reference dynamics ... is chosen to be the one obtained with the DSB where p_prior is a Gaussian"). It also refines networks from the previous iterate (App I Technique 5), noting "we plan to investigate more sophisticated warm-start approaches through meta-learning". So adapting a pretrained sampler's drift toward new endpoint constraints by warm-started regression is established; the proposal's contribution must be the fast/few-shot memory mechanism, not that adaptation pattern.

A natural missing baseline for the value/path readers: a KL-regularised or SB-style adaptation of the base FM policy toward the new-task action distribution, with the base sampler (made stochastic) as reference. Examples: DSB/IPF or bridge matching, and reward-tilted SOC fine-tuning such as Adjoint Matching (Domingo-Enrich et al. 2024; my knowledge, not verified here). Without it, a reviewer may ask why the principled minimum-KL correction was not compared.
ideas_to_borrow: State the positive version of the Sec 9 sentence. Under an Euler-Maruyama reference with noise sigma > 0, the departure term = sigma^2 (-log p_ref(Z|z_0)) + const, and E_Q[departure] = sigma^2 KL(Q|P_ref) + N d sigma^2/2. The discrete Girsanov identity KL = (dt/(2 sigma^2)) sum E||u_i||^2 is exact for Gaussian chains; I checked it numerically. The deterministic objective is the sigma -> 0 limit of sigma^2 KL (compare Mikami's 2 sigma^2 KL -> W_2^2 quoted in [18] Sec 3.1).

Add a 'stochastic path-energy' variant of the Sec 9 reader as an ablation. Sample from the tilted path law Q* proportional to P_ref exp(-lambda E~/sigma^2) (Langevin on Z, or SMC over the Euler-Maruyama chain) instead of K gradient steps to its mode. This tests directly whether mode-seeking causes the diversity loss the proposal anticipates.

Soft (entropy-regularised) value reader for Sec 10. Add sigma > 0 and use the Hopf-Cole / Doob h-transform form u* = sigma^2 grad log h, with h(t,z) = E_ref[exp(-(integral C_W + Phi_W)/sigma^2) | z_t = z] estimated by base-policy rollouts. [18] App H.2 gives the h-transform / potential machinery. This avoids solving a nonlinear HJB and keeps distributional spread.

SB baseline for task arrival. Use the base FM policy (with a matched stochastic sampler) as reference, N(0,I) as initial marginal and the new task's demo action distribution as terminal marginal; run DSB/IPF or bridge matching warm-started from the base (as in [18] App J.3 and Technique 5). This gives the minimum-KL correction to compare against the fast-memory residual. Its correction vanishes when the target equals the base marginal, the same property as the proposal's centering.

Retention via Girsanov (Lemma 19) for a stochastic sampler: KL(P_old || P_new) = (1/(2 sigma^2)) E_old integral ||Delta drift||^2 dt, plus Pinsker, gives action-level KL/TV bounds with no e^{2L} Lipschitz factor. Report it next to the Gronwall W2 bound (27)-(28).

Analytic ground truth. [18] validates DSB against a closed-form Gaussian SB (Prop 46: beta = (sqrt(5)-1)/2; Prop 43: rate kappa = rho/(1+rho)). The Sec 19 analytic Gaussian FM sanity check could be extended with a closed-form KL/SB solution so the Sec 9/10 variants have exact targets.

Training engineering for path distillation (eqs. 23-24): cached trajectories refreshed periodically (Algorithm 3), sampling one uniformly random time index per trajectory to decorrelate the loss (Technique 1), EMA of parameters at rate 0.999 (Technique 6), and warm-starting from the previous network (Technique 5).

Report per-cycle marginal-mismatch metrics, e.g. KL or TV of the endpoint marginal against its target, mirroring IPF's monotone diagnostics (Prop 4; App F Lemma 33: KL(pi^{2n}|pi^{2n+1}) = KL(pi^{2n}_1|nu_1)). Useful for tracking the consolidation/refresh cycles.
Terminology fix: use 'Schrödinger bridge' for the KL-minimising path law. [18] reserves plain 'bridge' for any process with the right marginals.
technical_issues_in_proposal: Sec 9's sentence is correct but gives no constructive statement of which assumptions WOULD make the departure a KL. Missing: (a) a non-degenerate noise sigma > 0 shared by the reference and the controlled process ([18] Lemma 19 needs identical sqrt(2) noise); (b) the same initial law; (c) a finite-energy drift difference; (d) a path LAW, not a single optimised path. A Dirac on one Z has infinite KL even w.r.t. a stochastic reference, because the conditional kernels are singular (Prop 24). Without (d), no relative-entropy reading of eq. (15) is possible under any noise level.

Even under a stochastic reference, K gradient steps on Z compute a MAP/mode of the tilted path law, not a KL-optimal law. The entropy term -H(Q) that separates the KL objective from the energy objective is exactly what the method drops. This is the mechanism behind the diversity loss the proposal mentions; the proposal states the symptom but not the cause.

Sec 9 and Sec 10 are presented as distinct readers, but with u_i = (z_{i+1} - z_i)/dt - v_theta(z_i,t_i,c), eq. (15) is a direct-transcription (open-loop) discretisation of a deterministic control problem of the Sec 10 form: running cost (1/2)||u||^2 plus lambda times a cost taken from the path energy E~. They differ in solver (finite K steps versus HJB/feedback), in that E~ depends on edges (z_i, z_{i+1}) and hence on u, and in having no explicit terminal cost. The factorial comparison of readers should account for this overlap. (My derivation, prompted by [18]'s KL/control identity.)

HJB (20) omits the (sigma^2/2) Laplacian term, so it is the deterministic zero-noise limit. The SB and stochastic-control connections the proposal alludes to ([18] App D.2, H.2 potentials and Doob h-transforms) require sigma > 0, where the HJB is linearisable (Hopf-Cole) and the optimal control is sigma^2 grad log h. The proposal should state that its Sec 10 formulation lies outside the SB/relative-entropy regime.

App C cites [18] for the stochastic-control/relative-entropy identity, but [18] never writes the SB as a control problem. It provides only the Girsanov KL formula for sqrt(2)-diffusions (Lemma 19, used for TV bounds) and points to Chen et al. (2021b) and Léonard (2014b). A primary SB/control reference should be added.

App C's 'distinct from FM' contrast is too broad. [18] shows SB solvers learn drifts by regression (Props 3, 29) and that an SB has a same-marginal ODE (App H.3). The contrast is valid only for the proposal's own independent-coupling linear-interpolant FM (eq. 11), and it should be qualified that way.

Terminology: 'does not by itself make the method a bridge' should read 'a Schrödinger bridge'. In [18]'s usage ('we would obtain a bridge between p_data and p_prior but not necessarily the Schrödinger bridge'), the proposal's FM policy is already a bridge.

Retention (Sec 13) relies only on an ODE Gronwall bound with C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L), which can be very loose for large Lipschitz constants. If a stochastic sampler is acceptable, [18]'s Lemma 19 gives an exact path-KL expression in terms of the same kind of on-trajectory velocity discrepancy R_old. Caveat: the SDE-sampler drift includes a score term, which for Gaussian-path FM is (t v - z)/(1-t), so the noise schedule must vanish near t = 1. The proposal does not discuss this alternative.
cited_works_worth_adding: Léonard, C. (2014b). A survey of the Schrödinger problem and some of its connections with optimal transport. DCDS-A 34(4). The standard SB reference: dynamic/static equivalence, entropic OT, the zero-noise limit to OT, and the stochastic-control viewpoint. A better primary citation for the App C definition than [18].

Chen, Y., Georgiou, T. T., and Pavon, M. (2021b). Optimal transport in systems and control. Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems 4. Also Chen, Georgiou, Pavon (2016), SIAM J. Appl. Math. The control-theoretic formulation of SB as minimum-energy steering, i.e. the 'stochastic-control/relative-entropy identity' the proposal invokes but does not cite.

Mikami, T. (2004). Monge's problem with a quadratic cost by the zero-noise limit of h-path processes. PTRF 129. Quoted in [18] Sec 3.1: 2 sigma^2 KL -> W_2^2 as sigma -> 0. It pins down how a quadratic cost arises only as a rescaled zero-noise limit of KL, which is exactly the Sec 9 statement.
Föllmer, H. (1988). Random fields and diffusion processes (Saint-Flour). Classical SB/entropy source; relevant to deterministic-start (Dirac) bridges in App C.

Csiszár, I. (1975). I-divergence geometry of probability distributions and minimization problems. Ann. Probab. 3. I-projections and the Pythagorean identity behind IPF; relevant if the proposal formalises KL projections for consolidation or refresh.

Liptser, R. S. and Shiryaev, A. N. (2001). Statistics of Random Processes I, Thm 7.7. The Girsanov theorem as used in [18] Lemma 19 for KL between diffusions; the right citation for any Girsanov-based retention or regularisation bound.

Song, Y. et al. (2021). Score-based generative modeling through SDEs (ICLR). Probability-flow ODE with the same marginals as the SDE ([18] App H.3); needed to relate an FM ODE policy to a stochastic sampler for which KL identities hold.

Tzen, B. and Raginsky, M. (2019). Theoretical guarantees for sampling and inference in generative models with latent diffusions (COLT). Stochastic-control analysis of diffusion generative models; relevant to the Sec 10 control reader.
Vargas, F., Thodoroff, P., Lawrence, N. D., and Lamacraft, A. (2021). Solving Schrödinger bridges via maximum likelihood. arXiv:2106.02081. Concurrent IPF-based SB solver; alternative baseline.

Cattiaux, P., Conforti, G., Gentil, I., and Léonard, C. (2021). Time reversal of diffusion processes under a finite entropy condition. arXiv:2104.07708. Conditions for the time reversals used in IPF; relevant only if SB baselines are implemented.
stated_limitations: "Whilst our implementation does not yet compete with state-of-the-art methods" (Sec 4).

"Even though the final time T > 0 within DSB can be arbitrarily small, we observed that this has limits as choosing T too close to 0 decreases the quality of the generative models. One reason ... if the endpoint of the original forward process is too far from the target distribution p_prior, then learning the score around the support of p_prior is challenging even for DSB" (Sec 5).

"Although DSB requires learning a sequence of network parameters alpha^n, beta^n" (Sec 3.3). The score-sum variant (App E.2.1) "requires storing 2n neural networks" and O(nN) passes, so it was discarded.
Joint training of forward and backward networks reaches "a bridge between p_data and p_prior but not necessarily the Schrödinger bridge" (Sec 3.3).

Very few steps fail: "in order to obtain similar results to N = 10 with N = 1 we need to substantially increase the size of the networks". Fig 12: with N=2, "The results deteriorate significantly after 5 iterations".
Theorem 1's uniform score-error assumption (8) "is a strong assumption".

IPF converges to the SB only under additional conditions (Prop 5: absolute continuity of p w.r.t. pi^infinity and a growth bound on h). The general rate is only o(1/n) for marginal KL; geometric rates are shown only in Gaussian cases (App G).
Sensitive to the prior: a small prior variance slows DSB convergence and reduces diversity (Fig 11). Small networks fail to recover the SB covariance in d=50 (Sec 4).
Training is costly because trajectories must be simulated at every IPF iteration after the first; this is mitigated by caching (App I, Technique 3).

errors_found.reader_claim: Ideas/relevance (retention via Girsanov): 'For a stochastic sampler with noise sigma and the same initial law, KL(P_old || P_new) = (1/(2 sigma^2)) E_old ∫ ||drift_old - drift_new||^2 dt ... gives action-level KL/TV bounds with no e^{2L} Lipschitz factor ... Caveat: ... the noise schedule must vanish near t = 1.'
errors_found.problem:
The Girsanov identity itself (Lemma 19) is correct, but applying it to the proposal's FM policy is more restrictive than the reader implies. Take an SDE sampler whose marginals match each model's Gaussian-path FM ODE (eq. 11 coupling):
- Its drift is v + (sigma_t^2/2)s, with implied score s = (t v - z)/(1-t).
- So Δdrift = Δv (1 + sigma_t^2 t/(2(1-t))).
- Hence KL = ∫ w_t E_{p_t^old}||Δv||^2 dt, with w_t = (1/(2 sigma_t^2))(1 + sigma_t^2 t/(2(1-t)))^2.
- Minimising over the noise level gives w_t >= t/(1-t), attained at sigma_t^2 = 2(1-t)/t.

Consequences:
- No noise schedule gives a bound in terms of the proposal's unweighted R_old (eq. 25).
- The weight diverges at t -> 1, so the KL can be infinite unless Δv vanishes near t=1.
- Letting sigma_t -> 0 near t=1, which is the reader's own caveat, makes the 1/(2 sigma^2) factor blow up.
- The result bounds a stochastic sampler's action law, not the deployed ODE policy.
- [18]'s own Girsanov-based result (Thm 1) still carries exp[D_alpha T] constants.
errors_found.evidence: Lemma 19 proof: "KL(µx(1)|µx(2)) = (1/4)∫ E[||b1 - b2||^2]dt" for the same sqrt(2) noise. Thm 1 bound: "||L(X0) - pdata||TV <= Cα(M + γ̄^{1/2}) exp[Dα T] + ...". I checked the minimisation with sympy (argmin sigma^2 = 2(1-t)/t, min w = t/(1-t)). I also checked numerically that s = (t v - z)/(1-t) for a 1-D Gaussian FM path (scratchpad/ref18_verify_w.py).
errors_found.corrected: A Girsanov retention bound for an SDE surrogate of the FM policy has the form KL <= ∫ w_t E_old||Δv_t||^2 dt, with w_t >= t/(1-t). This is a time-weighted R_old that diverges near t=1, not a drop-in, Lipschitz-free replacement for the Gronwall bound (27)-(28).

claim_check_overrides.claim: App C: "General FM instead learns a velocity associated with a selected probability-path construction." (contrasted with SB)
claim_check_overrides.reason:
The proposal does not attribute this sentence to [18]; the [18] citation supports only the preceding SB definition. As a description of general FM, the sentence is correct, and the contrast it draws is valid: an SB is defined by a KL-minimisation criterion relative to a reference, while FM regresses a velocity for whatever path or coupling the user selects.

The sentence does not claim that FM can never realise an SB. Choosing the SB's own path is one admissible selection, and [18] App H.3 shows the SB has a same-marginal ODE, dX~* = (1/2)(f* - b*)dt. The reader's nuance is worth adding as a footnote, but it does not make the sentence partially inaccurate.

missed_points: The discrete potential form of an IPF half-step (App D.2, Prop 26) reweights the base transition kernel by a backward-propagated potential: p̄^{n+1}(x_{k+1}|x_k) = p̄^n(x_{k+1}|x_k) ψ_{k+1}(x_{k+1})/ψ_k(x_k), with ψ_k = ∫ψ_{k+1} p̄^n dx_{k+1} and ψ_N = target/current terminal marginal. [18] says: "the IPF iterations appear as a policy refinement of the original forward dynamic p̄." This is the stochastic, discrete-time analogue of the proposal's Sec 10 value reader. With sigma > 0 and terminal cost Φ = -sigma^2 log(p_target/p_base,1), the value reader is exactly one IPF half-bridge, and a learned Φ_W makes it a 'learned-potential half-bridge'. The reader cites H.2 potentials but misses this direct correspondence, which is the clearest way to position Sec 10 against the SB literature.

Selection bias (proposal Sec 12, 'Selection can corrupt the initial law'). Keeping only successful paths conditions the path law on a terminal event, which is a Doob h-transform. [18] identifies each IPF step with this operation ("Πn+1 is a Doob h-transform of Πn", App H.2). Such a transform necessarily reweights the initial law by h_0(z_0), which is exactly the corruption the proposal describes. The proposal's two fixes each enforce only one constraint:
- Option 1 (fresh seeds, unfiltered endpoints) keeps the N(0,I) initial law but not the success-conditioned endpoint law.
- Option 2 keeps the success endpoints but pairs them with independent noise, discarding the teacher's coupling.
A Schrödinger bridge between N(0,I) and the success-conditioned endpoint law, with a stochasticised teacher as reference and solved by IPF, is the principled option that enforces both while staying KL-closest to the teacher. The reader does not connect [18] to this section.

Support for the proposal's residual and centering design. App E.2.3 reports that the mean-matching parameterisation (identity plus perturbation) beat drift matching: "networks ... have residual connections and therefore are better suited at representing functions of the x -> x + Φ(x) where Φ is a perturbation." Technique 5 writes each IPF refinement as an additive correction to the previous drift: b^n = b^{n-1} + 2∇log p^n - 2∇log q^{n-1}. The remark after Prop 43 ("if β^2 = 1 - α^2 then ... p* = p, i.e. the IPF leaves µ invariant") is the formal analogue of the proposal's exact-zero correction at W = W_0 (eq. 4). The reader states the centering analogy but not this textual support.

Fig 6 content visible in the PDF, as detailed in errors_found: approximate FID trajectories that plateau after 4-7 iterations and are non-monotone for N=10. The paper's claim that DSB iterations 'always improve' the model is not fully borne out. This is relevant if the proposal borrows IPF-style monotone-improvement diagnostics for consolidation cycles.

Lemma 19 allows non-anticipative, path-dependent drifts b_i(t, (X_s)_{s∈[0,T]}). So any Girsanov-based regularisation or retention identity the proposal adopts would still hold for drifts that depend on the generation history, provided the noise is shared and non-degenerate. The reader restates the lemma with Markov drifts only.

Deligiannidis et al. (2021) is cited in [18] for the result that IPF with empirical marginals stays close to IPF with the true marginals, only as the sample size grows. With the proposal's 1-16 experiences, an SB to the empirical demo measure would reproduce the demos. This constrains any SB-style baseline the reader recommends.
verification.novelty_threat_assessment:
LOW.

What [18] is, and how the proposal uses it:
- [18] is a methods and theory paper on solving Schrödinger bridges for score-based generative modelling. It covers IPF via time reversal (DSB), TV bounds for SGM, IPF monotonicity and convergence, and Gaussian ground truth.
- It has no fast weights, test-time training, few-shot adaptation, continual learning, memory consolidation or robotics content. It predates flow matching.
- The proposal cites [18] only to define an SB and to say that its own quadratic departure cost and FM construction are not SBs without extra probabilistic assumptions. Both statements are correct and appropriately hedged: Sec 9 says "Connections to stochastic control or Schrodinger bridges require their additional probabilistic assumptions."

The only overlaps are formal, and none pre-empts the core contribution (a persistent gradient-written fast memory read at every ODE step, plus the consolidation, retention and refresh lifecycle):
- App J.3 uses a pretrained DSB as the reference process for a new bridge. Adapting a pretrained sampler toward new endpoint constraints by warm-started drift regression is therefore established; the proposal does not claim otherwise.
- The IPF half-step is a potential-reweighted, 'policy refinement' Doob h-transform of the base dynamics (App D.2, H.2). This is the stochastic counterpart of the Sec 10 value reader.
- DSB's mean-matching regression on self-simulated trajectories, with fine-tuning from the previous iterate, parallels the Sec 11-12 path distillation.

These matter only if the proposal were to present its Sec 9/10 objectives as new formulations; it presents them as optional alternatives and compares them to HardFlow. The reader's suggestion that an SB/IPF adaptation is a 'natural missing baseline' is overstated for a regime of 1-16 context-conditioned demos: DSB needs many target samples, repeated network training, and positive densities.

Net effect: a positioning footnote at most. The proposal could note that Sec 10 with sigma > 0 and a log-density-ratio terminal cost reduces to an IPF half-bridge, and that Sec 9 is the MAP (sigma -> 0) counterpart of a KL-tilted path law. [18] creates no threat to novelty.

gap.landscape_summary:
By September 2026, the area around this proposal is crowded, and each of its contributions (a)-(d) now has a close precedent. What still looks unclaimed is the combination: a persistent, causally written, meta-trained fast net that is read through a centered velocity residual at every ODE step and repeatedly consolidated into the slow FM backbone with replay and reset gates. I found no robot-policy paper with a W2/Gronwall retention bound (e), although the regularizer the bound is built on has a direct precedent. Five clusters matter.

(1) Fast weights inside diffusion/flow transformers, read at every denoising step. One-Minute Video (CVPR'25) puts gated TTT-MLP layers in a video DiT. LaCT (2505.23884) updates fast weights "only ... on clean chunks" and applies them to noisy chunks inside an autoregressive video-diffusion transformer. This write-clean/read-noisy pattern is the one the proposal uses. DexWorldModel/CLWM (2604.16484, Apr 2026) keeps a long-term TTT memory updated "exclusively when new ground-truth observations and executed actions are received". It forks a working copy that stays "strictly frozen across all intermediate flow steps", and the noisy action is read through that copy. RoboTTT and WAM-TTT (already cited) follow the same line. So the claim that persistent fast weights shape the denoising path cannot be the novelty. The proposal's own Sec. 6 framing (the difference is intervention location plus lifecycle) is the right one, and it must be argued against DexWM, not only RoboTTT.

(2) Velocity-space steering of frozen FM policies. This cluster pre-empts (b) most directly. Proxy Policy Steering (2609.09148) adds gamma*[v_task - v_ref] at every denoising step. v_task is fine-tuned from v_ref, so the residual is exactly zero before task data, which is structurally the proposal's centered residual in Eq. 4. PPS reports that post-hoc final-action residuals underperform and that fitting the reference only at the clean endpoint hurts. FlowCorrect (2602.22056) learns a gated LoRA velocity residual from a few corrections, supervised on intermediate ODE velocities. TraceFlow (2609.20646) turns a growing store of successful and failed rollouts into a bounded per-step velocity correction. Retrieve-then-Steer (2605.10094) injects a success-memory prior at an intermediate sampler state. Related but less central: GLOVES (2606.06461), DynaGuide (2506.13922), DSRL (2506.15799), OptimusVLA (2602.20200).

(3) Activation and in-context memory. In-context imitation: ICRT, Instant Policy, RICL, ContextFlow (in-context FM, 2609.06852), MimicDroid, Zero-WAM. Memory architectures: Gated Memory Policy (cross-trial in-context adaptation in a DiT policy), MemoryVLA, MEM, SAM2Act, HALO (2606.25136), and SmoLSTM. SmoLSTM has an episode-persistent matrix memory that the FM head reads once per control step and does not re-enter per ODE step, which makes it a natural control for (a). Benchmarks include RoboMME, RoboMemArena and MemMimic.

(4) Test-time weight adaptation of VLAs. RL-based: EVOLVE-VLA, TT-VLA (2601.06748). Prompt-based: TTT-VLA latent prompt (2606.03127), VANE (shadow-copy commit/rollback), T3VF (2605.08215), WorldAgen (2609.08162). Writers and meta-learning: WIZARD, a hypernetwork writer that outputs LoRA weights from a demo video; VITA, which takes gradient steps on a meta-learned self-supervised loss and includes reset ablations; and OMLA (2503.18684). These bear on (c) and on the Sec. 14 gates.

(5) Consolidation and retention. ReGuide (2606.28939) absorbs success-filtered, denoising-guided rollouts into a diffusion policy with rehearsal. This is the direct precedent for (d), and it is exposed to the selection bias the proposal warns about. Also relevant: Sleeping Robots (wake-sleep frozen-actor distillation), CPC (2601.22475), and Masip et al.'s generative distillation for diffusion models, which matches teacher predictions on teacher-generated, re-noised samples and is a precedent for R_old (Eq. 25). 'Pretrained VLAs are surprisingly resistant to forgetting' (2603.03818) shows plain experience replay gives near-zero forgetting, which raises the bar for the old-task target (<=2 pp). ConSFT (2605.08879) addresses retention in FM VLAs without prior data.

Recommendations: rewrite the Sec. 21 table to position against PPS (centering), DexWM, LaCT and RoboTTT (per-step internal fast weights), TraceFlow and FlowCorrect (experience-driven velocity corrections), and ReGuide and Masip (consolidation). Add at least these baselines: PPS-style offline proxy residual; DexWM-style internal TTT that writes only from executed history and is frozen during the ODE; TraceFlow-style bounded nonparametric guidance; SmoLSTM/GMP-style activation memory read once per decision versus per step; an ER-only continual baseline.

Method note: the arXiv API returned HTTP 406 and arXiv web search was rate-limited (429). Candidates were found with WebSearch and verified by fetching each arXiv abs page, plus the PMLR page for Masip. Full PDFs were read for PPS, TraceFlow, Retrieve-then-Steer, GMP, One-Minute Video, LaCT, DexWM, WIZARD, FlowCorrect, GLOVES, Sleeping Robots, CPC, VANE, SmoLSTM, EVOLVE-VLA, TT-VLA, VITA, ReGuide and Masip. The other entries were verified from their abs pages only.

papers.title: Proxy Policy Steering
papers.authors_year: Ning, Wang, Ma, Fang (Cornell), 2026 (arXiv 2609.09148, v3 13 Sep 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Adapts a frozen flow-matching VLA (pi0.5, pi0) with two small (32M) proxy policies. v_ref is distilled from the base along the base's own denoising trajectories on target-task observations. v_task is initialized from v_ref and fine-tuned on about 50 demos. Sampling uses 'vPPS = vbase + gamma[vtask - vref]', and 'Their difference forms a calibrated velocity-space residual that steers the frozen base sampler at every denoising step.' The paper derives this as a product-of-experts / density-ratio correction applied at each noise level under the linear FM path (App. D). It reports a +55% absolute average gain over pi0.5 on 12 tasks (v3 PDF; the abs page says 53%). Ablations: 'Residual learning underperforms ... because the residual is applied only after the base has sampled a clean action'; 'w/o vel' (reference fit only at the clean endpoint, not along the denoising trajectory) drops 64% to 50%; 'w/o tune' (task proxy trained from scratch) drops to 48%.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Most direct pre-emption of contribution (b), the centered residual in Sec. 4, Eq. 4-5. PPS's v_task - v_ref with v_task initialized from v_ref is exactly zero before adaptation and cancels where task data is silent. That is the same design logic as R(m_t) - R(f_{W0}(q_t)), including the argument that centering removes shared approximation error. Its evidence also bears on two of the proposal's baselines and questions: it shows final-action residuals are weaker, and that endpoint-only versus trajectory supervision matters (relevant to Sec. 11-12, endpoint vs path distillation). Remaining distinctions the proposal can claim: PPS is offline, per-task, trained on 50 demos, with no causal online write, no persistent fast memory, no meta-trained writer and no consolidation or reset lifecycle. The Sec. 21 table must cite it, and the centering claim should be restated as 'centering by W0 inside a fast-weight reader' rather than as new in itself.

papers.title: DexWorldModel: Causal Latent World Modeling towards Automated Learning of Embodied Tasks
papers.authors_year: Deng, Liu, Jia, 2026 (arXiv 2604.16484)
papers.what_it_does: A flow-matching world-action model (CLWM) that replaces the KV cache with a 'Dual-State Test-Time Training (TTT) Memory'. The TTT-MLP uses a tanh gate as in One-Minute Video. The Long-Term TTT Memory 'is updated exclusively when new ground-truth observations and executed actions are received' through an online gradient step on a self-supervised loss. For each generation step a Working memory is forked, and 'the working weights W^work remain strictly frozen across all intermediate flow steps s in (0,1]'. It is read with the noisy latent or action (f_TTT(a_t^(s); W^work)) and gets one intermediate update from the predicted future frame before action decoding. The design gives O(1) memory for long-horizon dual-arm manipulation.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts contribution (a) and part of the Sec. 14 lifecycle. The pattern of persistent fast weights written only from the causal executed prefix, held fixed during the ODE, and queried by the noisy candidate at every flow step is already published for a flow-matching robot model, and it predates RoboTTT. Its long-term/working fork is itself a lifecycle mechanism that protects persistent memory from generated content, close to the proposal's rule that W_k comes only from the causal H_k. The proposal's remaining deltas are the external centered velocity reader, reset gates, and consolidation into theta. Its 'internal TTT-Linear/MLP' baseline (Sec. 16-18) should be specified in this write-from-executed-history, frozen-during-ODE form.

papers.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
papers.authors_year: Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Yang, 2026 (arXiv 2609.20646)
papers.what_it_does: A frozen pi0.5 or PrediMem flow-matching expert is steered by a growing TraceBank of the robot's own rollouts, each labeled with one terminal success/failure bit. A retrieval head and a progress-aligned tracker select success and failure action windows. Their kernel-density scores give attraction and repulsion terms added to the base velocity: 'Bound is the cap: it rescales the success term to a norm of at most c+||v_base|| ...'. The guidance strength declines to zero before the final solver steps, and 'the scores are recomputed at every active step.' Across rounds only the bank changes. On real-robot ordered packing, success goes from 21/50 to 39/50, and to 47/50 after one stacking round. The authors report that 'Stacking gains are finite, every branch peaking before round ten'. The cap matters: uncapped guidance reaches 24.25 vs 57.75 TSR for capped.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A concurrent, nonparametric competitor to (a): experience memory read inside the ODE solver as a bounded velocity correction, accumulated over deployment rounds with no weight update. It is the natural strong version of the proposal's 'history tokens/retrieval' baseline at matched memory and compute budgets (Sec. 16-18), and it maps onto the explicit episodic store B. Its failure modes are informative for the proposal: no gain on Counting/Occlusion, 'not designed to reconstruct missing upstream event information', and saturating stacking. They are consistent with App. B.4's point that hidden episodic facts need explicit storage. Its norm cap is directly relevant to controlling the magnitude of r_{phi,W}.

papers.title: ReGuide: From Test-Time Guidance to Self-Improving Diffusion Policies
papers.authors_year: Lin, Shakkottai, Kalathil, Kumar, 2026 (arXiv 2606.28939)
papers.what_it_does: Steers a behavior-cloned diffusion policy at test time with Phase-Conditioned Guidance: a dynamics-model gradient is applied at denoising steps through the estimated clean action. It then treats 'guided rollouts as reusable on-policy recovery data'. 'Successful guided rollouts are then absorbed back into the policy through ReGuide-FT, which fine-tunes the current checkpoint' on 'a rehearsal buffer containing both prior training data and newly collected guided rollouts', or through ReGuide-FS, which retrains from scratch. The loop can be iterated. It reports a 1.3-7.7x improvement in base success on Robomimic.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Direct precedent for (d), the fast-to-slow transfer in Sec. 11-12. Behavior induced by test-time modification of the denoising process becomes supervision for the slow diffusion policy, with rehearsal and repeated cycles. The differences: the test-time signal is a learned dynamics-model guidance rather than a fast-weight memory, and consolidation is endpoint BC on success-filtered executed trajectories. That is exactly the setting where the proposal's selection-bias argument (Sec. 12: filtering corrupts the noise law) should bite. ReGuide-FT is therefore the natural endpoint-distillation-with-replay baseline against the proposal's path distillation and fresh-noise re-pairing.

papers.title: FlowCorrect: Efficient Interactive Correction of Generative Flow Policies for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors_year: Welte, Shi, Wolf, Gilles, Rayyes, 2026 (arXiv 2602.22056)
papers.what_it_does: Deployment-time adaptation of a flow-matching policy (ManiFlow) from sparse human VR 'nudges'. It uses a small (~10k-parameter) LoRA on the DiT head that adds a velocity residual: 'f_{theta+Delta theta}(x_n,k_n,c) = f_theta(x_n,k_n,c) + alpha_t v_{Delta theta}(x_n,k_n,c)'. The residual is trained with a flow-edit loss that 'directly edits the continuous-time flow by matching intermediate ODE velocities to a target field that would reach the corrected trajectory', re-using the logged noise. An observation-conditioned gate alpha_t decides where the edit applies; removing it drops in-distribution success from 65.00% to 54.17%. The method reaches 80% success on previously failed cases while preserving previously solved ones.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Bears on (b) and (d). It is a gradient-written residual on the velocity field that is exactly zero at Delta theta = 0, supervised along the actual solver path rather than only at the endpoint, and gated to preserve old behavior. Close in spirit to the proposal's velocity reader plus centered residual, and to its path-distillation objective (Eq. 23). The differences: the writes are batch LoRA optimization from human corrections, not causal per-experience fast-weight writes, and there is no meta-trained writer and no consolidation into theta. It is a strong, simple baseline for 'few-shot residual velocity correction' in Sec. 16-18.

papers.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs
papers.authors_year: Zhao, Yang, Hu, Gao, Ou, Wan, Dong, Ma, Gong, 2026 (arXiv 2605.10094)
papers.what_it_does: In persistent deployment, a frozen pi0/pi0.5 stores 'progress-calibrated successful observation-action segments in a long-term memory'. At inference it retrieves and consistency-filters chunks into an 'elite action prior', then 'injects the elite prior into an intermediate state of the flow-matching action sampler' via x_{t0} = (1 - t0) a_elite + t0 eps. t0 is set by retrieval confidence; the method falls back to the original sampler when retrieval fails. It is 'non-parametric test-time adaptation without requiring parameter updates.' Stated limitations include state aliasing, contamination by false successes, and the lack of 'long-term forgetting' and change detection.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A competing way to let recent experience shape an FM policy's generation, as an initial-state prior rather than a per-step reader. It gives a cheap, well-defined 'explicit memory' baseline for (a): memory at t0 only versus memory at every ODE step. It also shares the persistent-deployment evaluation framing the proposal adopts. Its limitations (no forgetting or refresh, dependence on base success) are what the proposal's reset and consolidation lifecycle targets.

papers.title: Test-Time Training Done Right
papers.authors_year: Zhang, Bi, Hong, Zhang, Luan, Yang, Sunkavalli, Freeman, Tan, 2025 (arXiv 2505.23884)
papers.what_it_does: Large Chunk Test-Time Training (LaCT) updates nonlinear fast weights (up to 40% of parameters, optionally with Muon) over chunks of 2K-1M tokens. For autoregressive video diffusion it fine-tunes Wan 2.1 (1.3B/14B) with interleaved clean and noisy chunks: 'it applies fast weights to each chunk sequentially while only updating fast weights on clean chunks. This simple strategy ensures that each denoising operation only accesses previously cleaned frames.'
papers.relation_to_proposal: Precedent for the exact write/read split in (a): fast weights are written from clean causal history and read by noisy tokens at every denoising step inside a diffusion transformer, here in video rather than actions. It also informs the writer design in Sec. 5. LaCT's evidence that large chunks and large nonlinear states matter contrasts with the proposal's 1,072-parameter per-sample-SGD fast net and suggests a chunked or large-state writer ablation. Not a direct robot baseline, but it should be cited when claiming the read-at-every-denoising-step interface.

papers.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
papers.authors_year: Dalal, Koceja, Hussein, Xu, Zhao, Song, Han, Cheung, Kautz, Guestrin, Hashimoto, Koyejo, Choi, Sun, Wang, 2025 (CVPR 2025; arXiv 2504.05298)
papers.what_it_does: Inserts TTT-MLP layers into the pretrained CogVideo-X 5B diffusion transformer after each attention layer, using a learned gate 'gate(TTT, X; alpha) = tanh(alpha) (x) TTT(X) + X' with alpha initialized to 0.1. It adds bi-direction (a reverse-scan TTT) because diffusion models are non-causal. Local attention handles 3-second segments and TTT layers the global sequence. It leads Mamba 2, Gated DeltaNet and sliding-window baselines by 34 Elo on one-minute videos. Stated limitations: artifacts, and TTT-MLP being 1.4x slower at inference than Gated DeltaNet.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The canonical example of TTT layers inside a DiT; the proposal's reader factorial (Sec. 8, 'Internal TTT layer') should cite it. Two contrasts are worth stating in Sec. 6/21. First, here the fast weights are re-derived from the noisy tokens inside every denoising forward pass, not persistent weights written from clean experience. Second, the tanh gate only damps the TTT contribution at initialization (approximately 0.1), whereas the proposal's centering makes the correction exactly zero at W = W0 for all training.

papers.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
papers.authors_year: Masip, Rodriguez, Tuytelaars, van de Ven, 2024 (CoLLAs 2024, PMLR v274; arXiv 2311.14028)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that 'standard generative replay applied to diffusion models results in a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities'. It proposes generative distillation, which 'distils the entire reverse process'. The previous model generates a sample with DDIM, the sample is re-noised to x_t, and the new model matches the teacher's noise prediction: L_distil = E_{t, x_t}||eps_{old}(x_t,t) - eps_{new}(x_t,t)||^2. This is mixed with the current-task loss as L_GD = r L_simple + (1-r) lambda L_distil.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Prior art for the retention regularizer R_old in Eq. 25-26 (velocity or score matching to the old model on old-model-generated states) and for the endpoint-vs-path distinction in Sec. 11-12. The paper's finding that endpoint-style generative replay destroys denoising, while reverse-process distillation retains it, is exactly the comparison the proposal plans. The proposal's W2 bound (Eq. 27-28) remains new, but the regularizer it bounds should be credited, and generative distillation included as the consolidation-retention baseline. This paper is not from robotics.

papers.title: Gated Memory Policy: In-Context Memorization and Adaptation
papers.authors_year: Gao, Liu, Li, Song, 2026 (arXiv 2604.18933; CoRL 2026)
papers.what_it_does: A DiT diffusion policy with a lightweight cross-attention memory over cached history tokens (one pooled image token plus action tokens per past chunk). The memory covers in-trial memory and 'in-context adaptation based on the outcomes of multiple past trials', for example inferring friction from repeated casting attempts. A calibrated binary memory gate selects when to recall. History actions are injected with diffusion noise ('at diffusion step k, the model predicts future actions at noise level k, conditioned on history actions at noise level k-1'). It reports +30.1% over long-history baselines on the new MemMimic benchmark while staying competitive on Markovian RoboMimic tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The strongest activation-memory (non-weight) competitor for (a) and for cross-trial adaptation. Memory is read inside every denoising step through cross-attention, with gating and noise-aware conditioning. It should instantiate the proposal's 'history tokens' baseline at matched compute. Its MemMimic cross-trial tasks resemble the proposal's Stage B/D delayed cue-to-action-distribution associations and could serve as a robot testbed.

papers.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning
papers.authors_year: Bianchi, Yousefi, Sampieri, Roberti, Rigazio, Galasso, Franco, 2026 (arXiv 2606.07217)
papers.what_it_does: WIZARD meta-trains a network mapping task evidence (language plus a short demo video, encoded by the frozen VLA encoder) to expert LoRA updates for frozen pi0.5. It is trained on a meta-dataset of (z, Delta W) pairs with reconstruction, scale-aware and cosine losses. At test time it 'predicts the corresponding adaptation weights in a single forward pass, without target-task action labels or test-time optimization'. It reports up to ~2x gains on unseen LIBERO dataset collections and ~14x on unseen tasks. Limitations: single-task expert generation and dependence on evidence quality.
papers.relation_to_proposal: An alternative to the proposal's meta-trained gradient writer (c, Sec. 5 and 7): an amortized hypernetwork writer that outputs weights directly. The proposal should justify why a gradient write (Eq. 8) or a learned-loss write is preferable to a feedforward weight generator. An 'amortized writer' ablation at equal parameter budget would close this gap. WIZARD writes once per task, with no continual or persistent causal writes and no consolidation.

papers.title: VITA: Zero-Shot Value Functions via Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
papers.authors_year: Ziakas, Russo, 2026 (ICLR 2026; arXiv 2506.10085)
papers.what_it_does: A goal-conditioned value estimator for robot manipulation in which 'a lightweight adaptation module is updated via a gradient step on a meta-learned self-supervised loss'. It is updated sequentially over a trajectory so that it 'encodes history into its parameters', and is meta-trained MAML-style. Ablations compare no-reset implicit memory (VITA) with 'memoryless adaptation (TTT-RS), which resets the adaptation module to theta0 at every step', trajectory-level updates, and explicit-memory windows. VITA wins across datasets.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Robotics precedent for (c): fast weights with a meta-learned inner (self-supervised) loss, the proposal's learned-loss writer [17] option. It feeds a value function, which relates to the value/control reader in Sec. 10. Its reset versus no-reset versus explicit-window ablation matches the protocol comparisons the proposal plans in Sec. 14 and 16. RoboTTT cites it as 'the closest setting' to fast weights in robotics; the proposal's Sec. 21 should too.

papers.title: SmoLSTM: A Compact Vision-Language-Action Model with Recurrent Memory that Persists
papers.authors_year: Habekost, Mastouri Kashani, Gäde, Kerzel, Allgeuer, Weber, Wermter, Lee, 2026 (arXiv 2609.22854)
papers.what_it_does: A frozen SmolVLM feeds a 6-block matrix-memory LSTM (mLSTM, C_t = f_t C_{t-1} + i_t v_t k_t^T, a fast-weight-like associative state) whose state 'is never reset during an episode'. A rectified-flow head integrates 10-step chunks in 8 Euler steps. 'Crucially, only the 4.87M-parameter head runs per ODE step: the mLSTM trunk was already advanced once for this control step and is not re-entered.' Resetting the state at every control step drops full-task success on LIBERO-Mem from 77.5% to 7.0%.
papers.relation_to_proposal: An ideal control for claim (a). It has persistent associative, fast-weight-like memory across decisions, but the memory is read once per decision, and the query does not depend on the candidate z_t at each ODE step. Comparing the proposal's per-step, z_t-dependent query (Eq. 3) against this read-once design at equal memory size isolates whether per-step reading matters. Its reset-interval ablation is also a template for the Sec. 14 reset experiments.

papers.title: ContextFlow: In-Context Flow Matching for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors_year: Ding, Dai, Herzig, Hroub, Mai, Dai, Ghanem, Elhoseiny, 2026 (arXiv 2609.06852)
papers.what_it_does: 'A conditional flow-matching model that learns continuous action distributions for in-context imitation learning.' Demonstrations are compressed by perceiver-style multimodal context compressors into latent tokens that condition the FM action head. On LIBERO unseen configurations it 'outperforms ICRT by 35 percentage points' and matches task-specific fine-tuned pi0 without fine-tuning.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The current strongest 'history as context tokens' alternative specifically for FM policies. The proposal's central contrast is 'history acts through updated weights, not context tokens' (Eq. 1). ContextFlow-style compressed-context conditioning at matched compute and parameter budgets is the fair baseline for that claim in Sec. 16-18.

papers.title: VANE: Reliable Test-Time Training for Vision-Language-Action Models via Future Visual Representation Prediction
papers.authors_year: Ji, Xia, Sun, Feng, Ren, 2026 (arXiv 2608.09448)
papers.what_it_does: Prompt-only TTT for a VLA (QwenPi) using a context-routed Mixture of Latent Prompts and a future-visual-representation proxy loss. 'Candidate updates are isolated from the live policy, evaluated on subsequent observations, and committed only when supported by future evidence, making adaptation selective and reversible.' A shadow copy is updated and then atomically committed or rolled back. It reports +3.2 pp on SimplerEnv WidowX, with gains that are 'task- and embodiment-dependent'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Relevant to the refresh and reset gates in Sec. 14 and to the strict fast-only TTT protocol. VANE's propose-validate-commit/rollback of test-time writes is a concrete, published gating mechanism for adaptive state and should be cited when motivating acceptance gates. The proposal's gates act at consolidation and reset time rather than per write.

papers.title: In-Context Imitation Learning via Next-Token Prediction
papers.authors_year: Fu, Huang, Datta, Chen, Panitch, Liu, Li, Goldberg, 2024 (ICRA 2025; arXiv 2408.15980)
papers.what_it_does: ICRT, 'a causal transformer that performs autoregressive prediction on sensorimotor trajectories', executes new tasks by prompting with teleoperated trajectories of the new task, 'without updating its underlying policy parameters.'
papers.relation_to_proposal: Foundational in-context imitation baseline class: adaptation through activations rather than weights. The proposal's weights-versus-context argument (Eq. 1) should acknowledge it, and ContextFlow reports large gains over it for FM policies. Background for Sec. 21.

papers.title: Instant Policy: In-Context Imitation Learning via Graph Diffusion
papers.authors_year: Vosylius, Johns, 2025 (ICLR 2025; arXiv 2411.12633)
papers.what_it_does: Learns new tasks 'instantly (without further training) from just one or two demonstrations', modeling in-context imitation 'as a graph generation problem with a learned diffusion process' over demonstrations, observations and actions. It is trained on 'pseudo-demonstrations - arbitrary trajectories generated in simulation - as a virtually infinite pool of training data.'
papers.relation_to_proposal: A diffusion policy whose denoising is conditioned on in-context demos. It is an alternative to fast-weight memory for few-shot adaptation, and its pseudo-demonstration meta-training is a scalable data recipe for the proposal's meta-training over episodes (Sec. 7, Stage B/C).

papers.title: RICL: Adding In-Context Adaptability to Pre-Trained Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors_year: Sridhar, Dutta, Jayaraman, Lee, 2025 (arXiv 2508.02062)
papers.what_it_does: Post-hoc fine-tuning recipe that injects in-context learning into pi0-FAST. For a new task, 'RICL then fetches the most relevant portions of those demonstrations into the VLA context', improving performance 'with only 20 demonstrations per task, without any parameter updates.'
papers.relation_to_proposal: A retrieval-into-context baseline for the proposal's 'history tokens/retrieval' comparison (Sec. 16-18), showing that post-hoc ICL can be added to a pretrained VLA. It uses discrete-token pi0-FAST, not an FM head.

papers.title: MemoryVLA: Perceptual-Cognitive Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors_year: Shi, Xie, Liu, Sun, Liu, Wang, Zhou, Fan, Zhang, Huang, 2025 (arXiv 2508.19236)
papers.what_it_does: A hippocampus-inspired VLA. A Perceptual-Cognitive Memory Bank stores low-level and semantic tokens; working memory retrieves and fuses entries 'and updates the bank by merging redundancies', and 'a memory-conditioned diffusion action expert yields temporally aware action sequences.' It reports gains over CogACT and pi0 on SimplerEnv, LIBERO, MIKASA-Robo and 12 real tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Prior memory-augmented diffusion-action VLA that also uses hippocampal and consolidation language. The proposal's Sec. 21 note that 'the lifecycle is not new merely because it uses the words short and long memory' should cite it explicitly. It is activation-bank memory, with no weight writes and no consolidation into the policy.

papers.title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
papers.authors_year: Liu, Kim, Liu, Liu, Zhu, 2026 (arXiv 2603.03818)
papers.what_it_does: Finds that 'pretrained VLAs are remarkably resistant to forgetting compared with smaller policy models trained from scratch. Simple Experience Replay (ER) works surprisingly well on VLAs, sometimes achieving zero forgetting even with a small replay data size', and that seemingly forgotten skills recover rapidly with fine-tuning.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Raises the bar for the retention target in Sec. 13 and 16-18 (old-task loss <= 2 pp): with a pretrained backbone, plain ER may already meet it. The proposal's analytic check found replay essential (0.470 vs ~1e-12), but it must show that FM-specific retention (Eq. 25-26) and path distillation beat a well-tuned ER-only continual baseline on a pretrained FM VLA, not just on small from-scratch models.

papers.title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: Jayasinghe, Gontero, Trivedi, 2026 (arXiv 2606.17493)
papers.what_it_does: A wake-sleep framework: each skill is learned during wake, and the shared policy is consolidated offline during sleep from 'compact frozen skill memories'. For imitation these are frozen actor snapshots with observation buffers and 'frozen-actor distillation L = E_{o~B_i}||pi_theta(o) - pi_theta_i^wake(o)||^2'. Per-skill gradients are Nash-bargained, with adaptive anchoring to the previous consolidated checkpoint. It identifies 'skill-coupling collapse', using deterministic ACT and RL actors on Meta-World and SurgicAI.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A structural precedent for the fast-to-slow consolidation cycle in Sec. 11-14: offline sleep-phase distillation from frozen snapshots on stored observations, plus anchoring to the previous consolidated checkpoint, compares with the proposal's R_old and reset gates. The proposal differs by being FM-specific (endpoint vs path velocity distillation, noise re-pairing), and those differences should be stated.

papers.title: EVOLVE-VLA: Test-Time Training from Environment Feedback for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors_year: Bai, Gao, Shou, 2025 (arXiv 2512.14666)
papers.what_it_does: A 'test-time training framework enabling VLAs to continuously adapt through environment interaction'. A learned progress estimator provides dense reward, smoothed by accumulative progress estimation and progressive horizon extension, and a token-based VLA is optimized online with GRPO. Reported: +8.6% on long-horizon tasks, +22.0% in 1-shot learning, 20.8% on unseen tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Represents the 'TTT for VLA means online RL on slow weights' line (along with TT-VLA 2601.06748), which RoboTTT notes does not use fast weights. It gives the proposal's 'continual adaptation with consolidation' protocol a slow-weight online-RL comparison point. The name collision with TTT should be handled explicitly in Sec. 21.

papers.title: RoboMME: Benchmarking and Understanding Memory for Robotic Generalist Policies
papers.authors_year: Dai, Fu, Lee, Liu, Zhang, Yang, Finn, Fazeli, Chai, 2026 (arXiv 2603.04639)
papers.what_it_does: A 16-task standardized benchmark covering temporal, spatial, object and procedural memory. It also releases 'a suite of 14 memory-augmented VLA variants built on the pi0.5 backbone', finding that 'the effectiveness of memory representations is highly task-dependent'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A ready-made robot evaluation and baseline pool for Stage E and for the reader factorial (Sec. 8). Its 14 pi0.5 memory variants give fair activation-memory comparators on an FM backbone. The companion benchmark RoboMemArena (2605.10921), used by TraceFlow, is also relevant.

papers.title: SAM2Act: Integrating Visual Foundation Model with A Memory Architecture for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors_year: Fang, Grotz, Pumacay, Wang, Fox, Krishna, Duan, 2025 (arXiv 2501.18564)
papers.what_it_does: SAM2Act+ adds 'a memory bank, an encoder, and an attention mechanism to enhance spatial memory', inspired by SAM2, and introduces MemoryBench for memory-dependent manipulation, reaching 94.3% on it.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Background: an activation-memory-bank design for keyframe policies, and a benchmark (MemoryBench) for spatial and action-recall memory. It does not affect the FM-specific contributions but belongs in a complete memory-for-robots related-work section.

checks.title: Proxy Policy Steering
checks.why: EXISTS: the arXiv abs page lists Ning, Wang, Ma, Fang; v1 8 Sep, v2 9 Sep, v3 13 Sep 2026. Full v3 text read, including App. D. VERIFIED: Eq. 4 'vPPS = vbase + γ[vtask − vref]'; 'a task proxy, initialized from the reference'; the residual 'steers the frozen base sampler at every denoising step' (10 Euler steps, γ=0.4); 'When γ = 0, this exactly recovers the frozen base sampler'. The v3 PDF says 55% and the abs page says 53%. Ablations are on the simulation tasks (Fig. 4b): w/o ref 64→55, w/o vel 64→50, w/o tune 64→48. pi0 goes 5%→55%. HIGH IS JUSTIFIED for the reader: base + (adapted copy − its own initialization) at every solver step, exactly zero before adaptation, is the proposal's Eq. 4-5 with R∘f_W swapped for a 32M proxy. CORRECTIONS: (1) The proposal's stated reason for centering is exact reset ('This centering makes r = 0 exactly ... Resetting the fast weights then recovers the current base sampler'). It never makes PPS's shared-approximation-error argument, so that argument is PPS's and should be credited and adopted, not called 'the same logic'. (2) The 'final-action residual is weaker' evidence is weak. PPS's Residual baseline is a separate from-scratch policy that takes the base action as input, and the paper hedges: it underperforms 'likely because the residual is applied only after the base has sampled a clean action'. (3) 'w/o vel' fits the reference proxy to the base velocity field, which the subtraction needs by construction. It does not test the proposal's endpoint-vs-path consolidation (Eq. 21-23). PPS's Eq. 5 (velocity matching on the base's own sampler trajectory) is really a precedent for R_old (Eq. 25). (4) App. D is exact only under A3, which the authors call 'a modeling choice ... in general not the family of noise-level marginals of the clean target'. PPS has no memory, no causal or online writes, no meta-learned writer and no consolidation; it is single-task with 50 demos and 20k offline steps per proxy. The lifecycle claim survives; the reader and centering should be presented as building on PPS. Good baseline: PPS-style proxy fine-tuning on the same experiences.
checks.corrected_description: Offline, single-task, inference-time adaptation of a frozen flow-matching VLA (pi0.5/pi0). Two 32M proxies: v_ref is distilled from the base by velocity matching on the base's own denoising trajectories (Eq. 5). v_task is initialized from v_ref and FM-fine-tuned on 50 demos. At all 10 Euler steps the sampler uses v_base + γ(v_task − v_ref), γ=0.4; the residual is exactly zero before fine-tuning and γ=0 recovers the base. The paper derives this as a product-of-experts correction per noise level, under an explicitly non-exact modeling assumption (A3). +55% absolute over pi0.5 on 12 tasks (v3 PDF; abs page says 53%). No memory, no online or causal writes, no consolidation.

checks.title: DexWorldModel: Causal Latent World Modeling towards Automated Learning of Embodied Tasks
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2604.16484 v1, 13 Apr 2026, Deng/Liu/Jia (DexForce AI). Full text read. VERIFIED: the Long-Term TTT Memory 'is updated exclusively when new ground-truth observations and executed actions are received'. W_work is forked, and 'the working weights W_work remain strictly frozen across all intermediate flow steps s∈(0,1]'. W_work gets one update from the predicted f̂_{t+1} before action decoding. The TTT-MLP has a tanh gate with α initialized to 0.1. DOWNGRADE from high: (1) Internal TTT with persistent fast weights, read by noisy tokens in an FM/diffusion action model, is already in RoboTTT [6], which the proposal cites ('Internal gated TTT in a diffusion transformer; fast weights persist across decisions'). The proposal also concedes internal TTT changes the denoising path (Sec. 6). So DexWM pre-empts nothing the proposal claims; its only additions are the long-term/working fork and the world-action setting. (2) The characterization is imprecise. The action ODE reads W_work', which contains a self-generated predicted frame. Under SAI, 'the speculative context previously driving the ODE solver is seamlessly swapped with the calibrated true memory state' at s_mid, so in deployment the memory is NOT fixed during the ODE. (3) No evidence that the memory helps task success. The only TTT experiment is peak GPU memory versus a KV cache ('perfectly flat, O(1)'); success gains come from DINOv3 targets and EmbodiChain data. (4) The paper is internally inconsistent on flow-time direction: Eq. 4 has x(0)=ε, yet the update happens 'at flow time s = 0' after generation. It does not address adapting to new tasks, has no external/centered reader, and no consolidation or reset. It predates RoboTTT (April vs July 2026), but that is immaterial to the proposal. It is useful for specifying the internal-TTT baseline's lifecycle (fork to protect persistent memory from generated content); it is not itself a reproducible baseline (Wan2.2-5B world model).
checks.corrected_description: A flow-matching world-action model (latent DINOv3 video plus action, MoT backbone from Wan2.2-5B) that replaces the KV cache with gated TTT-MLP layers. A long-term fast-weight memory is written by gradient steps only from real observations and executed actions. A working copy is forked per step, frozen during latent-video integration, then updated once with the predicted frame before action decoding. With speculative asynchronous inference the memory is swapped mid-integration. The paper shows O(1) memory versus a KV cache but has no ablation of the memory's effect on success; its reported gains are driven by the data pipeline. It is a close sibling of RoboTTT, which the proposal already cites.

checks.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2609.20646 v1, 17 Sep 2026 (4 days before the proposal), Zhang/Liu/Zhang/Yang (HKU). Full text read. VERIFIED: 'Bound is the cap: it rescales the success term to a norm of at most c+∥v base∥...'. 'Retrieval is done once per query; the scores are recomputed at every active step.' λ(t) falls linearly to zero at t_cut (0.30 in the reference config), so guidance acts only on the early steps, not on every ODE step. Real robot T2: 21/50→39/50→47/50. Uncapped 24.25 vs capped 57.75 TSR (base 56.75). DOWNGRADE from high: the method is explicitly weight-free: 'TraceFlow changes no weight; its rounds change only the TraceBank contents, so Sec. IV measures nonparametric accumulation, not parameter learning or resistance to forgetting.' It does not touch fast weights, a meta-learned writer or consolidation. Its evidence is weaker than the agent implies. Simulation headline cells are 'per-suite selected configurations evaluated in one pass'. Under one shared configuration the 26-task aggregate is unchanged (34.92→34.99 TSR). The LIBERO changes are 'within noise'. Stacking histories are single runs, and the only baseline is the unguided checkpoint. It remains a relevant concurrent nonparametric alternative and a good retrieval-guidance baseline (kernel-density attraction/repulsion with a norm cap), and the cap is relevant to bounding r_{φ,W}. The App. B.4 link is a stretch. TraceFlow's Counting/Occlusion deficit comes from cross-episode retrieval keys lacking within-episode event information ('not designed to reconstruct missing upstream event information'). B.4 is about distilling hidden facts into a memory-free student.
checks.corrected_description: Concurrent nonparametric test-time guidance for a frozen FM VLA (pi0.5, PrediMem). A growing TraceBank holds the robot's own rollouts, each with one terminal success/failure bit. A frozen contrastive retrieval head plus a progress tracker select success and failure action windows. Their Gaussian-KDE scores add a norm-capped attraction/repulsion to the base velocity during the early Euler steps only; no weights change across rounds. Strong real-robot ordering gains (T2: 21→39→47/50) but selective, single-pass simulation gains (26-task aggregate unchanged; Counting/Occlusion below base); stacking peaks within 10 rounds.

checks.title: ReGuide: From Test-Time Guidance to Self-Improving Diffusion Policies
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2606.28939 v1, 27 Jun 2026, Lin/Shakkottai/Kalathil/Kumar (Texas A&M). Full text read. VERIFIED: a DDPM diffusion policy (not FM) on Robomimic Can/Square/Transport/Tool Hang with 10-80 demos. PCG applies dynamics-model (DINO-WM) gradients through the estimated clean action, only when k ≤ K_g and the phase distance lies between two percentile thresholds. ReGuide-FT 'fine-tunes the current checkpoint on a rehearsal buffer containing both prior training data and newly collected guided rollouts'; ReGuide-FS retrains from scratch. Gains are 1.3-7.7x, simulation only. DOWNGRADE from high: this is the general shape of the proposal's fast→slow loop (a test-time-modified sampler, then filtered executed data, then a slow update with rehearsal, iterated). But it is single-task self-improvement; the authors call it 'closer in spirit to self-training ... than to classical continual learning'. There is no memory, no multi-task retention measurement and no reset, and the proposal already cites Progress & Compress for distillation into slow weights. INCORRECT RELATION CLAIM: ReGuide stores (O_t, A_t^g) and retrains with the standard diffusion loss, which draws fresh noise. That is exactly the proposal's clean option 2 ('Select successful endpoints, but pair them with new independent Gaussian noise and use endpoint FM distillation'), so the Sec. 12 noise-law corruption, which comes from training on filtered teacher paths/noise, does not arise. ReGuide-FT is therefore an instance of fresh-noise endpoint distillation with rehearsal, not a baseline 'against' fresh-noise re-pairing. It does exhibit the success-conditioned narrowing the proposal says to report. It is a reasonable Stage C/D consolidation baseline.
checks.corrected_description: Single-task self-improvement for DDPM diffusion policies (Robomimic, simulation). Phase-conditioned, gated dynamics-model guidance applied through the estimated clean action generates recovery rollouts. Successful guided rollouts are merged into the dataset, and the policy is fine-tuned with a rehearsal mixture (FT) or retrained (FS), iteratively. Standard diffusion BC with fresh noise on success-filtered executed actions: 1.3-7.7x base success. No memory, no multi-task continual retention, no reset.

checks.title: FlowCorrect: Efficient Interactive Correction of Generative Flow Policies for Robotic Manipulation
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2602.22056 v3, 28 Aug 2026, Welte/Shi/Wolf/Gilles/Rayyes; the abs comment says 'Accepted at IROS 2026'. Full text read. VERIFIED: base is ManiFlow (consistency FM). A LoRA (~10k params) on the DiT head gives f_θ + α_t v_Δθ. The loss 'directly edits the continuous-time flow by matching intermediate ODE velocities to a target field that would reach the corrected trajectory', and 'we re-use the logged noise x0'. Removing the gate drops ID-30 success from 65.00 to 54.17. 80% success on previously failed cases. DOWNGRADE from high: (1) The target v*_{n,t} = (a_corr ⊖ x_{n,t})/((N−n)Δk) is a straight line to the corrected endpoint from the student's own current state, under the same logged seed. It is an endpoint objective evaluated along the solver path, not the proposal's path distillation of a teacher's intermediate evolution (Eq. 23). Reusing logged noise that was failure-selected is the practice the proposal warns against ('do not reuse a teacher noise sample that has been biased by success selection'). (2) Writes are batch LoRA optimization (500 epochs, ~30 min on a 4090) from human VR corrections. There is no causal per-experience write, no meta-trained writer and no consolidation into θ. (3) The evidence is small: 8 demos per task, 4 tasks, 10 trials per condition, and one ID-hard case at 3/10 because of conflicting nearby edits. The zero-at-Δθ=0 reset property holds by LoRA construction but is not a centered reader. It is a good 'batch-optimized velocity residual on the same experiences' baseline for the strict fast-only protocol, but it does not pre-empt the proposal.
checks.corrected_description: Deployment-time correction of a flow-matching policy (ManiFlow) from sparse human VR relative-pose nudges. A ~10k-param LoRA on the DiT head adds a velocity residual. It is trained by batch optimization with a flow-edit loss: along the ODE path under the logged noise, velocities are matched to straight-line targets toward the corrected action, plus anchor rollouts. A separately trained observation-level gate decides when the edit applies. Four real-robot tasks: hard-case success 3%→86% (ID-hard average), ID-30 49.8→65.0%. No meta-learning, no online per-experience writes, no consolidation.

checks.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2605.10094 v2, 12 May 2026, 9 authors as listed (Xi'an Jiaotong/One Robotics). Main text and limitations read. VERIFIED: a VLAC-critic progress estimator selects successful prefixes. Retrieval uses cosine similarity plus DTW consistency filtering, giving an elite prior a_elite. The sampler starts at 'x_{t0} = (1 − t0) a_elite + t0 ε', with t0 set by retrieval confidence. 'the method falls back to the original sampling process'. It is 'non-parametric test-time adaptation without requiring parameter updates'. Limitations include state aliasing, false-success contamination, and 'long-term forgetting, task-aware indexing, and mechanisms for detecting environment changes'. DOWNGRADE from medium: gains are modest (pi0.5 LIBERO-10 81.6→83.8, +2.2; CogACT SimplerEnv +2.5 to +3.6). Memory enters only through the initial state (SDEdit-like), so there is no overlap with fast weights, per-step reading, meta-learned writing or consolidation. Its limitations concern managing a nonparametric store, which is related to but not the same as the proposal's post-consolidation fast-weight reset. It is still a cheap, well-defined 'memory only via the initial state' baseline for Stage E, and the persistent-deployment framing is apt.
checks.corrected_description: Nonparametric test-time adaptation for frozen FM/diffusion VLAs in persistent deployment. The robot stores critic-verified successful observation-action prefixes, retrieves and DTW-filters chunks into a weighted elite prior, and starts the flow sampler from an intermediate state interpolating that prior with noise. Retrieval confidence sets the start time. Small gains on LIBERO-10 and SimplerEnv plus real bimanual tasks; no parameter updates.

checks.title: Test-Time Training Done Right
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2505.23884 v1, 29 May 2025; the 9 authors match (MIT/Adobe). The AR video diffusion sections and the relevant method were read. VERIFIED: 'it applies fast weights to each chunk sequentially while only updating fast weights on clean chunks. This simple strategy ensures that each denoising operation only accesses previously cleaned frames.' Wan 2.1 (1.3B/14B) is fine-tuned into an AR video model with LaCT plus sliding-window attention. Chunks span 2K-1M tokens, with a fast-weight ratio up to 40% of parameters and Muon. DOWNGRADE from medium: this is an internal TTT layer inside a video DiT. The proposal already concedes that internal TTT affects denoising and cites TTT layers [3] and RoboTTT [6], which realize the same clean-write/noisy-read pattern for robot actions. The video evaluation is validation denoising loss only (against SWA, Mamba2+SWA and full attention), with no adaptation or robot task. Its value is for the writer design: large chunks, large nonlinear state and Muon versus the proposal's 1,072-parameter per-experience SGD net is a sensible ablation. Cite it; it is not a baseline.
checks.corrected_description: Large-chunk TTT (LaCT): nonlinear SwiGLU fast weights (up to 40% of params) updated per chunk of 2K-1M tokens, optionally with Muon, combined with window attention. Applied to novel view synthesis, language modeling, and AR video diffusion (Wan 2.1 1.3B/14B). In the video case, fast weights are updated only on clean chunks and applied to interleaved noisy chunks. Evaluated by validation loss versus SWA, Mamba2+SWA and full attention.

checks.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2504.05298 v1, 7 Apr 2025, CVPR 2025; all 15 authors match. Method and limitations read. VERIFIED: 'gate(TTT, X; α) = tanh(α) ⊗ TTT(X) + X', with 'We initialize all values in α to 0.1'. Bi-direction is used because diffusion models 'are non-causal'. Attention is local per 3-second segment and TTT is global. +34 Elo over the second-best method. Artifacts; TTT-MLP inference and training are '1.4× and 2.1× slower than with Gated DeltaNet'. Gated DeltaNet wins on 18-second videos. The agent's two contrasts are accurate: fast weights are re-derived from noisy tokens in every forward pass, and the tanh gate only damps at initialization whereas the proposal's correction is exactly zero at W=W0. DOWNGRADE to background: this is within-sequence TTT for video generation, with no persistence across decisions, no adaptation from experience, and no robot. The proposal already cites TTT layers [3] and RoboTTT, which uses the same tanh-gate idea (α initialized to 0.001). Citation only.
checks.corrected_description: Adds gated, bidirectional TTT-MLP layers after each attention layer of the pretrained CogVideo-X 5B diffusion transformer (α initialized to 0.1). Attention is local over 3-second segments and TTT is global over the whole one-minute sequence. Fine-tuned on Tom & Jerry; +34 Elo over Mamba 2 / Gated DeltaNet / sliding-window baselines on 63-second videos. Slower than Gated DeltaNet, and still has artifacts.

checks.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
checks.why: EXISTS: the PMLR page masip25a matches the title and authors (Masip, Rodriguez, Tuytelaars, van de Ven), conference 'Conference on Lifelong Learning Agents', publication date 2025-02-17 (CoLLAs 2024 proceedings). arXiv 2311.14028 v2 matches. Method and experiments read. VERIFIED: 'standard generative replay applied to diffusion models results in a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities'. L_distil = E||ε_old(x_t,t) − ε_new(x_t,t)||² on re-noised teacher DDIM samples, and L_GD = r L_simple + (1−r)λ L_distil. CORRECTIONS: (1) Its distillation states are forward-noised teacher samples at random t (interpolant marginals), not the old model's ODE trajectory X_t as in Eq. 25. The proposal's W2 bound (same-noise coupling plus Gronwall) needs trajectory states, so Masip is prior art for the functional-regularizer family and for crediting R_old, not for the exact Eq. 25. (2) Masip's 'generative replay' arm is the proposal's own option 'Replay can instead use old teacher endpoints with fresh FM noise'. Its failure was shown with 2 DDIM teacher steps (Fashion-MNIST) and 10 (CIFAR-10), and more teacher steps 'alleviated ... to some extent'. That is a concrete warning for the proposal's retention replay, but it is not the proposal's planned endpoint-vs-path transfer comparison. Eq. 23 regresses on teacher path velocities for an adapted teacher, not on teacher-function matching, so 'exactly the comparison the proposal plans' is overstated. The setting is unconditional image DDPM with 5-task class splits, not robotics or FM. Medium is fair: the proposal should cite it in Sec. 13/21 and include it as a retention baseline.
checks.corrected_description: Continual training of an unconditional DDPM (Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10; 5 sequential two-class tasks). Replaying few-step DDIM teacher samples with fresh noise (generative replay) badly degrades denoising. Generative distillation instead matches the new model's noise prediction to the frozen previous model's at forward-noised teacher samples, mixed with the current-task loss (r L_simple + (1−r) λ L_distil). This greatly improves FID/KLD. It is a function-space retention regularizer on interpolant states, not on ODE trajectories.

checks.title: Gated Memory Policy: In-Context Memorization and Adaptation
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2604.18933 v2, 3 Aug 2026, Gao/Liu/Li/Song (Stanford). The year and authors are correct, but the stated 'CoRL 2026' is NOT supported. The arXiv page has no venue comment, the PDF lists none, and the project page only has a commented-out ''; RoboTTT cites it as an arXiv preprint. Full text read. VERIFIED: a DiT diffusion policy (DDPM-style, not FM) with cached history (one MAP-pooled image token plus h action tokens per past trajectory) read via cross-attention. A binary memory gate is calibrated on validation prediction error. 'at diffusion step k, the model predicts future actions ... at noise level k, conditioned on history actions at noise level k − 1'. +30.1% on MemMimic; cross-trial tasks cover unknown friction or mass (iterative pushing, flinging, casting); competitive on RoboMimic.
