Because the noisy action tokens are queries at every denoising step, it realizes the proposal's 'interaction during generation' through activations, with candidate-dependent reads. It is a strong history-tokens baseline and its cross-trial tasks suit Stages B/D/E. Medium is appropriate. Its limitation is a finite attention window, with no weights and no consolidation.
checks.corrected_description: A DiT diffusion policy (not FM) with a gated cross-attention memory over a sliding cache of past trajectories (one pooled image token plus action tokens each), read at every denoising step. History actions are diffusion-noised one level cleaner than the current step. A binary gate, calibrated offline on validation error, skips memory when unnecessary. +30.1% on the MemMimic in-trial/cross-trial benchmark and +26.6% on MIKASA-Robo. arXiv preprint; venue unverified (not CoRL 2026).

checks.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2606.07217 v1, 5 Jun 2026; the 7 authors match (ItalAI/Verona/Sapienza). Method, results and limitations read. VERIFIED: a meta-network maps a language plus short-video embedding to per-task LoRA for frozen pi0.5. It is trained on (z, ΔW) pairs with MSE, scale-aware and cosine losses, and 'predicts the corresponding adaptation weights in a single forward pass, without target-task action labels or test-time optimization'; results are 'up to ∼2× ... up to ∼14×'. The stated limitations are evidence quality and single-task expert generation. DOWNGRADE from medium: absolute success is low. LIBERO-Spatial is 0.40 vs 0.19 for MT-VLA, Goal 0.22 vs 0.14, Object 0.03 vs 0.01, and LIBERO-10 full-task 0.00, so the '~14×' rests on tiny bases. It writes once per task, with no continual or persistent writes, no denoising-specific reader and no consolidation, and it needs a library of expert LoRAs. Amortized weight generators are a long-standing alternative to gradient writers (fast-weight programmers, hypernetworks). The suggested 'amortized writer at equal budget' ablation is reasonable, but WIZARD does not threaten any proposal claim. Not a baseline.
checks.corrected_description: Weight-space meta-learning: a meta-network trained on pairs of (task embedding from instruction plus demo video, expert LoRA update) generates a task-specific LoRA for frozen pi0.5 in one forward pass, with no action labels or test-time optimization. Held-out LIBERO suites show gains over multi-task fine-tuning from low bases (e.g., Spatial 0.40 vs 0.19); LIBERO-10 full-task stays at 0. Real Franka tasks improve over a real-domain adapted baseline. Single-task, one-shot generation.

checks.title: VITA: Zero-Shot Value Functions via Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2506.10085 (v1 Jun 2025, v5 27 Feb 2026), Ziakas/Russo; the comment reads 'International Conference on Learning Representations, 2026'. Method and ablations read. VERIFIED: 'a lightweight adaptation module is updated via a gradient step on a meta-learned self-supervised loss'; 'VITA encodes history into its parameters'; MAML-style differentiation through the updates. The ablations compare TTT-TR, TTT-RS ('resets the adaptation module to θ0 at every step') and TTT-EX, and VITA wins. RoboTTT does say 'The closest setting to ours is Ziakas and Russo (83)'. CORRECTIONS: (1) VITA's inner loss is the standard TTT key/value reconstruction ||f_adapt(P_K z_t; θ) − P_V z_t||² with meta-learned projections. That matches the proposal's primary association writer (Eq. 7-8: cue view → content, meta-trained through downstream performance), NOT the learned scalar-loss writer [17]. (2) Its 'value' is a physical-time task-progress estimate V(z_t; g) regressed on progress labels, not the generative-time cost-to-go V_W(t,z,c) of Sec. 10, so the link to the value/control reader is loose. It is not a policy and does not touch denoising; the proposal already cites TTT layers [3] and RoboTTT [6]. DOWNGRADE to low. It is still worth citing as robotics precedent for never-reset, gradient-written, meta-learned fast weights, and as a reset/no-reset/explicit-window ablation template.
checks.corrected_description: A zero-shot goal-conditioned value (task-progress) estimator for manipulation videos. Frozen CLIP features pass through a small adaptation MLP whose weights take one gradient step per timestep on a TTT-style key/value reconstruction loss with meta-learned projections; the weights are never reset within a trajectory. MAML-style training through the updates. Beats reset, trajectory-level and explicit-window TTT variants; used for reward shaping in offline RL. Not a policy; no denoising.

checks.title: SmoLSTM: A Compact Vision-Language-Action Model with Recurrent Memory that Persists
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2609.22854 v1, 19 Sep 2026; the 8 authors match (Hamburg, Wermter group); comment 'Submitted to ICRA 2027'. Method and ablations read. VERIFIED: 'C_t = f_t C_{t−1} + i_t v_t k_t^T'; the state 'is never reset during an episode'; 8 Euler steps. 'Crucially, only the 4.87 M-parameter head runs per ODE step: the mLSTM trunk was already advanced once for this control step and is not re-entered.' Resetting every control step drops full-task success from 77.5% to 7.0%. The memory is a gated outer-product recurrent state, not gradient-written, and the FM head's conditioning comes from learned action-query positions, not from the noisy candidate. So it is a clean published 'read once per decision' control. The proposal already plans this control ('A reader evaluated only at t=0 ... distinct baselines'; Sec. 18 context-only vs candidate-aware readers), so it is a baseline instance, not a threat. DOWNGRADE to low. CAVEATS: the authors warn the reset ablation 'does not establish how a separately trained memoryless policy would perform'. It also resets within-episode context, so it fits the Sec. 16 reset/shuffled-memory controls better than the Sec. 14 post-consolidation refresh.
checks.corrected_description: A compact VLA. A frozen SmolVLM-256M plus modality encoders feed a 6-block mLSTM whose matrix memory persists across the whole episode. A rectified-flow head (4.87M params) integrates 10-step chunks in 8 Euler steps from the per-decision hidden states, without re-entering the recurrent trunk. 77.5% full-task success on LIBERO-Mem; per-step state reset drops it to 7.0%.

checks.title: ContextFlow: In-Context Flow Matching for Robot Manipulation
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2609.06852 v1, 6 Sep 2026; the 8 authors match (KAUST et al.); comment 'Accepted by ECCV 2026'. Main text read. VERIFIED: it is 'a conditional flow-matching model that learns continuous action distributions' for in-context imitation. Perceiver-style image/state/action compressors (32 learnable queries each) produce latent context tokens, with initialization from pi0. It 'outperforms ICRT by 35 percentage points' (73.5 vs 38.5) and matches 1-demo fine-tuned pi0 (73.5 vs 72.5). QUALIFICATION: the evidence covers only 4 unseen task configurations (2 LIBERO-Spatial, 2 LIBERO-Object), with one context demo each. RELEVANCE: in-context use of one demo matching parametric fine-tuning on that demo directly challenges the premise that history should act through updated weights (Eq. 1), although the proposal disclaims any universal separation. It is the right 'history as compressed context tokens' baseline for FM policies at matched compute. It has no continual learning, persistence across tasks or consolidation. Medium is fair.
checks.corrected_description: An in-context imitation FM policy initialized from pi0. Demonstration images, states and actions are compressed by perceiver-style resamplers into latent context tokens that condition the flow-matching action expert, with no test-time fine-tuning. On 4 unseen LIBERO configurations it reaches 73.5% vs ICRT 38.5% and vs 72.5% for pi0 fine-tuned on one demo; it also generalizes on real robots.

checks.title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2603.03818 v2, 17 Mar 2026, Liu/Kim/Liu/Liu/Zhu (UT Austin et al.). Main text read. VERIFIED quote: 'pretrained VLAs are remarkably resistant to forgetting compared with smaller policy models trained from scratch. Simple Experience Replay (ER) works surprisingly well on VLAs, sometimes achieving zero forgetting even with a small replay data size'. It also finds fast recovery of forgotten skills via fine-tuning. The VLAs tested are Pi0 and GR00T N1.5, both flow-matching action heads, which makes the paper directly relevant. QUALIFICATION of 'plain ER may already meet the 2 pp target': near-zero forgetting holds at the default 1000-sample (20%) replay buffer (Pi0 average NBT −0.016±0.022; GR00T 0.027±0.021). At 2% replay, 'Pi0 and GR00T still have low NBT around 0.1–0.2', which is 10-20 pp, far above 2 pp. EWC does poorly (Pi0 NBT 0.608). So the proposal must beat well-tuned ER under matched, small replay budgets on a pretrained FM VLA. This raises the evaluation bar for Sec. 13/17 rather than pre-empting novelty; medium is fair and ER-only should be a baseline.
checks.corrected_description: Empirical study on LIBERO suites (10 sequential tasks each). Pretrained flow-matching VLAs (Pi0, GR00T N1.5) forget far less than from-scratch BC models under experience replay: about zero forgetting at a 20% replay buffer and about 0.1-0.2 NBT at 2%, versus 0.4-0.5 for small models. EWC forgets heavily. Forgotten skills recover quickly with brief fine-tuning.

checks.title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
checks.why: EXISTS: arXiv 2606.17493 v1, 16 Jun 2026, Jayasinghe/Gontero/Trivedi (UIC). Main text read. VERIFIED: wake-sleep with 'compact frozen skill memories: frozen critics with unordered state buffers for reinforcement learning and frozen actor snapshots with unordered observation buffers for imitation learning'. Frozen-actor distillation is L = E_{o∼B_i}||π_θ(o) − π_{θ_i}^wake(o)||². Gradients are combined by Nash bargaining, with adaptive anchoring λ||θ − θ_{k−1}||² toward the previous consolidated checkpoint. The actors are SAC (Meta-World MT5) and ACT (SurgicAI); the paper defines skill-coupling collapse. DOWNGRADE to low: 'wake' trains the shared policy itself on the new skill; there is no separate fast memory. So this is standard continual-learning distillation from frozen snapshots (the LwF / Progress & Compress lineage; it benchmarks against P&C and Reset & Distill), which the proposal already covers via [16]. Anchoring is parameter-space L2, not the function-space R_old, and there is no reset gate. Its deterministic actors have no FM, endpoint or path aspect. It is an optional citation; its pairwise-reliability metric could complement per-task retention.
checks.corrected_description: Continual robot skill learning with one shared policy. Each skill is learned directly into the policy (wake) and then frozen as a snapshot memory (a critic plus state buffer for RL, or an actor plus observation buffer for imitation). Offline sleep consolidates the shared policy by Nash-bargained, gradient-combined distillation from all snapshots, with adaptive L2 anchoring to the previous consolidated checkpoint. Deterministic SAC/ACT actors on Meta-World MT5 and SurgicAI; introduces the skill-coupling collapse and pairwise reliability metrics.

papers.title: SlowFast-VGen: Slow-Fast Learning for Action-Driven Long Video Generation
papers.authors_year: Hong, Liu, Wu, et al., 2024 (arXiv 2410.23277; ICLR 2025)
papers.what_it_does: This is a masked conditional video diffusion model (the slow weights Phi) plus a TEMP-LoRA (the fast weights Theta). At inference the TEMP-LoRA is updated by gradient steps of the denoising loss on each chunk's own input and output: "Theta_{i+1} <- Theta_i - alpha grad Loss", "efficiently storing episodic memory in its parameters". It is re-initialised per episode ("Initialize TEMP-LORA parameters for this episode Theta^e_0"). A "slow-fast learning loop" then trains Phi while each episode's fast LoRA is held fixed ("Fix Theta_i and update Phi only"). The training data include OpenX-Embodiment, Metaworld and RLBench videos, and the paper reports long-horizon planning results.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the closest precedent I found for contributions (a) and (c) inside a diffusion generator. It has persistent fast weights, written by gradient descent on the model's own experience, that act at every denoising step through the network. It resets them per episode and uses an outer slow loop that trains the slow weights around them. It differs from the proposal in four ways. The fast weights are an internal LoRA, not an external centered velocity reader. The write loss is the denoising loss itself, not an associative cue/content loss. The outer loop is first-order. There is no fast-to-slow distillation, and it targets video generation rather than an action policy. The proposal's Sec. 21 claim that the distinction from internal TTT is "intervention location + lifecycle" should cite this. A TEMP-LoRA-on-action-expert variant (LoRA written by the FM loss on recent chunks) is a natural extra internal-write baseline.

papers.title: Online Reward-Weighted Fine-Tuning of Flow Matching with Wasserstein Regularization
papers.authors_year: Fan, Shen, Cheng, et al., 2025 (ICLR 2025; arXiv 2502.06061)
papers.what_it_does: Fine-tunes flow-matching models with online reward-weighted CFM. To prevent collapse it adds a velocity-difference regulariser to the reference model, "alpha * ||v_ft(x,t) - v_ref(x,t)||^2". Its Theorem 3 ("W2 Bound for Flow Matching") proves W2^2(p1^{theta1}, p1^{theta2}) <= e^{2L} int_0^1 E_{x~p_s^{theta1}} ||v^{theta1}(s,x) - v^{theta2}(s,x)||^2 ds. It assumes v^{theta2} is L-Lipschitz and a shared initial noise ("Assumption 2 ... x0 ~ p(x0) are shared"). The proof integrates the discrepancy along one model's flow map, then applies Gronwall and Jensen.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This directly pre-empts contribution (e), Sec. 13, eqs. (25)-(28). It has the same velocity-matching retention penalty against an old/reference model, the same same-noise coupling and the same Gronwall-plus-Cauchy-Schwarz/Jensen route, with the expectation taken along one model's ODE trajectories. The proposal's constant C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L) is sharper than e^{2L}, and it uses the bound as a retention certificate in continual learning rather than as a diversity regulariser. The proposal should cite this and present (27)-(28) as a refinement, not a new result. The ORW-style penalty (velocity MSE on data or current samples) is a natural ablation against R_old on old-policy ODE trajectories.

papers.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
papers.authors_year: Masip, Rodriguez, Tuytelaars, van de Ven, 2023/2024 (CoLLAs 2024; arXiv 2311.14028)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that standard generative replay for diffusion models transfers knowledge "only at the endpoint of the reverse process" and causes "a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities". It proposes generative distillation. The previous-task teacher generates a DDIM sample, noise is added, and the student matches the teacher's noise prediction, L_distil = E||eps_teacher(x_t,t) - eps_student(x_t,t)||^2, so knowledge is transferred "at each point of the reverse trajectory". On FID it is 9.01x better than generative replay on Fashion-MNIST and 2.28x better on CIFAR-10.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This bears on contribution (d) (endpoint vs. path FM distillation, Secs. 11-12) and on the replay retention term (25)-(26). It already shows empirically that matching the old model's field along its own generated samples beats endpoint-only replay. That is exactly the proposal's endpoint-vs-path falsifiable test, and its R_old is a flow-matching version of L_distil. The differences: Masip et al. noise teacher endpoints with the forward process rather than using the teacher's ODE path, work with images, and do not address the selection-bias/noise-law issue. It is required prior art and a baseline for the consolidation step.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Plasticity Injection
papers.authors_year: Nikishin, Oh, Ostrovski, Lyle, Pascanu, Dabney, Barreto, 2023 (NeurIPS 2023; arXiv 2305.15555)
papers.what_it_does: It freezes a network head and adds a fresh trainable copy minus a frozen copy of the same random initialisation: predictions = h_theta(x) + h_{theta1'}(x) - h_{theta2'}(x). Because "initially theta1' = theta2', immediately after plasticity injection the predictions of the neural network remain unaltered". The design goal is stated as "Unaffected predictions ... Preserving the trainable parameter count". Injection can be repeated to restore plasticity.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This directly pre-empts the "centered" residual of contribution (b), eq. (4): r = R(m_{W_k}) - R(m_{W_0}), which is exactly zero at W = W_0. That is the same twin-network-minus-frozen-copy construction, applied to a fast-memory reader rather than an RL head. The proposal's reset (W -> W_0) is analogous to re-injection. The centering trick should therefore be credited, and the novelty claim confined to its use on a velocity field with gradient-written fast weights and a reset gate.

papers.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
papers.authors_year: Zhang, Liu, Zhang, et al., Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.20646)
papers.what_it_does: It adds an external experience path to a frozen FM action expert (pi0.5, PrediMem). Retrieved successful and failed action windows define kernel densities, and their scores become a signed velocity correction applied during Euler integration. The correction is capped relative to the base velocity ("rescales the success term to a norm of at most c+ ||v_base||"), and its strength "declines to zero before the final solver steps". A TraceBank grows with the robot's own rollouts across rounds without weight updates. The cap is shown to matter: "24.25 versus 57.75 TSR against a 56.75 base".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This competes with contributions (a) and (b). It is an external, experience-dependent correction to the FM velocity at each (early) solver step, with an explicit stabiliser (a cap instead of centering), and it accumulates deployment experience. It is nonparametric (no fast weights, no consolidation), so it is the strongest current form of the proposal's "history tokens/retrieval" baseline. The proposal should compare its direct residual velocity reader against a capped retrieval-guidance reader under equal memory and compute. TraceFlow's finding that stacking gains peak within about ten rounds is relevant to the proposal's renewed-plasticity claims.

papers.title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
papers.authors_year: Liu, Kim, Liu, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2603.03818)
papers.what_it_does: This is an empirical study on LIBERO with the flow-matching VLAs pi0 and GR00T N1.5 against BC-Diffusion Policy, BC-Transformer and BC-ViT. It finds that "Simple Experience Replay (ER) works surprisingly well on VLAs, sometimes achieving zero forgetting even with a small replay data size (e.g., 2% of training data)". It also finds that seemingly forgotten skills are recovered by a few finetuning steps. In its Table 1, GR00T averages SR 0.919 and NBT 0.027, while BC-DP averages NBT 0.127.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This bears on the significance of Secs. 11-14 and on stages D and E. On a pretrained FM backbone, plain ER with a small buffer is already near-zero-forgetting, so the proposal's retention machinery (R_old, reset gates) must beat small-buffer ER on the same backbone. The "old-task loss <= 2 pp" target is already met by ER in this regime. The rapid-recovery finding also complicates reset-gate criterion (2).

papers.title: Continual Policy Consolidation for Lifelong Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: He, Li, Yuan, Sun, Chen, Schneider, Chen, 2026 (arXiv 2601.22475)
papers.what_it_does: This is a teacher-student framework that "separates skill acquisition from policy consolidation". RL teachers are trained independently and continually distilled (MSE on mean actions) into a Transformer-MoE student. The student uses DPP-selected prioritized trajectory replay (under 10% of data) plus expandable experts with two-phase parameter freezing. It reports near-zero BWT on CW10/CW20 and 69.4% SR on Continual MT25, with supplementary LIBERO results.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is prior art for the fast-to-slow consolidation lifecycle in contribution (d) in robot policies: separate learners, distillation into one generalist, a compact replay buffer, and protection of old capacity. Its student is a Gaussian MSE policy, not a flow-matching model, and it has no path distillation or memory reset. DPP trajectory selection is a ready-made design for the proposal's finite episodic store B.

papers.title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: Jayasinghe, Gontero, Trivedi, 2026 (arXiv 2606.17493)
papers.what_it_does: This is a wake-sleep framework. Each skill is learned during wake and stored as a "compact frozen memory": a frozen actor snapshot plus unordered observation buffer for imitation learning, or a frozen critic plus state buffer for RL. During sleep the shared policy is consolidated offline by distillation, L = E_{o~B_i}||pi_theta(o) - pi_{theta_i^wake}(o)||^2, with gradients combined by Nash bargaining and adaptive anchoring. It is evaluated with ACT policies on SurgicAI and SAC on Meta-World MT5, and it cites Reset & Distill and Progress & Compress as baselines. Its own limitation: actor memories "can become less informative after substantial policy drift".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is a direct robot-policy precedent for hippocampus-motivated offline consolidation in contribution (d): old-behavior distillation from frozen snapshots plus observation buffers, with an anchor. It is not flow-matching and has no fast memory used during action generation. It suggests extra baselines (sleep-time multi-memory distillation) and a metric (pairwise skill reliability) for stage D.

papers.title: Reset & Distill: A Recipe for Overcoming Negative Transfer in Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors_year: Ahn, Hyeon, Oh, Hwang, Moon, 2024 (arXiv 2403.05066)
papers.what_it_does: For each new task it resets the online actor and critic, learns the task from scratch, and then distills the online actor, plus stored expert buffers of earlier tasks, into an offline actor with KL losses. The loss combines KL to the new expert on D_tau with KL on stored subsets M_k of earlier experts. It shows that plasticity-loss remedies do not fix negative transfer, while reset plus distill does.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the simplest existing "fast learner -> distill with replay -> reset fast learner" lifecycle, the same skeleton as contribution (d) plus the refresh rule of Sec. 14, and simpler than Progress & Compress (no EWC). A proper ablation of the proposal's fast memory and reset gate should include an R&D-style lifecycle in which the fast component is a reset low-rank or full network rather than a 1,072-parameter associative memory.

papers.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
papers.authors_year: Shenfeld, Damani, Hübotter, Agrawal, 2026 (arXiv 2601.19897)
papers.what_it_does: SDFT uses "a demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher". The teacher pi(.|x,c) sees the demonstration and the student pi_theta(.|x) does not, and the student is trained on its own samples to match the teacher. The paper argues this is on-policy (unlike offline context distillation), reduces forgetting relative to SFT, and supports sequential acquisition of three skills. Its limits: it depends on in-context ability ("smaller models with weak ICL abilities fail to provide meaningful teacher signals") and it "struggles when the desired behavior requires a fundamental shift". It is LLM-only.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is conceptually the same move as the proposal's fast-to-slow transfer in contribution (d): distill an experience-conditioned (memory-adapted) teacher into a memory-free student. It adds evidence that sampling from the student (on-policy) rather than the teacher is what limits forgetting. The proposal currently distills teacher-generated adapted paths. An on-policy variant, with student ODE rollouts labelled by the memory-conditioned teacher's velocity, is a missing ablation. SDFT's limitation also echoes App. B.4 on hidden episodic facts.

papers.title: Preserving Foundational Capabilities in Flow-Matching VLAs through Conservative SFT
papers.authors_year: Zhang, Zhai, Zhang, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2605.08879)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that "unconstrained fine-tuning of flow-matching VLA models drives dense parameter overwrites". It proposes ConSFT, which reweights the FM loss per sample by sg(exp(-L_SFT/tau)), a trust-region-inspired confidence weight. It is evaluated on pi0, pi0.5 and GR00T-N1.6 on LIBERO and RoboTwin, where it matches ER without prior data. Its baselines include an LwF penalty that is exactly the velocity-field MSE to the reference model across denoising timesteps. It admits "no formal theoretical guarantee on the bounded error of the flow-matching ODE trajectories during multi-step inference".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This covers forgetting in FM-VLA fine-tuning, the proposal's target backbone family. Its LwF baseline is the proposal's retention penalty R_old evaluated on data points rather than on old ODE trajectories. It explicitly lacks the trajectory-level guarantee that the proposal's (27)-(28) provides, which is a positioning opportunity. ConSFT and ER are prior-data-free and data-based retention baselines for stage E.

papers.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: Du, Sun, Xu, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2608.26545)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that a small subset of replay data, "Memory Anchors", in regions "where representations of new-task observations collapse onto those of old-task observations even though the tasks require conflicting actions", carries most of the anti-forgetting effect. Excluding 10% of anchors increases forgetting more than 4.5x on LIBERO, and enriching the buffer reduces high-conflict forgetting by 63%. Tested with a U-Net diffusion policy, the pi0.5 VLA, and a real robot.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The conflict regions it identifies (same-looking observations, different required actions) are exactly the non-context-identifiable cases for which the proposal argues a fast memory or episodic store is needed (reset-gate criterion 4, App. B.4). It gives a principled selection rule for the finite store B and for old-behavior replay. It also shows that uniform replay is not the right baseline in high-conflict sequences.

papers.title: World Action Models Enable Continual Imitation Learning with Recurrent Generative Replays
papers.authors_year: Govind, Reilly, Patel, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2606.27374)
papers.what_it_does: REGEN uses a world-action model to recurrently synthesize pseudo-replay trajectories (future observations plus actions) for earlier tasks, conditioned only on task instructions and current observations. These are replayed during sequential fine-tuning. It reduces forgetting by up to 50% relative to sequential fine-tuning in simulation and the real world. It names "long-horizon visual degradation and action-observation inconsistency" as its bottlenecks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the current generative-replay alternative to the proposal's explicit finite replay store B (Secs. 11-14). The proposal notes that "a small associative MLP does not provide generative replay for free". REGEN is the robot-policy generative-replay comparator that the proposal's own Sec. 21 says must be added before submission.

papers.title: Efficient Continual Adaptation of Pretrained Robotic Policy with Online Meta-Learned Adapters
papers.authors_year: Zhu, Sun, Huang, et al., 2025 (arXiv 2503.18684)
papers.what_it_does: OMLA learns LoRA adapter parameters for a frozen pretrained robot policy with an online (MAML-style, second-order) meta-learning objective over previously seen tasks: g_t(phi) = grad_phi E_k L(D_k^val, U_k(phi)), with U_k(phi) = phi - alpha grad L(D_k^tr, phi). The adapters are then fine-tuned on each new task in a continual LIBERO-style stream. The policy head is a Gaussian mixture.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is prior art for contribution (c): a slowly meta-learned initialization of a small fast parameter set, trained by differentiating through inner gradient writes, with the backbone frozen, in continual robot adaptation. It mirrors the proposal's outer loop over phi and W_0 (Sec. 7). Differences: OMLA writes are per-task fine-tuning, not per-experience causal writes, and it has no FM reader or consolidation.

papers.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning
papers.authors_year: Bianchi, Yousefi, Sampieri, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2606.07217)
papers.what_it_does: WIZARD meta-learns a network that maps a language instruction plus a short demonstration video to task-specific LoRA parameters for a frozen pi0.5 VLA "in a single forward pass, without target-task action labels or test-time optimization". It notes that pure parameter regression fails and scale-aware LoRA objectives are needed. On LIBERO it reports up to about 2x gains on unseen collections and about 14x on unseen tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is an amortized alternative to the proposal's gradient writer in contribution (c): experience is written into weights, but by a hypernetwork rather than by gradient steps on l_assoc. It is a useful comparison for whether gradient writing is needed at all. It is task-level rather than continual, per-experience writing.

papers.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs
papers.authors_year: Zhao, Yang, Hu, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2605.10094)
papers.what_it_does: During persistent deployment it stores "progress-calibrated successful observation-action segments in a long-term memory". It retrieves and filters them into an elite action prior and "injects the elite prior into an intermediate state of the flow-matching action sampler", with confidence-adaptive strength. The pi0 and pi0.5 weights stay frozen.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is a nonparametric experience reader acting inside the FM denoising process (contribution (a)), accumulating across deployments. It and TraceFlow define the retrieval baselines that the proposal's parametric fast memory must beat at equal storage.

papers.title: Simple Recipe Works: Vision-Language-Action Models are Natural Continual Learners with Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors_year: Hu, Shim, Tang, et al., 2026 (RLJ 2026; arXiv 2603.11653)
papers.what_it_does: This is a systematic continual-RL study of VLAs (OpenVLA-OFT, a flow-matching VLA built on PaliGemma, and OpenVLA) on LIBERO, RoboCasa and ManiSkill. It finds that "simple Seq. FT with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is remarkably strong: it achieves high plasticity, exhibits little to no forgetting", attributing this to large pretraining plus parameter-efficient adaptation plus on-policy RL.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Together with 2603.03818, this raises the bar for the proposal's continual-adaptation protocol. Sequential LoRA fine-tuning of a pretrained FM backbone is a strong, cheap baseline for continual adaptation with consolidation. It also supports the on-policy-data argument (RL's Razor, SDFT) for consolidation targets.

papers.title: Task-agnostic Lifelong Robot Learning with Retrieval-based Weighted Local Adaptation
papers.authors_year: Yang, Wang, Zhang, Wang, Oliehoek, Kober, 2024 (arXiv 2410.02995)
papers.what_it_does: It stores a subset of past demonstrations and uses them both for experience replay and, at deployment, for "Retrieval-based Local Adaptation". Relevant demonstrations are retrieved without task IDs, and the policy is briefly fine-tuned with extra weight on "the most 'forgotten' action segment" before deployment.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is a precedent for combining an explicit episodic store with a test-time write of retrieved experience into weights in lifelong robot learning (contribution (c) and the store B). The proposal's persistent fast weights plus replay play the same role. It is a relevant baseline for the question of whether the fast associative memory beats fine-tuning briefly on retrieved episodes.

papers.title: Policy Consolidation for Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors_year: Kaplanis, Shanahan, Clopath, 2019 (ICML 2019; arXiv 1902.00255)
papers.what_it_does: The policy network interacts with "a cascade of hidden networks that simultaneously remember the agent's policy at a range of timescales and regularise the current policy by its own history". The policy is continually distilled into the cascade and back, without task boundaries.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is an early multi-timescale fast/slow policy consolidation by distillation (contribution (d)). It is a direct conceptual ancestor of the proposal's three timescales (k, t, j), missing from the related work alongside Progress & Compress.

papers.title: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: Liu, Zhu, Gao, et al., 2023 (NeurIPS 2023 D&B; arXiv 2306.03310)
papers.what_it_does: This is a lifelong robot manipulation benchmark with four task suites (130 tasks) and human demonstrations. It benchmarks ER, EWC and PackNet, and finds that "sequential finetuning outperforms existing lifelong learning methods in forward transfer" and that "naive supervised pretraining can hinder agents' performance".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the de facto benchmark on which almost all 2024-2026 continual VLA and diffusion-policy papers in this list report (2603.03818, 2605.08879, 2608.26545, CLARE, DMPEL, TAIL, WIZARD). The proposal's stage D (>=10 task arrivals) and stage E would be most comparable if run on LIBERO task streams with a pi0/pi0.5-style FM backbone.

papers.title: TAIL: Task-specific Adapters for Imitation Learning with Large Pretrained Models
papers.authors_year: Liu, Zhang, Asadi, et al., 2023 (ICLR 2024; arXiv 2310.05905)
papers.what_it_does: Uses per-task parameter-efficient adapters (LoRA, prefix and bottleneck) on a frozen pretrained policy for continual imitation learning on LIBERO. It finds "TAIL with LoRA can achieve the best post-adaptation performance with only 1% of the trainable parameters of full fine-tuning while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and preserving adaptation plasticity".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the canonical low-rank/sparse-adapter answer to continual policy adaptation. Per-task LoRA storage is an alternative "slow" store to consolidating into theta. Later work (DMPEL 2506.05985, CLARE 2601.09512) adds routing and expansion. It is a necessary baseline family if the proposal claims better retention per stored parameter.

papers.title: Maintaining Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning (published as "Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning", Nature 2024)
papers.authors_year: Dohare, Hernandez-Garcia, Rahman, Mahmood, Sutton, 2023/2024 (arXiv 2306.13812)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that deep networks "may also lose their ability to learn on new examples", that loss of plasticity is "substantially eased by L2-regularization, particularly when combined with weight perturbation" (shrink-and-perturb), and introduces continual backpropagation, which reinitializes "a small fraction of less-used units".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This bears on the proposal's "Renewed plasticity" goal (Sec. 3, item 4), reset-gate criterion (3) "can still adapt with same budget", and the "Renewed learning ... to detect loss of plasticity" metric (Sec. 17). The proposal resets only the fast memory. Slow theta and phi also drift over many consolidation cycles, and utility-based partial resets (continual backprop; Calibrated Partial Resets, 2607.24996) are the standard tools to test or cite.

papers.title: Learning Fast, Learning Slow: A General Continual Learning Method based on Complementary Learning System
papers.authors_year: Arani, Sarfraz, Zonooz, 2022 (ICLR 2022; arXiv 2201.12604)
papers.what_it_does: CLS-ER is a dual-memory experience replay method with a working model plus short-term (plastic) and long-term (stable) semantic memories, maintained as EMAs at different rates. A consistency loss aligns the working model with them on replayed episodic samples. It needs no task boundaries.
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the standard CLS-inspired deep continual-learning baseline (lens: CLS-ER, DualNet). The proposal's Sec. 2 invokes hippocampal-cortical CLS theory without citing any deep-learning CLS implementation. CLS-ER-style EMA slow copies are the cheapest competitor to explicit distillation plus reset gates.

papers.title: Building Normalizing Flows with Stochastic Interpolants
papers.authors_year: Albergo, Vanden-Eijnden, 2022/2023 (ICLR 2023; arXiv 2209.15571)
papers.what_it_does: Its Proposition 3 bounds W2^2(rho_1, rho_hat_1) <= e^{1+2K_hat} H(v_hat), where H is the velocity-regression objective and v_hat is K_hat-Lipschitz, via the same-initial-point flow-map coupling. Benton, Deligiannidis and Doucet ("Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods", arXiv 2305.16860) give related deterministic-sampling bounds.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Earliest form of the velocity-L2 -> W2 bound used in contribution (e), eq. (27). Together with ORW-CFM-W2 (2502.06061) it shows that the Gronwall-type flow-perturbation bound is known. The proposal's defensible novelty is the sharper C_L, its reading as a retention certificate evaluated on old-policy ODE trajectories, and the stated caveats (finite buffer, discretisation, closed loop).

papers.title: Dual-Memory Consolidation with Sleep-Wake Replay for Vision-Language-Action Specialization (SleepVLA)
papers.authors_year: Beaulieu, Gagné, Leduc, Tremblay, Apr 2026 (ResearchGate preprint; arXiv id not found)
papers.what_it_does: NOT VERIFIED. The ResearchGate page returned HTTP 403 to both curl and WebFetch, and arXiv search was rate-limited (429), so I could not open the paper. From search-engine snippets only: "a dual-memory consolidation framework that separates a fast, plastic episodic memory (the 'wake' phase) from a slow, stable semantic memory (the 'sleep' phase). During wake, fresh demonstrations are written into a high-capacity episodic buffer and used to train a lightweight residual head; during sleep ... the system distills the episodic content into the semantic memory through a generative replay procedure called Outcome-Weighted Distillation."
papers.relation_to_proposal: If the snippets are accurate, this is the closest match to the whole proposal lifecycle in contribution (d): a fast residual head on a VLA trained from recent demonstrations, then sleep-time distillation into the slow policy via generative replay, which frees episodic capacity (analogous to the reset). The manuscript must be obtained and checked before any novelty claim about fast-residual-to-slow VLA consolidation. Whether the base VLA is flow-matching and whether the residual acts per denoising step is unknown.

gap.landscape_summary:
As of Sep 2026, continual learning for robot policies has moved from small behavior-cloning policies trained from scratch (the LIBERO era: ER, EWC, PackNet, TAIL/LoRA adapters, LOTUS, M2Distill, SDP, DMPEL/CLARE/LiMoDE mixtures of experts, t-DGR/CRIL generative replay) to pretrained flow-matching VLAs (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T).

On those FM VLAs the forgetting problem is much milder than the proposal assumes:
- Plain experience replay with about 2% buffers gives near-zero forgetting on LIBERO (2603.03818).
- Sequential LoRA fine-tuning with on-policy RL forgets little (2603.11653).
- Real-world ER outperforms joint training at equal compute (2605.26820).
- Data-free fixes such as ConSFT now exist specifically for FM VLAs (2605.08879).
Replay design has also become more refined: Memory Anchors (2608.26545) shows that the anti-forgetting effect comes from conflict regions where similar observations need different actions, which are exactly the proposal's "non-context-identifiable" cases. WAM-based generative replay (REGEN, 2606.27374) replaces stored demonstrations.

Fast-to-slow consolidation is an active 2024-2026 line in robot learning:
- Reset & Distill (2403.05066): reset the online learner, distill into an offline actor with expert buffers.
- Continual Policy Consolidation (2601.22475): RL teachers distilled into a replayed, expandable MoE student.
- Sleeping Robots (2606.17493): wake/sleep with frozen actor memories, Nash-bargained distillation and anchoring.
- An apparently very close VLA paper, SleepVLA (fast residual head plus sleep-time outcome-weighted generative-replay distillation), which I could not open.
- Outside robotics, SDFT (2601.19897) shows that distilling an experience-conditioned teacher into a context-free student on the student's own samples limits forgetting.
None of these is flow-matching-specific, but Masip et al. (2311.14028) already showed for diffusion models that distilling the whole reverse process beats endpoint-only generative replay. That is the proposal's endpoint-vs-path question.

On the mechanism side:
- The centered residual R(W) - R(W0) is the plasticity-injection construction of Nikishin et al. (2305.15555).
- The retention bound W2^2 <= C * integral of E||dv||^2 along one model's ODE paths, with same-noise coupling, is already in Albergo and Vanden-Eijnden (Prop. 3) and in ORW-CFM-W2 (Theorem 3, e^{2L} constant). The latter also uses ||v - v_ref||^2 as the regulariser. The proposal's contribution there reduces to a sharper constant and a continual-retention reading.
- Test-time experience readers acting inside the FM sampler exist in nonparametric form: TraceFlow (2609.20646) caps an early-step velocity correction from success/failure trace banks; Retrieve-then-Steer (2605.10094) injects retrieved priors mid-sampler.
- SlowFast-VGen (2410.23277) already has gradient-written, per-episode-reset fast LoRA weights inside a diffusion model, with an outer slow loop, though for video rather than actions.
- Meta-learned writers for robot adaptation exist as MAML-style adapter priors (OMLA, 2503.18684), hypernetwork LoRA generators (WIZARD, 2606.07217) and retrieval-plus-local-fine-tuning (2410.02995).

Where the proposal still sits: no paper I found combines all of the following for an FM action policy:
- a persistent gradient-written parametric fast memory read at every ODE step through an external centered velocity reader;
- per-experience causal writes, meta-trained through the writes;
- FM-specific consolidation that compares endpoint and path distillation and corrects the noise law;
- a reset gate checked by memory removal;
- evaluation on delayed-cue, non-context-identifiable associations.
That combination and the controlled reader factorial are the defensible novelty. Each individual ingredient ((b) centering, (d) reset+distill with replay, (e) the W2 bound) has clear prior art that must be cited.

The strongest baselines to add for stages D and E:
- ER with a small buffer on a pretrained FM VLA;
- sequential LoRA fine-tuning;
- capped retrieval guidance (TraceFlow or Retrieve-then-Steer);
- TEMP-LoRA-style internal fast LoRA written by the FM loss;
- generative distillation of the old field;
- R&D-style reset-and-distill;
- on-policy (SDFT-style) versus teacher-sampled consolidation;
- anchor-aware replay selection.
All should run on LIBERO task streams.

checks.title: SlowFast-VGen: Slow-Fast Learning for Action-Driven Long Video Generation
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Hong, Liu, Wu, Zhai, Chang, Li, Lin, Lin, Wang, Yang, Wu, Wang. arXiv 2410.23277 (v2, 31 Oct 2024). OpenReview lists it as 'ICLR 2025 Spotlight'. The slow model Phi is a masked conditional latent video diffusion UNet (ModelScopeT2V, epsilon-prediction). It is diffusion, not flow matching. The fast model Theta is a TEMP-LoRA of rank 32. After each generated chunk, the LoRA is trained with the ordinary denoising loss on the input chunk concatenated with the model's OWN generated output. That write is 'action-agnostic' and excludes text conditioning (Eq. 3; Alg. 1a 'Theta_{i+1} <- Theta_i - alpha grad Loss'). The merged weights Phi+Theta therefore act at every denoising step of later chunks. The LoRA is re-initialised per episode (Alg. 1b 'Initialize TEMP-LORA parameters for this episode'). In the slow-fast loop, (X_i, X_{i+1}, Theta_i) is stored and the loop does 'Fix Theta_i and update Phi only'. That loop is first-order: nothing differentiates through the writes, and no init or writer is meta-learned. Phi learns to exploit the fast memory, and no adapted behaviour is distilled so that the memory can be removed. The paper has no forgetting, retention or memory-off evaluation. Its robot use is video planning plus an inverse-dynamics model: on a custom RLBench task, Dist is 0.013 with the loop vs 0.055 without it. Inference cost rises from 12.93 s to 13.81 s per sample. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2410.23277.txt.
checks.why: The facts in the list are accurate, but the threat is overstated, so I downgraded it from high. (a) Gradient-written persistent fast weights acting inside every denoising step are already covered by the proposal's closer robot-policy citations, RoboTTT [6] and WAM-TTT [5]. SlowFast-VGen adds an earlier (2024) diffusion-generator instance with an explicit hippocampus/neocortex CLS framing (its Sec. 3.5), so it should be cited in Secs. 2, 6 and 21. (c) It is not a precedent for the proposal's outer loop. Its loop trains the backbone with the fast weights frozen, first-order. The proposal instead freezes theta and meta-trains phi/W_0 through the writes, so the two loops run in opposite directions. (d) It has no consolidation of behaviour. Its writes use self-generated targets for consistency, which the proposal's Sec. 7 notes cannot identify a new task. An FM-loss-written LoRA on the action expert is a reasonable extra variant inside the internal-TTT baseline family the proposal already plans (same write data and lifecycle), but it is low priority.

checks.title: Online Reward-Weighted Fine-Tuning of Flow Matching with Wasserstein Regularization
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Fan, Shen, Cheng, Chen, Liang, Liu. The PDF header reads 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'. Theorem 3 states W2^2(p1^th1, p1^th2) <= e^{2L} int_0^1 E_{x~p_s^th1} ||v^th1 - v^th2||^2 ds, with v^th2 L-Lipschitz. The proof: Lemma 5 bounds the flow discrepancy along th1's flow map. Grönwall is applied with an integrating factor. 'Assumption 2' says the 'initial noise distribution x0 ~ p(x0) are shared', and Lemma 6 uses the same-noise coupling. The proof then drops e^{-Ls} <= 1 and applies Jensen. In the actual loss (Cor. 9/10) th1 = theta_ft and th2 = theta_ref. The integral is Monte-Carlo approximated as E_{t, x1~q(x1;th_ft), x~p_t(x|x1)}, i.e. at conditional-interpolant points of the fine-tuned model's samples, not along its ODE trajectories. Its purpose is anti-collapse and diversity in image reward fine-tuning. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2502.06061.txt.
checks.why: The pre-emption of eq. (27) is real: same structure, same same-noise coupling, same one-field Lipschitz assumption. The proposal's C_L=(e^{2L}-1)/(2L) is strictly sharper than e^{2L}, because it keeps the e^{L(1-s)} weight and uses Cauchy-Schwarz; the two agree as L->0. (27)-(28) must therefore be presented as a known Grönwall stability bound with a sharper constant, citing Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (earliest) and this paper. However, the proposal itself frames this as 'a limited mathematical retention statement', and it is a supporting lemma, not the core contribution, so I downgraded the threat from high to medium. Two distinctions are worth stating in the proposal. (i) Orientation: ORW's penalty is evaluated on the fine-tuned model's own samples, using the reference model's Lipschitz constant. R_old is evaluated on old-policy ODE trajectories and uses the new field's Lipschitz constant, which is what allows replaying stored old contexts. (ii) ORW's Monte-Carlo estimator equals the theorem's expectation only if the model's ODE marginals match the interpolation of its own endpoints. R_old integrates the exact old ODE paths. The suggested ablation is good: velocity MSE at interpolant points vs. on old ODE trajectories vs. on new-model trajectories.

checks.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Masip, Rodriguez, Tuytelaars, van de Ven. CoLLAs 2024, PMLR 274:431-456. An unconditional DDPM U-Net (epsilon-prediction) is trained on 5 two-class tasks from Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. In generative replay (GR), the teacher produces a DDIM sample (2 or 10 steps), forward noise is added, and the student regresses the added noise. In generative distillation (GD), the student instead regresses the teacher's noise prediction at those same noised points (Eq. 9). FID improves from 211.8 to 23.5 (F-MNIST) and from 96.4 to 42.3 (CIFAR); these are the '9.01x' and '2.28x' ratios. Distilling on current-task data (LwF-style) or on pure Gaussian inputs also beats GR. App. B.3 shows that plain ER with only 1000 (F-MNIST) or 100 (CIFAR) stored real samples performs comparably to GD. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2311.14028.txt.
checks.why: The facts are right, but 'exactly the proposal's endpoint-vs-path test' is wrong. The proposal's Secs. 11-12 compare endpoint FM distillation against regression on the teacher's OWN ODE path velocities (Gamma_t, V_t). Masip's GR is endpoint-style replay. GD is field matching at forward-noised teacher endpoints, and it never uses the teacher's reverse trajectory: 'at each point of the reverse trajectory' is rhetorical. GD is the epsilon-analogue of the proposal's R_old evaluated at interpolant points instead of on old ODE trajectories. It is therefore required prior art for Sec. 13 retention, and evidence that matching the old model's field beats endpoint replay in diffusion, especially with few-step teachers. A GD-style retention baseline makes sense. It does not bear on the fast memory, the reader or path distillation, so I downgraded the threat from high to medium. B.3 also supports the proposal's small explicit store.

checks.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Plasticity Injection
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Nikishin, Oh, Ostrovski, Lyle, Pascanu, Dabney, Barreto. NeurIPS 2023. The method freezes the head theta and adds a trainable copy theta1' and a frozen copy theta2' of the same random init: h_theta(x)+h_theta1'(x)-h_theta2'(x). 'Since initially theta1' = theta2', immediately after plasticity injection the predictions ... remain unaltered.' It is used to diagnose and mitigate plasticity loss in Atari Double DQN, and it can be repeated. An appendix ablation found that dropping the subtraction ('No Output Correction') gave 'mostly similar learning curves ... although not always'. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2305.15555.txt.
checks.why: The structural similarity to eq. (4) is real, but this is a generic 'start the intervention at exactly zero by subtracting a frozen copy' trick. Zero-initialised residuals and LoRA's zero-initialised B serve the same purpose. The proposal does not claim centering as novel. In eq. (4) the two terms share the slow reader phi and the query and differ only in the fast state, and the purpose is exact reset recovery, not plasticity. Comparing reset W->W_0 to re-injection is loose: injection keeps old knowledge frozen in place and grows the network, whereas the proposal discards the fast state after behaviour transfer. An optional footnote citation is enough; it is not a baseline. It is possibly useful as a plasticity diagnostic for Stage D renewed learning. Downgraded from high to low.

checks.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Jiaxuan Zhang, Ruizhe Liu, Yu Zhang, Yanchao Yang (4 authors). arXiv v1, 17 Sep 2026, four days before proposal v2. The description in the list is accurate. Further details: guidance runs only in early Euler steps (lambda(t) falls linearly to 0 at t_cut=0.3); retrieval happens once per query through a frozen, contrastively trained head with progress alignment. The gains are selective. The RoboMemArena 26-task aggregate is unchanged (34.92 -> 34.99 TSR), Counting and Occlusion get worse, and the LIBERO (+1.45) and LIBERO-Plus (+1.27, p=0.0733) changes are within noise. On the real robot T2 task it goes 21 -> 39/50, and 47/50 after one stacking round. Stacking histories are single-seed, and the concurrent methods are 'not compared head-to-head'. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2609.20646.txt.
checks.why: This is the closest existing instance of an external, experience-dependent, bounded velocity correction inside an FM robot policy's solver that accumulates deployment experience, and it is concurrent work. It weakens any novelty framing around 'memory acting during denoising'. However, it is nonparametric: no fast weights, writer, meta-training or consolidation, and no retention problem. It does not pre-empt the parametric lifecycle, so I downgraded the threat from high to medium. It should be the concrete instance of the proposal's 'history tokens / retrieval' baseline, matched on stored bytes and retrieval cost. Its capped-vs-uncapped result (57.75 vs 24.25 against a 56.75 base) warns that the proposal's unbounded residual in eq. (5) may need a norm bound. Its stacking plateau is about a growing bank changing which traces are retrieved, not network plasticity, so linking it to renewed-plasticity claims is a stretch. Its failure on Counting/Occlusion (missing event information) echoes App. B.4.

checks.title: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action Models are Surprisingly Resistant to Forgetting in Continual Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Huihan Liu, Changyeon Kim, Bo Liu, Minghuan Liu, Yuke Zhu (2026). The study uses full-parameter sequential fine-tuning with ER on pi0 and GR00T N1.5 across four LIBERO suites. The replay buffer holds M transitions per task, 1000 by default (about 20%). The Table 1 numbers in the list (GR00T SR 0.919, NBT 0.027; BC-DP NBT 0.127) are correct and are at that 20% buffer. Without replay, pretrained VLAs forget catastrophically (Table 2: Sequential NBT 0.56-0.76), and EWC does not help. At a 2% buffer the paper's own text says 'pretrained VLAs such as Pi0 and GR00T still have low NBT around 0.1-0.2'. pi0 regains its peak with less than 10% of the original training steps (Tab. 4, measured at a 0.2% buffer). The quote in the list is spliced: the abstract says 'sometimes achieving zero forgetting even with a small replay data size', and the '(e.g., 2% ...)' parenthetical comes from an intro sentence that says 'often'. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2603.03818.txt.
checks.why: The finding matters for the significance of Stages D-E, but the list overstates it, so I downgraded from high. Near-zero forgetting holds at a 20% buffer: GR00T's NBT of 2.7 pp is just above the proposal's 2 pp target, and pi0 is at -1.6 pp. At a 2% buffer forgetting is about 10-20 pp. Other papers disagree in small-buffer regimes: Memory Anchors reports pi0.5 NBT 0.12-0.45 on LIBERO-Goal, and ConSFT finds ER retains poorly on held-out suites. The correct takeaway is that the proposal must beat ER at matched replay bytes on the same pretrained FM backbone, with a buffer-size sweep. It is not true that the 2 pp target is already met with small buffers. The rapid-recovery finding argues for reporting relearning cost alongside reset-gate criterion (2). It does not threaten the fast-memory or reader contributions.

checks.title: Continual Policy Consolidation for Lifelong Robot Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: He, Li, Yuan, Sun, Chen, Schneider, Chen (arXiv v2, 6 Sep 2026). The description in the list is accurate: independently trained RL teachers are distilled into a student with MSE on mean actions, using DPP-selected trajectory replay (<10% of data) and an expandable Transformer-MoE with two-phase freezing. It reports near-zero BWT on CW10/CW20 and 69.4% final SR on Continual MT25. In the LIBERO supplement (QwenGR00T), ER plus expansion reaches 92.5% vs 92.1% for ER alone, and 'Statistical significance has not been established'. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2601.22475.txt.
checks.why: This is standard continual policy distillation in the Rusu 2015 / DisCoRL line. The teachers are separately trained networks, not a memory-adapted version of the student. There is no flow matching, no path or velocity distillation, and no fast state used at inference that gets reset. The proposal already cites Progress & Compress for this lifecycle skeleton. It is a useful citation for the 'continual policy learning' expansion the proposal's Sec. 21 asks for, and DPP selection is a usable heuristic for the store B. It is not a needed baseline. Its LIBERO ER number is further evidence that ER is strong on pretrained VLAs. Downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Jayasinghe, Gontero, Trivedi (16 Jun 2026). The description in the list is accurate except that it is not 'hippocampus-motivated'. The paper uses sleep and homeostatic plasticity only as 'design motivation rather than claims of neural fidelity', and the word hippocampus does not appear. For imitation learning, a skill memory is a frozen actor plus an unordered observation buffer, with sleep loss E_{o~B_i}||pi_theta(o)-pi_i^wake(o)||^2; this distillation is also used during wake. For RL (SAC, MT5) a memory is a frozen critic plus a state buffer. Gradients are combined by Nash bargaining, with adaptive anchoring and local excitability. Reset & Distill is the strongest non-oracle baseline on MT5 (AFSR 0.353 vs 0.578). The 'less informative after substantial policy drift' limitation is quoted correctly. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2606.17493.txt.
checks.why: This is generic offline consolidation by LwF-style output distillation from frozen snapshots on stored inputs. For a deterministic actor it is essentially the analogue of the proposal's R_old. It has no memory used at inference, no flow matching and no velocity or path distillation. Cite it in the continual robot policy paragraph; the pairwise-reliability metric is optional for Stage D. It is not a novelty threat, so I downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: Reset & Distill: A Recipe for Overcoming Negative Transfer in Continual Reinforcement Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Ahn, Hyeon, Oh, Hwang, Moon. arXiv v1 is from Mar 2024; the arXiv abstract page keeps the 'Reset & Distill' title. The published version (arXiv v3, Nov 2025) is retitled 'Prevalence of Negative Transfer in Continual Reinforcement Learning: Analyses and a Simple Baseline', ICLR 2025 (OpenReview: 'ICLR 2025 Poster'). The method description in the list is accurate. For each task, the online actor-critic is reset and trained by RL, then distilled into an offline actor with KL(pi_tau* || pi_offline) on D_tau plus KL terms on the stored expert subsets M_k. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2403.05066.txt.
checks.why: The lifecycle skeleton is correctly described. It is a simplification of Progress & Compress, which the proposal already cites. The 'fast' learner is a full RL network trained from scratch per task, not an immediate-adaptation memory read during generation. An R&D-style variant (fresh LoRA or adapter per task, distilled with replay) is still a sensible Stage D lifecycle baseline, especially since it was the strongest non-oracle baseline in the 'When Robots Sleep' paper. Cite it under the ICLR 2025 title. Downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Shenfeld, Damani, Hübotter, Agrawal (2026; v2 Aug 2026). The description in the list is accurate. The teacher is an EMA of the student conditioned in-context on the demonstration, and responses are sampled from the student (on-policy). The objective is derived as reverse KL, but 'we found in practice that Forward KL yields the best performance'. The ICL-strength and 'fundamental shift' limitation quotes are verbatim. It is LLM-only, with three sequential skills. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2601.19897.txt.
checks.why: The parallel is conceptual only (a context-conditioned teacher distilled into a context-free student), and the paper is LLM-only, so I downgraded from medium to low. The suggested FM ablation is sound: label student ODE rollouts with the memory-conditioned teacher's velocity. That is the on-policy orientation, and it matches the ORW theorem with the teacher's Lipschitz constant. One point in the proposal's favour: its teacher is the same backbone plus experience, so teacher samples stay close to the base distribution, which by SDFT's on-policy argument should limit forgetting. Treat it as an ablation idea, not a baseline, because it needs an in-context teacher.

checks.title: Preserving Foundational Capabilities in Flow-Matching VLAs through Conservative SFT
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Tianyi Zhang, Shaopeng Zhai, Haoran Zhang, Fuxian Huang, Qi Zhang (2026). The description in the list is accurate. The loss is J = sg(exp(-L_SFT/tau)) * L_SFT, with tau annealed, tested on pi0, pi0.5 and GR00T-N1.6 on LIBERO and RoboTwin. The LwF baseline is 'MSE between the predicted vector fields across sampled denoising timesteps' against the frozen pretrained model, with lambda=0.01, applied during target-task training, i.e. on target data rather than on old contexts or old-policy ODE trajectories. Results: LwF collapses (LIBERO-Goal 0.00, RoboTwin-Coord 0.00). ER (a 50/50 mix with pretraining data) retains less than ConSFT (LIBERO average 0.18 vs 0.34). ConSFT itself still loses 15-16 points on average. The setting is adaptation to a single target task, not a long continual stream. The 'no formal theoretical guarantee on the bounded error of the flow-matching ODE trajectories' quote is verbatim. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2605.08879.txt.
checks.why: It does not threaten the proposal's novelty, but it is the same backbone family and the same problem, with two material implications. (1) A naive velocity-field-MSE retention penalty against a reference failed badly in FM VLAs. The proposal must show that R_old, evaluated on old contexts along old ODE trajectories with tuned beta, avoids this, and should include the data-point LwF variant as an ablation. (2) ConSFT and ER are required Stage E baselines. The 'positioning opportunity' should be modest, because the proposal's (27) is only a conditional one-cycle bound, and it is not novel (see ORW and Albergo).

checks.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Du, Sun, Xu, Shah, Itkina, Song (27 Aug 2026). The description in the list is accurate. Anchors are found by (i) the overlap of new and old data in the policy's latent space, (ii) the new points with the highest action disagreement, and (iii) retrieval of the most similar old data. The main LIBERO results use a U-Net diffusion policy trained from scratch. With pi0.5 on LIBERO-Goal and a buffer that is small relative to the data, random-ER NBT is 0.12 and rises to 0.35 when 10% of anchors are removed; in the addition experiment, AnchorER 10% gives 0.45 -> 0.35. Real-robot OpenJar and SweaterFold results are included. The method needs the policy's latent space and past data. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2608.26545.txt.
checks.why: One key relation claim is wrong. Memory-Anchor conflicts are representation collisions between tasks that ARE distinguishable from the full context (the instructions differ) but whose features collapse. They are not the information-theoretically non-identifiable histories of App. B.4 and reset-gate criterion 4, where the same current context requires different actions because of past episodic facts. The paper is relevant to choosing old-behaviour replay contexts for R_old or ER (Secs. 13-14) and to designing high-conflict task orders in Stage D. Its pi0.5 small-buffer forgetting also counterbalances 2603.03818. Use AnchorER as a stronger ER baseline if Stage D includes conflicting tasks. It is not a novelty threat, so I downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: World Action Models Enable Continual Imitation Learning with Recurrent Generative Replays
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Govind, Reilly, Patel, Le, Das (25 Jun 2026). The description in the list is accurate. REGEN instantiates Cosmos-Policy, a world-action model built on a video foundation model, and recurrently generates future observations and actions for earlier tasks from their instructions and current observations. It reduces forgetting 'by up to 50%' relative to sequential fine-tuning and approaches privileged ER. The bottleneck quote is verbatim. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2606.27374.txt.
checks.why: REGEN requires a world-action model that predicts future observations. The proposal explicitly assumes no learned world model ('What is not assumed? A learned world model'), and an FM action policy cannot generate the observations or contexts needed for replay. It is therefore not a drop-in comparator for the store B. It is the generative-replay reference the proposal's Sec. 21 says to add, and a baseline only if Stage E uses a WAM backbone. Downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: Efficient Continual Adaptation of Pretrained Robotic Policy with Online Meta-Learned Adapters
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Zhu, Sun, Huang, Celiktutan (2025). The description in the list is accurate. LoRA adapters sit on a frozen vision-language policy (ViT plus temporal transformer plus Gaussian-mixture head). For each new task, the adapters are first online-meta-learned on previously seen tasks with the one-inner-step MAML objective g_t = grad E_k L(D_k^val, U_k(phi)), where meta-train points are selected by visual similarity, and then fine-tuned on the new task's demonstrations. The paper does not state a first-order approximation. The benchmark is LIBERO, plus real-robot experiments. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2503.18684.txt.
checks.why: This is a generic MAML-style learned initialisation for per-task adapter fine-tuning. It has no per-experience causal writes, no memory read during generation, no flow matching and no consolidation. The proposal's meta-learned writer, reader and W_0 have older, more direct precedents: MAML, fast-weight meta-learning, and learned-loss meta-learning [17], which the proposal already cites. Cite it as a robot-policy instance; it is not needed as a baseline. Downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Bianchi, Yousefi, Sampieri, Roberti, Rigazio, Galasso, Franco (5 Jun 2026). The description in the list is accurate. A meta-network maps a language instruction and a short video to LoRA weights for a frozen pi0.5, trained to reconstruct expert LoRA updates with a scale-aware loss; pure regression gives 0.00 success. Absolute numbers are low: LIBERO-Spatial 0.40 (vs 0.19 for the MT-VLA baseline and 0.94 for direct fine-tuning), LIBERO-Object 0.03, LIBERO-10 full-task 0.00. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2606.07217.txt.
checks.why: This is amortized, task-level, zero-shot weight generation with no continual writes and no retention question. It is a legitimate alternative 'writer' axis (hypernetwork vs. gradient) that the proposal could mention, but its performance is weak and it is not a required baseline. Downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Zhao, Yang, Hu, Gao, Ou, Wan, Dong, Ma, Gong (2026). Correction: it does NOT act throughout denoising. 'Instead of modifying the model or velocity field, we initialize the sampling process from an intermediate state: x_t0 = (1 - t0) a_elite + t0 eps', with t0 set by retrieval confidence (SDEdit-style), and pi0/pi0.5 frozen. The memory stores the robot's own successful segments, calibrated for progress by a pretrained VLAC critic, and filtered by DTW consistency before aggregation into an elite prior. LIBERO-10 gains are modest: pi0 81.6 -> 84.4 and pi0.5 92.4 -> 94.4. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2605.10094.txt.
checks.why: This is a nonparametric start-state or prior reader. It maps onto the proposal's contrast between a reader at t=0 or a final-action residual and a per-step reader, not onto the per-step velocity reader. It makes a good cheap retrieval baseline, and it offers a direct contrast between intervening only at initialisation and intervening throughout. It is not a novelty threat, so I downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: Simple Recipe Works: Vision-Language-Action Models are Natural Continual Learners with Reinforcement Learning
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Hu, Shim, Tang, Sung, Liu, Stone, Martín-Martín. Reinforcement Learning Journal 2026 (arXiv comment: 'Accepted at RLC 2026'). The study is continual RL (GRPO) with LoRA. The main model is OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO; Pi-0 (flow matching, built on PaliGemma) is used on RoboCasa, and OpenVLA on ManiSkill. Ablations (Table 3): replacing RL with supervised fine-tuning gives NBT 78.7, catastrophic; removing LoRA gives NBT 40.9. The authors note that diffusion/FM heads 'often requires more careful constraints (e.g. using a lower LoRA rank)'. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2603.11653.txt.
checks.why: The claim that 'sequential LoRA fine-tuning is a strong, cheap baseline' holds only with on-policy RL. The proposal's consolidation is supervised FM distillation, the regime where this paper's own ablation shows catastrophic forgetting. For the proposal's demonstration/correction protocol, sequential LoRA SFT is a necessary lower-bound baseline, not a strong one; it becomes strong only for a reward-based continual protocol. The paper does support the on-policy-data argument for choosing consolidation targets. Downgraded from medium to low.

checks.title: TAIL: Task-specific Adapters for Imitation Learning with Large Pretrained Models
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Z. Liu, J. Zhang, Asadi, Y. Liu, Zhao, Sabach, Fakoor. ICLR 2024. The quote in the list is verbatim. It uses per-task adapters (LoRA, prefix, bottleneck), with the adapter selected by task identity at inference, on a frozen pretrained policy with a Gaussian-mixture head (not flow matching), evaluated on LIBERO. Text: scratchpad/refs/cp/2310.05905.txt.
checks.why: This is the parameter-isolation family. It needs a task ID at test time and stores parameters per task, which the proposal's memory-off consolidation is meant to avoid. Per-task LoRA on the FM action expert is a reasonable baseline if the proposal claims better retention per stored parameter. Low novelty threat; the rating stays low.

checks.title: Building Normalizing Flows with Stochastic Interpolants
checks.corrected_description: Confirmed: Albergo, Vanden-Eijnden. ICLR 2023. Proposition 3: W2^2(rho1, rho_hat1) <= e^{1+2K_hat} H(v_hat), where H(v_hat) = int int |v_hat_t(x) - v_t(x)|^2 rho_t(x) dx dt. Here rho_t is the exact interpolant density (the law of the exact flow X_t from rho0), and v_hat is C^1 and K_hat-Lipschitz uniformly. The App. E proof differentiates Q_t = int |X_t - X_hat_t|^2 rho0, applies 2a.b <= |a|^2+|b|^2 and the Lipschitz bound, then Grönwall with Q_0=0 (same initial point). Benton, Deligiannidis, Doucet, 'Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods' (TMLR 2024, arXiv 2305.16860) also exists. Text: scratchpad/refs/aux_albergo2022_2209.15571.txt.
checks.why: This is the earliest form of eq. (27), in exactly the proposal's orientation: the expectation is along the reference (exact/old) flow, and the Lipschitz constant belongs to the other (learned/new) field. Setting v -> v_old and v_hat -> v_new gives W2^2 <= e^{1+2L} R_old. The proposal's (e^{2L}-1)/(2L) is sharper. It must be cited as the source of the bound. The proposal's defensible piece is using it as a retention penalty and certificate on old-policy trajectories inside a consolidation loop, with its stated caveats. It does not touch the core fast-memory claims, so the rating stays medium.

checks.title: Dual-Memory Consolidation with Sleep-Wake Replay for Vision-Language-Action Specialization (SleepVLA)
checks.corrected_description: NOT VERIFIED; I could not read any of the content. Web search indexes a ResearchGate record with this exact title (publication 404206201) and snippet text matching the list's description ('fast, plastic episodic memory' / 'lightweight residual head' / 'Outcome-Weighted Distillation'), dated April 2026. Attempts that failed: the ResearchGate page and contributor pages returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl; there is no Wayback snapshot; arXiv full-text search for 'SleepVLA', 'Sleep-Wake Replay' + VLA and 'Outcome-Weighted Distillation' found no matching paper; Crossref has no match; Semantic Scholar was rate-limited (429). Search results do surface ResearchGate contributor pages for Daniel Tremblay and François Leduc for this query, but I could not confirm the full author list (Beaulieu, Gagné), the date or any venue. There is no arXiv id, no DOI and no venue.
checks.why: No actual content could be checked, so the 'high' rating is unsupported and I downgraded it provisionally to low. If the snippet is accurate, the paper describes an SGD-trained residual head on a demonstration buffer with sleep-time generative-replay distillation into the VLA. That is a CLS-style lifecycle similar in spirit to the proposal's fast-to-slow lifecycle. The proposal already concedes that lifecycle vocabulary is not novel and cites Progress & Compress. It is unknown whether the backbone is flow matching, whether the residual acts per denoising step, or whether anything is meta-learned. Treat it as unverified grey literature: obtain the PDF (e.g. through a ResearchGate login) before citing it, and do not base any novelty claim on it either way.

papers.title: Proxy Policy Steering
papers.authors_year: Ning, Wang, Ma, Fang 2026 (arXiv:2609.09148, v3 13 Sep 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Adapts a frozen flow-matching VLA (pi0.5, pi0) to a new task from a few demonstrations without touching its weights. It first distills a small reference proxy from the base's velocities along the base's own denoising trajectories on target-task observations. It then initializes a task proxy from that reference and fine-tunes it on the demonstrations with the flow-matching loss. At inference it adds v_PPS = v_base + gamma[v_task - v_ref] at every denoising step. Quotes: "Their difference forms a calibrated velocity-space residual that steers the frozen base sampler at every denoising step." "When gamma = 0, this exactly recovers the frozen base sampler." It also shows that, under a shared linear FM schedule, applying the density-ratio correction pi_base*(pi_task/pi_ref)^gamma at each noise level "is equivalent to the additive residual in (4)". Results: +55 points absolute over pi0.5 across 12 tasks; it beats LoRA fine-tuning, residual policies and DSRL. Limitation noted by the authors: "we study the single-task regime".
papers.relation_to_proposal: This is the closest prior art to contribution (b) and to the recommended direct-residual reader (Eqs. 4-5). The proposal's centered residual R_phi(z,t,c,f_Wk(q)) - R_phi(z,t,c,f_W0(q)) has the same structure as v_task - v_ref with v_task initialized from v_ref: zero at initialization, an exact reset to the base sampler, and cancellation of shared approximation error. PPS also supplies a distributional (product-of-experts / density-ratio) meaning for such a residual, which Sec. 8 says the direct reader lacks ("No explicit optimality principle"). What remains distinct in the proposal: causal, gradient-written fast weights updated per experience; a meta-trained writer/query interface; persistent memory across decisions; consolidation into theta; and reset gates. The claim that a centered velocity residual is new must be dropped. PPS trained on the same k experiences is a mandatory baseline for the delayed-association and robot stages, as is its on-policy velocity distillation of v_ref, which is closely related to R_old in Eq. (25).

papers.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
papers.authors_year: Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Yang 2026 (arXiv:2609.20646, 17 Sep 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Adds an external experience memory (TraceBank) to a frozen FM action expert (pi0.5, PrediMem). It retrieves successful and failed action windows with a frozen retrieval head plus progress alignment, and builds kernel-density scores over them. It adds a signed, capped guidance term to the velocity during the early Euler steps, with the score recomputed at every active step. The bank grows with the robot's own binary-labeled rollouts across rounds, with no weight update. Quotes: "turns the action densities of retrieved successful and failed rollouts into a bounded correction to a frozen flow-matching action expert, using one terminal outcome bit per rollout and no other label"; "The term is capped relative to the base velocity, and its strength declines to zero before the final solver steps"; "Across rounds only the TraceBank contents change." Results: real-robot ordered packing went from 21/50 to 39/50, and to 47/50 after one stacking round. Uncapped guidance collapsed a task-success rate of 57.75 to 24.25. Gains are "finite", peaking before round 10. The method "does not help where a task fails for lack of event information in the policy state" (Counting/Occlusion).
papers.relation_to_proposal: Directly pre-empts the systems-level version of contribution (a): memory of recent deployment experience that is read inside the FM solver at every active step of a frozen policy and accumulates across episodes. The differences are the storage and the writer: nonparametric retrieval plus a kernel score, against gradient-written parametric fast weights with a meta-trained writer; TraceFlow also has no consolidation or reset. Its negative results support the proposal's App. B.4 point about hidden facts, and they show that a norm cap or schedule on the residual was needed in practice, which the proposal does not specify. It is a required nonparametric-memory baseline at matched experience and compute. Its RoboMemArena/LIBERO protocol is directly reusable.

papers.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs
papers.authors_year: Zhao et al. 2026 (arXiv:2605.10094)
papers.what_it_does: Treats deployment as a "persistent online adaptation process". It stores progress-calibrated successful observation-action prefixes in an online memory, retrieves state-relevant chunks, filters them with DTW consistency, and aggregates an "elite action prior". It "injects the elite prior into an intermediate state of the flow-matching action sampler and adjusts the guidance strength based on retrieval confidence" (x_t0 = (1-t0) a_elite + t0 eps), a "non-parametric test-time adaptation without requiring parameter updates".
