Gains are about 2-3 points on LIBERO-10 (pi0, pi0.5), with further gains on SimplerEnv and real bimanual tasks. Limitations noted by the authors: memory "may require more structured memory organization, long-term forgetting, task-aware indexing"; performance depends on success-estimator precision.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts the claim that experience can adapt a frozen FM policy's generation without weight updates across persistent deployment. The injection point differs: the source or intermediate state (SDEdit-like), not the velocity. The storage also differs: a raw episodic store, not fast weights. It is the strongest simple baseline for the proposal's 'history tokens/retrieval' row and should be run at the same experience budget. Its admitted lack of forgetting and memory management is exactly the gap the proposal's reset/refresh gates address, so it frames the proposal's contribution well.

papers.title: Value Gradient Guidance for Flow Matching Alignment (VGG-Flow)
papers.authors_year: Liu, Xiao, Domingo-Enrich, Liu, Zhang 2025 (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv:2512.05116)
papers.what_it_does: Poses FM alignment as deterministic optimal control of the ODE with v = v_base + v_tilde and cost lambda/2 * int ||v_tilde||^2 - r(x1). Via the HJB equation it derives the optimal control law v_tilde* = -(1/lambda) grad V ("the residual velocity field matches the gradient of the value function"), plus a value-consistency PDE. It learns grad V amortized, initialized from the one-step-Euler reward gradient plus a learnable residual. Limitation noted by the authors: "the finetuned distribution approximates the ideal KL-regularized distribution well only in the case of a relatively small lambda"; the method is "more prone to mode collapse".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Sec. 10's value/control reader (Eqs. 17-20: dz/ds = v_theta + u, cost int 1/2||u||^2 + C_W + Phi_W, u* = -grad V_W, deterministic HJB) is essentially the VGG-Flow formulation, with a memory-dependent running cost added. The proposal cites only HardFlow and Tedrake. VGG-Flow must be cited, and its amortized grad-V learning is the natural implementation and baseline for this reader. It also documents the diversity/mode-collapse caveat that Sec. 10 raises informally.

papers.title: Adjoint Matching: Fine-tuning Flow and Diffusion Generative Models with Memoryless Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.authors_year: Domingo-Enrich, Drozdzal, Karrer, Chen 2024 (ICLR 2025; arXiv:2409.08861)
papers.what_it_does: Casts reward fine-tuning of flow/diffusion models as control-affine SOC, where the learned control is a residual on the base drift. It proves that the naive KL-regularized objective is biased by the initial value function V(X0,0): "naively adding a KL regularization ... leads to a biased distribution", and "when the sampling procedure is noiseless, i.e., sigma(t) = 0, fine-tuning naively will not have any effect because X0 completely determines X1." A specific "memoryless noise schedule" is necessary and sufficient to obtain p_base(x) exp r(x). The paper gives the Adjoint Matching regression objective.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Bears directly on the correctness of Sec. 10 and on its statement that "Optimizing each noise seed can send many seeds to the same outcome; control optimality does not imply the desired distribution". This is the known 'initial value function bias', and it has a known fix. If the value reader is meant to realize pi_old * exp(-Phi_W), it must use a memoryless SDE sampler, or learn the source distribution as Uehara et al. do. A deterministic-ODE HJB reader cannot do this. Adjoint Matching is also a principled offline training objective for a memory-conditioned control residual. It is not itself a deployment baseline, but it should be cited and its objective adopted for the value reader.

papers.title: Training Free Guided Flow Matching with Optimal Control (OC-Flow)
papers.authors_year: Wang, Cheng, Liao, Qu, Liu 2024 (ICLR 2025; arXiv:2410.18070)
papers.what_it_does: Training-free guidance of pretrained FM models by solving an optimal control problem with an additive control on the velocity, x_dot = f(x) + theta_t, with running cost 1/2||theta_t||^2 and a terminal reward. It is solved with PMP/co-state iterations, with convergence analysis in Euclidean space and on SO(3). Quotes: "the expectation of the running cost upper bounds the KL divergence between the prior joint distribution ... and the joint distribution after guidance" (Prop. 1, affine Gaussian path); "existing backprop-through-ODE methods can be interpreted as special cases of Euclidean OC-Flow."
papers.relation_to_proposal: Sec. 9's whole-path objective (Eq. 15) is a discretized open-loop instance of OC-Flow: the departure residual (z_{i+1}-z_i)/dt - v_theta is the control theta_i, its squared norm is the running cost, and lambda*E_tilde replaces the reward. The proposal states "The quadratic departure term is not, by itself, a KL divergence between deterministic path laws". OC-Flow's Prop. 1 gives a KL upper-bound interpretation under stated assumptions, and it offers convergence guarantees the proposal says are missing. OC-Flow, with the memory energy as reward, should be the reference solver and baseline for the path-energy reader, alongside HardFlow.

papers.title: ReGuide: From Test-Time Guidance to Self-Improving Diffusion Policies
papers.authors_year: Lin, Shakkottai, Kalathil, Kumar 2026 (arXiv:2606.28939)
papers.what_it_does: Uses phase-conditioned, gated dynamics-model guidance of a frozen diffusion policy to generate recovery rollouts, then "treats guided rollouts as reusable on-policy recovery data". Successful guided rollouts are absorbed by ReGuide-FT, which "fine-tunes the current checkpoint with a rehearsal-style mixture of demonstrations and guided rollouts" at a fixed ratio rho, or by ReGuide-FS (retrain from scratch). The loop is iterated; base success rises 1.3-7.7x on Robomimic. Limitations noted by the authors: task-specific thresholds; simulation only; trajectory-level success filtering.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts the core shape of contribution (d): an inference-time adapted teacher (steering) produces samples that are consolidated into the base weights with replay, then the loop repeats. The proposal's distinct elements are FM-specific endpoint/path distillation, fresh-noise re-pairing to avoid source corruption, retention gates on old tasks, and a memory reset. ReGuide filters successes, which is exactly the selection bias the proposal warns about, so it is a good test case. It is the natural consolidation baseline: ReGuide-FT with rehearsal against the proposal's endpoint FM distillation with replay.

papers.title: On the Guidance of Flow Matching
papers.authors_year: Feng, Yu, Deng, Hu, Wu 2025 (ICML 2025; arXiv:2502.02150)
papers.what_it_does: Presents a general framework for energy guidance of flow matching. It asks how to "add a guidance VF g_t(x_t) to the original VF v_t(x_t), such that the new VF ... generates samples from the new distribution p'(x) = 1/Z p(x)e^{-J(x)}". It derives an asymptotically exact Monte-Carlo guidance, "novel training losses for training-based guidance" (a learned g_phi), and approximate gradient guidances that recover diffusion guidance under an uncoupled affine Gaussian path. It covers dependent couplings (e.g., minibatch OT) and applies to offline RL.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The direct reader r_{phi,W} is formally a learned additive guidance vector field. Feng et al. give its exact form and training losses for the case where the adapted policy should be a reweighting of the base. This supplies a principled objective and an interpretation that Sec. 8 calls missing, and it states the coupling assumptions under which the additive form is exact. It is needed background for the claim that r changes the action distribution in an interpretable way. It also informs the whole-path and value readers, which are special guidance constructions.

papers.title: Steering Your Diffusion Policy with Latent Space Reinforcement Learning (DSRL)
papers.authors_year: Wagenmaker, Nakamoto, Zhang, Park, Yagoub, Nagabandi, Gupta, Levine 2025 (arXiv:2506.15799)
papers.what_it_does: Adapts a BC diffusion or flow policy "by running RL over its latent-noise space". The method "requires only black-box access to the BC policy" and avoids "the need to modify the weights of the base policy at all". It is sample-efficient in simulation and the real world, including steering pi0. Limitation noted by the authors: exploration is "inherently determined by the underlying diffusion policy", with no guarantee that all policies are steerable.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The main alternative adaptation interface, the source noise. The proposal (App. C) keeps Gaussian source noise and adapts only the transition field, but never compares against noise-space steering. For a fair 'adaptation per unit experience' claim, a DSRL-style latent policy trained on the same experience, or supervised as in FlowDAgger, should be a baseline. It also preserves the base exactly, which matches the proposal's retention story at zero consolidation cost.

papers.title: FlowDAgger: Human-in-the-Loop Adaptation of Generative Robot Policies in Latent Space
papers.authors_year: Murray, Chen, Bagaria, Fortier, Hellebrekers, Mullins, Gajarla, Mees, Cakmak, Kolobov 2026 (arXiv:2607.08877)
papers.what_it_does: Maps each human corrective action to "the noise that would have produced it under the frozen base policy" by per-step fixed-point reverse integration. The resulting (s, w*) pairs supervise a lightweight latent policy that steers the frozen FM or world-action model. It adapts "from a handful of interventions", "outperforms supervised fine-tuning and latent-space RL baselines and preserves pretrained skills on held-out tasks".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Competes with requirement 1 of the proposal (immediate usefulness from a few causal experiences) on real FM VLAs. It retains old behavior by construction because the base weights are untouched. It is a supervised, few-shot counterpart to DSRL and a strong baseline for the delayed-association and robot stages. Its argument against action-space residuals (they can "push the policy off the behaviors the base reliably produces") bears on the velocity-residual design choice.

papers.title: Policy Decorator: Model-Agnostic Online Refinement for Large Policy Model
papers.authors_year: Yuan, Mu, Tao, Fang, Zhang, Su 2024 (ICLR 2025; arXiv:2412.13630)
papers.what_it_does: Learns a small residual policy by RL on top of a frozen Diffusion Policy or Behavior Transformer; the executed action is pi_base(s) + pi_res(s). Two mechanisms control exploration. A bounded residual action: "we bound the output of the residual policy within a certain scale ... the range of the residual action (-alpha, alpha)". A progressive exploration schedule mixes in the residual with a probability epsilon that grows over training.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The canonical instance of the proposal's 'final-action residual' baseline, which the proposal lists without citing. Its bounded residual and gradual activation are simple engineering versions of the proposal's centering and gating. It should be cited and used as the final-action residual baseline under the same experience and compute budget.

papers.title: From Imitation to Refinement -- Residual RL for Precise Assembly (ResiP)
papers.authors_year: Ankile, Simeonov, Shenfeld, Torne, Agrawal 2024 (arXiv:2407.16677)
papers.what_it_does: Adds a closed-loop per-timestep residual policy, trained with RL, on top of a chunked BC diffusion policy. It then distills teacher behavior into a vision student: "we collect a dataset of successful trajectories ... from pi_teacher". The authors report "a significant performance gap when distilling our state-based ResiP policy into a vision-based policy", which points to "a fundamental limitation in the policy distillation process itself".
papers.relation_to_proposal: A precedent for the base+residual-teacher to distilled-student pipeline in the proposal's fast-to-slow consolidation. It also filters teacher data to successes, which is the selection bias Sec. 11-12 warns about. Its documented distillation gap is empirical support for the proposal's caution that transfer after reset is not automatic. It should be cited, and it serves as a final-action residual plus distillation baseline.

papers.title: Self-Improving Vision-Language-Action Models with Data Generation via Residual RL (PLD)
papers.authors_year: Xiao, Lin et al. 2025 (ICLR 2026; arXiv:2511.00091)
papers.what_it_does: Probe, Learn, Distill. The method has three stages: "we freeze the VLA backbone and train lightweight residual actors via off-policy RL"; then a hybrid rollout collects base-distribution-aligned data; then "these curated trajectories are distilled back into the generalist with standard SFT, applicable to both flow-matching and autoregressive heads". Results: about 99% on LIBERO and gains on unseen tasks. The authors hypothesize that the data "is biased towards the base policy, thus fine-tuning forgets less of the base model's generalizability", citing KL as a forgetting indicator.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A direct precedent for contribution (d) at VLA scale: fast adaptation on a frozen backbone, followed by distillation into the slow policy with a data distribution chosen to limit forgetting. The proposal's distinct elements are that the fast learner is a gradient-written memory rather than an RL residual, the explicit FM endpoint/path objectives, the R_old retention term, and reset gates. PLD-style consolidation is a required comparison for the 'endpoint FM distillation + replay' claim.

papers.title: Policy Agnostic RL: Offline RL and Online RL Fine-Tuning of Any Class and Backbone (PA-RL)
papers.authors_year: Sobol Mark, Gao, Sampaio, Srirama, Sharma, Finn, Kumar 2024 (arXiv:2412.06685)
papers.what_it_does: Replaces the RL policy-improvement step with supervised learning on "optimized" actions. Candidates are sampled from the base policy, improved by global re-ranking with Q and local gradient steps on the action, then distilled into diffusion or autoregressive policies (including OpenVLA via LoRA) with "standard likelihood maximization".
papers.relation_to_proposal: The proposal's claim that "adapted samples become distillation targets" (fast-to-slow information flow) is PA-RL's mechanism, applied there to Q-optimized actions rather than memory-adapted ones. It should be cited as prior art for distilling inference-time-improved samples into a generative policy. Its on-policy action caching is relevant to the proposal's regenerate-unfiltered-samples prescription.

papers.title: Behavior Uncloning: Distilling Mode Redirection into Policy Weights without Inference-Time Steering (MoRE)
papers.authors_year: Wang, Lei, Li, Liu, Zheng, Li, Zhang, Fan 2026 (arXiv:2606.29201)
papers.what_it_does: Distills a temporary classifier-guided redirection signal into policy weights (Diffusion Policy and pi0.5), then discards the classifier. The objective is L = E_des[L_BC] + gamma E_undes[L_red], where "The retain term uses the policy's original imitation loss, e.g., noise prediction for Diffusion Policy and velocity matching for flow-based VLAs." It is motivated by avoiding the inference-time overhead of steering modules. SR improves by +44 points on average.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A precedent for turning an inference-time steering signal into slow weights with an explicit retention term. It is structurally analogous to L_slow = L_fit + beta*R_old (Eq. 26) and to the memory-removal test. Its use of velocity matching on retained data and a gating mask for where to redirect is relevant to the proposal's consolidation and gate design. It should be cited in the consolidation related work.

papers.title: Test-Time Gradient Guidance of Flow Policies in Reinforcement Learning (QGF)
papers.authors_year: Zhou, Peng, Xu, Li, Springenberg, Frans, Levine 2026 (arXiv:2606.11087)
papers.what_it_does: Performs "policy optimization entirely at test time": a BC-trained flow policy is guided toward pi ∝ pi_hat * exp(Q)^(1/beta) by adding critic gradients during denoising. The gradient is taken "at an approximate action derived from following the learned velocity flow field for a single, large, Euler integration step". The paper shows that gradients at noisy actions are biased and that BPTT is high-variance. It is competitive with train-time offline RL and scales with model size.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The simplest strong instance of the proposal's value/control reader, applied at test time to a frozen FM policy. It is the natural baseline for the value reader, with a critic trained on the same experience. Its analysis of where to evaluate the guidance signal (clean estimate versus noisy z_t) applies to the proposal's reader, which queries memory with the noisy candidate z_t.

papers.title: Q-VGM: Q-Guided Value-Gradient Matching for Offline-to-Online RL of Flow-Matching VLA Policies
papers.authors_year: Wang, Zhang, Liu, Mao, Wang, Mu 2026 (arXiv:2606.08015)
papers.what_it_does: Motivated by an optimal-control view of denoising, it derives "a local approximation connecting clean-action value gradients to local velocity corrections at late denoising steps". It uses these corrections as "critic-guided targets for fine-tuning the pretrained action expert through velocity matching" on pi0.5, avoiding BPTT. LIBERO success goes from 84.6 to 90.7 offline and 98.4 online; real bimanual tasks go from 66.7% to 98.3%.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Shows how a value-type velocity correction (the proposal's value reader) can be consolidated into the FM expert through velocity matching. This is a path-level analogue of the proposal's path distillation (Eq. 23), done at VLA scale. It is relevant to contribution (d) and to the choice between endpoint and velocity/path targets.

papers.title: DynaGuide: Steering Diffusion Polices with Active Dynamic Guidance
papers.authors_year: Du, Song 2025 (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv:2506.13922)
papers.what_it_does: Steers off-the-shelf diffusion policies using "guidance from an external dynamics model during the diffusion denoising process". Classifier-style guidance from predicted outcomes can include "any number of positive and/or negative" objectives. Separating the guidance module from the base policy lets it steer toward multiple objectives and underrepresented behaviors.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A precedent for an external module read at denoising steps of a frozen policy. It separates "storage/predictor" from base, which parallels the proposal's external-reader argument against internal TTT. ReGuide and LPB build on this line. The proposal's claim of an 'explicit external reader' should be positioned against this guidance literature, not only against TTT.

papers.title: FAR: Failure-Aware Retry for Test-Time Recovery and Continual Policy Improvement
papers.authors_year: Hao, Syed, Ichnowski, Schneider 2026 (arXiv:2607.01111)
papers.what_it_does: After a failure, it identifies failure-inducing chunks with an IQL value drop and builds contrastive positive/negative pairs. It updates the diffusion policy with a diffusion-DPO-style preference loss, which "only requires 5-10 gradient steps and can be completed within seconds", then retries. Successful recovery trajectories go into a replay buffer "for continual policy improvement".
papers.relation_to_proposal: A competing fast/slow lifecycle carried out entirely in weight space. Fast updates to the policy itself come from a few recent experiences, including failures, and slow consolidation uses replay. There is no external memory, centering or reset. It is a strong 'direct test-time weight update' baseline for the claim that a separate fast memory with centered readout adapts better per unit experience and forgets less.

papers.title: FlowCorrect: Efficient Interactive Correction of Generative Flow Policies for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors_year: Welte, Shi, Wolf, Gilles, Rayyes 2026 (arXiv:2602.22056)
papers.what_it_does: Keeps the flow policy frozen and learns LoRA adapters plus a small gate, f = f_theta + alpha_t * v_DeltaTheta, from sparse relative human corrections. The flow-edit objective "directly edits the continuous-time flow by matching intermediate ODE velocities to a target field that would reach the corrected trajectory", reusing the logged noise. "Anchor data" of uncorrected successes discourages global drift. Updates are "online, incremental". About 80% success on previously failed cases while previously solved cases are preserved; removing the gate drops in-distribution success from 65.00% to 54.17%.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Overlaps contribution (b) and the retention logic. It adds a gated, additive velocity correction learned online from a few experiences, with anchor/replay data preserving old behavior. The gate plays the role of the proposal's centering and reset. Its velocity-matching target along logged trajectories is close to the proposal's path distillation. The proposal differs in its external associative fast memory, meta-trained writer and consolidation. FlowCorrect should be a baseline for the 'few corrections' regime.

papers.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning (WIZARD)
papers.authors_year: Bianchi et al. 2026 (arXiv:2606.07217)
papers.what_it_does: A meta-network generates task-specific LoRA parameters for a frozen VLA (pi0.5) from a language instruction and a short demonstration video "in a single forward pass, without target-task action labels or test-time optimization". It is meta-trained with "a reconstruction loss in weight-space" against a repository of expert LoRA adapters. Reported gains are up to ~14x on unseen LIBERO tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: An amortized alternative to contribution (c), the meta-trained writer: experience maps to weights that modulate a frozen generative robot policy. It differs from the proposal's second-order-meta-trained gradient writer and small external memory. It should be discussed when justifying gradient-based writes over hypernetwork writes.

papers.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
papers.authors_year: Benton, Deligiannidis, Doucet 2023 (TMLR 2024; arXiv:2305.16860)
papers.what_it_does: Proves W2(pi_hat_1, pi_1) <= epsilon * exp(int_0^1 L_t dt) for deterministic FM sampling, where epsilon is the L2 velocity error and L_t is a time-varying Lipschitz constant, using the Alekseev-Groebner formula and Groenwall's lemma. It notes that an earlier Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden bound uses a uniform Lipschitz constant "whereas for most practical data distributions we expect the Lipschitz constant to explode as one approaches the data distribution".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Contribution (e), the retention bound W2^2 <= C_L R_old with C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L) (Eqs. 27-28, App. B.1), is a same-noise-coupling Groenwall bound of the same kind. It should be credited to this line of work and to Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden 2022, Prop. 3. Benton's point implies that a uniform L, and hence C_L, can be vacuous for concentrated or multimodal action data near t = 1. Retention bounds need a time-varying L_t, or the proposal should state that the bound is qualitative.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning of Continuous-Time Diffusion Models as Entropy-Regularized Control
papers.authors_year: Uehara, Zhao, Black, Hajiramezanali, Scalia, Diamant, Tseng, Biancalani, Levine 2024 (arXiv:2402.15194)
papers.what_it_does: Frames reward fine-tuning as "entropy-regularized control against the pretrained diffusion model" with neural SDEs, regularizing "with respect to both a drift term and an initial distribution" so that the pretrained bridges are preserved and reward collapse is mitigated. The authors state that the method is "not suitable for purely ODE-based models".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Together with Adjoint Matching, this is the standard SOC account of control-affine residuals on generative dynamics. It shows why the proposal's deterministic value reader lacks KL/tilt semantics. The two known remedies are to tilt or learn the initial distribution (this paper) or to use a memoryless SDE (Adjoint Matching). The proposal fixes Gaussian source noise (App. C), which rules out the former, so Sec. 10 should state which remedy it adopts.

papers.title: Real-Time Execution of Action Chunking Flow Policies (RTC)
papers.authors_year: Black, Galliker, Levine 2025 (arXiv:2506.07339)
papers.what_it_does: Performs asynchronous action chunking for FM VLAs (pi0-class) by inference-time inpainting. It adds "a gradient-based guidance term to the learned velocity field v at each denoising step", using PiGDM on the previous chunk's committed actions, with soft masking. Quote: "The guidance weight clipping, beta, is our addition; we found that without it, the algorithm became unstable with the small number of denoising steps commonly used in control problems."
papers.relation_to_proposal: Deployed FM robot policies already add a history-dependent correction to the velocity at every denoising step (short-term memory of executed actions), so the proposal's residual must compose with such guidance on real backbones. It is further evidence, alongside TraceFlow's cap, that additive per-step terms with few solver steps need magnitude control. Relevant to Stage E engineering and to the novelty framing of 'memory acts during denoising'.

papers.title: D-Flow: Differentiating through Flows for Controlled Generation
papers.authors_year: Ben-Hamu, Puny, Gat, Karrer, Singer, Lipman 2024 (ICML 2024; arXiv:2402.14017)
papers.what_it_does: Controls generation by "differentiating through the flow, optimizing for the source (noise) point". It argues that for Gaussian-path FM/diffusion models "differentiating through the generation process projects gradient on the data manifold, implicitly injecting the prior into the optimization process". Applications include inverse problems and conditional molecule generation.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The canonical alternative to Sec. 9, which optimizes interior path nodes and "never z_0". The implicit-manifold-prior argument is a reason to expect source optimization to preserve plausibility better than free node optimization with a quadratic departure penalty. D-Flow should be an ablation of the path-energy reader alongside HardFlow and OC-Flow.

gap.landscape_summary:
As of September 2026, inference-time steering and adaptation of frozen diffusion and flow-matching (FM) robot policies is crowded, and moves fast in 2026 especially. The work falls into seven groups.

1. **Noise-space steering.** DSRL; FlowDAgger, which inverts human corrections into noise; Latent Policy Steering; a DSRL-for-navigation paper.
2. **Output or action residuals.** Policy Decorator; ResiP and ResFiT; RFS, which combines a residual with noise steering; Warp RL, an identity-initialized invertible warp that generalizes additive residuals; Coda, a learned endpoint corrector for frozen FM VLAs.
3. **Velocity-space corrections at every or early denoising steps of a frozen FM or diffusion policy.**
   - Proxy Policy Steering: a centered v_task - v_ref residual with a density-ratio interpretation.
   - FlowCorrect: a gated LoRA velocity edit learned from sparse corrections, with anchor data.
   - DynaGuide and LPB: dynamics-model guidance.
   - Real-time chunking: history-conditioned PiGDM guidance with clipping.
   - Critic-gradient guidance: QGF, QPILOTS, Guided Action Flow.
4. **Memory of deployment experience steering a frozen FM sampler without weight updates.**
   - Retrieve-then-Steer: success memory feeding an intermediate-state prior.
   - TraceFlow: success and failure traces turned into a capped velocity guidance field, growing over rounds.
   - Also CCDP (in-episode failures as negative guidance) and retrieval-conditioned policies (Retrieve-Don't-Retrain, RA-VLA).
5. **Optimal-control theory for residual control of generative dynamics.**
   - Uehara et al. and Adjoint Matching: stochastic optimal control, the initial-value bias, and the memoryless noise schedule.
   - VGG-Flow: deterministic optimal control and HJB; the residual velocity equals the negative value gradient.
   - OC-Flow: additive control with a quadratic running cost that bounds KL.
   - Feng et al.: general and learned FM guidance vector fields.
6. **Consolidating steering into weights.**
   - ReGuide: guided rollouts, then rehearsal fine-tuning, iterated.
   - PLD: residual RL, then distribution-aware SFT distillation, with a forgetting argument.
   - PA-RL: optimized actions distilled into the policy.
   - MoRE: redirection distilled into weights with a retain loss using velocity matching.
   - Q-VGM: value-gradient velocity targets.
   - Noise Hypernetworks: test-time optimization amortized into a network.
   - FAR: fast test-time weight updates from failures plus replay-based continual improvement.
7. **Amortized weight writers.** WIZARD (LoRA generated for frozen pi0.5 from a demo video) and HyperAlign.

**Where the proposal sits.** I found no single paper that combines the proposal's full recipe. That recipe is: a small, causally gradient-written, meta-trained parametric fast memory, queried by the noisy candidate z_t and read as a centered velocity residual at every ODE step; then consolidation into the FM backbone by endpoint or path FM distillation with old-task replay; then memory reset gated on transfer and retention, with a retention bound. Every individual component, however, now has a close 2025-26 precedent.

- **Contribution (a), memory read during denoising of a frozen FM policy.** Pre-empted at the systems level by TraceFlow and Retrieve-then-Steer (nonparametric). Internal TTT (RoboTTT, and TTT inside video diffusion transformers) also reads fast weights at every step.
- **Contribution (b), centered or resettable velocity residual.** Pre-empted in structure by Proxy Policy Steering: the task proxy is initialized from the reference, the correction is exactly zero at gamma = 0, and it is justified as a density ratio. FlowCorrect (gated additive velocity) and Feng et al. (guidance vector field theory) are also relevant. The proposal's claim that the direct reader has "No explicit optimality principle" is outdated.
- **Contribution (c), meta-trained writer.** Faces amortized alternatives (WIZARD) and test-time weight updates (FAR, TT-VLA).
- **Contribution (d), fast-to-slow consolidation with replay.** Closely matched by ReGuide-FT (rehearsal ratio), PLD and PA-RL. The proposal's genuinely distinct parts are FM-specific: re-pairing with fresh noise, endpoint versus path distillation, R_old retention, and reset gates.
- **Contribution (e), the retention bound.** The same Groenwall/Alekseev-Groebner bound appears in Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (2022) and Benton et al. (2023). Benton shows that uniform-Lipschitz constants are typically vacuous near the data end.
- **Sec. 10 value/control reader.** Essentially VGG-Flow's formulation. Adjoint Matching and Uehara et al. document the bias the proposal only hints at ("many seeds to the same outcome") and give the known fixes: a memoryless SDE, or a learned source distribution.
- **Sec. 9 whole-path reader.** A discretized instance of OC-Flow. D-Flow and HardFlow are the standard alternatives.

**Implications.**
- Reframe the novelty as the lifecycle (causal parametric writes, then FM consolidation, then gated reset) plus a controlled reader comparison.
- Add these baselines at matched experience and compute:
  - PPS, TraceFlow/Retrieve-then-Steer, DSRL/FlowDAgger, FlowCorrect and FAR for the adaptation phase;
  - ReGuide-FT/PLD for consolidation;
  - QGF or VGG-Flow for the value reader;
  - OC-Flow and D-Flow for the path reader.
- Specify a norm cap or schedule on the residual; both RTC and TraceFlow found one necessary at few solver steps.
- Cite and adopt the memoryless SOC construction if the value reader is to target a tilted distribution.

**Caveats on this search.** The arXiv search endpoint began returning HTTP 429 part-way through, so later discovery used WebSearch plus arXiv abstract pages. Every listed paper's abstract page was opened and its title confirmed; I read full text or key method sections for most of them. Several additional 2026 steering papers were confirmed to exist but are not entered above: QPILOTS 2606.14801, CCDP 2503.15386, Coda 2609.21216, Warp RL 2606.31043, HyperAlign 2601.15968, Noise Hypernetworks 2508.09968, V-GPS 2410.13816, RoboMonkey 2506.17811, TACO 2512.02834, Guided Action Flow 2607.02092, RA-VLA 2608.25585 and TT-VLA 2601.06748. They are relevant as compute-matched best-of-N or verifier baselines and as further nonparametric-memory variants.

checks.title: Proxy Policy Steering
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2609.09148 v3 (13 Sep 2026), authors Ning, Wang, Ma, Fang. I read the full text, including App. D. The quotes check out: 'Their difference forms a calibrated velocity-space residual that steers the frozen base sampler at every denoising step'; 'When gamma = 0, this exactly recovers the frozen base sampler'; limitation 'we study the single-task regime'. Result confirmed: +55% absolute over pi0.5 on 12 tasks. HIGH is justified for one component. This is the closest prior art to the recommended reader (Eqs. 4-5): a frozen FM base plus an adapted-minus-reference copy of the same small network, added at every Euler step. The correction is exactly zero before adaptation, and it is motivated by cancelling shared approximation error ('the two proxies share the error, and their difference isolates the change induced by task supervision'). Its ablations show the centering matters: w/o ref 64->55%, w/o tune 48%. It sits in the CFG / autoguidance / proxy-tuning line. Three corrections to the search agent. (i) The proposal never claims the centered residual is new. Sec. 21 says the defensible contribution is the full lifecycle plus a fair comparison of interfaces. So the fix is to cite PPS and position against it, not to 'drop a claim'. (ii) The density-ratio meaning is weaker than stated. App. D says the per-level PoE (A3) 'is a modeling choice, not a consequence of (7)' and that {p_PPS,k} 'is in general not the family of noise-level marginals of the clean target'. It also needs each term to be the marginal velocity of an FM-trained policy on a shared linear schedule. R_phi in the proposal is a reader head, not an FM velocity, so this reading does not carry over and does not fill Sec. 8's 'No explicit optimality principle' gap. (iii) PPS is not a memory. It trains two 32M proxies for 20k steps each on 50 demos (2.9 h), single task. It has no per-experience causal writes, meta-trained writer, consolidation or reset. Its L_ref (velocity distillation on the base's own denoising states) has the same form as R_old in Eq. 25. Recommended baseline: a PPS proxy fine-tuned on the same k experiences. This isolates the meta-trained associative writer from the centered-residual interface. It is required at Stage E and informative at Stage B.
checks.corrected_description: Offline, single-task inference-time adaptation of a frozen FM VLA. A 32M reference proxy is distilled on the base's own denoising states. A task proxy is initialized from it and fine-tuned with FM on 50 demos. v_base + gamma(v_task - v_ref) is applied at all 10 Euler steps, with gamma = 0.4 fixed. The PoE/density-ratio link holds only per noise level, under a stated modeling assumption (A3). It does not give the clean-target marginals.

checks.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2609.20646 (17 Sep 2026), authors Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Yang. Full text read; the quotes are exact. Real-robot T2 went 21/50 -> 39/50 -> 47/50. The cap statistic was misphrased by the search agent: uncapped 24.25 vs capped 57.75 against a 56.75 base, on an 8-task pi0.5 probe. On LIBERO-10, direct vs bounded showed no difference (p = 0.580). The gains are selective. The 26-task aggregate is unchanged (34.92 -> 34.99), Counting and Occlusion drop, LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus changes are within noise, settings are chosen per suite, and the only baseline is the unguided checkpoint. Real overlap: deployment experience is read inside the FM solver of a frozen VLA, and the read depends on the current candidate ('the score is therefore recomputed as A_t moves'). It accumulates across rounds with no weight update. That is a concurrent systems-level instance of requirements 1-2. Downgraded from high for three reasons. First, the store is nonparametric and keyed on the current state. Second, rollouts are admitted 'in the next round only', so there are no within-episode causal writes. Third, there is no gradient-written memory, meta-trained writer, consolidation or reset. The authors say it 'does not help where a task fails for lack of event information in the policy state'. The proposal's Stage B benchmark fixes the present context and varies only the prefix, which a retrieval keyed on the current state cannot solve. So TraceFlow sets the proposal apart rather than pre-empting it. It should be the nonparametric retrieval baseline (the Sec. 17 retrieval row). Its cap ablation is a useful warning that the proposal sets no norm bound or schedule on r. Linking its failures to App. B.4 is loose: B.4 is about memory-free students, while TraceFlow fails because of its retrieval key.
checks.corrected_description: Frozen pi0.5/PrediMem action expert. A TraceBank is keyed by a frozen contrastive retrieval head with progress alignment. Kernel-density scores over retrieved success windows (attract) and failure windows (repel) are recomputed at each early Euler step. The correction is capped relative to ||v_base|| and switched off after t_cut. The bank grows by rounds from binary-labeled rollouts, with no weight update. Its only baseline is the unguided checkpoint.

checks.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2605.10094 v2 (12 May 2026), Zhao et al. Full text read; the quotes are exact. Results: LIBERO-10 +2.8 (pi0) and +2.0 (pi0.5); SimplerEnv +3.7 on CogACT; real bimanual +6 to +12 points. It pre-empts one framing: deployment as a 'persistent online adaptation process' for a frozen generative VLA without parameter updates. That matches the proposal's strict fast-only protocol, and the method is a natural retrieval baseline. Downgraded from high for four reasons. (1) It injects a retrieved elite prior into an intermediate state, SDEdit-style, with confidence-adaptive t0. It has no velocity correction and no readout that depends on the candidate during integration. (2) The memory is raw success chunks keyed on the current visual state, with FIFO eviction at 3.5k entries. It needs a VLAC progress critic (precision 0.970), and unverified memory hurts (87.6 vs 92.4). (3) The authors list state aliasing ('Visually similar states may require different actions due to ... task phase'), so it cannot address delayed-cue tasks. (4) Its 'long-term forgetting' concerns eviction in a nonparametric store. That is not the parametric consolidation/reset gap the proposal targets, so 'exactly the gap' is overstated.
checks.corrected_description: Nonparametric, success-only online memory of progress-calibrated observation-action prefixes, keyed by VLA visual features. At inference it retrieves top-K chunks, filters them by DTW consistency and aggregates an elite prior. The prior initializes the FM sampler at x_t0 = (1-t0)a_elite + t0*eps, with t0 set by retrieval confidence. Gains are small (+2 to 3 points on LIBERO-10).

checks.title: Value Gradient Guidance for Flow Matching Alignment (VGG-Flow)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2512.05116, NeurIPS 2025 (confirmed in the arXiv comment and the PDF footer), authors Liu, Xiao, Domingo-Enrich, Liu, Zhang. Read the method, discussion and App. B. Confirmed: Eq. 6 min E[lambda/2 int ||v_tilde||^2 - r(x1)] with v = v_base + v_tilde; the HJB gives v_tilde* = -(1/lambda) grad V (Eq. 8), plus value consistency (Eq. 9). g_phi = -eta*grad r(one-step Euler x_hat_1) + nu_phi. Limitation, exact: 'approximates the ideal KL-regularized distribution well only in the case of a relatively small lambda'. The mode-collapse quote is about 'our hyperparameter settings are in theory more prone to mode collapse', not an inherent property. Sec. 10 (Eqs. 17-20) is indeed this formulation applied to FM, plus a memory-dependent running cost C_W. The proposal cites only generic HJB [14] and HardFlow [7], so this citation is missing, and it gives a ready amortized implementation. One more finding the search agent missed: App. B Prop. 4 proves W2(p1,q1)^2 <= e^{2L+1} int E||v_tilde||^2 dt by same-noise coupling plus Groenwall. That is essentially the proposal's retention bound (Eqs. 27-28), whose constant (e^{2L}-1)/(2L) is slightly tighter. App. B.2 shows KL is not controlled by the L2 term alone, which supports rather than contradicts the proposal's caveat. Medium rather than high: the value reader is an optional later experiment with no novelty claim. VGG-Flow is offline reward fine-tuning of SD3 weights, not deployment-time adaptation.
checks.corrected_description: Deterministic optimal-control alignment of FM (SD3): v = v_base + v_tilde, cost lambda/2 int||v_tilde||^2 - r(x1). The HJB gives v_tilde* = -(1/lambda) grad V. grad V is learned with amortized consistency and boundary losses, and v_tilde is regressed onto it. The appendix proves a same-noise Groenwall W2 bound, W2^2 <= e^{2L+1} int E||v_tilde||^2 dt.

checks.title: Adjoint Matching: Fine-tuning Flow and Diffusion Generative Models with Memoryless Stochastic Optimal Control
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2409.08861, ICLR 2025 (confirmed via ICLR proceedings and dblp), authors Domingo-Enrich, Drozdzal, Karrer, Chen. Read the intro and Sec. 4. The quotes are exact ('leads to a biased distribution'; 'when the sampling procedure is noiseless ... X0 completely determines X1'). Theorem 1: memoryless sigma(t) = sqrt(2 eta_t) is required to reach p_base*exp(r). This confirms and sharpens a caveat the proposal already states correctly ('control optimality does not imply the desired distribution'). It does not show Sec. 10 is wrong: the deterministic HJB in Eq. 20 is standard. Correction: 'a deterministic-ODE HJB reader cannot do this' is partly wrong. AM trains with the memoryless SDE but states that 'sample generation can use any noise schedule after fine-tuning, including sigma(t) = 0'. So a value residual trained by memoryless SOC could still run as a deterministic velocity residual at deployment. This is the principled route if Sec. 10 wants pi_old*exp(-Phi_W) semantics. Must-cite for the optional value reader. It poses no novelty threat and is not a deployment baseline, so high is unsupported.
checks.corrected_description: Reward fine-tuning of FM/diffusion as control-affine SOC. The naive KL objective is biased by V(X0,0). The memoryless noise schedule is necessary and sufficient for the tilt p_base*exp(r), and the fine-tuned model can then be sampled with any schedule, including an ODE. Adjoint Matching is a regression objective for the control.

checks.title: Training Free Guided Flow Matching with Optimal Control (OC-Flow)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2410.18070, ICLR 2025 (per the PDF header), authors Wang, Cheng, Liao, Qu, Liu. Read the method, Theorem 2 and the Prop. 1 proof. Confirmed: additive control x_dot = f^p + theta_t with cost -1/2||theta||^2, solved by E-MSA/PMP, including on SO(3). Quote: 'existing backprop-through-ODE methods can be interpreted as special cases of Euclidean OC-Flow'. Eq. 15 is a direct-transcription version of this problem: the path nodes correspond to controls theta_i = (z_{i+1}-z_i)/dt - v_theta. It differs in that E_tilde is a path (running) energy, not only a terminal reward. So OC-Flow should be cited with HardFlow as a reference solver. Two claims are overstated. (1) Prop. 1 bounds the KL between joint (x^p, x1) laws under an affine Gaussian path. Its constant depends on the terminal conditional sigma_1(x1) and degenerates as sigma_min -> 0. The marginal version needs a 'square-shaped data' assumption and an extra L1 term. It does not contradict the proposal's statement that the quadratic term 'is not, by itself, a KL'. (2) Theorem 2 guarantees the objective increases each iteration under global Lipschitz assumptions. That is not the global-optimum guarantee the proposal says is missing. The path-energy reader is itself optional.
checks.corrected_description: Training-free guidance of a pretrained FM ODE with additive per-step controls, quadratic control cost and a terminal reward, solved by E-MSA/PMP. It guarantees monotone improvement under Lipschitz assumptions. Its KL bounds hold only under restrictive affine-Gaussian or 'square-shaped data' conditions.

checks.title: ReGuide: From Test-Time Guidance to Self-Improving Diffusion Policies
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2606.28939 (27 Jun 2026), authors Lin, Shakkottai, Kalathil, Kumar. Full text read. Confirmed: guided rollouts treated as 'reusable on-policy recovery data'; ReGuide-FT fine-tunes with a fixed rehearsal ratio rho; ReGuide-FS retrains from scratch; 1.3-7.7x on Robomimic. The listed limitations are also confirmed. It is a real precedent for the loop 'steered teacher -> rollouts absorbed into weights with rehearsal -> iterate'. Downgraded from high for four reasons. (1) This loop is generic: self-training and expert iteration, PA-RL, PLD, and P&C [16], which the proposal already cites. (2) ReGuide is single-task by its own account: 'continual learning typically targets sequential acquisition of distinct tasks, while we iteratively refine a policy on the same task'. It reports no old-task retention. (3) The steering comes from a DINO-WM dynamics model toward phase targets, not from an experience memory. (4) The base is a DDPM Diffusion Policy, not FM. Correction on selection bias: ReGuide retrains with the ordinary diffusion loss on (O, A_guided) pairs with fresh noise. That is the proposal's accepted option 2 ('select successful endpoints, pair with new independent Gaussian noise'), not the noise-law corruption case. It targets a success-conditioned distribution. Reasonable consolidation-baseline template.
checks.corrected_description: Single-task self-improvement of a DDPM Diffusion Policy. Phase-conditioned, two-threshold-gated dynamics-model guidance is applied through the clean-action estimate to produce recovery rollouts. Successful rollouts are merged into the dataset (fine-tune with rehearsal ratio rho, or retrain from scratch) and the loop repeats. Simulation only (Robomimic).

checks.title: On the Guidance of Flow Matching
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2502.02150, ICML 2025 spotlight (arXiv comment), authors Feng, Yu, Deng, Hu, Wu. Read the framework, the MC and approximate guidance, and the assumptions. Confirmed: guidance VF g_t such that v' = v + g_t generates p' proportional to p*e^{-J}; asymptotically exact MC guidance; training losses; covers dependent couplings; offline RL experiments. The relevance is narrower than claimed. If the memory-adapted policy is a reweighting (tilt) of the base, this gives the exact additive velocity and training losses. But the proposal's meta-training (Eq. 12) is FM regression to expert actions, which need not be a tilt of the base: a tilt cannot create mass where the base has none. So this is an interpretation for a special case, not the 'explicit optimality principle' Sec. 8 lists as missing. Useful background citation only.
checks.corrected_description: General theory of energy guidance for FM. It gives the exact additive guidance VF for p' proportional to p*e^{-J}, an unbiased MC estimator, training-based losses, and local/covariance approximations that recover diffusion guidance under uncoupled affine Gaussian paths. It also covers dependent couplings.

checks.title: Steering Your Diffusion Policy with Latent Space Reinforcement Learning (DSRL)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2506.15799 v2, authors Wagenmaker, Nakamoto, Zhang, Park, Yagoub, Nagabandi, Gupta, Levine. Read the abstract, method, pi0 experiments and limitations. The quotes are exact. Full limitation: 'the exploration capabilities of DSRL are inherently determined by the underlying diffusion policy ... we do not have a guarantee that all diffusion policies are steerable'. It is a noise-space alternative the proposal never discusses, so one sentence in App. C is warranted. But DSRL is RL: it needs rewards, online rollouts and resets (~10^4 steps for pi0 on LIBERO). The proposal puts reward-only adaptation out of scope, and its target regime is 1-16 experiences. PPS and FlowDAgger both report DSRL gains little there; FlowDAgger: 'DSRL barely moves the base' at 50 rollouts. A supervised noise-space method (FlowDAgger) is the more apt comparison. Downgraded to low.
checks.corrected_description: RL over the input-noise space of a frozen diffusion/flow policy, using black-box forward passes only. It is sample-efficient compared with weight fine-tuning but still needs rewards and many interactions. It can only select behaviors the base can already produce.

checks.title: FlowDAgger: Human-in-the-Loop Adaptation of Generative Robot Policies in Latent Space
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2607.08877 (9 Jul 2026), Murray ... Kolobov. Read the method, results and limitations. The quotes are exact. It adapts pi0.5 and Cosmos-Policy from 5-20 real interventions (50 rollouts on MetaWorld). It preserves held-out saturated tasks (Table 3), while LoRA-DAgger and SFT collapse them. Medium is fair: it competes on requirement 1 (few causal experiences, frozen FM base, retention by construction) and is a strong Stage-E baseline. The mechanism differs: noise-space action inversion plus a supervised latent policy, with no associative memory, meta-trained writer or consolidation. Its own limitation, 'adaptation capacity is therefore bounded by the support of the pretrained model', is an argument for velocity residuals. Its warning that residuals can 'push the policy off the behaviors the base reliably produces' is about final action-space residuals, so it bears more on the proposal's final-action baseline than on the velocity reader.
checks.corrected_description: Frozen FM/diffusion policy or world-action model. Each human corrective action is inverted by per-step fixed-point reverse Euler to the noise that produces it. A lightweight latent (noise) policy is trained on (s, w*) pairs. Adapts from 5-20 real interventions and preserves held-out skills. Bounded by the base's support.

checks.title: Policy Decorator: Model-Agnostic Online Refinement for Large Policy Model
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2412.13630, ICLR 2025 (confirmed via OpenReview and ICLR proceedings), authors Yuan, Mu, Tao, Fang, Zhang, Su. Read the method. Confirmed: executed action pi_base(s) + pi_res(s); residual bounded to (-alpha, alpha) via tanh scaling; epsilon-greedy-style progressive schedule. It is the right citation for the final-action residual idea. But it is RL (SAC, sparse reward, many environment steps). The proposal's final-action baseline must read from the same fast memory and feedback (Sec. 17), so Policy Decorator is a citation, not the baseline itself. The analogy between bounded residual / gradual activation and centering / gating is weak. Centering guarantees exactly zero correction at W0 (exact reset). The proposal's gates are accept/reset criteria for consolidation, not exploration schedules.
checks.corrected_description: Online RL (SAC) of a small bounded residual policy on top of a frozen Diffusion Policy or Behavior Transformer. The residual output is scaled to (-alpha, alpha), and during training it is mixed in with a probability epsilon that grows linearly.

checks.title: From Imitation to Refinement -- Residual RL for Precise Assembly (ResiP)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2407.16677 v4, authors Ankile, Simeonov, Shenfeld, Torne, Agrawal. Read the method, distillation sections and appendix. The quotes are exact. The distillation is not fast-to-slow consolidation. A sim-trained, privileged-state teacher (chunked BC plus a per-step PPO residual, about 75M environment steps) is distilled offline into a Diffusion Policy student for sim-to-real. The teacher reaches about 98% and the student saturates near 80% even with 100k rollouts; the paper calls this 'a fundamental limitation in the policy distillation process itself', and DAgger-style online distillation helped. This loosely supports the proposal's caution that transfer is not automatic. But ResiP is neither a few-experience method nor a memory, and it is not usable as a baseline at the proposal's budgets.
checks.corrected_description: Per-timestep residual PPO policy on top of a frozen chunked BC diffusion policy, trained in simulation with privileged state. Successful teacher rollouts are re-rendered and distilled offline into a vision Diffusion Policy for real deployment, with a persistent teacher-student gap.

checks.title: Self-Improving Vision-Language-Action Models with Data Generation via Residual RL (PLD)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2511.00091, Xiao, Lin et al. (NVIDIA/CMU). An ICLR 2026 poster page exists on iclr.cc; from the listing I could not confirm whether it is main-track or workshop. Read the abstract, method, ablations and analysis. The quotes are exact, including the hypothesis that the data are 'biased towards the base policy, thus fine-tuning forgets less' with KL as a forgetting indicator. It is a VLA-scale precedent for fast adaptation on a frozen backbone followed by SFT distillation with deployment-aligned data. Differences: the fast learner is a set of per-task RL residual specialists (~250k online steps), not a memory. It has no reset/renewal step and no sequential multi-task retention protocol. Correction: PLD's Stage 3 'standard SFT' on pi0 is ordinary FM training on curated endpoints with fresh noise, essentially the proposal's endpoint FM distillation. So it is not a different distillation objective to compare against. What it adds is the teacher-data collection policy (hybrid rollouts aligned with the base's state visits), which the proposal could adopt for its teacher-context sampling.
checks.corrected_description: Probe-Learn-Distill. Lightweight residual actors are trained by off-policy RL on a frozen VLA. Hybrid base-then-residual rollouts collect data aligned with the base's state distribution. The curated trajectories are SFT-distilled back into the generalist (FM or autoregressive heads). About 99% on LIBERO; the authors hypothesize less forgetting because the data stay close to the base policy.

checks.title: Policy Agnostic RL: Offline RL and Online RL Fine-Tuning of Any Class and Backbone (PA-RL)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2412.06685, authors Sobol Mark, Gao, Sampaio, Srirama, Sharma, Finn, Kumar. Read the abstract and method. Confirmed: base samples are improved by Q re-ranking (global) and action-gradient steps (local), then distilled by 'standard likelihood maximization'. Real-world OpenVLA went from 40% to 70%. It is one instance of the general 'improve samples at inference, distill into the policy' pattern (expert iteration), and worth a citation in the consolidation discussion. The relevance claim about the action cache overreaches. The cache is a compute device that stores OpenVLA samples for reuse in TD backups. It has nothing to do with the proposal's advice to regenerate unfiltered teacher samples.
checks.corrected_description: Actor-critic RL for any policy class. Optimized actions (critic re-ranking plus local gradient ascent on base samples) are distilled into the policy by supervised likelihood; an action cache speeds up OpenVLA TD backups.

checks.title: Behavior Uncloning: Distilling Mode Redirection into Policy Weights without Inference-Time Steering (MoRE)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2606.29201 (28 Jun 2026), Wang, Lei, Li, Liu, Zheng, Li, Zhang, Fan. arXiv lists 'Dayou Li', the PDF 'Danyou Li'. Read the method. The objective and the retain-term quote are exact, and the +44 SR points is correct. Nuance: the 'steering signal' is a frozen mode-classifier gradient backpropagated through policy features during a short editing phase (<500 steps). No steered samples are distilled. The retain term is data replay: desired-mode demos with the original imitation loss. It is not velocity distillation toward a frozen old policy on its own trajectories, which is what R_old does. So it is only a loose analogue of L_fit + beta*R_old. Cite in the consolidation related work; low threat.
checks.corrected_description: Post-hoc policy editing. A frozen mode classifier's cross-entropy gradient is backpropagated through policy features on masked undesired-mode samples. A retain loss uses the original BC/velocity-matching objective on desired-mode data. The classifier is discarded, so inference is unchanged.

checks.title: Test-Time Gradient Guidance of Flow Policies in Reinforcement Learning (QGF)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2606.11087 (9 Jun 2026), Zhou, Peng, Xu, Li, Springenberg, Frans, Levine. Read the method, analysis and limitations. Confirmed: 'policy optimization entirely at test time'; target pi proportional to pi_hat*exp(Q)^{1/beta}; the gradient is taken at the single large-Euler-step estimate; noisy-action gradients are biased and BPTT is high-variance; it scales with model size. It is critic-gradient guidance: a score plus a grad-Q heuristic. It does not learn a cost-to-go in generative time via HJB. The proposal says 'An arbitrary learned compatibility score does not become a value function because we take its gradient'. So QGF is a guidance baseline for settings with rewards, not 'the simplest instance of the value reader'. It needs an offline RL critic trained on large datasets, which the proposal's few-experience, cue-driven setting lacks. Its analysis of clean-estimate vs noisy-z_t gradients is useful for any reader queried with z_t.
checks.corrected_description: Test-time RL for BC-trained flow policies: at each denoising step it adds 1/beta * grad Q evaluated at the one-step Euler clean estimate, avoiding both biased noisy-action gradients and BPTT.

checks.title: Q-VGM: Q-Guided Value-Gradient Matching for Offline-to-Online RL of Flow-Matching VLA Policies
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2606.08015 v5 (17 Sep 2026), Wang, Zhang, Liu, Mao, Wang, Mu. Read the abstract, method and results. The quotes and numbers are correct: LIBERO 84.6 -> 90.7 offline and 98.4 online; real bimanual tasks 66.7 -> 98.3. It is RL fine-tuning of pi0.5's action expert: late-step velocity targets derived from grad Q, fitted by velocity matching. It is not memory consolidation. The analogy to Eq. 23 path distillation is loose: the targets are local corrections from a critic, not velocities of a teacher's path. Cite only if the value reader is pursued.
checks.corrected_description: Offline-to-online RL for FM VLAs. A late-denoising-step approximation turns clean-action critic gradients into local velocity targets, which fine-tune the action expert by velocity matching without BPTT. The chunk critic is trained with IQL offline and TD online.

checks.title: DynaGuide: Steering Diffusion Polices with Active Dynamic Guidance
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2506.13922 v2, NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv comment), authors Du and Song. Read the abstract and intro. The quotes are exact. The external module is a learned dynamics model scored against goal observations; it is not an experience store. The search agent's 'storage/predictor' description is inaccurate: DynaGuide separates a dynamics model from the policy. The proposal says explicitly that its residual 'is not an independent world model'. Useful background for the lineage of external guidance at denoising steps (alongside LPB, ReGuide and TraceFlow), not a threat.
checks.corrected_description: Classifier-style guidance of a frozen diffusion policy at denoising steps, using a separate DinoV2-latent dynamics model scored against any number of positive/negative goal observations.

checks.title: FAR: Failure-Aware Retry for Test-Time Recovery and Continual Policy Improvement
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2607.01111 (1 Jul 2026), Hao, Syed, Ichnowski, Schneider. Read the method, results and limitations. Confirmed: an IQL value drop marks failure chunks; contrastive pairs feed a Diffusion-DPO loss that 'only requires 5-10 gradient steps and can be completed within seconds'; retries use perturbations; replay buffers support advantage-weighted continual improvement. Limitation: 'diffusion policies trained from scratch in single-task settings'. It illustrates a direct test-time weight update. That kind of baseline (few-step fine-tuning of theta or LoRA on the same experiences) is missing from the proposal's Sec. 17 table and should be added in generic form. FAR itself needs an IQL critic and failure signals from the environment. Low novelty threat.
checks.corrected_description: Test-time preference fine-tuning (Diffusion-DPO surrogate) of a single-task diffusion policy from failure/value-ranked contrastive action pairs, plus perturbed retries. Recovered successes feed IQL-style advantage-weighted continual training.

checks.title: FlowCorrect: Efficient Interactive Correction of Generative Flow Policies for Robotic Manipulation
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2602.22056 v3, IROS 2026 (arXiv comment), authors Welte, Shi, Wolf, Gilles, Rayyes. Read the method and results. Confirmed: f = f_theta + alpha_t v_DeltaTheta with a LoRA head adapter plus a small gate; the flow-edit quote is exact; logged noise x0 is reused; anchor successes are kept; 'online, incremental' updates; 80% on previously failed cases; removing the gate drops ID success 65.00% -> 54.17%. Medium is fair. It overlaps the proposal's gradient-written additive velocity correction, learned from a few experiences, read at every solver step, with retention via anchor replay. Mechanistically it is closer to the proposal's internal-TTT arm (LoRA inside the head) than to the external associative reader. It has no meta-learning, cue association or consolidation. Corrections: the gate is an observation-conditioned 'where to apply the edit' switch. It is neither the proposal's centering (exact reset) nor its consolidation/reset gate. The flow edit builds same-seed velocity targets from the logged noise, the kind of seed reuse the proposal cautions about. Good baseline for the few-corrections regime.
checks.corrected_description: Frozen ManiFlow policy plus a LoRA velocity delta, trained online from sparse relative human corrections. The loss matches intermediate ODE velocities (from the logged noise) to targets that reach the corrected action. A separately trained binary gate applies the edit only in corrected regions, and anchor successes limit drift.

checks.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning (WIZARD)
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2606.07217 (5 Jun 2026), authors Bianchi, Yousefi, Sampieri, Roberti, Rigazio, Galasso, Franco. Read the abstract and method. Confirmed: a single forward pass maps instruction + demo video to LoRA for a frozen pi0.5, with no action labels or test-time optimization; weight-space reconstruction against a repository of expert LoRAs; up to ~14x on unseen tasks, from very low base rates (pi0.5 is at 0% on unseen suites). It is an amortized hypernetwork alternative to gradient-based writes, worth one sentence when justifying the writer (Sec. 5, [17]). It writes internal weights once per task, with no persistent causal memory, velocity reader or consolidation.
checks.corrected_description: Hypernetwork meta-learning that predicts task-specific LoRA weights for a frozen VLA from a language instruction and a short demo video, trained by regression onto a bank of expert LoRA adapters.

checks.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2305.16860 v2, TMLR 02/2024, authors Benton, Deligiannidis, Doucet. Read Sec. 1-3. Theorem 1: W2 <= eps*exp(int L_t), where L_t is the Lipschitz constant of the approximate field and eps is the L2 error along the true flow. That is the same structure as Eq. 27 (Lipschitz of the new field, velocity error on old-policy trajectories). The quote about Lipschitz constants that 'explode' is exact. Benton notes the result is 'similar in content to Proposition 3 in Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (2023)'. I checked that Prop. 3 (ICLR 2023, arXiv 2209.15571): W2^2 <= e^{1+2K} H(v). VGG-Flow Prop. 4 is a third instance. So Eqs. 27-28 should be credited as a standard coupling-plus-Groenwall bound. The proposal's constant (e^{2L}-1)/(2L) is marginally tighter. The time-varying-L_t caveat strengthens the proposal's own remark that 'a large Lipschitz constant makes the bound loose'. The proposal calls this only 'a limited mathematical retention statement', so the threat is low: it calls for citation, not a change of claims.
checks.corrected_description: Deterministic-sampling FM error bound W2(pi_hat_1, pi_1) <= eps*exp(int_0^1 L_t dt), via Alekseev-Groebner and Groenwall, with a time-varying Lipschitz constant (needed when data lack full support), plus bounds on L_t under Gaussian smoothing.

checks.title: Fine-Tuning of Continuous-Time Diffusion Models as Entropy-Regularized Control
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2402.15194 v2 (Feb 2024, marked 'Under review'), Uehara ... Biancalani, Levine. Read the abstract, intro and related work. The quotes are exact, including 'not suitable for purely ODE-based models' and regularization 'with respect to both a drift term and an initial distribution'. Standard SOC background for why tilt semantics need an initial-distribution term, or else the memoryless schedule of Adjoint Matching. The proposal already declines to claim KL semantics for its deterministic readers. App. C's Gaussian-source choice concerns the direct memory reader; it would not stop a separate value reader from learning a source. So 'rules out the former' is too strong.
checks.corrected_description: Reward fine-tuning of diffusion SDEs as entropy-regularized control against the pretrained model. It optimizes both the drift and the initial distribution to preserve the pretrained bridges and reduce reward collapse; it is not applicable to purely ODE models.

checks.title: D-Flow: Differentiating through Flows for Controlled Generation
checks.why: Exists: arXiv 2402.14017 v2, ICML 2024 (arXiv comment), authors Ben-Hamu, Puny, Gat, Karrer, Singer, Lipman. Read the abstract and discussion. The quotes are exact. The implicit-prior argument applies 'for Diffusion/FM models trained with Gaussian probability paths'; the stated main limitation is long runtime. A sensible ablation for the optional Sec. 9 path-energy reader: optimize z_0 versus interior nodes. That reader is optional and must first beat the direct reader, so the threat is low.
checks.corrected_description: Controlled generation by optimizing the source noise through a differentiable FM/diffusion ODE solve. Under Gaussian paths, gradients are implicitly projected onto the data manifold. Runtime is the main limitation.

gap.landscape_summary:
By September 2026, fast-weight and test-time-training (TTT) memory is a mainstream way to build sequence models, and there is a unifying theory for it. Architectures include Titans, Atlas, Miras, LaCT, TTT-E2E, In-Place TTT, Gated DeltaNet and MesaNet. The theory works that treat every memory, softmax attention included, as a choice of regression objective, retention regulariser and optimiser are Test-time regression and Miras (plus the Irie & Gershman TMLR review, arXiv 2508.08435). Equivalence results cut against the proposal's framing that "history acts through updated weights, not context tokens":
- A linear layer trained by gradient descent is exactly unnormalised attention over its training patterns (Irie et al. 2022).
- Gradient-written fast-weight layers stacked on a transformer are linear attention (Clark et al. 2022).
- One linear self-attention layer can implement a gradient-descent step on a regression loss (von Oswald et al. 2023).
The proposal's own [4] adds to these. On the empirical side, deep nonlinear memories beat linear ones as contexts get long: Titans' deep-memory ablation, and TTT-MLP over Gated DeltaNet on 63-second videos (the order flips on 18-second videos). The Irie & Gershman review still reports that "the transformer still outperforms FWPs on precise retrieval tasks by a large margin".

How the proposal's contributions (a)-(e) sit against this work:

(a) Reading fast memory during denoising already exists in generative models. One-Minute Video puts TTT-MLP layers inside a pretrained DiT, recomputed on every forward pass. LaCT's autoregressive video diffusion writes fast weights only on clean, committed chunks and reads them while denoising the next noisy chunk — the closest structural precedent. In robotics, RoboTTT (already cited) does this internally. Gated Memory Policy (CoRL 2026) reads a history memory through a gated residual inside a diffusion transformer at every denoising step.

(b) A weight-space residual on the flow field learned from robot experience is pre-empted by FlowCorrect (2026): f_{theta+dtheta} = f_theta + v_dtheta, a gated LoRA trained on sparse human corrections by matching intermediate ODE velocities, with the backbone frozen. The idea of a temporary, centred and discarded fast adaptation around slow weights goes back to Hinton & Plaut (1987; fast weights decaying to zero on top of slow weights) and to MbPA (2018; local gradient adaptation with a proximal pull to the base parameters, discarded after each prediction).

(c) Meta-trained gradient writers for an external MLP memory are established: MNM (2019, including RL), Clark's Fast Weight Layers (2022), and TTT-E2E (2025, meta-learned initialisation through gradients of gradients). Writer design has moved well beyond the proposal's single gradient step on a reconstruction loss:
- delta rule and gating (Schlag 2021; Gated DeltaNet);
- momentum plus data-dependent weight decay (Titans, whose ablations show these two components contribute most);
- retention as a regulariser (Miras);
- Muon and large-chunk updates (LaCT);
- locally optimal solves (MesaNet) and sliding-window optimisation (Atlas);
- Fisher-weighted elastic anchors (Elastic TTT);
- learned multi-pass local rules (LM Sleep);
- task-aligned instead of reconstruction objectives (In-Place TTT).
One design consequence is specific to this proposal. Its centring gives r = 0 exactly at W = W_0, so any forgetting should retain toward W_0 rather than decay toward 0 as in Titans or Gated DeltaNet. That is Elastic TTT's "global anchor", which that paper found worse than an EMA anchor in its streaming setting.

(d) Fast-to-slow consolidation with re-initialisation is conceptually pre-empted in language models by Nested Learning's Continuum Memory System: fast levels are re-initialised to a meta-learned initial state, and knowledge flows back through that state. Fast-weight "sleep" consolidation also appears (LM Sleep, 2026). For diffusion models, Masip et al. show that endpoint-only generative replay causes "a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities", while distilling the teacher along the whole reverse process fixes it. This bears directly on the proposal's L_end versus L_path/R_old choice. Complementary learning systems theory (McClelland 1995; Kumaran, Hassabis & McClelland 2016) is the canonical frame for the whole lifecycle and is missing from the proposal's biology section.

(e) The retention bound W2 <= C * integral ||v_new - v_old||^2 is a restatement of known flow-matching error bounds: Benton et al., W2 <= eps * exp(integral L_t dt), and Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden, Prop. 3. It should be credited, and could be tightened with time-varying Lipschitz constants.

Where this leaves the proposal: each of its pieces has close prior art. The defensible novelty is the specific combination — an external, W_0-centred fast-weight residual on the velocity field, a meta-trained writer across accepted backbone checkpoints, and flow-matching distillation with replay plus reset gates — together with a controlled comparison against internal TTT (LaCT, In-Place TTT or TTT-E2E style), gated history attention (Gated Memory Policy) and a LoRA flow-edit (FlowCorrect).

Two capacity warnings bear on the proposal's 1,072-parameter memory:
- TTT-E2E: "when updating only 1 or 3 layers, our method does not scale with context length".
- Schlag et al. 2021: the "overcapacity regime" once the number of associations exceeds the key dimension.

Other items whose titles were confirmed but which are left out of the list as background or lower relevance:
- Read but not listed: Neural Episodic Control (1703.01988), Ba et al. 2016 (1610.06258), MesaNet (2506.05233), Atlas (2505.23735), DeltaNet (2406.06484), Learning Fast and Slow for LLMs (2605.12484, where naive fast-to-slow distillation "plateaus well below" joint training), When Robots Sleep (2606.17493), FearNet (1711.10563).
- Abstract only: Memory-Conditioned Flow-Matching for PDE rollouts (2602.06689), FlowEdit (2606.20518).
- Only the title was confirmed: Longhorn (2407.14207), CLS-ER (2201.12604), DualNet (2110.00175), Schlag, Munkhdalai & Schmidhuber's Fast Weight Memory (2011.07831).
- Schmidhuber 1992 (Neural Computation, DOI 10.1162/neco.1992.4.1.131) was checked through Crossref metadata only; the full text was not read.

papers.title: FlowCorrect: Efficient Interactive Correction of Generative Flow Policies for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors_year: Welte, Shi, Wolf, Gilles, Rayyes, 2026 (arXiv 2602.22056v3)
papers.what_it_does: Keeps a pretrained flow-matching manipulation policy (ManiFlow DiTX) frozen and learns a LoRA adapter (~10k params) on the head plus a small gate from sparse human relative corrections: 'f_{theta+dtheta}(x_n,k_n,c) = f_theta(x_n,k_n,c) + alpha_t v_dtheta(x_n,k_n,c)'. Training uses a flow-edit loss that 'directly edits the continuous-time flow by matching intermediate ODE velocities to a target field that would reach the corrected trajectory', with logged noise x0 and a few uncorrected 'anchor' rollouts. Real UR10 results: 'With a low correction budget, FlowCorrect achieves an 80% success rate on previously failed cases while preserving performance on previously solved scenarios'. Full retraining did better on the hard cases (e.g. 40/40 vs 32/40 on Pick-and-Place). Limitation stated: conflicting nearby edits cause over-correction.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Directly pre-empts contribution (b) and partly (a). It is a residual on the velocity field, learned from robot experience, applied at every ODE step, zero at initialisation, with the base flow unchanged where the gate is off (Sec 4, Eq 4-5). The differences left for the proposal are: meta-trained one-shot gradient writes instead of 500-epoch adapter fitting, cue-dependent associative recall, explicit W_0 centring, and a consolidation/reset lifecycle. Its failure mode (one observation-agnostic update overriding nearby edits) is exactly what a cue-conditioned associative memory should fix, and the proposal should test that. It belongs in Sec 21 and as a baseline for the direct residual reader under matched experience budgets.

papers.title: Gated Memory Policy: In-Context Memorization and Adaptation
papers.authors_year: Gao, Liu, Li, Song, 2026 (CoRL 2026; arXiv 2604.18933)
papers.what_it_does: A diffusion-transformer visuomotor policy that reads cached history (past action chunks plus one pooled image token per chunk) through a lightweight cross-attention module inside the DiT. The output is added through a binary gate: 'z_bar = mu_t h_{t:t+h} + z_{t:t+h} is passed to the feed-forward layer', so mu=0 recovers the memoryless path. History actions are noised to level k-1 when denoising at level k, so the memory read depends on the denoising step. Supports 'in-context adaptation based on the outcomes of multiple past trials'. Reports +30.1% over long-history baselines on its MemMimic benchmark and +26.6% over VLA baselines on MIKASA-Robo. Limitation: a finite attention window.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Strongest recent robotics competitor for the 'history tokens/retrieval' baseline arm (Sec 17). It already achieves a gated, exactly-removable memory read at every denoising step and cross-trial adaptation, i.e. (a) and much of the reset property in (b), through attention rather than fast weights. Experiment B's delayed cue-to-action associations overlap MemMimic's cross-trial tasks. The superiority claim for an external fast-weight reader must beat GMP at matched memory and compute. Its validation-calibrated gate is also a template for the proposal's acceptance gates.

papers.title: Test-Time Training Done Right (LaCT)
papers.authors_year: Zhang, Bi, Hong, Zhang, Luan, Yang, Sunkavalli, Freeman, Tan, 2025 (arXiv 2505.23884)
papers.what_it_does: Large-chunk TTT (2K-1M tokens per update) with nonlinear SwiGLU fast weights up to 40% of model size. Writer variants: GD, momentum 'M <- beta M + sum eta_i grad; W <- L2norm(W - M)', and Muon; 'Muon variant consistently outperforms our Momentum variant'. Applied to novel view synthesis, language modelling, and a 14B autoregressive video diffusion model. In the video model 'it applies fast weights to each chunk sequentially while only updating fast weights on clean chunks. This simple strategy ensures that each denoising operation only accesses previously cleaned frames.'
papers.relation_to_proposal: The closest architectural precedent for (a) outside robotics: a persistent fast-weight memory written only from committed (clean) outputs and read by the generator at every denoising step of the next sample. This is the proposal's write-after-decision, read-during-generation schedule, but internal to the transformer. It weakens any claim that reading memory throughout denoising is new. It also shows momentum/Muon writers clearly beat plain GD, which bears on Eq 8's single GD step. A LaCT-style internal layer with a clean-write/noisy-read mask is the natural internal-TTT arm of the factorial in Sec 8.

papers.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context (TTT-E2E)
papers.authors_year: Tandon, Dalal, Li, Koceja, Rod, ..., Choi, Sun, 2025 (arXiv 2512.23675)
papers.what_it_does: Treats long-context language modelling as continual learning. At test time it takes gradient steps (next-token loss) on the MLP layers of the last 1/4 of blocks. At training time 'we improve the model's initialization for learning at test time via meta-learning ... through gradients of gradients'. Adds 'a static, second MLP layer as a "safe" storage for pre-trained knowledge'. Ablation: 'when updating only 1 or 3 layers, our method does not scale with context length'. It contrasts itself with Clark et al., who add fast weights 'only to the end of the model instead of interleaving them', and reports that 'interleaving proves to be critical'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts the meta-learning part of (c): the same outer loop (differentiate future loss through inner gradient writes to learn W_0; Sec 7, Eq 12). Two findings hit the proposal's design directly. (1) Fast weights attached only at the end underperform interleaved internal ones, evidence against the external-readout hypothesis that the proposal must address in the reader factorial. (2) Very small fast-weight capacity (1-3 layers) failed to scale, a warning for the 1,072-parameter memory. The frozen 'safe' MLP is an analogue of the proposal's slow/fast split. It is a strong internal-TTT comparison.

papers.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
