papers.authors_year: Behrouz, Zhong, Mirrokni, 2024/2025 (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv 2501.00663)
papers.what_it_does: A deep MLP neural memory trained online on the associative loss ||M(k_t) - v_t||^2. The writer uses 'surprise' with momentum and a data-dependent forgetting gate: 'M_t = (1 - alpha_t) M_{t-1} + S_t, S_t = eta_t S_{t-1} - theta_t grad l(M_{t-1}; x_t)'. It compares three integration locations: Memory as Context, as Gate, and as Layer. Ablation: 'the greatest contribution comes from weight decay, momentum, convolution, and persistent memory'. Table 5 shows linear memory at 85.34 and no weight decay at 85.60 on long-context accuracy, versus 92.68 for the full module. MAC beats MAL on long-context NIAH.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Bears on the writer design in (c) (Sec 5, Eq 7-8). The proposal's writer is Titans without momentum or forgetting, and Titans' ablations say those two pieces matter most. Titans' MAC/MAG/MAL comparison is a precedent for the proposal's reader-location factorial (Sec 8). Caution: Titans' decay pulls M toward 0. Under the proposal's centring (r = 0 only at W = W_0), forgetting must be retention toward W_0, otherwise decay biases the velocity even with no experience written. Momentum+decay writers should be ablated.

papers.title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures (Hope / Continuum Memory System)
papers.authors_year: Behrouz, Razaviyayn, Zhong, Mirrokni, 2025 (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv 2512.24695)
papers.what_it_does: Recasts models as nested optimisation levels with different update frequencies. Proposes a Continuum Memory System (CMS): a chain of MLP blocks, each updated every C^(l) steps. In the nested variant 'the initial state of the MLP block in level s+1 is meta-learned in level s' and at the end of its context 'the value of the memory will be re-initialized to theta_0'. Forgotten knowledge can be recovered because 'the knowledge transfer through backpropagation (for their initial state) can circle back the knowledge'. Motivated explicitly by online (synaptic) versus offline (systems) consolidation. Hope beats in-context learning, EWC and InCA on continual-learning class-incremental tasks built on Llama-3 backbones.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The conceptual pre-emption of (d) and the refresh logic in Sec 14: a multi-timescale MLP memory whose fast levels are reset to a slowly learned, meta-learned initialisation, with knowledge moving from fast to slow levels. The proposal's mechanism differs: flow-matching behaviour distillation with replay and validation-gated acceptance, rather than backprop into the initial state, applied to action generation. It should be cited as the closest general-ML statement of a fast-memory/slow-init/reset lifecycle, and the distinction made explicit.

papers.title: Metalearned Neural Memory
papers.authors_year: Munkhdalai, Sordoni, Wang, Trischler, 2019 (NeurIPS 2019; arXiv 1907.09720)
papers.what_it_does: An external memory 'conceptualize[d] ... as a rapidly adaptable function that we parameterize as a deep neural network. Reading ... amounts to pushing an input (the key vector) through the function ... Writing to memory means changing the function'. Keys are bound to values either 'by applying one step of modulated gradient descent to the memory function's parameters' or by a learned local update rule that 'reduces the error between the memory function's predicted output in response to the write-in key and the target value'. Controller and memory are meta-trained end-to-end on algorithmic tasks, bAbI and maze RL.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Prior art for the core of (c) and Sec 5: an external small MLP whose weights are the persistent memory, written by a one-shot gradient step on a cue-to-content regression loss with slowly meta-learned interfaces, including in RL. Eq 6-8 plus Sec 7 is essentially MNM with the readout routed into the flow-matching velocity. Its learned local rule is the direct precedent for the proposal's learned-loss writer alternative [17]. It should be cited, and the proposal's novelty restated as the reader location and lifecycle, not the writer.

papers.title: Memory-based Parameter Adaptation (MbPA)
papers.authors_year: Sprechmann, Jayakumar, Rae, Pritzel, Badia, Uria, Vinyals, Hassabis, Pascanu, Blundell, 2018 (ICLR 2018; arXiv 1802.10542)
papers.what_it_does: Explicitly inspired by complementary learning systems. It stores examples in an episodic memory and, at test time, takes a few gradient steps on the output network using retrieved neighbours, with a proximal term '-beta(theta - theta_x)' pulling back toward the slow parameters. 'The local adaptation is discarded after the model produces its output'. It shows 'an attention-based procedure is a particular case of local adaptation', since attention fits a constant function locally.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts the centred, resettable fast-adaptation idea in (b), and the pairing of an explicit episodic store B with temporary weight changes (Sec 3, Sec 14 item 4). The proposal's centring and reset are a persistent-across-decisions variant of MbPA's always-reset local adaptation. MbPA's attention-as-special-case result is also relevant to the internal-versus-external debate. An MbPA-style baseline (temporary local gradient adaptation of the velocity reader from the same replay store B) would isolate the value of persistent meta-trained writes.

papers.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
papers.authors_year: Masip, Rodriguez, Tuytelaars, van de Ven, 2023/2024 (CoLLAs 2024; arXiv 2311.14028)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that 'standard generative replay applied to diffusion models results in a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities'. In standard replay, knowledge from the previous-task model reaches the student 'only at the endpoint of the reverse process'. The proposed generative distillation instead matches the teacher's noise predictions at noised teacher samples, transferring knowledge 'at each point of the reverse trajectory'. This substantially improves continual learning at modest extra cost.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Directly bears on (d) and (e). Endpoint re-pairing with fresh noise (Eq 21-22, L_end) is the flow-matching analogue of standard generative replay, which this paper found catastrophic for diffusion models. Its fix (distil teacher predictions along the trajectory) matches the proposal's R_old retention term (Eq 25) and path distillation (Eq 23). It is prior evidence on the proposal's falsifiable 'endpoint ~ path distill' question and should be cited in Sec 11-13. Generative distillation should be the retention baseline.

papers.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
papers.authors_year: Benton, Deligiannidis, Doucet, 2023/2024 (TMLR 02/2024; arXiv 2305.16860)
papers.what_it_does: Theorem 1: 'W2(pi_hat_1, pi_1) <= eps exp{int_0^1 L_t dt}', where eps is the L2 velocity error and L_t a time-varying Lipschitz constant of the approximate flow, proved with the Alekseev-Groebner formula and Groenwall. It notes the result 'is similar in content to Proposition 3 in Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (2023)'; the difference is the time-varying Lipschitz constant, 'required in practice since in many cases L_t explodes as t -> 0 or 1'. It also bounds the Lipschitz constant of the true velocity field.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts the retention bound in (e): Eq 27-28 (W2^2 <= C_L R_old with C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L), Appendix B.1) is a same-coupling Groenwall bound of the same type. It should be credited to Benton et al. and Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden. Benton's time-varying L_t is needed because the proposal's constant-L assumption can fail near t=0 or t=1 for low-dimensional action targets. The bound's novelty lies only in applying it to retention during consolidation.

papers.title: It's All Connected: A Journey Through Test-Time Memorization, Attentional Bias, Retention, and Online Optimization (Miras)
papers.authors_year: Behrouz, Razaviyayn, Zhong, Mirrokni, 2025 (arXiv 2504.13173)
papers.what_it_does: Recasts Transformers, Titans and linear RNNs as associative memories defined by (i) memory architecture, (ii) attentional-bias objective, (iii) retention gate and (iv) learning algorithm. It 'reinterpret[s] forgetting mechanisms ... as a form of retention l2-regularization' in a Learning-Retaining view: W_t = argmin l_tilde(W; k_t, v_t) + Ret_t(W, W_{t-1}), with local plus global retention. It proposes KL, elastic-net and Bregman retention gates, and the models Moneta, Yaad and Memora.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Gives the proposal a principled vocabulary and design space for the writer and forgetting choices it defers ('a decay or proximal penalty may help adaptation but also erases information', Sec 5). In Miras terms the proposal's one-step writer is L2 bias with no retention, and its centred design calls for global retention toward W_0. The attentional-bias view also formalises that attention and the proposal's MLP memory differ in objective and architecture, not in kind.

papers.title: Test-time regression: a unifying framework for designing sequence models with associative memory
papers.authors_year: Wang, Shi, Fox, 2025 (arXiv 2501.12352)
papers.what_it_does: Casts associative recall as memorisation-by-regression plus retrieval. 'Prominent layers, including linear attention, state-space models, fast-weight programmers, online learners, and softmax attention, arise as special cases defined by three design choices: the regression weights, the regressor function class, and the test-time optimization algorithm.' It shows 'softmax attention with QKNorm is a locally-constant nonparametric regressor' and derives higher-order attention.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Theory relevant to whether an external fast-weight MLP differs from attention (Sec 6 and 21, [4]). Under this framework, attention over history tokens and the proposal's gradient-written tanh-MLP are two regressors in one design space: nonparametric local-constant versus parametric MLP fitted by one GD step with uniform weights. The comparison the proposal should make is therefore about regression choices (capacity, weighting, optimiser) at matched budget, not tokens versus weights. It supports the proposal's cautious non-separation stance and suggests explicit writer ablations.

papers.title: The Dual Form of Neural Networks Revisited: Connecting Test Time Predictions to Training Patterns via Spotlights of Attention
papers.authors_year: Irie, Csordas, Schmidhuber, 2022 (ICML 2022; arXiv 2202.05798)
papers.what_it_does: Proves that 'Linear layers in neural networks (NNs) trained by gradient descent can be expressed as a key-value memory system which stores all training datapoints and the initial weights, and produces outputs using unnormalised dot attention over the entire training experience' (Proposition 1). It uses this to visualise which training patterns drive test-time predictions.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Applies exactly to the proposal's fast memory. In f_W(q) = tanh(qA+b)B + d_0 (Eq 6), gradient writes to the output layer B, d_0 are equivalent to W_0's output plus unnormalised dot attention of the current query's tanh features over stored write-time features, with error-signal values. Only the A, b writes break the equivalence. So the claim that 'history acts through updated weights, not context tokens' (Sec 1) is largely an implementation distinction, and a kernelised linear-attention reader over stored (cue, error) pairs is a principled matched baseline. It should be cited alongside [4].

papers.title: Meta-Learning Fast Weight Language Models
papers.authors_year: Clark, Guu, Chang, Pasupat, Hinton, Norouzi, 2022 (arXiv 2212.02475)
papers.what_it_does: Fast Weight Layers (FWLs) give the benefits of dynamic evaluation 'much more efficiently by expressing gradient updates as linear attention'. FWLs 'are added on top of the transformer after the last attention layer', and the fast-weight initialisation is meta-trained so 'the model learns to make good use of gradient updates'. It improves perplexity over the base LM.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A precedent for an external, gradient-written, meta-trained fast-weight readout attached after a slow backbone: the proposal's direct reader in another modality. It also shows the gradient-written layer is linear attention, which weakens any expressive-separation claim. TTT-E2E later reports this end-only placement underperforms interleaving, the key empirical risk for the proposal's external-reader hypothesis (Sec 2 and 8).

papers.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
papers.authors_year: Dalal, Koceja, Hussein, Xu, ..., Sun, Wang, 2025 (CVPR 2025; arXiv 2504.05298)
papers.what_it_does: Adds TTT-MLP layers (fast weights = two-layer MLP updated by a gradient step on the reconstruction loss ||f(theta_K x; W) - theta_V x||^2) into a pretrained CogVideo-X 5B diffusion transformer. Inputs are gated: 'gate(TTT, X; alpha) = tanh(alpha) (x) TTT(X) + X', with alpha initialised to 0.1 'to avoid this degradation' of the pretrained model. TTT-MLP leads Gated DeltaNet, Mamba 2 and sliding-window attention by 34 Elo on 63-second videos. On 18-second videos, however, 'Gated DeltaNet performs the best'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: An existing case of fast-weight memory read at every denoising step of a pretrained diffusion model (a), though internal and recomputed each forward pass from the current noisy tokens rather than persistent across decisions. Its near-zero gated insertion is an alternative to the proposal's exact centring (Eq 4) that it should discuss. Its result that nonlinear fast weights win only at longer contexts, while linear gated-delta memories win at shorter ones, is directly relevant to a 1-16-experience regime (Experiment B).

papers.title: Fast Spatial Memory with Elastic Test-Time Training
papers.authors_year: Ma, Yu, Zhen, Yang, Chai, et al., 2026 (arXiv 2604.07350)
papers.what_it_does: Notes that LaCT's 'fully plastic inference-time updates remain vulnerable to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting'. It adds an EWC-style consolidation operator on the fast weights, 'theta_{c+1} = theta'_c - lambda F_c (.) (theta'_c - theta*_c)', with an online Fisher/MAS/SI importance estimate. Three anchor policies are compared: Global ('anchors remain fixed to initialization', which 'degenerates into an importance-weighted l2 regularizer ... similar to weight decay'), Streaming, and Streaming-EMA. 'Streaming-EMA is the best practice.'
papers.relation_to_proposal: The most direct evidence on the proposal's deferred forgetting/proximal choice (Sec 5) and on the stability side of (e). The proposal's exact reset needs retention toward W_0, which is the 'global anchor' this paper found inferior to EMA anchors in streaming use. So centring and good streaming memory may trade off, and the proposal should test elastic and EMA-anchored writers against global-anchor and no-retention writers. It also imports EWC into fast weights, overlapping the proposal's EWC / Progress & Compress comparison.

papers.title: In-Place Test-Time Training
papers.authors_year: Feng, Luo, Hua, Zhang, He, Huang, Cai, 2026 (ICLR 2026; arXiv 2604.06169)
papers.what_it_does: Makes TTT a 'drop-in' enhancement for pretrained LLMs by treating 'the final projection matrix of the ubiquitous MLP blocks as its adaptable fast weights'. It replaces 'TTT's generic reconstruction objective with a tailored, theoretically-grounded objective explicitly aligned with the Next-Token-Prediction task', using chunk-wise updates. A 4B model improves on contexts up to 128k.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The most natural internal-TTT arm when the flow-matching transformer theta is pretrained and frozen: fast weights in existing MLP down-projections, no new layer. Its critique of 'misaligned fast weight objectives' applies to the proposal's reconstruction-style association loss (Eq 7). That supports testing a task-aligned writer, such as a velocity-aligned loss or the learned-loss writer [17], early rather than 'only after the association writer has a working baseline'.

papers.title: Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference
papers.authors_year: Lee, McLeish, Goldstein, Fanti, 2026 (arXiv 2605.26099)
papers.what_it_does: 'A sleep-like consolidation mechanism in which a model periodically converts recent context into persistent fast weights before clearing its key-value cache.' During sleep, N offline recurrent passes update SSM fast weights 'through a learned local rule', trained end-to-end by backpropagating through the process. It finds that 'vanilla State-Space Models (SSMs) such as Gated Delta Nets (GDNs) fail despite having enough fast weight capacity' as reasoning depth grows, and that longer sleep helps.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Relevant to (c) and (d): a biologically framed periodic consolidation with context clearing and a learned write rule. Its main finding, that the bottleneck is the computation spent turning experience into weights rather than capacity, questions the proposal's single inner gradient step per experience (Eq 8). It suggests a multi-step or learned write during idle periods as an ablation. Note that the 'consolidation' here is context-to-fast-weights, not fast-to-slow.

papers.title: AURA: Action-Gated Memory for Robot Policies at Constant VRAM
papers.what_it_does: A constant-size fast-weight memory 'wrapped around a frozen vision-language-action backbone'. It writes by a TTT-Linear/delta-rule step with a learned forgetting gate, 'W_t = (1 - alpha) W_{t-1} - eta grad L_inner', and reads 'o_t = q_t^T W_t' into an action head. A learned gate fires writes only on action-prediction surprise. It matches the best O(1) baseline at 5-9x fewer writes. On OpenVLA-OFT/LIBERO-Long 'the gate does not hurt success' (0.233), and the author states the memory 'does not by itself raise robot success'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A robotics precedent for an external, gradient-written (delta-rule plus decay) fast-weight memory beside a frozen policy backbone with meta-learned write hyperparameters, overlapping (c) and the 'external memory, frozen theta' stance of Sec 4. It reads into the action head once rather than into the velocity at every denoising step, and has no consolidation. The evidence is weak (single author, synthetic benchmarks, no success gain), so cite it rather than use it as a baseline. Its surprise-gated writes are a relevant writer variant for bounded memory (Sec 5).

papers.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
papers.authors_year: Yang, Kautz, Hatamizadeh, 2024/2025 (ICLR 2025; arXiv 2412.06464)
papers.what_it_does: Combines the delta update rule with data-dependent gating: 'these mechanisms are complementary: gating enables rapid memory erasure while the delta rule facilitates targeted updates'. It provides a hardware-efficient parallel algorithm and beats Mamba2 and DeltaNet on language modelling, retrieval and long-context tasks. DeltaNet (Yang et al. 2024, arXiv 2406.06484) is the ungated parallel predecessor.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The standard linear fast-weight writer against which the proposal's nonlinear MLP memory (Eq 6-8) should be ablated. It isolates whether nonlinearity or the gating/erasure mechanism drives adaptation with 1-16 experiences, and One-Minute Video found Gated DeltaNet best at shorter contexts. Its erasure gate conflicts with exact W_0 centring unless erasure targets W_0.

papers.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
papers.authors_year: Schlag, Irie, Schmidhuber, 2021 (ICML 2021; arXiv 2102.11174)
papers.what_it_does: Shows 'the formal equivalence of linearised self-attention mechanisms and fast weight controllers from the early '90s' (Schmidhuber 1992). It infers 'a memory capacity limitation of recent linearised softmax attention variants' (an overcapacity regime once sequence length exceeds key dimension). It replaces additive outer products 'by a delta rule-like programming instruction, such that the FWP can more easily learn to correct the current mapping from keys to values'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Foundational to the proposal's framing and missing from its references. It establishes that fast-weight memories and (linear) attention are the same object, and that gradient steps on squared association error are delta-rule updates. The capacity analysis bears on the proposal's 16-dimensional cue and 32 hidden units: interference is expected as experiences accumulate before consolidation. Experiment D (10 or more task arrivals) should report capacity and overwrite curves.

papers.title: Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent
papers.authors_year: von Oswald, Niklasson, Randazzo, Sacramento, Mordvintsev, Zhmoginov, Vladymyrov, 2022/2023 (ICML 2023; arXiv 2212.07677)
papers.what_it_does: Gives 'a simple weight construction that shows the equivalence of data transformations induced by 1) a single linear self-attention layer and by 2) gradient-descent (GD) on a regression loss'. Trained transformers on regression tasks match or exceed GD, becoming 'mesa-optimizers'.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The converse of the dual-form result: attention over history tokens can implement the proposal's gradient writer inside the forward pass. So the history-token baseline (Sec 17) can in principle emulate a one-step association writer. A win for the fast-weight reader must come from compute or memory efficiency, persistence, or the lifecycle, not from computing something attention cannot. This supports the proposal's hedged position in Sec 1 and 21.

papers.title: Using Fast Weights to Deblur Old Memories
papers.authors_year: Hinton, Plaut, 1987 (Proc. 9th Annual Conf. Cognitive Science Society)
papers.what_it_does: Each connection has 'a slowly changing, plastic weight which stores long-term knowledge and a fast-changing, elastic weight which stores temporary knowledge and spontaneously decays towards zero'. 'The effective weight on the connection is the sum of these two', a 'temporary overlay of fast weights' on slow weights. Rehearsing a few old associations lets fast weights 'temporarily cancel out the changes in the slow weights caused by the subsequent learning'. (Scanned PDF; I read page 1 as an image.)
papers.relation_to_proposal: The original statement of the proposal's central structural idea in (b): a fast, resettable additive component on top of slow weights, zero at rest, so removing it recovers the slow system. It also uses fast weights to counteract interference from slow learning, relevant to the retention and refresh logic (Sec 13-14). It should be cited as the conceptual origin of fast and slow memory with centring and decay.

papers.title: Why there are complementary learning systems in the hippocampus and neocortex: insights from the successes and failures of connectionist models of learning and memory
papers.authors_year: McClelland, McNaughton, O'Reilly, 1995 (Psychological Review 102:419-457)
papers.what_it_does: Argues 'memories are first stored via synaptic changes in the hippocampal system, that these changes support reinstatement of recent memories in the neocortex, that neocortical synapses change a little on each reinstatement'. Connectionist models 'discover the structure in ensembles of items if learning of each item is gradual and interleaved'. 'The hippocampal system permits rapid learning of new items without disrupting this structure, and reinstatement of new memories interleaves them with others'. Catastrophic interference (McCloskey & Cohen) motivates this. Also confirmed through PubMed (PMID 7624455).
papers.relation_to_proposal: The canonical computational theory behind the proposal's whole lifecycle: fast associative store, slow structured learner, and interleaved replay to consolidate without interference (Sec 2, 11-14). Its absence from the biological-motivation section, which cites only rodent experiments [8-10] and Spens & Burgess [11], is a clear related-work gap. It also predicts the proposal's finding that replay is needed (old-task error 0.470 without replay versus about 1e-12 with it).

papers.title: What Learning Systems do Intelligent Agents Need? Complementary Learning Systems Theory Updated
papers.authors_year: Kumaran, Hassabis, McClelland, 2016 (Trends in Cognitive Sciences 20:512-534)
papers.what_it_does: Updates CLS theory. 'Replay allows goal-dependent weighting of experience statistics'. 'Recurrent activation of hippocampal traces can support some forms of generalization'. 'Neocortical learning can be rapid for information that is consistent with known structure'. It draws explicit links to AI agents (experience replay). Also confirmed through PubMed (PMID 27315762).
papers.relation_to_proposal: Directly relevant to the proposal's split between reusable skills (consolidate) and non-context-identifiable facts (keep episodically; Sec 1, App B.4). It suggests two design levers the proposal does not use: prioritised or goal-weighted replay during consolidation, and faster slow-learning for schema-consistent updates. It also supports the optional recurrent Hopfield-style recall (Eq 13) as a generalisation mechanism. It should be cited in Sec 2 and 11.

papers.title: Unsupervised Predictive Memory in a Goal-Directed Agent (MERLIN)
papers.authors_year: Wayne, Hung, Amos, Mirza, ..., Hassabis, Lillicrap, 2018 (arXiv 1803.10760)
papers.what_it_does: Shows 'memory is not enough; it is critical that the right information be stored in the right format'. MERLIN's memory formation 'is guided by a process of predictive modeling'. Memory agents trained purely end-to-end (RL-MEM) fail when delays exceed the BPTT window: 'Memory systems trained end-to-end for performance ... were less able to learn to write essential information into memory', and extending the window did not rescue some tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Bears on the writer-training design in (c) (Sec 5 and 7). It supports the proposal's choice of a local association loss with a fixed pretrained target encoder rather than purely end-to-end writes. It also warns that meta-training the query encoder and reader only by differentiating future action loss through unrolled second-order writes will not scale to long gaps between write and use (Experiments D-E, lifelong deployment). The proposal should state its truncation horizon and add an auxiliary predictive write objective as an ablation.

checks.title: FlowCorrect: Efficient Interactive Correction of Generative Flow Policies for Robotic Manipulation
checks.why: Verified against the arXiv abs page and the full v3 text (arXiv comment: 'Accepted at IROS 2026'). The quotes are accurate: 'f_{θ+Δθ}(x_n,k_n,c) = f_θ(x_n,k_n,c) + α_t v_Δθ(x_n,k_n,c)'; the objective 'directly edits the continuous-time flow by matching intermediate ODE velocities to a target field that would reach the corrected trajectory'; about 10k LoRA parameters on the DiTX MLP head; a gate thresholded to binary at inference; 10 corrections per failure case plus 5 anchor rollouts; 500 epochs, about 30 minutes (Table II). On the hard cases (Table I), retraining beats FlowCorrect on Pick-and-Place (40 vs 32 of 40) and Pouring (40 vs 32), ties on Insertion (32 vs 32) and loses on Cup Uprighting (35 vs 38). FlowCorrect also wins the overall 30-condition in-distribution score (65.0% vs 57.5%, Table III). Downgraded from high for four reasons. (i) 'Zero at initialisation' is never stated; it is an inference from standard LoRA. (ii) Adaptation is one offline batch adapter fit, not persistent per-decision writes. (iii) There is no meta-learned writer, no cue-dependent recall of earlier episodes, and no consolidation, retention or reset cycle. (iv) The proposal's already-cited RoboTTT [6] is closer for learning from corrections through fast weights. What it does pre-empt is narrower: a gated residual on the velocity of a frozen robot flow-matching policy, applied at every ODE step, fitted from a handful of real corrections, and leaving the base flow exactly unchanged when the gate is off. That makes it the obvious cheap baseline for Stage E ('just fit a velocity adapter on the same corrections'). Its stated failure mode is a natural test case for cue-conditioned memory: 'a single locality gate and observation-agnostic LoRA update can lead to over-correction'.
checks.corrected_description: IROS 2026. Offline LoRA adapter (about 10k parameters, 500 epochs, about 30 minutes) on the MLP head of ManiFlow's DiTX, plus a binary gate on the current observation. It is trained with a flow-edit loss on logged noise, from 10 relative VR corrections per failure case plus 5 anchor rollouts. It is not per-decision memory, not meta-learned, and has no consolidation. Retraining is better on 2 of 4 hard-case sets and tied on 1; FlowCorrect is better on the overall 30-condition in-distribution score.

checks.title: Gated Memory Policy: In-Context Memorization and Adaptation
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v2, Aug 2026). The CoRL 2026 venue is supported only by the official real-stanford GitHub repo title '[CoRL 2026]'. The PDF has no venue line, and the project page carries a commented-out 'RSS 2026' and cites an arXiv preprint. Quotes are accurate: 'z̄_{t:t+h} = μ_t h_{t:t+h} + z_{t:t+h} is passed to the feed-forward layer'; one MAP-pooled image token plus h action tokens per chunk; history actions noised to level k−1 at denoising step k; +30.1% on MemMimic and +26.6% over MemoryVLA on MIKASA-Robo; the finite-window limitation. It is a DDIM diffusion policy, not flow matching. Downgraded to medium for three reasons. It is attention over cached history with no weight-based memory, consolidation or reset lifecycle. The binary gate zeroes a jointly trained cross-attention branch per timestep (calibrated from validation error), rather than resetting a persistent state to a pretrained base. The proposal already lists history tokens/retrieval as a required baseline and does not claim attention cannot do this. It is nonetheless the most important concrete baseline. MemMimic 'Match Color' (bin colours seen, then shuffled; place the cube by its original colour) is structurally the proposal's Experiment B delayed cue-to-action task. GMP reports '99.0%±1.0% success rate with a memory buffer of 6000 image frames' at 0.16 s for 8 denoising steps (Supp 8.1). Its cross-trial Iterative Pushing and Casting tasks are the 'adapt from outcomes' setting. Any fast-weight claim must beat it at matched memory and latency.
checks.corrected_description: Diffusion Transformer (DDIM) visuomotor policy with a cross-attention history branch (cached action chunks plus one pooled image token per chunk). A binary gate is calibrated on a validation set, and history actions are noised one step cleaner than the current denoising level. Trained end-to-end; no fast weights or consolidation. Venue: CoRL 2026 according to the authors' GitHub; the paper is otherwise an arXiv preprint (v2, Aug 2026).

checks.title: Test-Time Training Done Right (LaCT)
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v1, May 2025; the only version). Quotes are accurate: chunks of 2K to 1M tokens; SwiGLU fast weights up to 40% of parameters; the Table 3 GD, Momentum ('M ← βM + Σ η_i∇W L_i; W ← L2norm(W − M)') and Muon rules; 'our Muon variant consistently outperforms our Momentum variant'; and for autoregressive video, 'only updating fast weights on clean chunks. This simple strategy ensures that each denoising operation only accesses previously cleaned frames.' Downgraded to low. The write-after-commit, read-during-denoising schedule is already in the proposal's cited RoboTTT [6], which updates fast weights on each observation, persists them across timesteps and reads them during k-step flow-matching denoising in a GR00T DiT. The proposal also disclaims novelty here (Sec 6: 'The difference is the intervention location and lifecycle, not whether denoising is affected at all'). The optimizer evidence comes from chunks of 2K tokens or more, with a dot-product loss and L2 weight normalisation after every update. Transfer to single-experience writes into a 1,072-parameter MLP is untested. Normalising W after each write would also break exact W_0 centring unless W_0 is normalised too. Worth a citation for writer-optimizer ablations; the internal-TTT arm is already in Sec 17.
checks.corrected_description: Large-chunk TTT layers (SwiGLU fast weights, dot-product loss, L2-normalised GD, momentum or Muon updates), mixed with window attention, for novel view synthesis, language modelling, and a Wan 14B autoregressive video diffusion model. In the video model, fast weights are updated only on clean chunks and read by the noisy chunks.

checks.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context (TTT-E2E)
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v2). Quotes are accurate: test-time training of only the MLPs of the last 1/4 of blocks; initialisation meta-learned 'through gradients of gradients'; 'a static, second MLP layer as a "safe" storage'; 'when updating only 1 or 3 layers, our method does not scale with context length'; and Clark et al. adds fast weights 'only to the end of the model instead of interleaving', with 'interleaving proves to be critical'. Downgraded from high. Learning W_0 through inner gradient writes is MAML-style and already present in the proposal's cited TTT [3] and RoboTTT [6] (learned W_0), so it does not newly pre-empt the meta-training. The layer ablation concerns scaling to 8K-128K-token contexts in a 760M LM, which is weak evidence for a regime of 1-16 experiences. The 'interleaving is critical' line is a related-work remark; the closest reported test is the final-layer-only curve. The search agent missed that NIAH (Table 2) is far worse than full attention: 'the key mechanism in our method is compression, which leaves out seemingly irrelevant details'. That supports the proposal's explicit episodic store and warns that a gradient-written memory may miss Experiment B's arbitrary bindings. A TTT-E2E-style arm is a fair, distinct comparison: task-loss (flow-matching-loss) updates of the backbone's own last-block MLPs from a meta-learned initialisation.
checks.corrected_description: Long-context LM with sliding-window attention that takes next-token-loss gradient steps on the MLPs of the last 1/4 of blocks at test time, from a meta-learned initialisation, with a frozen 'safe' MLP per updated block. Scales like full attention on loss up to 128K tokens but is much worse at needle-in-a-haystack recall.

checks.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
checks.why: Verified. NeurIPS 2025 is confirmed by neurips.cc poster 119639 and the proceedings PDF; the arXiv page lists no venue. Quotes and numbers are accurate: ℓ = ||M(k_t) − v_t||²; M_t = (1−α_t)M_{t−1} + S_t with S_t = η_t S_{t−1} − θ_t∇ℓ; MAC, MAG and MAL; 'the greatest contribution comes from weight decay, momentum, convolution, and persistent memory'. Table 5 long-context accuracy: full memory module (LMM) 92.68, linear memory 85.34, without weight decay 85.60, without momentum 87.12. MAC scores 97.95 vs MAL 96.91, about 1 point. Downgraded from high because Titans pre-empts nothing the proposal claims. The proposal's writer (Eq 7-8) is the standard TTT-MLP writer it already cites [3], and it leaves decay and proximal terms as an explicit experimental choice (Sec 5). The ablations come from million-token LM sequences, and the value of forgetting and momentum with 1-16 writes is unclear. The search agent's design point is correct: Titans' decay shrinks toward 0, which under centring must become decay toward W_0. Cite it, and use a momentum plus decay-to-W_0 writer as an ablation rather than a separate baseline.
checks.corrected_description: Deep MLP neural memory written online by surprise with momentum and a data-dependent decay toward zero, combined with attention as context, gate or layer. NeurIPS 2025. Its ablations are on long-context language tasks.

checks.title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures (Hope / Continuum Memory System)
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v1; comment: 'A version of this work is published at ... NeurIPS 2025'). Quotes are accurate: the Continuum Memory System is a chain of MLP blocks updated every C^(ℓ) steps; in the nested variant 'the initial state of the MLP block in level s+1 is meta-learned in level s' and is 're-initialized to θ_0'; knowledge 'can circle back'; Hope beats in-context learning, EWC and InCA on class-incremental CLINC, Banking and DBpedia with Llama-3 backbones. Downgraded from high. The paper says 'in this work, we focus on the first stage: memory consolidation as an online process', so it explicitly does not implement offline (replay) consolidation. Its transfer from fast to slow levels happens through backpropagated or meta-learned initial states during training. There is no deployment-time distillation of adapted behaviour, no replay, and no validation-gated acceptance; a search for 'distill' finds nothing. It is a conceptual multi-timescale precedent (resetting to a slowly learned initialisation is also standard in TTT and MAML), not a pre-emption of the proposal's consolidation lifecycle. Cite in Sec 21.
checks.corrected_description: Conceptual framework plus the Hope architecture. MLP memory levels update at different frequencies; the fast levels are re-initialised to meta-learned initial states, and knowledge moves between levels via backprop or initialisation during training. The paper explicitly focuses on online consolidation and does not use replay or distillation.

checks.title: Metalearned Neural Memory
checks.why: Verified (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv v2). Quotes are accurate: memory as 'a rapidly adaptable function that we parameterize as a deep neural network'; binding 'by applying one step of modulated gradient descent' or 'a learned local update rule'; controller, memory initialisation φ0 and update modules meta-trained end-to-end on algorithmic tasks, bAbI and maze RL. It is genuine prior art for an external MLP memory written by one gradient step on key-to-value MSE, with meta-learned initialisation and interfaces, and should be cited. Downgraded from high because the proposal does not claim novelty for the writer. It already cites TTT [3] for gradient-written MLP fast models, and places its contribution in the reader location and flow-matching lifecycle, as the search agent itself concedes. Correction: MNM's learned local rule is a gradient-free, perceptron-style update toward activations predicted by a meta-learned 'backward feedback prediction function'. It is not a learned loss, so it is only a loose precedent for ML3's learned-loss writer [17].
checks.corrected_description: LSTM controller plus an external MLP memory. Writes are one modulated gradient step on MSE(f(k_w), v_w), or a meta-learned gradient-free perceptron-style local rule. Everything is meta-trained with task and memory objectives. Evaluated on algorithmic tasks, bAbI and maze RL.

checks.title: Memory-based Parameter Adaptation (MbPA)
checks.why: Verified (ICLR 2018). Quotes are accurate: inspired by complementary learning systems (CLS); kNN retrieval from an episodic buffer; a few gradient steps on the output network with a '−β(θ − θ^x)' pull toward the slow weights; 'The local adaptation is discarded after the model produces its output'; attention viewed as fitting a constant function locally. The paper even calls the self-diminishing correction 'consolidation' in CLS terms. Downgraded from high. MbPA's adaptation is per query, non-persistent, not meta-learned and uses no separate fast network. The proposal's centring is a structural zero of a persistent memory's residual, which is related but different. It should stay a baseline: retrieve the K nearest experiences from store B, take a few flow-matching-loss steps on the reader or last layers, then discard. At equal storage this isolates the value of persistent, meta-trained writes.
checks.corrected_description: Episodic kNN memory plus per-query temporary gradient adaptation of the output network (with a proximal pull to the slow weights), discarded after each prediction. ICLR 2018; framed with complementary learning systems.

checks.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
checks.why: Verified (CoLLAs 2024, PMLR 274). Quotes are accurate: standard generative replay 'results in a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities'; knowledge reaches the student 'only at the endpoint of the reverse process'; generative distillation transfers it 'at each point of the reverse trajectory'. Table 1: Fashion-MNIST FID 211.8 with generative replay vs 23.5 with generative distillation. Several caveats reduce the threat. The failure is tied to low-step teacher samples (2 DDIM steps on Fashion-MNIST, 10 on CIFAR-10) chained over 5 tasks, and more teacher steps 'alleviated the catastrophic loss ... to some extent'. The models are unconditional image diffusion models, not conditional flow-matching policies. The proposal's retention term R_old (Eq 25) is already a teacher-velocity-matching loss of the generative-distillation type, so the fix is already there for retention. The live risk is the recommended endpoint baseline (Eq 21-22), and 'old teacher endpoints with fresh FM noise' replay, repeated over 10 or more arrivals in Experiment D. Masip distils at forward-noised teacher samples, not along teacher ODE paths, so it is not the same as Eq 23. It must be cited in Sec 11-13, and generative replay vs generative distillation should be explicit retention arms.
checks.corrected_description: Continual training of unconditional DDPM/DDIM image models over 5 tasks. Replaying teacher samples (endpoint only) degrades badly with low-step teachers; adding teacher noise-prediction distillation at forward-noised teacher samples fixes most of it at the cost of about one extra forward pass.

checks.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
checks.why: Verified (TMLR 02/2024). Theorem 1 states 'W2(π̂1, π1) ≤ ε exp{∫_0^1 L_t dt}', proved via Alekseev-Gröbner and Grönwall. The paper says it 'is similar in content to Proposition 3 in Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (2023)', and that the time-varying L_t is needed because 'L_t explodes as t → 0 or 1'. The proof structure matches the proposal's Eq 27-28 and Appendix B.1: same-noise coupling, the Lipschitz constant taken on the new (approximate) field, and velocity error measured along the old (true) trajectories. The proposal's C_L = (e^{2L}−1)/(2L) is a constant-L version with a slightly sharper, time-weighted constant than Benton's e^{2L}. The bound is therefore not new and needs attribution. Rated medium rather than high: it is a supporting lemma the proposal already qualifies, not a core claimed contribution. One point bears on the proposal directly. For concentrated action targets, the spatial Lipschitz constant of the flow-matching field grows like 1/σ near t=1, so a uniform-L bound is exponentially loose, while ∫L_t dt stays logarithmic. The proposal should state the time-varying form.
checks.corrected_description: Deterministic flow-matching sampler error bound W2 ≤ ε·exp(∫L_t dt), using a time-varying Lipschitz constant of the learned field, plus bounds on the Lipschitz constant of the true velocity field. The proposal's retention bound is a constant-L special case with a sharper constant.

checks.title: It's All Connected: A Journey Through Test-Time Memorization, Attentional Bias, Retention, and Online Optimization (Miras)
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v1, Apr 2025). Accurate except one small misquote: the abstract says 'reinterpret forgetting mechanisms ... as a form of retention regularization'; there is no 'l2', and ℓ2 is only one retention instance. Correctly described: the Learning-Retaining view with local and global retention, the KL, elastic-net and Bregman variants, and the Moneta, Yaad and Memora models. It supplies vocabulary: the proposal's writer is ℓ2 attentional bias with one GD step and no retention, and decay toward W_0 is global retention centred at W_0. It pre-empts nothing and offers no evidence for a regime of 1-16 writes. Downgraded to low.
checks.corrected_description: Framework describing sequence models as associative memories along four axes (memory architecture, attentional-bias objective, retention gate, learning algorithm), with new variants Moneta, Yaad and Memora for long-context language modelling.

checks.title: Test-time regression: a unifying framework for designing sequence models with associative memory
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v3, May 2025). The abstract quote about three design choices and the statement that 'softmax attention with QKNorm is a locally-constant nonparametric regressor' are accurate. It usefully frames attention over history and a gradient-written MLP as points in one regression design space. The proposal already disclaims any expressive separation (Sec 1; Sec 5, citing [4]). Background citation only; no threat.

checks.title: The Dual Form of Neural Networks Revisited: Connecting Test Time Predictions to Training Patterns via Spotlights of Attention
checks.why: Verified (ICML 2022). The Proposition 1 quote is accurate, and the paper states that 'none of the mathematical results we'll discuss is novel' (the dual perceptron, Aizerman 1964). The search agent's derivation is right: writes to B and d_0 in Eq 6 act as unnormalised dot attention over write-time tanh features, with error signals as values, and writes to A and b break the equivalence. The proposal already cites [4] (KV-binding TTT is secretly linear attention) and says history-through-weights 'does not imply a universal mathematical separation'. This adds precision, not threat. A kernelised linear-attention reader over stored (cue, error) pairs is covered by the planned history/retrieval baseline.

checks.title: Meta-Learning Fast Weight Language Models
checks.why: Verified (EMNLP 2022 short paper, per arXiv comment). Quotes are accurate: Fast Weight Layers provide dynamic evaluation 'much more efficiently by expressing gradient updates as linear attention'; they 'are added on top of the transformer after the last attention layer'; fast weights start at the slow weights with learned step sizes; the write objective is the LM loss. Transformer-XL perplexity on WikiText-103 drops from 18.1 to 16.6. It is the closest precedent for an external, gradient-written, meta-trained readout after a backbone, so medium is justified. The counter-evidence (TTT-E2E: interleaving 'proves to be critical') is a related-work remark about scaling large LMs to long contexts, not a controlled test. It signals a risk rather than establishing one. Cite in Sec 21; the proposal's internal-vs-external reader factorial already addresses the question.
checks.corrected_description: EMNLP 2022 (short). Fast Weight Layer on top of the last transformer layer, updated by LM-loss gradients (computed as linear attention) with meta-trained initialisation and step sizes.

checks.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
checks.why: Verified (CVPR 2025). Quotes are accurate: the TTT-MLP loss ||f(θ_K x; W) − θ_V x||²; 'gate(TTT, X; α) = tanh(α) ⊗ TTT(X) + X' with α initialised to 0.1 'to avoid this degradation'; +34 Elo on 63-second videos; for 18-second videos 'Gated DeltaNet performs the best'. Downgraded to low. The fast weights are rebuilt inside each forward pass from the current noisy video tokens (in both directions), so nothing persists across samples. The tanh(0.1) gate is an initialisation trick, not exact centring. The 'short context' where Gated DeltaNet wins is about 100k tokens, which says nothing about 1-16 experiences. The proposal's cited RoboTTT [6] already uses the same tanh gate in a robot flow-matching DiT and reports RoboTTT beating a Gated DeltaNet replacement on robot tasks, which argues against that extrapolation.
checks.corrected_description: Gated TTT-MLP layers inserted into CogVideo-X 5B and fine-tuned. Fast weights are recomputed within each forward pass over the whole (noisy) token sequence; they are not a memory that persists across generations.

checks.title: Fast Spatial Memory with Elastic Test-Time Training
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v1, Apr 2026). Quotes are accurate: 'fully plastic inference-time updates remain vulnerable to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting'; θ_{c+1} = θ'_c − λF_c ⊙ (θ'_c − θ*_c); Global, Streaming and Streaming-EMA anchors; 'Streaming-EMA is the best practice'; the global anchor 'degenerates into an importance-weighted ℓ2 regularizer ... similar to weight decay'. Downgraded to low for three reasons. (i) The inference that 'the proposal's exact reset needs retention toward W_0' is wrong: reset is an explicit assignment W ← W_0 (Appendix B.2), and retention matters only if a decay or proximal writer is chosen. (ii) In Table 1 the global anchor (28.35 PSNR) still beats no consolidation (26.91) and a plain streaming anchor (26.96). (iii) The setting is 4D reconstruction with 4 chunks of 2048 tokens, far from 1-16 writes. An elastic or EMA-anchored writer is at most a writer ablation.
checks.corrected_description: LaCT variant for 4D reconstruction that adds an EWC/MAS/SI-weighted elastic pull of the fast weights toward an anchor after each chunk update. EMA anchors work best; a global anchor is intermediate.

checks.title: In-Place Test-Time Training
checks.why: Verified (ICLR 2026 Oral, per arXiv comment). Quotes are accurate: the final MLP projection W_down serves as fast weights, a 'drop-in' enhancement; a next-token-aligned target replaces reconstruction; chunk-wise updates; Qwen3-4B up to 128k. Downgraded to low. The 'misaligned fast weight objectives' critique targets reconstructing a token's own key and value projections. The proposal's Eq 7 already maps a masked cue to separate event content, which is a predictive association. Repurposing existing MLP down-projections is one way to build the internal-TTT arm already in Sec 17 (and RoboTTT). A velocity-aligned (flow-matching-aligned) writer target is worth noting as an ablation.

checks.title: Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference
checks.why: Verified (arXiv v3, Jun 2026). Quotes are accurate: sleep 'converts recent context into persistent fast weights before clearing its key-value cache'; N offline recurrent passes update SSM fast weights 'through a learned local rule'; Gated DeltaNets 'fail despite having enough fast weight capacity'. Its consolidation moves context into SSM fast weights, and its gains are on deep multi-hop reasoning (cellular automata, graph retrieval, math), not shallow cue-to-action recall. It weakly motivates a multi-step or idle-time write ablation.

checks.title: AURA: Action-Gated Memory for Robot Policies at Constant VRAM
checks.why: Verified (single author, KAIKAKU; arXiv v1, Jun 2026). Quotes are accurate: a TTT-Linear/delta memory 'W_t = (1 − α)W_{t−1} − η∇W L_inner', read by einsum into the action head, with meta-learned η and α and an action-surprise write gate. On OpenVLA-OFT LIBERO-Long it scores 14/60 = 0.233, equal to the base, and 'does not by itself raise robot success'. The evidence is weak by the author's own disclosures: synthetic streams, single seeds, n=60. The memory is linear, read once per decision (not per denoising step), and has no consolidation. Optional citation for write gating.

checks.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
checks.why: Verified (ICLR 2025). The quote 'gating enables rapid memory erasure while the delta rule facilitates targeted updates' is accurate. One gradient step on a linear memory's MSE association loss is exactly the delta rule, so the proposal's planned TTT-Linear arm already covers DeltaNet-style writing. GDN adds a scalar decay gate toward 0, which conflicts with W_0 centring unless recentred. The One-Minute Video 'short context' evidence is for about 100k tokens. RoboTTT [6], already cited, found its nonlinear TTT beat a GDN replacement on robot assembly tasks. This is a gated variant of the TTT-Linear arm, not a new baseline.

checks.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
checks.why: Verified (ICML 2021). Quotes are accurate (formal equivalence to fast-weight controllers from the early '90s, the capacity limitation, the delta-rule-like update). It is foundational, but the proposal already cites the modern forms ([3], [4]), plans 'capacity and write-rate sweeps' (Sec 5) and caveats capacity (Sec 14). The capacity argument is for additive outer-product linear memories with d-dimensional keys, not directly for a 16-32-16 tanh MLP. Background citation.

checks.title: Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent
checks.why: Verified (ICML 2023, arXiv v2). The quote is accurate. The equivalence is between one linear self-attention layer and one GD step on linear regression, shown on toy regression tasks. It does not directly cover the proposal's tanh-MLP writer (the A and b updates). It supports the proposal's already-hedged position that no separation from attention is claimed (Sec 1, Sec 21). Background.
checks.corrected_description: Equivalence shown only for linear self-attention and one GD step on linear regression, with empirical evidence on toy regression.

checks.title: Using Fast Weights to Deblur Old Memories
checks.why: Verified from the scanned PDF, rendered and read (page 1 header: 'In Proceedings of the Ninth Annual Conference of the Cognitive Science Society, Seattle, WA'; Hinton and Plaut, CMU). Quotes are accurate: each connection has 'a slowly changing, plastic weight which stores long-term knowledge and a fast-changing, elastic weight which stores temporary knowledge and spontaneously decays towards zero'; 'The effective weight on the connection is the sum of these two'; 'temporary overlay of fast weights'; rehearsal lets the fast weights 'temporarily cancel out the changes in the slow weights caused by the subsequent learning'. It is the right historical origin for additive fast and slow weights that vanish at rest. The differences: its fast weights sit on the same connections, and it uses them to restore old associations, not to adapt to new experience or be distilled into the slow weights. Background citation, no threat.
checks.corrected_description: Hinton and Plaut, Proc. 9th Annual Conference of the Cognitive Science Society, 1987 (pp. 177ff). Dual slow/fast weights per connection, with fast weights decaying to zero. Fast weights learned from rehearsing a few old associations cancel interference from later slow learning.

gap.landscape_summary:
By Sep 2026 the maths the proposal uses for consolidation and retention is almost all published. The contribution that is still new is the combination: a meta-trained fast-weight writer, a centered velocity residual, and FM distillation with replay, all run as one fast-to-slow lifecycle for robot policies.

(e) Retention bound (eq 27-28). This is a known result with the same constant. Gao, Huang and Jiao, Gaussian Interpolation Flows, Proposition 39(ii), states W2^2 <= (exp(2C3)-1)/(2C3) * integral of ||v - v~||^2 p_t. Here v~ is the approximating field with Lipschitz constant C3, and p_t is the reference flow's marginal. That is the proposal's C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L), and the proof is the same: Alekseev-Groebner/Gronwall, then Cauchy-Schwarz. Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden (Prop. 3, constant e^{1+2K}) and Benton-Deligiannidis-Doucet (Thm 1, constant exp(2 * integral of L_t)) are looser versions of the same inequality. Nothing contradicts the bound, but the literature shows its assumptions are weak points:
- The uniform global Lipschitz constant is unrealistic. Benton notes that "for most practical data distributions we expect the Lipschitz constant to explode as one approaches the data distribution". Near-deterministic cue->action targets are exactly that case, so C_L becomes vacuous.
- A one-sided Lipschitz condition with an integrable C_t is enough (Boffi et al.; Kwon et al.).
- The inequality can run the other way: put the Lipschitz condition on the frozen old field and measure the error along the new policy's trajectories (Gao et al. Prop 39(i)). The old field's Lipschitz constant can be checked; the new field's cannot be controlled beforehand.
- Euler discretization, which the proposal says it does not cover, is handled by Bansal et al. (and Beyler & Bach).
- Across cycles, the stability theory of iterative retraining on self-generated data (Bertrand et al., ICLR 2024; it includes OT-CFM) replaces the proposal's bare remark about the triangle inequality.

Appendix A (path distillation). This restates rectified-flow theory. Liu, Gong & Liu (Theorem 3.3 and the "nonlinear extension" in Sec. 2.3) prove marginal preservation for E[Xdot_t | X_t] of any time-differentiable process under "rectifiability" (existence and uniqueness of the ODE), citing Kurtz and Ambrosio-Crippa. The proposal's counterexample (eq 33: Gamma_t = (1-2t) eps, b* = -2z/(1-2t)) is Hertrich-Chambolle-Delon Prop. 13 (coupling X1 = -X0, v_t(x) = -2x/(1-2t), zero loss, not rectifiable). Their Theorem 14 and Example 16 give a fix: add a little Gaussian smoothing and the coupling becomes rectifiable. Reflow-style same-seed endpoint pairing is a third consolidation target the proposal omits. It sits between independent-noise endpoint FM (eq 21-22) and piecewise-linear path distillation (eq 23).

(d) Consolidation with replay. The retention penalty R_old (student velocity matched to the frozen teacher at intermediate states) is in substance "generative distillation" (Masip et al., CoLLAs 2024). That paper found that endpoint-only generative replay causes "a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities", while matching the teacher across the whole reverse process fixed it (FID 211.8 -> 23.5 on Fashion-MNIST). This is direct prior evidence on the proposal's endpoint-versus-path question and should be a baseline. The idea of distilling a memory-conditioned teacher into a memory-free student, with replay and "sleep", appeared in 2026 for LLMs (SDFT, which argues distillation should be on-policy; "Language Models Need Sleep") and for robots (When Robots Sleep: frozen-snapshot distillation on observation buffers plus anchoring). For flow-matching VLAs, cheaper retention baselines exist: ConSFT, Memory-Anchor replay selection, and the finding that pretrained VLAs barely forget under simple experience replay.

(a)/(b) Reading memory inside the solver. The closest competitor, TraceFlow (17 Sep 2026), adds a bounded, early-step correction to a frozen flow-matching action expert's velocity. The correction comes from retrieved successful and failed rollouts of the robot itself, with no weight update. It is the nonparametric counterpart of the centered residual reader. Lim et al. show that the optimal empirical FM field is itself a "memory-augmented" kernel-attention velocity.

(c) Meta-trained writer. The structure has long precedents: OML (slow representation, fast online-SGD head, meta-trained through online updates), ANML, Continual-MAML/OSAKA (fast weights, consolidation at task boundaries with update modulation) and MOLe for robots. The scaling concerns are known: second-order/implicit gradient cost (iMAML) and short-horizon bias when the writer is meta-trained over 1-16 writes but deployed for a lifetime. WIZARD (2026) meta-learns a weight generator for pi0.5 directly.

Value/control reader. Adjoint Matching shows that deterministic-ODE control with a quadratic cost does not produce the reward-tilted distribution because of initial-value bias ("when the sampling procedure is noiseless ... fine-tuning naively will not have any effect because X0 completely determines X1"). A memoryless noise schedule fixes this, and it addresses the proposal's own worry about mode collapse.

papers.title: Gaussian Interpolation Flows
papers.authors_year: Yuan Gao, Jian Huang, Yuling Jiao (arXiv 2023, v2 2024; JMLR)
papers.what_it_does: Proves well-posedness, Lipschitz regularity of the velocity field and Lipschitz flow maps for Gaussian-interpolation (FM/diffusion ODE) flows. Section 6 gives stability in the velocity field. Prop 39(ii): if sup ||grad_x v~|| <= C3, then "W2^2(Y1#mu, nu) <= (exp(2C3) - 1)/(2C3) * integral_0^1 integral ||v(t,x) - v~(t,x)||^2 p_t(x) dx dt", proved with the Alekseev-Groebner formula, Gronwall and Cauchy-Schwarz. Prop 39(i) is the reverse version: the reference field is Lipschitz with time-varying theta_u, and the error is measured along the approximating flow's marginals. Prop 20 shows the velocity Jacobian bounds 'blow up at time t = 1' unless the target score is Lipschitz.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts Sec. 13 eq 27-28 and App. B.1 exactly, including the constant C_L = (e^{2L}-1)/(2L). Map v = v_old, v~ = v_new and p_t = the law of the old-policy ODE state X_t. The proposal should present eq 27 as this known result, not a new one. Prop 39(i) is the useful variant: it needs Lipschitz control only of the frozen old field, which can be checked, and measures the velocity error along new-policy trajectories (an on-policy retention penalty). Prop 20 explains why a uniform L is unrealistic near t=1.

papers.title: Building Normalizing Flows with Stochastic Interpolants
papers.authors_year: Michael S. Albergo, Eric Vanden-Eijnden (ICLR 2023; arXiv 2022)
papers.what_it_does: Introduces stochastic interpolants and the quadratic velocity-regression objective. Prop 3: if v^ is C^1 and Lipschitz in x uniformly on [0,1] x R^d with constant K^, then "W2^2(rho1, rho^1) <= e^{1+2K^} H(v^)", where H(v^) = integral integral |v^_t(x) - v_t(x)|^2 rho_t(x) dx dt along the exact path. Appendix E proves it with the same-noise coupling and Gronwall. It also suggests regularizing E||grad v^||^2 to keep the bound small.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The original version of the proposal's eq 27, with a looser constant (e^{1+2L} versus (e^{2L}-1)/(2L)). The penalty is evaluated along the reference flow and the Lipschitz condition is on the learned field, the same structure as R_old in eq 25. Its suggested Jacobian regularizer is a concrete way to keep C_L small during consolidation, which the proposal could add to L_slow.

papers.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
papers.authors_year: Joe Benton, George Deligiannidis, Arnaud Doucet (TMLR 2024)
papers.what_it_does: Thm 1: under an L2 velocity-error bound eps^2 along the true flow and a time-varying Lipschitz constant L_t of the approximate field, "W2(pi^1, pi1) <= eps exp{integral_0^1 L_t dt}" (Alekseev-Groebner plus Gronwall). Thm 2-3 bound the integral of L*_t for the true field under a lambda-regularity assumption and give polynomial W2 bounds with Gaussian smoothing. It criticizes Albergo-VE's uniform Lipschitz constant: "for most practical data distributions we expect the Lipschitz constant to explode as one approaches the data distribution; for example, this will happen for data supported on a submanifold." It also notes the asymmetry: reversing the roles would require controlling the error "along the paths of Y".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts eq 27 and exposes its weakest assumption, a global, time-uniform L for the new field. Robot action targets that are nearly deterministic given context (the delayed cue->action tasks) are the case where L_t blows up near t=1, so C_L can become vacuous. The proposal should switch to integrable L_t or Gaussian smoothing, and report estimates of L_t, not just cite 'a large Lipschitz constant makes the bound loose'.

papers.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
papers.authors_year: Xingchao Liu, Chengyue Gong, Qiang Liu (ICLR 2023; arXiv 2022)
papers.what_it_does: Defines rectified flow and the 'nonlinear extension' (Sec 2.3): for any time-differentiable process X, v^X(z,t) = E[Xdot_t | X_t = z], estimated by min_v integral E w_t ||v(X_t,t) - Xdot_t||^2. Theorem 3.3: "Assume X is rectifiable and Z is its rectified flow. Then Law(Z_t) = Law(X_t)". Rectifiable means v^X is locally bounded and the ODE has a unique solution, with uniqueness via Kurtz Cor. 1.3 and Ambrosio-Crippa. Reflow retrains on same-seed pairs (Z0, Z1) of the previous flow. The paper distinguishes distillation (faithfully approximating the coupling) from rectification ("yields a different coupling").
papers.relation_to_proposal: App. A (eq 31-32) and the eq 23-24 path-distillation claims are Theorem 3.3 and Sec. 2.3 applied to piecewise-linear teacher paths. The caveats that it matches marginals but not same-seed trajectories, and needs uniqueness/regularity, are Liu's 'rectifiable' condition and the distillation-versus-rectification distinction. Reflow (straight lines between a teacher's own noise seed and its adapted endpoint) is a missing consolidation option between eq 21-22 (independent fresh noise) and eq 23 (full path).

papers.title: On the Relation between Rectified Flows and Optimal Transport
papers.authors_year: Johannes Hertrich, Antonin Chambolle, Julie Delon (arXiv 2025, v3 Feb 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Studies invariances, well-posedness and optimal-transport claims for rectified flows. Prop 13: for mu0 = mu1 = N(0,I) and coupling X1 = -X0, the loss minimizer is "v_t(x) = -2/(1-2t) x", the loss is zero, the coupling is non-optimal, and it "is not rectifiable, i.e., the ODE Zdot_t = v_t(Z_t) does not admit a unique solution". Theorem 14: if P_{X0|X1=x1} has a smooth positive density, the coupling is rectifiable and v_t is smooth. Example 16: any coupling becomes rectifiable after adding small Gaussian noise to X0.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The App. A counterexample (Gamma_t = (1-2t) eps, eq 33: b* = -2z/(1-2t)) is exactly Prop 13, so it should be cited, not presented as new. Theorem 14 and Example 16 give a constructive fix the proposal lacks: smooth teacher paths or seeds slightly with Gaussian noise so the path-distillation target is guaranteed rectifiable. This turns 'endpoint distillation is the recommended first baseline' into a testable, regularized path-distillation variant.

papers.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
papers.authors_year: Sergi Masip, Pau Rodriguez, Tinne Tuytelaars, Gido M. van de Ven (CoLLAs 2024; arXiv 2023)
papers.what_it_does: Continual training of diffusion models. Standard generative replay transfers knowledge "only at the endpoint of the reverse process" and causes "a catastrophic loss in denoising capabilities". 'Generative distillation' instead matches the student's noise prediction to the frozen previous-task teacher on noised teacher samples, L_distil = E||eps_teacher(x_t,t) - eps_student(x_t,t)||^2, mixed with the current-task loss as L_GD = r L_simple + (1-r) lambda L_distil. FID drops from 211.8 to 23.5 (Fashion-MNIST) and from 96.4 to 42.3 (CIFAR-10) versus generative replay. Distilling on current data (LwF-like) or on pure Gaussian inputs also beats generative replay. Limitations: lambda is tuned with hindsight, and generation overhead is large.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Direct precedent for Sec. 13 R_old (eq 25-26), a velocity/noise-matching retention term against a frozen snapshot at intermediate generative states, and for the Sec. 12 endpoint-versus-path question in a continual setting. Its result (endpoint-only replay fails, whole-process matching works) already answers part of the proposal's falsification test. Masip's inputs are noised teacher endpoints, not old-ODE states, which is a cheaper alternative to eq 25's exact trajectories. Must be a baseline and cited.

papers.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
papers.authors_year: Jiaxuan Zhang, Ruizhe Liu, Yu Zhang, Yanchao Yang (arXiv, 17 Sep 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Adds a "progress-aligned guidance field that turns the action densities of retrieved successful and failed rollouts into a bounded correction to a frozen flow-matching action expert". A TraceBank stores the robot's own rollouts with one terminal bit and grows across deployment rounds. The correction is the score of kernel densities over retrieved action windows, added to the base velocity at the current solver state. It is "capped relative to the base velocity, and its strength declines to zero before the final solver steps", with no weight update. Real robot: 21 -> 39 of 50 ordered packs (47 after one stacking round). Gains are selective across RoboMemArena/LIBERO, and it notes the cap "keeps the same retrieval from collapsing the base policy". Related work lists Retrieve-then-Steer and OptimusVLA as retrieval-into-sampler methods.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The closest current competitor to contributions (a) and (b): experience read at every denoising step, used as an additive, bounded residual on the FM velocity of a frozen policy, and accumulated across rounds. It is nonparametric (episodic store), not a gradient-written fast net, which is exactly the proposal's 'history tokens/retrieval' baseline recast in velocity space. The proposal needs to show the fast-weight writer beats a TraceFlow-style kernel-score reader under the same store, budget and reset protocol.

papers.title: Online Fast Adaptation and Knowledge Accumulation: a New Approach to Continual Learning (OSAKA / Continual-MAML)
papers.authors_year: Massimo Caccia, Pau Rodriguez, Oleksiy Ostapenko, et al. (NeurIPS 2020; arXiv 2020)
papers.what_it_does: Defines a setting where an agent must quickly solve new out-of-distribution tasks and also remember old ones fast. Continual-MAML pre-trains a meta-initialization with MAML. At deployment it builds fast weights theta_t from current data. New knowledge is written into slow meta-parameters only when loss exceeds a threshold ('update modulation'). Fast weights are kept until a context shift is detected, and then "we use a buffer to accumulate data ... update the slow weights phi ... One can think of the update after the task boundary detection as a knowledge consolidation phase."
papers.relation_to_proposal: A generic (non-FM) precedent for the whole Sec. 14-15 lifecycle: meta-learned initialization W_0, persistent fast weights, buffered consolidation into slow weights, and a reset at boundaries, with gated slow updates similar to the proposal's acceptance gates. The proposal's claim of a 'complete algorithm' must separate itself from this; the difference is the FM-specific reader and distillation target.

papers.title: Meta-Learning Representations for Continual Learning (OML)
papers.authors_year: Khurram Javed, Martha White (NeurIPS 2019)
papers.what_it_does: Splits the model into a Representation Learning Network (slow, 'only updated in the outer loop') and a Prediction Learning Network (fast, updated online by SGD). The meta-objective backpropagates through online SGD updates on a k-length trajectory and scores them on the trajectory plus a remember set: "During the inner gradient steps ... we only update the parameters in the PLN. We then update both the RLN and the PLN". It learns sparse representations that reduce interference.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Structurally the same as Sec. 5 and 7: slow encoders phi decide the cues, a small fast net W is written by gradient steps, and phi and W_0 are meta-trained second-order through sequential writes. OML's remember-set term in the meta-loss is a principled way to meta-train the writer for low interference across many writes, which the proposal's eq 12 (fit-only meta-loss) lacks.

papers.title: Learning to Continually Learn (ANML)
papers.authors_year: Shawn Beaulieu, Lapo Frati, Thomas Miconi, Joel Lehman, Kenneth O. Stanley, Jeff Clune, Nick Cheney (ECAI 2020)
papers.what_it_does: A neuromodulated meta-learning algorithm. A neuromodulatory network produces element-wise gating of a prediction network that is updated by SGD in the inner loop. Meta-training differentiates through a whole sequential learning process and scores it on validation data, learning selective plasticity against catastrophic forgetting (Omniglot, up to 600 sequential tasks).
papers.relation_to_proposal: Precedent for meta-learning how sequential gradient writes should be gated. It is directly related to the proposal's query/content encoders deciding what gets written, and to its optional learned-loss writer. A gated-write variant is a natural ablation for the Sec. 5 writer.

papers.title: Flow map matching with stochastic interpolants: A mathematical framework for consistency models
papers.authors_year: Nicholas M. Boffi, Michael S. Albergo, Eric Vanden-Eijnden (arXiv 2024, v2 2025)
papers.what_it_does: Learns two-time flow maps X_{s,t}. Lagrangian map distillation (LMD) and Eulerian map distillation (EMD) distill a pre-trained velocity field into few-step maps. Under only a one-sided Lipschitz condition (b_t(x)-b_t(y))·(x-y) <= C_t|x-y|^2 with C_t in L^1, Prop 3.9 gives "W2^2(rho1, rho^1) <= e^{1 + 2 integral_0^1 |C_t| dt} L_LMD(X^)". Prop 3.10 gives an EMD bound with no Lipschitz constant. It notes LMD works better because the learned map "can be singular or nearly singular".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Relevant to consolidation (Sec. 11-12) and retention (Sec. 13). It shows teacher-to-student FM distillation losses that control W2 under a one-sided, time-integrable Lipschitz assumption, weaker than eq 27's global uniform L. It also offers an alternative distillation family (map/consistency-style) if the slow policy should also get faster.

papers.title: On the Convergence and Straightness of Rectified Flow
papers.authors_year: Vansh Bansal, Saptarshi Roy, Alessandro Rinaldo, Purnamrita Sarkar (arXiv 2024, v8 Jun 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Thm 1: with a Lipschitz learned drift (constant L^), "W2^2(rho~1, rho1) <= e^{1+2L^} integral_0^1 eps^2(t) dt", which it says "closely resembles those established in prior works (Kwon et al., 2022; Pedrotti et al., 2024; Boffi et al., 2024)". Thm 2 bounds W2 for the Euler-discretized ODE with T steps by a curvature (piecewise-straightness) term gamma_{2,T}(Z)/T^2 plus velocity error. It also analyzes straightness of 1-rectified flow and reflow.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Fills the gap the proposal admits ("It is not a certificate for ... numerical integration"). The consolidation experiments use 16 Euler steps, and this gives a discretized-flow W2 bound usable for the retention claim. It also suggests the retention penalty should monitor path curvature, not only velocity mismatch.

papers.title: On the Stability of Iterative Retraining of Generative Models on their own Data
papers.authors_year: Quentin Bertrand, Avishek Joey Bose, Alexandre Duplessis, Marco Jiralerspong, Gauthier Gidel (ICLR 2024)
papers.what_it_does: Studies repeated retraining on a mix of real data and the model's own samples. Theorems 1-2: iterative retraining is stable (converges to or stays near the optimum) "if the initial generative model is close enough to the real data distribution and that the proportion of real data is sufficiently large". Training only on its own output leads to collapse. Verified empirically with OT conditional flow matching, DDPM and EDM.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Directly relevant to repeated consolidation cycles (Sec. 11-15, App. B.1). The slow FM policy is repeatedly retrained on teacher- or self-generated samples plus replay. The proposal only says 'small one-cycle deviations can accumulate' and offers no cross-cycle bound; this gives a stability condition in terms of the fraction of genuine (real-robot) data per cycle.

papers.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning (SDFT)
papers.authors_year: Idan Shenfeld, Mehul Damani, Jonas Hubotter, Pulkit Agrawal (arXiv Jan 2026, v2 Aug 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Uses "a demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher": the same model conditioned on a demonstration (teacher) is distilled into itself without it (student). Training minimizes reverse KL "on trajectories generated by the student itself, yielding on-policy updates". It beats SFT on new-task accuracy with much less forgetting, and in sequential experiments "enables a single model to accumulate multiple skills over time without performance regression".
papers.relation_to_proposal: Conceptual precedent (LLM domain) for contribution (d): distilling a memory- or experience-conditioned teacher into a memory-free student to consolidate. Its central claim, that distillation should be on the student's own state distribution, contrasts with the proposal's off-policy targets (teacher paths in eq 23; old-policy states in eq 25). An on-policy variant should be an ablation.

papers.title: Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories
papers.authors_year: Ali Behrouz, Farnoosh Hashemi, Adel Javanmard, Vahab Mirrokni (arXiv Jun 2026; OpenReview Sep 2025)
papers.what_it_does: Proposes a 'Sleep' paradigm that lets models "distill their short-term fragile memories into stable long-term knowledge with replay". It has a Memory Consolidation stage (Knowledge Seeding by on-policy distillation plus RL-based imitation) and a Dreaming stage that generates synthetic rehearsal curricula. Evaluated on long-horizon, continual-learning and knowledge-incorporation tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Pre-empts the framing of contribution (d) (fast-to-slow consolidation with replay, inspired by sleep) in the LLM setting. The proposal's novelty must rest on FM-specific transfer objectives and robot evaluation, not on the lifecycle concept itself.

papers.title: Adjoint Matching: Fine-tuning Flow and Diffusion Generative Models with Memoryless Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.authors_year: Carles Domingo-Enrich, Michal Drozdzal, Brian Karrer, Ricky T. Q. Chen (ICLR 2025; arXiv 2024)
papers.what_it_does: Treats reward fine-tuning of FM/diffusion models as stochastic optimal control. It proves an 'initial value function bias': naive KL-regularized control gives p*(X0,X1) = p_base exp(r(X1) + V(X0,0)), not the tilted distribution. "When the sampling procedure is noiseless, i.e., sigma(t) = 0, fine-tuning naively will not have any effect because X0 completely determines X1." A memoryless noise schedule is proved sufficient and necessary. The Adjoint Matching regression algorithm follows.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Bears on the Sec. 10 value/control reader (eq 17-20): additive control of a deterministic generative ODE with quadratic cost. The proposal worries that "optimizing each noise seed can send many seeds to the same outcome". Adjoint Matching explains why and gives the principled fix (memoryless SDE control targeting p_base·exp(r)). Any value-reader experiment should use this formulation or explain why not.

papers.title: Meta-Learning with Implicit Gradients (iMAML)
papers.authors_year: Aravind Rajeswaran, Chelsea Finn, Sham Kakade, Sergey Levine (NeurIPS 2019)
papers.what_it_does: Computes MAML meta-gradients by implicit differentiation of a proximally regularized inner solution. The meta-gradient is independent of the inner optimizer's path, with "a memory footprint no more than that which is required to compute a single inner loop gradient". It avoids the memory and vanishing-gradient cost of backpropagating through many inner steps.
papers.relation_to_proposal: The proposal meta-trains phi and W_0 by second-order backpropagation through sequential gradient writes (eq 8, 12), done inside every denoising step. iMAML (and first-order MAML, which the MAML paper found close to full second-order) are the standard ways to scale this. Note that iMAML assumes a converged inner problem, which does not fit a few online writes. The proposal should state which approximation it uses at robot scale.

papers.title: Understanding Short-Horizon Bias in Stochastic Meta-Optimization
