papers.authors_year: Yuhuai Wu, Mengye Ren, Renjie Liao, Roger Grosse (ICLR 2018)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that meta-objectives unrolled over short horizons are biased toward overly small step sizes (greedy behavior). Meta-optimization "chooses too small a learning rate by multiple orders of magnitude, even when run with a moderately long time horizon (100 steps)".
papers.relation_to_proposal: The writer and eta_f are meta-trained over 1-16 experiences (Sec. 16), but deployed fast weights persist across many decisions and consolidation cycles. The known horizon bias predicts a miscalibrated write strength over long deployments, a risk to the 'can still adapt with same budget' reset gate (Sec. 14) that the proposal does not mention.

papers.title: Deep Online Learning via Meta-Learning: Continual Adaptation for Model-Based RL (MOLe)
papers.authors_year: Anusha Nagabandi, Chelsea Finn, Sergey Levine (ICLR 2019)
papers.what_it_does: Continual online adaptation of a robot dynamics model. Online SGD from a meta-learned prior, plus "an expectation maximization algorithm with a Chinese restaurant process prior to develop and maintain a mixture of models" for non-stationary task distributions: new models are created for task changes and old ones recalled. Meta-training makes direct online SGD adaptation effective.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Robot-side precedent for a meta-trained gradient writer acting on robot experience (c). It retains skills with a mixture of adapted models instead of consolidating into one backbone. That mixture is an alternative to Sec. 14's 'keep the teacher/memory until transfer passes', useful for non-identifiable histories (App. B.4).

papers.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning (WIZARD)
papers.authors_year: Christian Bianchi, Siamak Yousefi, Alessio Sampieri, Andrea Roberti, Luca Rigazio, Fabio Galasso, Luca Franco (arXiv Jun 2026)
papers.what_it_does: "Generating task-specific LoRA parameters for a frozen VLA policy. Given only a language instruction and a short demonstration video, WIZARD predicts the corresponding adaptation weights in a single forward pass, without target-task action labels or test-time optimization." Meta-trained to map task evidence to expert LoRA updates. Uses pi0.5, a flow-matching VLA, on LIBERO: up to ~2x on unseen collections and ~14x on unseen tasks.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A 2026 competitor for (c): a meta-learned writer that maps experience to weights of an FM robot policy. It is amortized (hypernetwork) rather than a gradient write into a 1,072-parameter fast net, and has no persistent memory or consolidation. It is a natural 'amortized writer' ablation against eq 8.

papers.title: Preserving Foundational Capabilities in Flow-Matching VLAs through Conservative SFT (ConSFT)
papers.authors_year: Tianyi Zhang, Shaopeng Zhai, Haoran Zhang, Fuxian Huang, Qi Zhang (arXiv May 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Fine-tunes flow-matching VLAs (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T-N1.6) with a confidence-scaled, trust-region-inspired regression objective that "suppresses excessive gradients from low-confidence samples". It needs no prior data or reference network, noting explicit KL regularization for flows "requires a parallel reference network" and probability-flow ODE integration. It retains capabilities about 20 points better than vanilla SFT and "match[es] the efficacy of data-heavy Experience Replay in a prior-data-free regime".
papers.relation_to_proposal: An FM-specific retention mechanism for the slow backbone (Sec. 13) that needs neither the frozen old network nor old-policy ODE trajectories required by R_old (eq 25). A cheap retention baseline for the '<= 2 pp old-task loss' target in stages D/E.

papers.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: Maximilian Du, Zhanyi Sun, Chen Xu, Paarth Shah, Masha Itkina, Shuran Song (arXiv Aug 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Shows that a small set of replay experiences, those where "representations of new-task observations collapse onto those of old-task observations even though the tasks require conflicting actions", anchors retention. "Excluding only 10% Memory Anchors ... leads to more than a 4.5x increase in catastrophic forgetting on LIBERO". The ANCHORER method enriches experience-replay buffers with such anchors (a 63% reduction in high-conflict forgetting). Tested with a U-Net diffusion policy, the pi0.5 flow VLA and a real robot.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Evidence for the proposal's own caveat that "an average over old contexts controls that average, not every possible context" (after eq 28) and for App. B.4 (same context, conflicting actions). It gives a concrete rule for choosing which old contexts c ~ D_old to put in the retention penalty (eq 26) and the replay store B.

papers.title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
papers.authors_year: Nethmi Jayasinghe, Diana Gontero, Amit Ranjan Trivedi (arXiv Jun 2026)
papers.what_it_does: A wake-sleep framework. Each new skill is learned during wake, and the shared policy is consolidated offline during sleep using "frozen actor snapshots with unordered observation buffers for imitation learning". The sleep loss is frozen-actor distillation L = E_{o~B_i} ||pi_theta(o) - pi_{theta_i^wake}(o)||^2, with gradients combined by Nash bargaining plus adaptive anchoring to the previous consolidated checkpoint. Uses ACT/SAC policies, not FM. Improves Meta-World MT5 average success by 64% over the strongest non-oracle baseline.
papers.relation_to_proposal: A robot-domain precedent for (d): distilling frozen snapshots on stored observations during an offline consolidation phase with anchoring, which is structurally the proposal's L_fit + beta·R_old cycle. It lists 'trajectory-level distillation' as future work, which the proposal's FM path distillation would address.

papers.title: Is Flow Matching Just Trajectory Replay for Sequential Data?
papers.authors_year: Soon Hoe Lim, Shizheng Lin, Michael W. Mahoney, N. Benjamin Erichson (arXiv Feb 2026, v2 May 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Derives the velocity field targeted by empirical FM on sequential data: an ODE that is "a nonparametric, memory-augmented continuous-time dynamical system" whose "optimal field admits a closed-form expression as a similarity-weighted mixture of instantaneous velocities induced by observed transitions" (a linear drift plus a kernel-attention memory term). This yields FreeFM, a training-free forecaster that samples directly from historical transitions.
papers.relation_to_proposal: Gives the closed-form, nonparametric velocity-space memory an FM policy would compute from an explicit episodic store B. It is both an interpretive link to the proposal's Hopfield/attention discussion (eq 13, [12]) and a cheap non-learned baseline for the velocity reader in stages B-C.

papers.title: A Quantitative Characterization of Forgetting in Post-Training
papers.authors_year: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan (arXiv Mar 2026)
papers.what_it_does: Theory of forgetting in continual post-training of generative models under a two-mode mixture abstraction. It proves "forward-KL objectives trained on data from the new distribution drive the old weight to zero" (mass forgetting), while reverse-KL avoids it with drift controlled by overlap. It quantifies how replay interacts with each: "For forward-KL, replay must modify the training distribution to change the population optimum". It also analyzes on-policy self-distillation methods (e.g., SDFT).
papers.relation_to_proposal: Offers theoretical guidance for Sec. 13 and the analytic sanity check (Sec. 19, Gaussian models). FM regression on new-task data is a data-matching objective (training-distribution weighted), so retention depends on how replay reshapes the training mixture. This is complementary to the W2 stability bound and predicts mass forgetting without replay, matching the proposal's no-replay result of 0.470 versus about 1e-12.

checks.title: Gaussian Interpolation Flows
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page and full text (fm_2311.11475.txt). Authors are Gao, Huang and Jiao; v2 is dated 9 Jul 2024. It is published in JMLR 25(253):1-52, 2024, confirmed in the jmlr.org v25 listing. Prop 39(ii) is confirmed verbatim: if sup||grad_x v~|| <= C3, then "W2^2(Y1#mu, nu) <= (exp(2C3)-1)/(2C3) * integral integral ||v - v~||^2 p_t". It is proved with Alekseev-Groebner, Gronwall and Cauchy-Schwarz. With v = v_old and v~ = v_new this is exactly the proposal's eq 27-28 and App. B.1, including C_L, and the proposal does not cite it. Prop 20 is also confirmed: the bounds "blow up at time t = 1" unless the target score is Lipschitz. Downgraded from high: eq 27 is a supporting lemma. The proposal never claims it is new and already qualifies it. The result is a missing citation, not a threat to the fast-memory reader, the lifecycle, or the endpoint-vs-path question. Correction on Prop 39(i): it needs only a ONE-SIDED, time-varying bound (Lemma 29: grad_x v <= theta_t I) on the reference (old) field, not a Lipschitz constant. The error is measured along the approximating (new-policy) law q~_t. 'Which can be checked' is overstated: a global sup over R^d for a transformer can only be estimated empirically, not certified.
checks.corrected_description: JMLR 2024. Well-posedness and Lipschitz theory for Gaussian-interpolation flows. Prop 39(ii) gives W2^2 <= (e^{2C3}-1)/(2C3) * (L2 velocity error along the reference flow), assuming the approximating field is C3-Lipschitz; this is identical to the proposal's eq 27-28. Prop 39(i) instead needs a one-sided Jacobian bound theta_t on the reference field and measures the error along the approximating flow. Prop 20: Jacobian bounds blow up at t=1 unless the target score is Lipschitz.

checks.title: Building Normalizing Flows with Stochastic Interpolants
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Albergo and Vanden-Eijnden; comment 'ICLR 2023'; v3 9 Mar 2023) and the full text. Prop 3 is confirmed: if v^ is C^1 and K^-Lipschitz uniformly, then "W2^2(rho1, rho^1) <= e^{1+2K^} H(v^)", with H measured along the exact interpolant flow. The Appendix E proof uses Gronwall on Q_t. Step (E.4) actually needs only the one-sided inequality 2(X-X^)·(v^(X)-v^(X^)) <= 2K^|X-X^|^2. The regularizer (E.7) is only suggested; the paper says "In the numerical results presented in the paper no such regularization was included." It penalizes E||grad v^||^2 under rho_t, which does not bound the sup-Lipschitz constant the theorem needs, so as a way to keep C_L small it is only a heuristic. This is the looser, earlier version of eq 27, and Gao et al. explicitly subsume it (their bound is "slightly better than ... Proposition 3"). Cite the two together. It does not threaten any proposal contribution.
checks.corrected_description: ICLR 2023. Introduces stochastic interpolants and the quadratic velocity-regression loss. Prop 3: W2^2 <= e^{1+2K^} * (L2 velocity error along the exact flow), with the learned field K^-Lipschitz; this is a looser-constant predecessor of eq 27. Appendix E proposes, but does not use, a Jacobian-norm regularizer.

checks.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Benton, Deligiannidis, Doucet; v2 11 Feb 2024) and the full text; it was published in TMLR 02/2024. Thm 1 is confirmed: "W2(pi^1, pi1) <= eps exp{integral L_t dt}", via Alekseev-Groebner. The critique of Albergo-VE is quoted exactly ("...expect the Lipschitz constant to explode ... data supported on a submanifold"), and so is the asymmetry remark (control of the error "along the paths of Y"). Thms 2-4 use lambda-regularity plus Gaussian smoothing and are confirmed. The relation is valid but partly anticipated: Sec. 13 already says "a large Lipschitz constant makes the bound loose", and Sec. 11 mentions "a terminal noise floor". A 1D check of the exact FM field with terminal sigma=0.05 (lip_onesided_check.py in the scratchpad) sharpens the point. For a unimodal near-deterministic target the blow-up is contractive: the one-sided constant stays <= ~0, and integral L_t is about 3 while sup L is about 10. For a bimodal target, even the one-sided constant peaks near 1.5e3 between the modes at t≈0.99, and integral L_t is about 198. So eq 27 is vacuous for the proposal's own multimodal cue->action family, even with integrable L_t. Medium, not high: the issue weakens a qualified side claim, not the core method.
checks.corrected_description: TMLR 2024. W2 error bound for deterministic FM sampling with time-varying Lipschitz L_t of the learned field (W2 <= eps*exp(integral L_t)). Bounds integral L_t for the true field under lambda-regularity with Gaussian smoothing, giving polynomial bounds. Explicitly criticizes the time-uniform Lipschitz assumption that eq 27 relies on.

checks.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Liu, Gong, Liu; 7 Sep 2022) and the full text; ICLR 2023. Sec 2.3 (nonlinear extension, v^X = E[Xdot_t | X_t]) is confirmed. So are Def 3.2 (rectifiable = locally bounded v^X plus a unique ODE solution) and Thm 3.3 ("Law(Z_t) = Law(X_t)"). The proof uses a test function, the chain rule, the weak continuity equation, and uniqueness via Kurtz Cor 1.3 and Ambrosio-Crippa. This is essentially the proposal's App. A argument (eq 31-32) and its 'if well posed' caveat; the proposal cites [13] instead of this canonical source. The distillation-vs-rectification quote is confirmed. Downgraded from high: App. A is a qualified background argument, not a claimed novel theorem, and the proposal's contribution is the continual/adapted-teacher setting. Reflow on unfiltered same-seed teacher pairs is a reasonable optional consolidation arm, halfway between eq 21-22 and eq 23. It is not an essential baseline. Caveat: a deterministic teacher coupling (eps, T(eps)) is exactly the case where rectifiability is not guaranteed (see Hertrich).
checks.corrected_description: ICLR 2023. Rectified flow plus a nonlinear extension: regressing any time-differentiable interpolation process yields a flow that preserves all time marginals (Thm 3.3), provided the process is 'rectifiable' (unique ODE solution). Reflow retrains on the flow's own (Z0, Z1) pairs. This is the canonical source for the marginal-preservation argument in the proposal's App. A / eq 23-24.

checks.title: On the Relation between Rectified Flows and Optimal Transport
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Hertrich, Chambolle, Delon; v3 15 Feb 2026; comment 'Accepted for NeurIPS 2025') and the full text. Prop 13 is confirmed: for X1 = -X0 ~ N(0,I), v_t(x) = -2x/(1-2t), the loss is zero, the coupling is non-optimal and "not rectifiable". Its linear interpolant is (1-2t)X0, so this is exactly the proposal's App. A counterexample (Gamma_t = (1-2t)eps, eq 33), which should be cited. Thm 14, Ex 15 and Ex 16 are confirmed. Overclaim to correct: Thm 14 and Ex 16 concern linear interpolants of a coupling (X0, X1), not piecewise-linear teacher paths (eq 23). A deterministic teacher ODE coupling (eps, T(eps)) has a degenerate conditional law, so it also fails Thm 14 without noise injection; Sec. 5's sqrt(1-c)Z0 + sqrt(c)W is the version that keeps N(0,I). The paper also cuts against the proposal: the authors say such counterexamples "are heavily based on symmetry such that they probably will not appear in practice". That weakens App. A's use of the counterexample as the reason to prefer endpoint distillation. Ex 15 (the independent coupling is rectifiable) supports eq 21-22.
checks.corrected_description: NeurIPS 2025. Invariances and OT relations of rectified flows. Prop 13: the X1=-X0 Gaussian coupling has v_t = -2x/(1-2t), zero loss, and is non-optimal and non-rectifiable; this is identical to the proposal's App. A counterexample. Thm 14: a smooth positive conditional density P(X0|X1) implies rectifiable, smooth fields. Ex 16 and Sec. 5: small Gaussian noise injection on X0 restores rectifiability, for linear-interpolant couplings.

checks.title: Continual Learning of Diffusion Models with Generative Distillation
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Masip, Rodriguez, Tuytelaars, van de Ven; CoLLAs 2024, PMLR 274) and the full text. All numbers and quotes are confirmed: "only at the endpoint of the reverse process", L_distil, L_GD = r L_simple + (1-r) lambda L_distil, FID 211.8->23.5 and 96.4->42.3, the LwF-like and Gaussian-input variants also beating generative replay, and the limitations (lambda chosen with hindsight, generation overhead). It is a genuine precedent for R_old-style field matching against a frozen snapshot, should be cited, and is a reasonable retention baseline. Its sampling (interpolated teacher endpoints) is a cheaper alternative to exact old-ODE states. Downgraded from high, and the claim that it 'already answers part of the falsification test' is overstated. (i) It addresses OLD-task retention with a previous-task teacher, not fast->slow transfer of an adapted teacher. (ii) Endpoint replay's failure is tied to 2-step and 10-step DDIM teachers, and the paper says more teacher steps "alleviated the catastrophic loss ... to some extent". (iii) Generative distillation is output matching at forward-noised teacher samples, not trajectory-velocity regression (eq 23). Endpoint-vs-path consolidation remains untested.
checks.corrected_description: CoLLAs 2024. Continual training of DDPM-style models: generative replay with few-step DDIM teachers degrades denoising. 'Generative distillation' matches the student's noise prediction to the frozen previous-task model at forward-noised teacher samples, which greatly improves FID/KLD. This is a direct precedent for the proposal's R_old retention term, not for its endpoint-vs-path consolidation comparison.

checks.title: TraceFlow: Guiding Frozen Flow-Matching Robot Policies with Success and Failure Traces
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Yang; v1 17 Sep 2026, four days before the proposal, so concurrent) and the full text. Confirmed: the abstract wording, TraceBank with a terminal bit, the kernel-density score (eq 3) added to the base velocity with a cap relative to ||v_base|| (eq 4), and no weight updates. Real robot: 21->39/50, and 47/50 after one stacking round. The cap ablation is 24.25 (uncapped) vs 57.75 (capped) TSR against a 56.75 base. Simulation gains are selective. Corrections: guidance acts only in EARLY solver steps (lambda(t) declines to zero at t_cut), not at every step. The store is a cross-episode trace bank keyed on the CURRENT VLM state. The paper states it "does not help where a task fails for lack of event information in the policy state" (Counting and Occlusion fall below base), so as published it would not solve the proposal's Stage B delayed-association task, where the present context is identical across prefixes. It also has no head-to-head baselines and uses single-seed stacking histories. It stays high because it is the closest published instance of the proposal's recommended first method: an experience-conditioned additive velocity correction inside a frozen FM robot policy's solver. The proposal's baselines lack a velocity-space retrieval reader. A cue-keyed kernel-score reader over the same episodic store should be added, and the value of capping should be tested for the centered residual.
checks.corrected_description: Training-free guidance for frozen FM VLA action experts. Retrieves successful and failed action windows from a growing trace bank (keyed on current VLM state, progress-aligned) and adds a capped kernel-density score (attraction/repulsion) to the base velocity during early solver steps only. Improves ordering/transfer tasks, including 21->39 (47 after stacking) of 50 on a real robot. Explicitly fails on memory-dependent suites where event information is absent from the current state.

checks.title: Online Fast Adaptation and Knowledge Accumulation: a New Approach to Continual Learning (OSAKA / Continual-MAML)
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Caccia et al., 11 authors; journal ref NeurIPS 2020) and the full text. Confirmed: MAML pre-training, fast weights theta_t from current data, the update-modulation threshold lambda, the prolonged adaptation phase (gamma), and the quote "we use a buffer to accumulate data ... One can think of the update after the task boundary detection as a knowledge consolidation phase." Structural differences make the lifecycle analogy loose. C-MAML's fast weights are a full adapted copy of the SAME network. 'Consolidation' is an outer-loop MAML update of the initialization phi on buffered data, not behavioral distillation from a memory-conditioned teacher into a different backbone. The gate is a loss threshold, not a validated acceptance gate on transfer and retention. The proposal already concedes the lifecycle is not new ("not new merely because it uses the words short and long memory") and cites Progress & Compress. At most a low-priority citation.
checks.corrected_description: NeurIPS 2020. OSAKA setting plus Continual-MAML: MAML-pretrained initialization phi, online fast weights adapted from phi, loss-gated outer-loop updates of phi, and buffered updates of phi after detected task boundaries. The consolidation is into the meta-initialization of the same network.

checks.title: Meta-Learning Representations for Continual Learning (OML)
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Javed and White; comment 'Accepted at NeurIPS19') and the full text. RLN/PLN and the quote "During the inner gradient steps ... we only update the parameters in the PLN. We then update both the RLN and the PLN" are confirmed. The meta-loss uses the trajectory plus random samples. The slow-encoder/fast-net analogy is fair but generic, and the TTT layers [3] the proposal already cites cover it more directly. Correction: the claim that eq 12 is 'fit-only' and lacks OML's interference control is partly wrong. The proposal's episodes put distractors before later queries (Sec. 16), so the later-query FM loss already penalizes interference between writes within an episode. What is missing is OML's random-sample term that protects base behavior on unrelated contexts. The centered reader guarantees that only at W=W0, not after writes. Worth citing, low threat.
checks.corrected_description: NeurIPS 2019. Meta-learns a slow representation network (updated only in the outer loop) so that online SGD on a fast prediction head learns quickly with little interference. The meta-loss backpropagates through k sequential online updates and scores on the trajectory plus random samples.

checks.title: Flow map matching with stochastic interpolants: A mathematical framework for consistency models
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Boffi, Albergo, Vanden-Eijnden; v2 3 Jun 2025) and the full text. Confirmed: Assumption 3.3 (one-sided Lipschitz with C_t in L^1), Prop 3.9 "W2^2(rho1, rho^1) <= e^{1+2 integral|C_t|} L_LMD(X^)", Prop 3.10 (e^1 L_EMD, with no Lipschitz constant), and the remark that the learned map "can be singular or nearly singular". Clarification: the one-sided condition applies to the TEACHER drift b. L_LMD evaluates the teacher velocity along the student map, structurally like Gao Prop 39(i), so it supports a one-sided, integrable-C_t variant of eq 27. The losses are two-time flow-map losses, not the velocity-regression consolidation or R_old the proposal uses. Few-step consistency-style distillation is tangential to the proposal's goals. Low threat.
checks.corrected_description: Learns two-time flow maps. Lagrangian and Eulerian map distillation from a pre-trained velocity field, with W2 bounds: LMD under a one-sided, time-integrable Lipschitz condition on the teacher drift, and EMD with no Lipschitz constant but requiring map gradients. Relevant mainly as a weaker-assumption template for eq 27.

checks.title: On the Convergence and Straightness of Rectified Flow
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Bansal, Roy, Rinaldo, Sarkar; v8 7 Jun 2026) and the full text. Thm 1 (W2^2 <= e^{1+2L^} integral eps^2(t)) and the "closely resembles those established in prior works" quote are confirmed. So is Thm 2: W2^2 <= 27e^{4L^}/max{L^^2,1} * (gamma_{2,T}(Z)/T^2 + eps_vl^2), with discrete-time error at the grid points. It is useful to cite for the proposal's admitted 'numerical integration' gap, but it compares a discretized learned flow to the CONTINUOUS reference flow. gamma_{2,T}(Z) is the curvature of the reference (frozen old) flow, so it is fixed during consolidation. The suggestion that the retention penalty should monitor path curvature is therefore misapplied: curvature informs the step count T, not the penalty. The constant 27e^{4L^} is worse than eq 28 and has the same uniform-Lipschitz weakness Benton raises. Background-level.
checks.corrected_description: W2 convergence bounds for rectified-flow sampling. Continuous-time bound e^{1+2L^} * integral eps^2 under a Lipschitz learned drift. An Euler-discretization bound governed by the piecewise-straightness (curvature) gamma_{2,T} of the reference flow. Straightness analysis of 1-RF and reflow for Gaussian and mixture targets.

checks.title: On the Stability of Iterative Retraining of Generative Models on their own Data
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Bertrand, Bose, Duplessis, Jiralerspong, Gidel; v5 2 Apr 2024) and the full text; ICLR 2024. The abstract claim and the empirical tests with OTCFM, DDPM and EDM are confirmed. Scope is overstated: Thms 1-2 are for maximum-likelihood training with local strong concavity (Assumptions 1-2), infinite samples from a FIXED p_data (Thm 1), and mixing weight lambda near theta*. The FM evidence is empirical only. The proposal's cycles intentionally change targets (new skills from adapted teachers), and R_old anchors to the previous self-generated policy. That is conceptually related to self-consuming loops and to the proposal's admitted cross-cycle drift, but the paper supplies no directly usable bound. Cite as motivation for keeping a fraction of real replay data per cycle.
checks.corrected_description: ICLR 2024. Iterative retraining of a generative model on a mix of real data and its own samples is locally stable (MLE setting, fixed data distribution) if the initial model is close to the data and the real-data proportion is large enough. Pure self-training collapses. Empirical checks with OTCFM, DDPM and EDM.

checks.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning (SDFT)
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Shenfeld, Damani, Hubotter, Agrawal; v2 7 Aug 2026) and the full text. Confirmed: "using a demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher", reverse-KL distillation "on trajectories generated by the student itself", and "accumulate multiple skills over time without performance regression". The mechanism closely matches the proposal's consolidation step: a context- or memory-conditioned version of the model teaches a memory-free version of itself, with continual evaluation. The proposal's consolidation is therefore not conceptually new, although the proposal already disclaims lifecycle novelty. The domain gap is large (LLMs, discrete tokens, reverse KL, in-context demos), so medium. The actionable point is valid: eq 23 and eq 25 are off-policy (teacher or old-policy states). An on-policy FM variant, regressing on states from the student's own ODE (cf. Gao Prop 39(i) and Boffi LMD), should be an ablation.
checks.corrected_description: LLM continual learning. The same model conditioned on an expert demonstration acts as teacher for itself without the demonstration. On-policy reverse-KL distillation on student-generated trajectories beats SFT on new tasks with much less forgetting and accumulates skills sequentially.

checks.title: Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Behrouz, Hashemi, Javanmard, Mirrokni; v2 10 Jul 2026; comment: public on OpenReview since September 2025) and the full text. Confirmed: the 'Sleep' paradigm ("distill their short-term fragile memories into stable long-term knowledge with replay"), Memory Consolidation via Knowledge Seeding (upward distillation from a smaller self into an expanded network, combining on-policy distillation with RL-based imitation), and Dreaming (an RL-generated synthetic curriculum). The overlap is at the level of the sleep-inspired fast->slow framing only. The mechanism (parameter expansion, upward distillation, LLMs) differs, and the proposal already says the lifecycle is not new by name and rests its case on FM-specific transfer and reader comparisons. Cite for framing; low threat.
checks.corrected_description: LLM 'Sleep' paradigm: periodic consolidation of fast, fragile memories into slower, expanded parameters via upward 'Knowledge Seeding' distillation (on-policy distillation plus RL-based imitation), followed by an RL 'Dreaming' phase that generates synthetic rehearsal curricula.

checks.title: Adjoint Matching: Fine-tuning Flow and Diffusion Generative Models with Memoryless Stochastic Optimal Control
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Domingo-Enrich, Drozdzal, Karrer, Chen; v5 7 Jan 2025) and the full text. The ICLR 2025 submission appears on OpenReview (forum xQBRrtQM8u); acceptance was not independently confirmed. Confirmed: the initial-value-function bias p*(X0,X1) = p_base exp(r(X1) + V(X0,0)), the quote "When the sampling procedure is noiseless, i.e., sigma(t) = 0, fine-tuning naively will not have any effect because X0 completely determines X1", and that the memoryless schedule is "not only sufficient but also necessary". The relation to Sec. 10 is apt: it explains the per-seed collapse the proposal already names ("Optimizing each noise seed can send many seeds to the same outcome"). It is an amortized fine-tuning method with a specific SDE schedule, relevant only if the value reader is trained as reward-tilting control. Sec. 10 is an optional later experiment, so this is a citation or design note, not a threat.
checks.corrected_description: Casts reward fine-tuning of FM/diffusion models as stochastic optimal control. Proves naive KL-regularized control is biased by the initial value function (no effect for deterministic sampling), shows a memoryless noise schedule is necessary and sufficient to reach p_base*exp(r), and gives a regression-based Adjoint Matching algorithm.

checks.title: Robotic Policy Adaptation via Weight-Space Meta-Learning (WIZARD)
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Bianchi, Yousefi, Sampieri, Roberti, Rigazio, Galasso, Franco; v1 5 Jun 2026) and the full text. The abstract quote, the pi0.5 backbone, LIBERO results (up to ~2x on unseen collections, ~14x on unseen tasks) and a Franka real-robot test are confirmed. The meta-network is trained to REGRESS expert LoRA weights from a task embedding (instruction plus demo video), not end-to-end through future policy loss. It is task-level and one-shot: no causal online writes, no persistence across decisions, no velocity reader, no consolidation or reset. The link to the proposal's writer is only that experience maps to weights of an FM policy. An amortized-writer ablation is optional, not required. Low threat.
checks.corrected_description: Hypernetwork that generates task-specific LoRA weights for a frozen pi0.5 flow-matching VLA from a language instruction plus a short demo video in one forward pass. Trained to reconstruct per-task expert LoRA adapters. Zero-shot task adaptation on LIBERO and a real Franka.

checks.title: Preserving Foundational Capabilities in Flow-Matching VLAs through Conservative SFT (ConSFT)
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Zhang, Zhai, Zhang, Huang, Zhang; v2 19 May 2026) and the full text. Confirmed: the objective J = sg(exp(-L_SFT/tau)) * L_SFT; the claims that it "suppresses excessive gradients from low-confidence samples", that KL regularization needs "a parallel reference network" and probability-flow ODE likelihoods, the "over 20%" retention margin over SFT, and "matching the efficacy of data-heavy Experience Replay". It does not overlap any proposal contribution; it is only a candidate cheap retention baseline, so low. Its own limitations cut against using it for consolidation: it "decelerates target task convergence when acquiring fundamentally new control primitives" (consolidation targets are new behavior by design) and "provides no formal theoretical guarantee on the bounded error of the flow-matching ODE trajectories", which is the gap R_old targets. Reasonable as an optional replay-free comparison next to EWC.
checks.corrected_description: Confidence-reweighted SFT for flow-matching VLAs (pi0, pi0.5, GR00T): samples are weighted by sg(exp(-loss/tau)), a trust-region-inspired proxy that yields sparse updates and retains prior capabilities without prior data or a reference network, at the cost of slower acquisition of very new behavior.

checks.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Du, Sun, Xu, Shah, Itkina, Song; v1 27 Aug 2026) and the full text. Confirmed: representations that "collapse onto those of old-task observations even though the tasks require conflicting actions", the >4.5x forgetting increase when excluding 10% of anchors, the 63% reduction with enriched buffers (the method is called AnchorER), and a U-Net diffusion policy, pi0.5 and real-robot suites. Useful for choosing which old contexts enter D_old in eq 26 and the replay store B. The link to App. B.4 is loose: anchors are cross-task conflicts where tasks are distinguishable in principle but representations collapse, whereas B.4 concerns histories that are information-theoretically indistinguishable from the current context. It is a replay-selection ablation, not a competitor. Low threat.
checks.corrected_description: Shows that a small set of replay samples in 'conflict regions' (new-task observation representations overlap old-task ones while required actions differ) drives retention under experience replay. AnchorER enriches the buffer with such samples, cutting high-conflict forgetting by 63% on LIBERO (diffusion policy, pi0.5) and on a real robot.

checks.title: When Robots Sleep: Offline Skill Consolidation for Shared-Policy Robot Learning
checks.why: Checked the arXiv page (Jayasinghe, Gontero, Trivedi; v1 16 Jun 2026) and the full text. Confirmed: wake-sleep consolidation from frozen memories, the imitation loss L = E_{o~B_i}||pi_theta(o) - pi_{theta_i^wake}(o)||^2, Nash-bargained gradients, adaptive anchoring to theta_{k-1}^sleep, and 'trajectory-level distillation' as future work. Correction: the +64% Meta-World MT5 result uses SAC with FROZEN-CRITIC memories, not actor distillation. Frozen-actor distillation is used for ACT on SurgicAI, where results are mixed ("remaining competitive on pairwise reliability"). Policies are deterministic, not FM, and there is no separate fast memory: the wake learner is the shared policy itself. It is a robot-domain precedent for offline distillation from frozen snapshots, and the proposal already cites Progress & Compress for this idea. Low threat.
checks.corrected_description: Wake-sleep continual robot learning: each new skill is learned in wake. In sleep the single shared policy is consolidated offline against frozen skill memories (critics plus state buffers for SAC, frozen actors plus observation buffers for ACT), combining per-memory gradients by Nash bargaining with adaptive parameter anchoring. +64% average success on MT5 comes from the critic-memory variant.
